Structural one-shot kernel and proof obligations

Development design notes · ash-lang 7949b6d

Informative design work. Proposals and experiments may be incomplete or superseded. Read the language specification for current rules.

All design notes

This is the mathematical companion to OneShot.lean, governed by DN-0033. It describes checked results for an annotated control kernel and the remaining proof programme. It defines no current Ash semantics. The evidence register records the verification boundary.

Corrected-invariant milestone status

The fixed M1 inventory has 32 syntactic transition alternatives. The corrected common state has preservation endpoints for all 32. The earlier 28/32 and 31/32 counts record historical intermediate coverage and do not measure the current boundary. M0 structural resource admission, M1 transition coverage, M2 initial source admission and M3 constructive preservation are complete. M4 request availability and fuel-bounded execution are complete for valid snapshots whose immutable operation environment satisfies the admitted builtin cell-signature law.

The source request rule retains recursively checked selected-clause syntax. Capture constructs the actual selected-clause source site, including its retained continuation and saved resumption record, and connects it to the complete common state. The count records transition-family coverage, not a fraction of the broader research programme. General declaration admission, Core correspondence remains open.

ExecutableState.leave_handler and leave_clause preserve the corrected state at handler and consumed-clause exit. The latter projects the checked tail of the spent-owner requirement instead of retaining its prefix. close_value restores Unit at the recorded caller, and retire_value consumes the exact physical owner and removes its records. Each derives the actual event and all successor-state fields from the common predecessor and a closed returned value. finish_close_unit and retire cover the overlapping raw Unit alternatives through these general results. They introduce no successor-check premise, ownership oracle or runtime cleanup plan.

ExecutableState.read_cell and write_cell now preserve the same common state. They reuse the physical cell selection/update relation and require the declared builtin operation signatures. Accounting.Run.builtin retains the existing continuation root. The proofs derive reply source, access, ownership and histories from the predecessor; they add no successor-admission premise.

The common unwind source now retains Accounting.Wait and checks its executable root. Accounting.Run.dispose uses the exact lexical capture and closing scope; the special scalar discard-root constructor has been removed. All six administrative unwind proofs use this same invariant. Plain caller code skipped during unwind contributes no execution demand. Removing saved scalar records preserves the check through the generated-root store-independence proof.

start_unwind_cleanup, finish_unwind_cleanup, and finish_unwind_close derive the actual callback or caller interpretation from that predecessor. Each returns the operational event and every common-state field, without a successor premise.

leave_resource derives release safety from the authenticated returned value. The experiment's Auth.lambda judgment now requires captured resource support to appear in the existing function port, including its input, result and requested resources. The existing substitution-support lemma preserves this finite annotation. Positive fixtures retain higher-order callbacks and a pure closure returning a reference with no requested effects. A fully resource-free port cannot describe a closure retaining a resource. This is a source-judgment change within DN-0033, not a change to current Ash or Core.

Source resumption now retains a structural caller-cleanup guard, ResumeShape, separately from its restored source certificate. The corrected preservation proof uses cleanup existence, not the former scalar ResumeBudget check. Removing that unused source restriction removes its dependency on the scalar saved-demand annotation. Explicit scalar-budget results remain conditional; the ownership-only execution root does not prove a callback-effect bound. SourceAdmission.Code.request now checks the actual selected clause rows and retains their declared continuation rights. Its recursive premise checks that syntax for each fresh owner and saved-demand annotation; it also retains the predecessor's pending source. Code.capture_body_with_rights projects the body certificate at the same lexical cut. Actual declaration lookup fixes the rights from clause syntax.

The source transports cover changes both on the active stack and inside saved captures. Pure continuation insertion reuses DeepPureHistory; spent-owner insertion extends the existing transport to saved contexts. The earlier shallow interfaces remain available. Compilation, permissions, world/history weakening and absent-owner consumption preserve the stronger judgment.

A finite derivation admits an actual selected clause whose body resumes its continuation and then performs an inherited operation. The existing inherited disposing-request example also remains admitted. These are structural source examples, not complete initial-machine admission or capture preservation. Authenticated clause extraction additionally retains the selected handler's answer annotation and boundary mode. Complete initial source admission remains unfinished.

What consistency means here

For this operational language, the primary target is type and resource safety: accepted programs preserve their types, interpretation requirements, and completion obligations as they execute. Equational consistency is a separate target: the proposed laws must admit a model that distinguishes observable results. Neither target requires a monadic source calculus or transformer embedding.

The full safety theorem should quantify over every finite execution from an accepted initial configuration. Each reachable configuration must preserve the joint invariant and either step, return an appropriately typed result, or meet an explicitly specified external or internal outcome. An unmatched operation, missing resource, repeated continuation consumption, or abandoned running cleanup cannot be introduced as an allowed outcome just to make progress true. Environment assumptions for foreign operations must be stated separately.

This safety theorem does not imply termination. An obligation can remain owned forever in a diverging computation. A claim that every acquired resource is eventually released needs additional termination or liveness assumptions.

Initial calculus terms and Core programs

In the expression-level proof programme, an initial calculus term means an expression in the scoped Code representation used as the starting expression of execution. This representation also permits runtime activation identities and residual expressions. Membership in Code therefore does not establish that a term is suitable for initial execution. The current admission boundary is the explicit premises of initial_finite_prefix: source typing with an actual plan signature, local plan checking, checkInitial = true, a completion derivation and declaration-signature agreement. checkInitial computes the requirement evaluation, empty-row acceptance and closed initial resource support. These are source judgments and finite checks; they do not assume a successful next state. That scheduled theorem does not establish initial admission for the newer lexical unwinding judgments. The lexical clause compiler now includes effectful footprint callbacks under resources and choices; callbacks that invoke owners, general consuming handler bodies and complete initial admission remain open.

An initial calculus term is distinct from Ash surface text and from current Core. References below to source admission at this experimental layer mean extending that initial-term judgment and proving its full execution invariants. They do not assert a completed Ash frontend or Core translation, nor acceptance of every semantically safe program. The separate correspondence obligation must relate validated current Core programs to calculus terms and their executions.

Current theorem boundary

Scheduled capture and exhaustive progress connects all one-shot runtime cases to one retained source/runtime invariant. From that invariant, Run.progress proves an ordinary terminal or an actual step to another retained state. Run.finite_prefix constructs any requested number of actual steps unless a terminal is reached first. The terminal ledger accounts for every issued owner exactly once.

Universal preservation for retained events now covers every finite sequence of stable computation, access-checked disposal and six focus forms, starting from that same retained invariant. The fixed operation signature supplies request ports; the retained continuation contract supplies resume ports; context and annotated stack shape supply both pair components, branch conditions and resource initializers.

The remaining full-safety work is to extend consuming-clause admission to handler and effectful-cleanup scopes, establish complete initial admission for that grammar, and prove preservation for every execution admitted by a final structural transition judgment. A pure-cleanup rule wraps any locally admitted body and retains its callback through capture and disposal. Both consuming declaration recipe layers now include that rule, and their capture and signature-transport proofs cover it. Resource recipes also account for operations supplied by locally acquired providers and retain their checks through declaration selection and capture. The finite-prefix existence theorem does not replace that universal preservation obligation. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous integration are separate targets.

Direct control representation

There is one sequencing operation. A binding pushes a frame, a request selects an interpretation boundary, and a resume restores captured control above the remaining clause work. There is no computation wrapper or conversion operation.

Control has four constructors: empty control; a frame followed by control; a live clause with its recursively owned saved capture and outer control; and a spent clause followed by outer control. A saved capture can itself contain live clauses. The proofs place no bound on this nesting.

append extends the active tail and leaves dormant captures intact. The empty control is its identity and append is associative. These structural equations do not permit exchanging handler boundaries or moving resources across them.

Three projections have different purposes:

Projection Meaning
owners Unique resource, cleanup, close, and live ticket obligations, including recursively saved captures
visible Resource access provided by the active enclosing control; dormant captures are excluded
pending Ticket consumptions recorded in retained frame annotations, including saved captures

Owning a dormant resource does not make it accessible to the executing clause. Conversely, a frame with no owned resource can still contain required future consumption of an outside ticket.

Exact effect instances and dynamic interpreter activations are separate identities. DistinctNames prohibits duplicate activation names and duplicate ticket names, including spent tickets. The ownership ledger also prevents reallocating an already completed owner identity.

Structural capture and recomposition

Cut i whole cap tail selects the nearest exact instance on the active spine. Its hit constructor stops at a matching frame; its pass constructors require nonmatching frames and pass live or spent clause boundaries without searching their saved captures. SourceCut additionally requires the selected boundary to be a source handler. A matching builtin cell blocks source capture.

Induction on the cut derives whole = cap.append tail. Comparing two cut derivations proves that both the captured segment and tail are unique.

Fits c A B types a control segment that expects input type A and has answer type B. Frame ports compose at equal intermediate types. A live clause checks both its saved segment and its outer continuation. Append composition and decomposition yield the intermediate handler answer type at a capture.

For a selected operation result type Q, handler answer type A, and final answer type R, capture changes cap.append tail into live k Q A cap tail. A later resume under clause-local control front changes front.append (live k Q A cap tail) into cap.append (front.append (spent k A tail)). The original handler and crossed frames return in their original order, above the remaining clause work.

Supported c ambient checks each frame's retained access against its enclosing visible resources and ambient support. A saved capture is checked against the outer context of its live clause. Structural decomposition and support monotonicity prove support preservation through both moves.

WellFormed combines port compatibility, support, unique ownership, distinct names, kind-specific frame shapes, source-delimited saved captures, and separation of ambient resources from owned resources. capture_wellFormed and resume_wellFormed preserve all of these fields. This judgment does not yet include expression typing or sound pending-use and request annotations.

The operation payload has an additional explicit check: CaptureAdmission requires its access annotation to be available outside the captured segment. captured_private_access_cannot_cross proves that a privately owned captured resource cannot occur in an admitted payload annotation. Deriving that annotation from the payload expression remains necessary.

discard_wellFormed now establishes the corresponding invariant preservation for admitted disposal. Its input port is unit, the result type of discard; the retained clause prefix can still have any compatible answer type. The theorem materializes the close plan above a fresh close owner and the spent clause continuation. Its name proof bounds every materialized ticket-name occurrence by its occurrence in the original forest; nested retirement therefore cannot introduce a duplicate identity.

Structural disposal

Closes captured original surviving plan traverses control from inside to outside. Bindings and source handlers add no close action; a resource adds a release; an armed cleanup adds an invocation. A live clause recursively closes its saved capture, retires its ticket, then continues outward. Spent clauses add nothing. There is no constructor for running cleanup, unfinished close, resource finishing, or ticket retirement already in progress.

Each cleanup invocation checks three properties at its closing position:

  1. Its pending captured-ticket uses are empty. Cleanup actions are function values, and the current fragment's function boundary prevents retaining an enclosing structural resume capability. Handler-local capabilities created during the action are a separate expression-level matter.
  2. Its access annotation is supported by the actual materialized plan suffix and surviving outer context.
  3. Each residual request selects the same exact interpreter activation in its original and surviving contexts. Merely finding another interpreter for the same effect instance is insufficient.

The third check is the finite structural judgment SameRequests. Recursive closing carries separate original and surviving contexts because removed source handlers must remain visible to the comparison but unavailable to the closing action. The original context retains the captured candidate boundaries above the supplied discard continuation; it is not a snapshot of some earlier handler installation time.

The surviving context must come from planControl, not a projection that skips dormant captures. A later dormant capture can contribute a resource release to the materialized suffix, exposing a builtin interpreter at an earlier action's position. An annotated counterexample has an outside source override selected before materialization but a builtin selected afterward. The corrected rule rejects it. This demonstrates a mismatch between the old structural check and its generated control, not a counterexample involving accepted Ash source.

Discardable combines this close derivation with InternalUses: every pending consumption in abandoned control must name a ticket owned inside that control. This rejects abandoning the only scheduled consumption of an outside ticket. It checks annotations; it does not establish that those annotations describe all future expression behaviour.

The empty pending-use check for cleanup actions is essential here: their bodies will execute even though the captured expression suffix is abandoned. Merely owning a ticket inside that capture does not authorize an invoked action to use it after close-plan construction has replaced its live owner with retirement. close_actions_ticket_closed proves the barrier throughout the recursive forest, and a rejection example separates it from InternalUses.

Induction on closing proves that the plan contains exactly the abandoned owners, once each when the original owners were unique. It also proves that protected running completion cannot occur in the abandoned control. The pending-use theorem proves that no outside ticket occurs in the abandoned annotations. These are separate results, because ownership accounting alone does not imply either interpretation safety or pending-use safety.

PlanChecks checks access and resolvable requests against each invocation's actual suffix. close_plan_checks and close_plan_preserves_support prove that closing produces such a supported plan. PlanAt identifies a particular invocation occurrence and its suffix; CleanupOrigin independently traverses the original control. Induction connects them in close_plan_preserves_interpretation: every planned invocation comes from an original cleanup position and retains the same request interpretations there. The proof accounts for nested retirement frames, which provide no interpreter.

The discard-specific support and interpretation theorems additionally account for the administrative close frame and retained clause prefix. These are properties of the generated control and each static invocation position. They do not yet prove that arbitrary callback expression steps preserve those positions or their contexts.

Operational ownership preservation

rawPlan constructs a close plan without the support and pending-use checks. The raw ownership events use this function rather than assuming Discardable. This separation prevents the ownership theorem from being obtained by defining execution to require the desired safety conclusion.

For every raw event, the proof establishes the multiset equation owners(before) + created = owners(after) + discharged. Capture creates a ticket; resume consumes it and moves its capture; discard consumes it, creates a close obligation, and transfers captured owners into the close plan. Starting a cleanup preserves its owner and adds the saved body result's access to its running frame. A finishing event discharges the matching owner. Expression-only steps use an identity control event.

The state ledger records issued and completed owners. Its invariant is issued = owners(control) + completed, with no duplicate issued identities. Fresh allocation is checked against the entire issued history. Event preservation and induction on finite executions establish that live ownership is unique, completed ownership is unique, and an owner cannot be both live and completed.

admitted_discard_joint_preservation combines structural disposal admission with the raw event rule to construct an actual ownership step. Its result preserves both the lifetime ledger and accessible support. The ledger theorem checks freshness against all issued owners; discard_wellFormed separately needs freshness against the live forest because its invariant has no lifetime history field.

Here completion is an abstract ownership event. finishAction alone does not require a proof that a cleanup expression returned. The expression machine below now connects that event to actual application and returned unit. Neither layer claims that every callback terminates, and the raw control events are not claimed to preserve every field of WellFormed.

Expression dependencies

The expression layer has begun in Expressions.lean. It defines administrative variables, closures, application, sequencing, branches, requests, handlers, resume/discard, resource scopes, and cleanup scopes. Its dependency traversal distinguishes free value variables, resource identities, and structural tickets. Effect-instance arguments carry explicit resource tags, including nested arguments. This is a fragment and dependency model, not the complete Core syntax or kind/type system.

Closed values may retain resources but no free value variables or structural tickets. Substitution proves that the returned value supplies any additional resource dependencies and that free ticket membership is unchanged. A binding frame records the suffix's retained dependencies after removing its parameter. To use this frame as an environment-complete annotation, all other lexical values must already be substituted; ClosedExcept checks that prerequisite. Binding return then preserves available support and leaves no free variables.

Raw named substitution does not rename resource binders. ResourceFresh structurally checks that no resource dependency of the inserted value is bound anywhere in the destination expression. Under that condition, each inserted resource remains free wherever the substituted variable occurred freely. Without it, a dependency can be hidden by capture even while a dependency upper-bound theorem remains true. Local bind and beta steps require freshness; generating fresh administrative binders and proving that generation preserves meaning remain necessary before a progress claim.

pending_suffix_blocks_discard connects this syntax to the control kernel: given an actual source cut through a derived binding frame, a free suffix ticket owned outside the capture prohibits disposal. This is one necessary condition for CompatibleCuts, not a procedure for checking every reachable cut. The cleanup constructor derives its free-ticket barrier from a closed value, but still receives its residual requests as an external annotation.

The local reduction relation proves a dependency upper bound for substitution, branch selection, and strict evaluation contexts. It does not dispatch effects or execute cleanup. Neither free-ticket membership nor the union of branch dependencies establishes exactly-once consumption on each execution path. A handler's locally bound ticket is removed from its free dependencies; that removal does not verify the clause's use of the ticket.

Structural continuation usage

Usage.lean adds that separate usage judgment. Uses P S u e v checks expression e under ticket policy P, scope S, and incoming state u, yielding outgoing state v. A state is either available or consumed. A scope contains no ticket or one ticket with separate resume and disposal permissions. P supplies the permissions of each nested clause's administrative ticket binder; correspondence with source declarations and dynamic allocation remains unproved.

The following rules show sequential threading, branch agreement, and the function barrier. They check structural usage only; ordinary typing, resource support, and possible nonlocal captures are separate obligations.

structural-usage

Resume checks its operand first and requires the ticket to remain available afterward. It then consumes the ticket if resumption is permitted. Discard requires available authority and disposal permission and consumes it directly. Each nested handler clause receives only its own ticket and must finish its structural check in consumed state. A disposal permission does not discharge the independent Discardable obligation for its actual capture.

Substitution preserves usage when the replacement is a value that separately passes usage checking. Closed free dependencies alone are insufficient: a function inside a handler clause can illegally capture that clause's ticket even when the entire surrounding value has no free ticket. A checked rejection example demonstrates this distinction. local_step_preserves_usage covers binding return, beta reduction, branch selection, and the existing strict contexts. It does not yet cover request dispatch or cleanup execution.

SyntaxPath independently traverses explicit completion syntax through strict children and one arm of each conditional. It does not expand latent function bodies, dispatched operation clauses, or resumed captures. UseProtocol independently admits either an empty unchanged path or one permitted consumption from available to consumed. Induction on usage derives this protocol for every syntactic path; another proof exhibits a path for every expression, preventing vacuity. A consuming derivation therefore has exactly one permitted event on every such path. This is a theorem about structural usage, not a claim about complete execution traces.

Every explicit path event occurs in the expression's free ticket dependencies. Consequently a suffix required to consume ticket k records k in its binding frame. consuming_suffix_blocks_discard combines that result with structural capture and closing: if k is owned outside an actual cut through the frame, the cut cannot be discarded. Reachable-cut analysis remains necessary for CompatibleCuts, including nonlocal effects from called functions and clauses.

Expression-bearing execution

Execution.lean gives the administrative expressions actual control payloads. A strict context stores the pending syntax and its lexical ticket scope. Focusing pushes that context; returning a value reconstructs its expression under the saved scope. Handler entry installs the interpretation before executing its body. Beta reduction enters the function body without an enclosing structural ticket. Ordinary values are represented by substituted closed syntax; this is not yet a proof of the full Core environment model.

Static ticket binders and dynamic owners are distinct. A clause binds its source ticket name to the newly allocated owner. Pending frame annotations translate free ticket dependencies through that scope, failing if a name is unresolved. This records the actual owner rather than assuming that a binder's numeral already identifies it. Handler clauses retain no enclosing ticket, while returning through a frame restores the lexical scope needed by its pending code. Connecting these administrative translation checks to all source usage derivations remains necessary.

HandlerCut selects and moves the actual source handler, intervening frames, and recursively owned captures. Its reconstruction theorem preserves those payloads, not just their erasure. Its projection is the existing SourceCut. Builtin cell selection similarly searches only active control, stopping at a nearer matching source override. Reads return the stored integer; writes replace it without changing the cell's owner. The prototype uses fixed numeric read and write keys; Core operation authentication is not proved by these rules.

Cleanup acquisition stores its callable. Normal completion stores the body value in a running frame and evaluates action () by ordinary application. The running frame's access is the union of the action's dependencies and the saved result's dependencies. Keeping only the action's access would lose a real dependency while its body result waits. A checked support theorem proves this transition preserves retained-frame support when the saved value is supported outside the frame. Only a returned unit removes the running frame and returns the saved value.

Concrete disposal retains callable values and cell payloads in its close plan, omits abandoned expression contexts and source handlers, and rejects running or unfinished close control. Its projection agrees with rawPlan; materialized control agrees with planControl. The same application and unit-return rules execute a disposal callback before advancing outward. An example proves that an admitted disposal runs a callback which reads a retained cell before release. Another begins with a handler and cleanup expression, executes an outward callback request, captures and resumes its running frame, then returns the original body result.

raw_step_erases proves that every expression transition projects to a raw ownership event. Fresh allocation then yields ledger preservation for arbitrary finite machine executions. These are ownership and concrete execution results; frame ports, current-expression types, payload support, usage admission, and capture compatibility are not yet a joint invariant. In particular the unchecked machine can return resourceRef r from a released resource scope while preserving the ledger. That counterexample is proved explicitly and must be excluded by the eventual typing/support theorem, not by weakening what resource safety means.

Resource identities in this machine are already instantiated administrative names. Source instantiation and fresh handler activations remain unproved. Ordinary arrow/effect typing, handler coverage, and residual-request inference are also separate from the supplied port and request annotations. These gaps prevent a progress or full Core-correspondence claim.

Expression and retained-control support

Access.lean supplies a separate access layer over the raw expression machine. AccessValid combines Supported for the whole recursive control with support for the current expression's resource dependencies. Dormant captures contribute owned resources and retained dependencies, but do not make their resources visible to the current clause.

AccessChecks is a structural judgment on the configuration before a step. It quantifies over candidate release, source-capture, and disposal decompositions:

  1. A returned closed value must not retain the identity of the resource being released. It may retain a still-enclosing resource.
  2. A closed request operand crossing a selected source cut must have all its resource dependencies in the surviving tail or explicit ambient support.
  3. A resolved disposal with a constructed raw plan must satisfy Discardable for that capture, plan, and surviving control.

These premises inspect existing values, cuts, and close derivations. They do not assume AccessValid for the resulting configuration. The independent raw step relation is unchanged.

raw_step_preserves_access proves preservation across every raw constructor under these premises. Focus transfers context dependencies into a pending frame; plug reconstructs their union with the returned value. Capture combines the selected handler's retained dependencies with the operand substitution bound. Cleanup start retains the saved result; cleanup return restores it. Disposal uses the previously proved support of the materialized close plan.

AccessRunSteps adds the local checks to execution with fresh lifetime allocation. Induction proves access_run_joint_preservation: the ledger and expression/control support survive every finite such execution. Visibility implies live ownership. Induction through Supported also shows that every retained frame dependency, including those in dormant captures, has an owner somewhere in the recursive control or is provided by the ambient assumption. With empty ambient support, the ledger therefore excludes completed resources from both the current expression and all retained frames. This does not imply that every live obligation is eventually discharged.

Checked examples reject the earlier dangling-reference release and prove that its final unsupported state cannot be reached by a locally admitted execution from supported initial configurations. Positive examples execute acquisition and release, preserve an outer reference while releasing an inner resource, and admit the full outward-capture/resumption cleanup trace. These are access and ownership derivations, not ordinary expression-type derivations.

The remaining bridge is source admission: prove that source checking supplies these local checks for every reachable configuration. AccessChecks does not establish coverage of operations, continuation-use protocols, result/port typing, or interpretation preservation throughout arbitrary callbacks. Its nonempty ambient list is assumed support; lifetime validity of external support must be specified separately.

Annotated expression types and frame ports

Typing.lean defines Typed signature environment ticket allowed expression type for the administrative monomorphic fragment. It checks ordinary values, application, binding, branches, requests, handlers, resume/discard, resources, and cleanup. ClausesTyped checks the operation signature and the clause's operand, resumption, and common answer types. Covers checks every operation in the signature, and handler typing also rejects duplicate clause keys. These judgments are proposed proof-fragment rules; their full execution soundness is not yet proved.

The shared port type now includes resource-indexed cell references and function annotations. A function records argument/result types, a latent request bound, and retained resource support. Ty.resources includes identities in all those positions. This is a conservative internal annotation, not a public lifetime syntax or the full Core type/effect system. Effect lists express membership bounds; polymorphism, kind checking, row/lacks constraints, and annotation inference remain separate.

A lambda checks its body without an enclosing structural ticket. Its retained support comes from free body dependencies: direct resource identities are included, and free ordinary variables contribute the resource support of their lexical types. Unused environment entries contribute nothing. The lambda's parameter is removed before this capture check. typed_value_support proves that every actual dependency of a typed value appears in its type's resource support. Therefore the resource rule's exclusion of its own identity from the result annotation implies the local returned-value access check. The rule also excludes that identity from residual outward effects. Fresh administrative names and realization of lexical type environments are still prerequisites for source correspondence.

typed_payload_at_boundary derives the local payload check when its annotated type support is available outside the actual capture. The stronger SignatureSupported assumption bounds operation operand/result annotations by the exact instance's resource identities, allowing selected-handler support to supply that boundary premise. This is only a sufficient shortcut: an ordinary callable payload can retain a resource absent from its effect instance. Checked examples admit such a payload using boundary support and reject treating its signature as instance-bounded. General source checking needs support summaries that retain this distinction.

ContextTyped derives ports from the actual pending syntax. Typed focus yields a child type and a context from that input to the original result type. Plugging a child of that type reconstructs a typing derivation for the whole expression. Given lexical ticket translation and a typed outer stack, focus constructs an actual PlainData frame and raw machine transition with composable ports. This replaces supplied ports for that transition with expression-derived evidence; it does not yet type every frame in every reachable machine configuration.

Canonical-form lemmas identify typed values at unit, boolean, integer, reference, and function types. Coverage yields an actual ClauseAt selection, and selection from ClausesTyped yields the corresponding clause-body typing. These facts are ingredients for progress. The substitution layer below connects them to beta, binding return, and the instantiated clause expression. Their connection to dynamic capture instantiation and the entire typed machine remains necessary.

Resume and disposal have separate effect contracts in TicketType. The typing rules require the relevant contract to fit the current effect bound. A handler clause initially uses the handler residual bound for both contracts. That assignment is not evidence that an arbitrary captured close fits the contract. PlanTyped therefore traverses the actual disposal plan: each invocation must have a checked Unit -> Unit function annotation whose latent requests equal the action's request annotation. Each such request must be provided by a cell in that invocation's actual remaining materialized suffix or appear in the outward close bound. InvocationAt identifies the exact suffix, and plan_provided_resolves proves that every discharged request resolves to its actual builtin even with arbitrary outer control appended. A resource released before an invocation provides nothing at that position. Release and retirement entries add no callback. DisposalTyped combines this judgment with actual raw plan construction and Discardable for the surviving control.

disposal_invocation_typed proves that each scheduled application has result unit under its local effect bound: suffix-provided cell effects plus outward effects. The cell-reading disposal example therefore has a cell effect at its invocation and an empty outward close bound. Removing the retained cell, or releasing it before invocation, rejects that empty bound. This connects close-plan annotations to callable typing and concrete suffix interpretation; it does not yet establish that callback reductions preserve effects, nor that source admission supplies the plan check at every reachable discard. Interpretation checks and ownership remain independent required parts of that later joint theorem.

Closed substitution and local preservation

Substitution.lean proves environment relevance before substitution. AgreeOn requires two ordinary environments to agree on the free value-variable dependencies of an expression or clause list. Extending both at a binder restores agreement for its body; direct resource and ticket identities are unaffected. retained_support_congr then preserves the capture annotation of a lambda under that environment change. A closed typed value has no free ordinary variables, so its typing transports to any ordinary environment.

substitution_support_bound compares two representations of the same retained value: a free variable whose environment entry carries an annotated type, and the closed syntax inserted for it. If the variable is unused, substitution is the identity. If it occurs, the previously proved value-support bound accounts for every inserted resource through the variable's original type annotation. This proof does not silently enlarge a closure's support list.

Mutual induction over expressions and clauses yields typed_substitution and clauses_typed_substitution. They preserve the exact result annotation, including function support and latent requests. Lambda, binding, and clause parameters shadow substitution at matching names; different binders use commuting environment extensions. Clause keys and coverage survive unchanged. The replacement must be both a closed value and typed at the parameter's type.

Immediate effect weakening preserves latent function and ticket contracts. Code checked without an enclosing ticket can be placed in an enclosing ticket context without adding a use of it; nested clause binders retain their own contracts. These lemmas connect typed substitution to beta reduction, whose body is checked across the function barrier. Induction over the independent LocalStep relation proves local_step_preserves_types for binding return, beta, branch selection, and all its local contexts. Combining that result with existing usage and dependency proofs yields local_step_preserves_joint for types, structural usage, and available expression support.

selected_clause_substitution_typed uses the actual ClauseAt selection, ClausesTyped, and the known operation signature to type the clause expression after operand substitution. It preserves the clause's lexical ticket binder and declared resume/close contracts. The execution machine's mapping from that binder to a fresh dynamic owner remains a separate invariant.

Checked examples preserve a closure's resource support when a retained ordinary variable becomes a literal handle. A shadowed handle contributes no support to an identity closure, allowing the surrounding resource to return that closure. The cleanup example's selected clause has a typed operand instantiation. A separate counterexample proves that typed substitution can hold while ResourceFresh fails: annotation preservation does not establish resource-name hygiene. The raw bind and beta rules continue to require that hygiene check.

These theorems concern local expression reduction. They do not dispatch operations, move continuations, execute disposal, or discharge scope owners. Full machine preservation must connect them to the typed control forest, resource store, dynamic ticket mapping, and admission of every reachable cut.

Typed control transitions and ticket bindings

Dispatch.lean proves transition-local constructions for capture, resumption, and disposal entry. handler_cut_ports follows the actual HandlerCut and a supplied Fits derivation to determine the captured segment's answer port from handler.answer. It is not a separately chosen existential type. Clause selection also determines the lexical ticket binder; typed and usage-preserving substitution install the same operand in that clause.

ScopeAgreement relates the type scope, usage scope, and runtime scope at that binder. The runtime owner can differ from the lexical binder. TicketBinding adds structural live/spent cases over actual active stack occurrences. A live occurrence has the static ticket's input and answer ports and an available protocol state. A spent occurrence retains the answer port and consumed state. Its input, effects, and permissions are historical annotations, not facts recoverable from a spent frame. The prefix may include other clauses; dormant captures are not searched. This relation alone is not name uniqueness, nearest-owner lookup, or proof of the captured segment's declared effect contracts.

ticket_binding_state_unique combines occurrence correspondence with the ticket-name component of DistinctNames to prove that one runtime owner cannot have conflicting states. spent_binding_blocks_available excludes an available binding for a spent owner under that premise. The proof inventories ticket occurrences across active and dormant control and includes retirement names. A checked counterexample places a spent occurrence above a live occurrence of the same owner. Its lifetime ledger holds because spent names are not live owners, while name uniqueness fails. Ownership and name invariants must therefore remain separate components of the complete machine invariant.

typed_capture_step uses coverage to find an actual executable clause and constructs a fresh RunStep. The resulting entry has expression typing, structural usage, a live TicketBinding, composed ports, expression/control support, and the lifetime ledger. Payload support is derived from its annotated type at the actual outside boundary. The theorem permits callable payloads whose retained resources are absent from the effect instance.

typed_resume_step takes a live structural binding and independently checked resume typing and usage. It obtains the permission from the usage derivation, matches the value's type to the capture input, restores the capture above the whole clause prefix, and constructs a spent binding below that restored control. It preserves the value's type and usage, composed ports, accessible support, and lifetime ledger for this step.

typed_discard_step checks the actual capture and surviving prefix through DisposalTyped. It constructs the raw close-plan entry, retains its PlanTyped derivation, consumes the ticket, and preserves typed unit, usage, ports, support, and ledger. Close permission and the outward close effect bound come from the independent usage and typing derivations. The transition creates a fresh protected close owner; it does not complete cleanup callbacks.

An instance of the capture and resume theorems moves a running cleanup under lexical binder 9 and runtime owner 3, with Unit input and Integer answer. The disposal theorem admits the cell-reading callback with an empty outward close bound because the remaining materialized suffix provides the cell. Negative examples reject a wrong capture input annotation and mismatched static binders.

These are constructions under explicit local premises, not full source preservation. Fits does not type retained expressions. Capture does not establish that the old request row permits the operation, realize old lexical environments, or derive hygiene for instantiated source binders. No theorem here validates the saved continuation's future resume effects or all future cuts. Plan typing alone also does not supply callback usage derivations. A whole-machine invariant must provide these facts and preserve them through every transition, including callback execution and owner discharge.

Name history across execution

Names.lean adds history for ticket names and handler activations to the existing expression machine. NameHistory bounds the multiplicity of every retained ticket name by its count in the owner-allocation record. It similarly bounds active and dormant handler activations by a separate allocation history. Together with fresh allocation, these bounds establish the recursive DistinctNames invariant, including spent and retiring ticket names.

raw_step_name_bounds proves the necessary count bounds for every raw transition. For disposal, raw_plan_ticket_name_bound follows from raw ownership accounting and the relation between owned tickets and retained names; it does not assume Discardable or post-state name validity. Expression shapes and actual frames determine newly entered handler activations. Focus and closed value exits cannot masquerade as handler entry. Capture and resumption move existing activations without adding allocation events.

NamedStep retains the actual raw transition, existing owner freshness, and fresh handler activation allocation against history. named_steps_preserve proves name-history and ledger preservation for every finite sequence. named_execution_has_unique_ticket_state then extends the dispatch layer's state-uniqueness result across those executions. Handler-activation history is monotone, and named_execution_never_reallocates excludes reallocation after an earlier activation has exited.

Control.spentNames counts true spent clause markers, including those inside dormant captures. Retirement frames are excluded because they still own tickets. ticket_name_count_accounting splits retained ticket names into owned occurrences and spent markers. Combining this equality with the name bound and ownership ledger places each spent marker in the completion record. spent_binding_was_discharged exposes that connection for runtime bindings.

Completion records grow monotonically along ordinary RunSteps. Consequently, consumed_binding_never_available excludes a later available binding for an already consumed owner, even after its spent boundary disappears. This result uses the ledger and name-history premises at the starting configuration; it does not reconstruct how an arbitrary supplied initial history was obtained. The history of a run from empty initial records is accumulated from its actual allocation and discharge events.

NamedAccessSteps puts name allocation and resource access checks on the same actual transitions. named_access_steps_preserve establishes their joint preservation with the ledger. The running-cleanup example captures, resumes, finishes cleanup, exits the handler and leaves the spent clause under these checks, starting with empty histories. A raw entry can reuse an exited handler activation, but the history check rejects it. The prior conflicting live/spent example likewise fails NameHistory.

Freshness remains an input to these administrative execution rules. Source freshening and an allocator implementation remain to be proved. Resource support still requires local pre-state admission checks; no initial source checker is shown to supply them. These finite-execution results do not yet preserve the complete expression/stack type, usage, and effect invariant.

Typing retained code

Retained.lean types actual stored expressions. FrameTyped checks pending contexts, handler clauses and coverage, callable cleanup values, saved cleanup results, and cell answer types. StackTyped composes these derivations through both active frames and dormant captures. Erasing these derivations gives the earlier port judgment Fits; the converse fails.

TicketSignatures records historical input and answer types. ScopeTyped connects a runtime binder and owner to this table. Live, spent, and retirement frames refer to the same historical contract. The table grants neither ownership nor permission to consume a ticket. TicketSignaturesBacked relates its domain to allocation history, making ownership freshness sufficient for fresh table extension. Extending the table preserves all existing frame and scope derivations.

handler_cut_retains_typing decomposes a typed stack at the actual selected handler. capture_constructs_typed_configuration derives the operation result type from the typed request and selects a typed clause from that handler. It constructs a capture step and extends the table while preserving typing of all retained code. Administrative substitution hygiene remains an explicit premise. resume_preserves_configuration_typing uses runtime binder resolution and the shared ticket signature to restore the capture above the entire clause prefix.

raw_value_step_preserves_typing covers every raw transition whose current expression is a closed value. This includes plugging a pending context, handler and cell return, starting and finishing cleanup, leaving a spent clause, closing, and retirement. Callable cleanup types justify application to unit; saved-result types justify restoring the result after cleanup. A typed cell answer excludes the released identity from the actual returned value.

make_plan_retains_types derives PlanContentsTyped from the actual saved stack. Materialization preserves callback and retirement typing, and discard_preserves_configuration_typing uses that result for the ticket chosen by runtime binder resolution. This checks code and value types independently of resource support, exact interpretation, outward effects, and usage admission.

Positive examples cover running-cleanup capture, resumption and completion, and materialization of cell-reading disposal. Negative examples reject integer cleanup values, boolean saved results at integer answer ports, and a cell answer that exposes its released identity, even where the earlier port check succeeds.

Immediate effect bounds are existential in AtType and are not related across frames by this layer. The historical table also omits future continuation effects and usage permissions. Arbitrary annotations in raw non-value entry rules prevent a theorem that every raw transition preserves these types. The following layer constructs typed entries. A joint type/effect/usage invariant and source initialization remain necessary.

Deriving administrative entries

Entries.lean derives the annotations that raw entry rules leave unconstrained. Mutual expression and clause proofs show that every free ticket belongs to the current static ticket scope, and that handler clauses have no free outer tickets. ScopeTyped then translates a pending context's free ticket names to actual runtime owners. Focus derives both ports and this translation from the source expression, producing a typed frame and an actual raw step.

A second mutual proof places every free ordinary variable in the typing environment. Consequently, a typed value under the empty environment satisfies ClosedValue, and a typed parameter body satisfies ClosedExcept. These facts derive lexical closure for bind, application, cleanup registration, and capture. Administrative resource-name freshness remains independent: typing alone does not prevent substitution from capturing an instantiated resource identity.

Handler entry derives its answer port, coverage, and free-ticket barrier from the typed handler expression. The constructed frame retains the supplied activation name explicitly. Cell entry derives the answer port and its no-escape condition. Cleanup entry derives the callable's latent request list, closed value, and saved-body answer port. Each construction produces an actual raw transition and a typed resulting configuration for the existing typed tail.

Bind and function application construct actual typed transitions with lexical premises derived from typing and resource freshness supplied separately. Application enters the function body under no structural ticket, as the raw machine requires. Branch selection preserves configuration typing. typed_capture_lexical_admission derives a closed operand and lexical closure of every selected clause from the typed request and actual retained handler. It does not derive resource freshness, payload support, or continuation effects.

CellUpdate follows the active exact-dispatch spine, including live and spent clause boundaries. Its typing proof preserves all retained code while updating the integer payload. Read and write preservation require withCellSignatures: the builtin read returns an integer and write returns unit. A checked counterexample assigns a Boolean result to a builtin read, demonstrating why arbitrary signatures cannot justify the machine's fixed integer result.

Another counterexample gives a raw handler entry a Boolean answer annotation while its typed source returns an integer. Type-directed entry derives the correct annotation. A positive focus example translates lexical ticket 9 to pending runtime owner 3; a different free ticket is rejected by typing.

These results cover the remaining local value-type cases through preservation or type-directed construction. They do not supply one joint effect/usage invariant for every execution, reconstruct source resource names, or prove progress. Immediate effect bounds remain unrelated across frames at this layer.

Effect interfaces across the ordered stack

Effects.lean connects the previously separate immediate effect bounds across retained control. ContinuationContract records input and answer types plus resume and disposal effects. EffectScope connects those exact fields to a runtime binder and historical owner. Its projection supplies the earlier type-only ticket registry; it grants no ownership or consumption permission.

EffectFrame checks actual pending contexts, handler clauses, cleanup functions, and saved values against an incoming and outward effect interface. A handler adds its exact instance to the incoming bound; a cell adds its builtin instance. Plain frames and cleanup propagate the bound, checking their stored code and callback requests against it. Closing and retirement provide no new effects.

EffectStack composes those interfaces in stack order. It admits a smaller incoming requirement and a larger outward bound. A live boundary separately checks its dormant capture against the historical resume contract and requires both declared contracts at the active tail. Spent boundaries provide no effects. EffectConfigurationTyped combines current expression typing, the earlier retained-stack type derivation, and this connected effect judgment on the same actual stack.

Composition, decomposition, and nearest-handler cut decomposition are proved for arbitrary finite stacks and recursively saved captures. Capture selects the outward row of the actual handler, types the substituted clause under that row, and preserves existing frame contracts when adding the fresh ticket contract. Resumption checks that same historical contract and restores the capture above the entire clause prefix. Enlarging an outward bound requires a subset proof; it does not remove any requirement of retained code.

current_request_is_interpreted_or_exported proves that a typed current request resolves through the existing nearest exact resolver or belongs to the outward bound. With an empty outward row, it must resolve. Dormant captures are excluded from active lookup. This is instance-level availability, not operation-level progress or a proof that removing an interpreter is safe.

Close-plan materialization derives an interface from the plan's local builtin providers plus its declared closing row to that closing row. Each invocation's requests are checked at its actual remaining suffix. Disposal composes this interface through closing control and the retained clause prefix. PlanTyped remains an explicit premise; effect preservation does not replace Discardable, resource support, or continuation usage checks.

Every raw transition starting from a closed value preserves the connected type/effect judgment, including pending-context plugging, cleanup application, saved-result restoration, and owner discharge. Ordinary bind, application, branch selection, and builtin cell operations preserve it as well. Focus and scope entry construct actual raw steps with type/effect-checked annotations. The application and bind type proofs retain the raw machine's separate resource-hygiene requirement when used as execution steps.

The nested-handler example has a real pending request for a second effect. Its capture records a nonempty residual; resume, plug, and bind reach the outer activation through the inner handler and spent ticket. A raw trace accompanies the typing and lookup result. The dormant-handler example first exhibits an inhabited state retaining a matching handler, then rejects using it for active dispatch. A disposal example retains a cell-reading callback's builtin while exporting no effects.

This layer uses sufficient contracts: live boundaries require both declared effect bounds regardless of usage permissions, and capture gives resume and disposal the same residual required by the current clause typing rule. It does not infer distinct minimal bounds. The joint layer below combines these transition results with usage, ownership, support, and allocation history. Source-derived admission of every reachable capture and disposal remains open.

Scheduled continuation demand

Demand.lean connects structural usage to runtime ticket identities for individual code fragments. Its CodeDemand judgment records either no outer consumption or one consumption of the runtime owner corresponding to the lexical ticket. It checks nested clauses and latent function bodies in both cases. ContextUses decomposes actual focused expressions and recomposes their usage when the child is plugged back in.

The translation theorem equates demand membership with translated dependency membership. It deliberately does not equate list multiplicities: a conditional with resume in one arm and disposal in the other contains two ticket occurrences but requires one consumption on either path. Sequential double consumption is rejected by usage checking.

Whole-control accounting and accessibility are established for the transitions in the following layer; complete machine preservation remains open.

Continuation usage across retained control

ControlUsage.lean defines FrameDemand, StackUsage, and ConfigurationUsage. Frame demands come from checked executable code. Live boundaries own their ticket but add no demand themselves: its future consumption must occur in code. Retirement frames add a demand for their own ticket and expose no resumption authority. Spent boundaries add neither.

StackUsage has an external ticket interface for segment composition. An active frame's demanded tickets must be available in its remaining active suffix or that interface. A live boundary checks its dormant capture against the tail's active tickets and the external interface, excluding the boundary's own ticket. It does not expose the dormant capture's tickets to surrounding code. All dormant code participates in total demand accounting.

At a complete configuration, the external interface is empty. Current-expression demands must be actively accessible. The concatenated current and retained demands must be a permutation of recursively owned live and retiring tickets, which must be unique. owned_tickets_project connects this inventory to the existing control ownership projection; owned_tickets_unique derives its uniqueness from Unique. Registry entries record historical permissions, so an empty-demand scope may retain a consumed ticket's mapping.

Structural append and decomposition theorems preserve this interface. Capture uses the actual handler cut and selected clause, inserts a fresh runtime owner with that clause binder's permissions, and preserves configuration usage. Restoration uses balance and uniqueness to establish that no remaining demand names the consumed owner. It can then remove that owner from the full clause prefix's external interface, including the interfaces of nested dormant code, and restore the capture in front of the retained clause work.

For disposal, the demand-to-pending bridge accounts separately for retirement. InternalUses bounds captured pending uses by captured live tickets. Combined with global balance, uniqueness, and active accessibility, it establishes that the capture's demand list is a permutation of its owned ticket list. Actual makePlan retains callback usage proofs and registered retirement owners; materialization replaces abandoned demands with the plan's retirement demands. This establishes usage preservation under those structural premises. It does not replace Closes, resource support, or the disposal effect contract.

Every raw transition starting from a closed value preserves configuration usage, including plugging pending code, starting/finishing cleanup, and retirement. A separate theorem rejects normal value return through a live unconsumed clause boundary. These are safety statements; they do not establish eventual consumption during divergence.

Examples check a nested live prefix with an outside demand in its dormant capture, distinct activation names, an actual restoration step, existing cleanup capture and cell-disposal states, and an inhabited balanced-count state rejected for inaccessible current resumption. Internal-ticket disposal also executes demand replacement and retirement while preserving usage. The next layer extends these local results to admitted finite executions.

Usage preservation through execution

UsageExecution.lean proves configuration-usage preservation for every RawStep constructor. Focus splits current demand between the actual child and saved context. Ordinary computation and entry preserve the checked code demands; builtin cell updates preserve the control's ticket structure. Capture, resumption, disposal, and closed-value cases reuse the structural control proofs above.

The only additional usage premises are fresh registry allocation and internal captured demand at disposal. UsageRegistryHistory identifies registry keys with historically issued tickets. Fresh owner allocation then excludes registry overwrite. The existing AccessChecks.discard supplies Discardable, which contains the required InternalUses derivation. These are checks on the actual pre-state and close plan, not assumed properties of the resulting state.

advanceUsageTickets computes the registry update from event and resulting configuration data. The raw-step proof establishes that its insertion branch is precisely capture and records the selected binder's permissions. Registry history is preserved, including entries for consumed tickets. This theorem checks the registry domain; agreement with type/effect registry contracts is a separate obligation.

named_access_steps_joint_usage uses the same NamedAccessSteps as the existing name/access theorem. From initial ledger, name history, support, usage, and registry history, it proves all five properties at the end of any such finite execution. No extra per-step usage oracle is supplied. The two concrete examples instantiate the theorem for outward cleanup capture/resumption from empty histories and for disposal of a resource-bearing capture whose cleanup reads its retained cell before release. The latter starts from an administrative state; its prior source execution is not assumed proved.

The theorem still requires explicit access checks at each reached pre-state. It does not derive them from a source checker or prove progress. The following layer joins types/effects to the same registry and configuration for individual transitions and concrete executions.

Joint contracts and transition preservation

Joint.lean defines a single historical Registry. Each owner maps to a TicketRecord containing an effect contract and consumption permissions. Projection yields the existing effect table, its type table, and the usage table. The judgments remain independent: a type/effect derivation cannot grant permission to resume or dispose. Registry insertion installs the two contract facets under the same runtime owner.

Valid combines the ledger, name history, support, effect configuration typing, whole-control usage, and registry history. initial_configuration_valid derives this invariant for empty control and histories from a closed annotated expression's type, usage, and resource-dependency checks. This is initialization of the invariant, not proof that source checking admits every future cut.

The capture theorem starts from that complete invariant and the actual handler cut. Type checking determines the selected clause and capture contract; the same raw event supplies its binder to usage insertion. Freshness follows from the same issued-owner history. Resumption recovers its contract from the actual active live boundary. Disposal checks the actual plan against that record's closing effect bound and the independent structural support/interpretation judgment. All six facets then follow along the same event. The private proof assembly lemma combines already-derived component results; it is not an execution-admission rule with an assumed postcondition.

Closed-value preservation includes callback invocation, saved-result restoration, resource return, close completion, and retirement. OrdinaryStep describes the existing bind, application, branch, and exact builtin transitions and projects to RawStep; their proofs preserve the complete invariant. Focus and handler, cell, and cleanup entry construct type-directed annotations and preserve all facets. Entry access checks are derived from the pre-expression's form.

An eleven-event execution starts from a fully checked resource-bearing live capture, disposes it, evaluates its cleanup callback, reads cell 4 containing 17, and releases the obligations. The same registry and NamedAccessSteps witness carry Valid through that execution. A separate resource entry/return example starts from an expression with empty histories. The negative permission example keeps the effect projection unchanged but denies disposal; effect typing holds while the joint invariant is impossible.

These results cover each transition family, but do not give a universal theorem for arbitrary raw annotation choices. A complete admitted execution relation must connect the type-directed annotation choices, actual boundary checks, and freshness requirements to source checking, then preserve that admission through execution. Disposal-plan checking and cut compatibility remain substantive requirements. General theorems retain ambient support and outward requests as explicit parameters; both concrete executions are closed in those parameters. Source instantiation, relative progress, and the Core comparison are still open; no full one-shot safety claim follows yet.

Derived admission and progress cases

Admission.lean derives release checks from result typing and focus/ordinary-step checks from their expression forms. Capture uses the actual operand type's resource support at the selected outside boundary. The stronger SignatureSupported shortcut remains optional; an admitted callable payload example retains an outside cell absent from its effect instance.

The module also separates closing compatibility from current caller control. OpenRequests requires identical local targets in original and materialized prefixes, or a request unresolved in both and declared in the outside interface. OpenCloses traverses the actual capture and planned suffix, including nested live captures. It has no rule for running or other protected completion frames. Materialization supplies one shared outside caller to both prefixes and yields the existing exact-interpretation Closes judgment.

PreparedDisposal contains an actual successful makePlan, PlanTyped, OpenCloses, and internal ticket-use evidence. Its outside resource interface is computed from retained dependencies not owned by the capture. For closed ambient and outgoing interfaces, prepared_disposal_at_live_boundary derives the needed outside support and requests from Joint.Valid, even with additional clause control before the live boundary. This compares original and closing lookup under the same current caller; it does not preserve a historical outside target across caller changes. Positive examples cover local and external cell requests. The certificate does not grant execution authority or imply a complete admission checker.

A negative example has all six fields of Joint.Valid but a running cleanup inside its dormant capture; makePlan returns none. It therefore cannot have a prepared certificate. This exhibits a missing progress premise for an administrative state, without establishing source reachability or inconsistency. AccessChecks.discard only checks a plan conditional on its existence, so that field alone cannot fill the gap. Source admission must establish readiness for reachable disposal, rather than classify a failed admission check as a permitted terminal outcome. Certificate completeness and preservation through future capture remain open.

PreparedCaptures recursively checks retained control and supplies a certificate for every live record permitting disposal. Resume-only records do not require one. prepared_discard_access_checks connects this structural judgment to the current discard's access field. Examples admit resource-bearing disposal, reject the protected running-capture disposal, and retain that capture under a resume-only record. Source establishment remains open; the next layer proves local preservation with a certificate check for new captures.

Progress.lean proves progress cases without assuming a transition witness. value_progress derives empty control or an actual NamedAccessStep preserving the same registry and all joint fields. Canonical forms supply unit for protected completion frames. Usage balance and uniqueness exclude a returned value at a live boundary: its ticket cannot be consumed by the dormant capture or the outside tail. At empty control, the ledger proves that completed owners are exactly the issued owners, without duplicates.

resume_value_progress derives the lexical owner and its active live boundary from code demand and active accessibility. Typing supplies a closed operand; resumption then preserves the joint invariant through full-prefix restoration. These two progress cases retain ambient/outward parameters.

For closed interfaces, prepared_discard_progress adds disposal progress from Joint.Valid and PreparedCaptures. Current demand supplies the live boundary and its disposal permission. The matching historical record supplies the certificate; finite issued history supplies a fresh close identity. The actual admitted step preserves Joint.Valid. The following layer strengthens this result with PreparedCaptures preservation. These cases alone do not establish termination, the remaining non-value cases, or progress for all source-admitted executions.

Preservation of prepared captures

PreparedExecution.lean proves preservation of PreparedCaptures for every raw transition. RegistryExtends keeps existing records immutable. AllocationPrepared distinguishes events without newly captured tickets from a new live capture whose record supplies a concrete disposal certificate when its permissions allow disposal. It checks only that local obligation, not the complete successor invariant.

Control decomposition and recomposition preserve certificates in both active and dormant control. Resumption moves the captured segment above the complete clause prefix; disposal replaces it with closing control containing no live captures. Cell updates affect active payloads without changing dormant saved captures. These structural facts cover every RawStep constructor, including cleanup invocation and completion.

Ready conjoins the existing joint invariant and retained certificates. Value, ready-resumption, and closed-disposal progress now preserve this stronger state judgment. Ordinary computation and exact builtins preserve it as well. ready_capture_constructs exposes an actual named transition and valid chosen type/effect contract before asking for the new certificate. Only successor readiness is conditional on that certificate. Keeping the operational and typing witnesses outside the implication prevents an impossible certificate premise from hiding an arbitrary choice of clause or effect bound.

Positive examples instantiate new capture with disposal permission and an actual empty plan, and resource-bearing disposal with retained cleanup. They start from checked administrative states; source reachability is not proved. ready_initial_configuration initializes the stronger judgment from the same closed expression checks, but does not establish future cut compatibility. New capture certificates, payload support, lexical substitution hygiene, and fresh source instantiation must still follow from source checking. The local preservation proof does not yet establish general progress or a universal joint safety theorem for admitted source executions.

Fresh instantiation counterexample and Core judgment

FreshnessGap.lean checks a counterexample with one lambda containing resource 4 0 unit, bound once and called twice. Closed value typing, usage, resource dependencies, and Ready all hold initially. Eight raw events perform the first call's allocation and release and reach the second call's resource entry. The prefix satisfies RunSteps with fresh issued history. Its endpoint also satisfies Ready, but is not a value and has no NamedStep: the only possible entry recreates resource identity 4, already present in issued history. The value initializer cannot take a focus step.

This theorem concerns the uninstantiated administrative syntax. It does not claim acceptance by a complete source admission checker, nor prove every intermediate state satisfies access checks and joint typing. It establishes that Ready alone is insufficient for general progress, and that initializing it is not a substitute for source-to-runtime instantiation.

Current Core's normative scoped-cell rules require a fresh activation on every successful execution, including the same source site. They also require older closures to retain their lexical activations. The implementation in machine.rs uses next_activation, installs the chosen key with environment.instantiation.acquire, and advances the counter after successful preparation. The existing unit test resource_capacity_is_live_exact_atomic_and_reused_with_fresh_keys executes the same Core resource node three times, releasing between acquisitions, and checks keys 0, 1, and 2. This focused command passes:

cargo test --lib resource_capacity_is_live_exact_atomic_and_reused_with_fresh_keys

Judgment: this is a missing instantiation step in the model, not evidence that Core needs a semantic change. The model must distinguish a source resource identity from each runtime activation and instantiate its scoped body, exact instances, type/row metadata, and retained lexical context consistently. Earlier closures must keep their original activations. The required model delta must preserve lifetime freshness and ordinary repeated function calls; neither weakening the ledger nor excluding repeated calls repairs correspondence. The focused runtime test supports this judgment but is not a simulation proof for the complete fragment. The following scoped layers implement and prove fresh instantiation in the model, including repeated calls; a general Core simulation remains open.

Lexical metadata instantiation foundation

Instantiation.lean separates source resource names from runtime activation atoms in the existing monomorphic metadata fragment. ResourceName.bound requires lookup in an immutable lexical Environment; ResourceName.activation is already realized and requires no lookup. Structural ArgumentRealizes, EffectRealizes, and TypeRealizes judgments preserve nominal heads and recursively realize resource references, nested applications, function input/output ports, latent effect rows, and retained resource lists. They add a metadata interpretation layer, not another computation calculus.

NameBound checks whether a source-name lookup succeeds. NamesBound applies that check to the finitely occurring resource leaves of metadata. The existence theorems construct realizations from those checks; the uniqueness theorems prove determinism. These results require no injectivity of the lexical environment. Two lexical aliases may denote one exact runtime instance.

freezeArgument, freezeEffect, and freezeType embed runtime metadata using only activation atoms. Their realization under any later environment is the original runtime metadata. The uniqueness theorem then rules out rebinding an already-realized request or type. This includes resources retained only in latent rows or port types. It does not yet prove that every runtime closure captures or freezes the right lexical metadata; expression integration must establish that invariant.

type_resources_realize transports the full resource-leaf list through the structural relation. realized_type_support derives the runtime support bound from support for each realized source leaf. Neither lookup availability nor resource occurrence grants live access or ownership.

PreparedActivation contains a key absent from issued resource history. prepareActivation constructs one above the finite history. Rebinding a source slot preserves EnvironmentHistory, changes its lookup to the fresh key, and keeps the chosen key distinct from every previous lexical binding whose key was issued. This is a historical property; released keys can remain in history. For a body already realized at that key, the existing cell-entry transition preserves the ledger. It does not by itself instantiate a source body.

The examples acquire keys 0 and 1 for source slot 4 and distinguish their exact user effects with nested resource type arguments. Old frozen metadata remains at key 0 under the inner environment. A request with a unit operand then skips the newer exact handler and cell, selects the older handler, and performs an actual capture step. Activation selection therefore need not come from the operand.
