This is an administrative HandlerCut/RawStep example, not a proof of source reachability or Joint.Valid preservation for an instantiated program.

The separation follows Core's lexical activation requirement. Its private runtime implementation in instantiation.rs uses immutable binding contexts and an opaque activation-atom namespace distinct from validated Core variables. The Lean metadata relation does not yet cover Core's generic type and row substitution, work budgets, storage limits, or fallible preparation. In particular, existence of an unbounded fresh natural number does not prove that a bounded Core acquisition succeeds.

The existing Core regression same_site_closure_uses_its_outer_activation in resource_scope_runtime.rs also passes. It calls an outer closure while a recursive visit has activated the same source scope again, then adds the outer value 41 to the resumed inner value 1. It supports the lexical-environment comparison; it is not a formal simulation or a metadata-only closure test.

cargo test --test resource_scope_runtime same_site_closure_uses_its_outer_activation

The remaining repair must integrate realization with source bodies, ordinary substitution, closure environments, saved contexts, handler clauses and cleanup code, and operation signatures. It must preserve older lexical instantiations while realizing new bound occurrences. The existing arbitrary runtime Signature must be related to source declarations under instantiation; neither a globally injective environment nor the restricted SignatureSupported shortcut is a substitute. The FreshnessGap theorem remains valid for the unmodified administrative machine. Metadata realization alone has not repaired its repeated-call execution or proved general progress or Core correspondence.

Scoped code instantiation and substitution

ScopedExpressions.lean extends the metadata foundation to a scoped representation of the same expression grammar. It retains one sequencing form and the existing operation, handler, resumption, disposal, resource, and cleanup forms. Resource references use tagged names; operation and handler metadata use the earlier Effect representation. This is code instantiation, not another computation semantics.

Code.instantiate replaces a free source name when its immutable lexical environment supplies an activation. Missing names remain source names, and existing activation atoms stay fixed. The traversal includes lambda bodies, ordinary binding suffixes, handler clauses, and cleanup code. At a resource declaration it instantiates the initializer in the preceding environment and masks the declaration's binder for the body. Ordinary value and ticket binders do not mask the resource namespace. Nested reuse of a source resource name therefore preserves an outer-dependent initializer while deferring the inner body's resource binding.

Code.instantiation_free gives exact free-name accounting: the result's free source resource names are the original list filtered by missing environment lookups. Code.instantiation_closes_iff turns that equality into the precise closing criterion, finite free-name coverage. No liveness or authority follows from this lookup property. Resource-closed code may retain activation atoms and locally bound resource templates; it need not be closed in the ordinary variable or ticket namespaces.

Code.closed_instantiation_identity proves that later instantiation leaves resource-closed code unchanged, including its deferred local acquisition sites. Code.instantiation_subst proves that ordinary substitution of such code commutes with instantiation throughout all expression and clause forms. In particular, substitution beneath a same-name resource declaration cannot rebind activation atoms retained by the inserted code. This is an algebraic property of the two transformations. It does not replace typing, ordinary variable hygiene, or the restrictions on structural ticket capture.

acquisition_closes_body applies the prepared fresh binding to a closed declaration's body. Applying it to the whole declaration would mask the binding again and leave the site deferred. The resulting body is resource-closed. effect_instantiation_realizes connects executable traversal to the previous structural effect realization judgment: successful realization traverses to exactly the frozen runtime effect.

The examples exercise an outer-dependent initializer under a same-name nested declaration, a closed lambda with a deferred resource site, an inserted older closure, and a prepared acquisition whose new request uses the new key while its inserted old closure retains the earlier key. These are transformation equalities and closure checks, not typed execution examples.

The operational layer below now executes this scoped representation and retains its code in contexts, handlers, and cleanup actions. Callable bodies keep unallocated templates; acquisition instantiates their bodies at each execution. Merely erasing name tags could not supply that behavior. A preserved resource-name closure invariant now covers evaluation and substitution boundaries. Value/effect typing, usage, live support, signature transport, and the relation to administrative configurations remain to be connected. Full Core handle/evidence elaboration and generic type/row binders remain outside this fragment.

Scoped execution with fresh acquisitions

ScopedExecution.lean carries scoped Code through the full transition grammar: ordinary sequencing and application, focus/plug, exact handlers and cells, capture, full-prefix resumption, disposal, cleanup invocation/completion, and retirement. Contexts, handler clauses, callback values, saved return values, and recursively dormant captures retain this code. This is the operational refinement of the same calculus, not a new sequencing model.

The resource-entry rule takes a source binder and a runtime activation separately. After the initializer returns an integer, it requires the enclosing declaration to be resource-closed and instantiates its body with that binder mapped to the chosen runtime key. The cell frame owns the same key. RunStep requires every created owner to be fresh against issued history. The source binder is never an ownership event. Unallocated resource sites remain inside callable bodies for later invocations.

Code.dependencies collects runtime activation atoms. A source resource binder does not remove an atom with the same numeral. This disjointness removes the old resource-name capture problem at ordinary substitution; ordinary-variable closure and ticket barriers are still separate obligations. ClosedValue checks value form, resource-name closure, and ordinary/ticket dependency closure. Unresolved source resource references are not runtime values. Request and handler rules require frozen exact runtime effects, so unresolved metadata cannot be silently treated as an activation or inferred from operands.

The full transition set projects to the original structural Flow relation. Capture uses the actual exact handler cut; resumption restores the saved segment above the complete clause prefix; disposal retains the executable cleanup plan and uses its ownership projection. All finite scoped executions therefore preserve the lifetime ledger and exclude duplicate completion. These conclusions do not establish access, type/effect, or usage admission.

resource_entry_progress constructs a fresh identity above issued history and an actual transition from a resource-closed declaration with an integer initializer. It proves closure of the resulting body and ledger preservation. It does not require a desired transition witness or assume the successor invariant. Frame answer types are still annotations; this theorem is not the complete typed progress theorem.

The ten-event repeated-call trace binds one lambda containing source resource slot 4 and calls it twice. Both acquisitions return unit. The trace allocates and releases runtime keys 0 and 1 and reaches empty control with both owners completed. Source slot 4 never appears in issued history. This supplies the operational repair diagnosed by FreshnessGap in the old administrative machine; that old theorem remains valid for its unchanged rules.

ScopedClosure.lean supplies all-transition preservation of resource-name closure. A plain context is closed when plugging unit leaves no free source resource names; the context theorem factors closure of any plugged expression into closure of the hole and context. Handler clauses are checked directly. Callback and saved-value closure follows from the evidence carried by their frame data. Stack closure recurses through active control and saved captures. Capture derives closure of the selected clause; substitution preserves it; resumed and disposed control retain it. Acquisition supplies its body's new binding. The finite-execution theorem combines closure with the ownership ledger.

A separate generic three-event cell-read trace realizes a source body's exact request and operand at the same runtime key, reads the newly active builtin cell, and releases it on return. fresh_scoped_cell_read constructs such an execution against any duplicate-free issued history. This connects metadata instantiation to actual builtin execution in addition to the unit-returning repeated-call example.

RunSteps in this layer does not inherit the old Joint.Valid judgment by erasure. The layers below now add handler-activation history and live support under local checks. Value/effect typing, structural usage, and source-derived retained disposal certificates still need transport or reconstruction. Resource-name closure alone does not prove that retained activation atoms remain live. Complete source admission, general progress, and Core simulation remain required and unproved. Core's bounded preparation failures also remain outside the unbounded fresh-key construction.

Scoped naming, dependencies, and live support

ScopedNames.lean transports lifetime naming to the scoped machine. enteredActivations records the handler activated by an actual handler entry; other transition families add no handler identity. Raw name-count bounds cover active and dormant control, spent clause boundaries, and retirement markers. NamedStep adds fresh handler history to fresh owner issuance. NamedSteps preserves that history together with the ledger and resource-name closure. Once allocated, a handler activation cannot be allocated again after its frame exits.

TicketBinding relates a lexical ticket and its ports to an actual active live or spent boundary. It establishes structural occurrence, not the validity of permission bits or effect rows. The generic control-name lemmas show that an owner has a unique protocol state. Combining ticket counts with the ledger puts retained spent markers in completion history; retirement frames remain owners until discharged. Completed or consumed tickets cannot become available later. Supplied initial histories certify accounting membership. Concrete earlier allocation events follow only when those histories themselves arise from an appropriate initial execution.

The sequential-handler example installs the same source expression twice, using handler activations 0 and 1, and reaches empty control with both names in history. Its named execution preserves closure and ownership and excludes later reuse of activation 0. This is operational evidence for name accounting, not complete source type/usage admission.

ScopedDependencies.lean connects the scoped code's runtime dependencies to substitution and instantiation. Ordinary substitution introduces dependencies only from the original code or inserted value. Instantiation introduces only activation atoms supplied by the lexical environment. Masking a local source binder reduces those supplied bindings; it does not hide atoms already present in code. Acquisition therefore introduces at most its selected key. Traversal covers operation arguments, handler metadata and clauses, lambdas, sequencing, and cleanup code. Frozen effect metadata has the runtime instance's exact resource list. These results bound dependency transport; they do not establish live support by themselves.

ScopedAccess.lean checks that current-expression resource dependencies are visible or ambient and that retained control satisfies the existing structural Supported judgment. Its AccessChecks are the three pre-state obligations already used by the administrative layer: the returning value excludes the cell being released; an actually selected request's operand is supported outside its captured segment; and the actual disposal plan satisfies the structural closing judgment against surviving control.

Every scoped raw transition preserves access from that invariant and those local checks. Acquisition uses the new dependency bound: older atoms remain supported by the preceding control, and the newly introduced atom is supported by the entered cell. Capture uses the exact selected handler and operand check. Resumption restores the full prefix; disposal uses the checked materialized control; running callbacks retain their actual saved-value dependencies. No successor-support premise replaces these arguments.

Finite named, access-checked executions now preserve resource-name closure, the ledger, lifetime name history, and live resource support together. With closed interfaces, neither executing code nor retained frames can reference a completed resource. This is a safety property, not termination or eventual release. Handler-name freshness is independent of owner freshness, and both remain independent of resource support and continuation permissions.

The positive access example acquires key 0 at source slot 4, realizes metadata and operand, reads payload 17, and releases the cell. Every event supplies its local check and freshness evidence in NamedAccessSteps; closure, ledger, name history, and access are proved from the initial state. This example has empty handler history; the sequential-handler example above exercises handler allocation and retained history. A negative example has a resolved activation reference yet fails release admission because that reference retains the owner being discharged. Resource-name closure therefore cannot substitute for lifetime access.

The following usage layers add structural consumption to these four facets. Complete value/effect typing and source-derived admission remain absent. In particular, the disposal check remains conditional on an actual plan; source-derived retained readiness must supply plan existence. Capture's outside-payload check and all new certificates must also follow from source checking. These results do not yet prove general progress or Core simulation.

Scoped structural usage

ScopedUsage.lean connects scoped code to Syntax.Uses, the existing structural judgment for one-shot consumption. Its usageShape projection keeps every sequencing node, branch, function, handler, clause, ordinary binder, and ticket binder. It forgets resource names, acquisition slots, and effect-instance metadata, which the usage rules never inspect. Uses, ClausesUse, and CodeDemand transparently apply the existing judgments to that structure; they introduce no new sequencing or computation model.

Instantiation preserves the projection exactly, including beneath deferred resource templates and in latent functions and clauses. Ordinary substitution commutes with it. Consequently instantiation preserves and reflects usage and syntactic paths for every environment. Usage substitution requires an actual value whose own usage checks under no enclosing ticket; it establishes neither ordinary-variable hygiene nor resource closure or support.

The projection also preserves the exact list of free tickets. This includes duplicates from alternative branches and masking by nested clause binders. Resource instantiation therefore changes neither that list nor its translation from lexical ticket names to runtime owners. A free ticket in usage-checked code requires consumption in the matching scope; checked clauses have no free outer tickets. Scheduled consumption still counts one action per path, rather than counting the two occurrences in alternative branches as two demands.

The actual scoped Focus judgment splits usage between the child and its context. Plugging a checked child into the checked context recomposes usage. The corresponding demand theorem divides scheduled consumption between child and frame. Bind substitution preserves the demand, beta-reduction of a lambda applied to a value has empty local demand, and acquisition preserves the body's demand through its lexical instantiation. These results supply the expression premises for the retained-control usage proof below.

The positive example interleaves acquisition, a cell request, ordinary binding, and branches that respectively resume and dispose the enclosing ticket. Both syntactic paths pass the one-shot protocol. The paths are syntactic alternatives, even when a condition is a literal; they do not assert that both arms execute. Functions and nested clauses are checked separately from the enclosing path. Negative examples reject double consumption, function capture of an enclosing ticket, and a nested clause consuming a different ticket.

Another checked example exposes the projection's limit: an unresolved resource reference passes usage and projects to a value, while the scoped reference is neither resource-name closed nor a runtime value. No theorem treats this projection as operational simulation. Effect dispatch, live support, and Core correspondence must retain the resource identities that usage deliberately ignores. Likewise, the supplied ticket policy remains an administrative input; source checking must justify permissions and their relation to capture records.

Scoped retained control and execution usage

ScopedControlUsage.lean defines FrameDemand, StackUsage, and ConfigurationUsage over actual scoped code and control. Their structure follows the administrative usage construction: ordinary frames carry checked code demand; handlers carry scoped clause checks; callbacks and saved values check under no enclosing ticket; retirement owns one internal consumption. Saved captures are checked recursively, but only the active spine supplies access to live tickets. Configuration usage balances current and retained demands against recursively owned tickets and requires unique ownership.

Stack decomposition and recomposition preserve those interfaces. An actual handler cut splits the demand of the selected capture from surviving control. Capture installs a fresh ticket record using the selected clause binder's policy and substitutes the checked operand into that clause. Resumption first uses the balance invariant to show that no other code demands the consumed ticket; only then does it remove that ticket from the outside interface and restore the full captured prefix. A nested example preserves demand for an outside ticket inside another dormant capture. Another example balances the counts but rejects a current resume because its owner is only dormant.

Disposal requires makePlan to produce a concrete plan. InternalUses and active accessibility show that the captured demand is exactly the captured ticket ownership. Materializing the plan preserves callback usage and replaces that demand with registered retirement owners. The internal-ticket example executes disposal followed by retirement and preserves configuration usage. A returned value cannot pass an unconsumed live clause boundary. The value-step proof also covers plugging saved contexts, resource and handler return, cleanup invocation/completion, close completion, and retirement.

ScopedUsageExecution.lean connects every scoped raw transition to those judgments. Resource entry instantiates the body with its fresh key before preserving its demand; it never substitutes the source slot for the runtime owner. Builtin updates preserve ticket ownership and access. advanceUsageTickets reads the concrete created-owner list and successor scope; the raw-step case split proves that capture alone inserts the selected policy record. Registry history retains exactly the historically issued ticket domain. Fresh owner issuance and registry history derive allocation absence, while the existing structural disposal access check supplies InternalUses.

The finite named-access execution theorem now preserves resource-name closure, the lifetime ledger, handler-name history, live resource support, configuration usage, and ticket-registry history together. Each successor registry is constructed from its actual transition. No successor usage, balance, or support condition is assumed. Concrete executions inhabit the theorem: fresh acquisition/read/release and handler entry/capture/resume/return. The latter allocates and consumes a ticket while retaining nonempty handler-name history.

The scope is preservation under explicit access checks, not source-derived readiness or general progress. Registry history proves the domain's allocation correspondence, not source authority for permissions. Internal retirement is accounted as ownership discharge: it requires a registered ticket but does not inspect that ticket's dispose permission. Any stronger contract forbidding indirect abandonment must be checked separately; the present theorem does not authenticate it. Disposal plan existence, capture-payload support, and permission provenance still need source admission. The later scoped joint and progress layers connect value/effect typing to this same execution; full source-readiness preservation and Core correspondence remain open.

Scoped type instantiation and signature coherence

ScopedSignatures.lean supplies executable instantiation for ValueType. The traversal agrees with TypeRealizes and maps every resource leaf, including function inputs, nested outputs, latent effect arguments, and retained support. A realized type becomes frozen metadata, so later environments cannot change it. The corresponding operation-descriptor traversal preserves its family and operation identities while realizing its arguments and both ports. Existence requires all source resource leaves to have bindings; uniqueness does not require the environment to be injective. These are metadata results, not yet expression-typing preservation.

The finite monomorphic signature model contains user-operation descriptors only. Its structural realization relates each source argument and port to the corresponding runtime argument and port. Coherent checks every pair of runtime entries: equality of the exact effect-instance/operation key requires equality of both complete port types. checkCoherent decides that proposition. Acceptance is equivalent to the existence of a single signature respecting every supplied entry. The constructed lookup returns only entries in the table and supplies every coherent entry's ports. Repeated aliases with equal ports are permitted; contradictory aliases cannot be resolved by selecting one declaration order.

Permutation independence applies to this declaration table, including lookup failure for absent keys. It says nothing about interpreter-stack order. operationSignature wraps user lookup with the existing fixed read/write signatures, so user descriptors cannot replace builtin cell operation types.

Extending a table requires coherence of both parts and port agreement for every key shared across the old/new boundary. These conditions are necessary and sufficient for coherence of their concatenation; a coherent extension preserves old successful lookups. Resource freshness alone does not supply cross-table agreement. A counterexample gives two individually coherent descriptors whose callable ports retain distinct fresh resources while their resource-free keys are identical. Freezing protects an older descriptor from rebinding but does not make that conflicting extension coherent.

Other examples admit two lexical aliases of one runtime resource and reject aliases that disagree on an operation result. A callable-port example retains a resource absent from its effect instance, exceeding the optional restricted SignatureSupported condition. It demonstrates the abstract signature layer's generality; it does not establish that such an arbitrary descriptor comes from an authenticated current Core declaration. Actual payload support remains a separate boundary check.

Current effect typing derives operation ports by substituting the exact instance's arguments into its authenticated declaration. Operations have no local parameters. Current Core validation checks those identities, arguments, and substituted ports independently. The remaining bridge must derive the finite descriptors from that authority and establish coherence when their realized table changes. This module does not authenticate arbitrary descriptors, add operation-local polymorphism, or change Core rules. Scoped expression/environment typing, generative resource entry, and their joint preservation with control still need construction before general progress and Core simulation can follow.

Declaration-derived resource signatures

DeclaredSignatures.lean models declaration-derived operation ports for the resource-parameter part of the metadata fragment. DeclarationRegistry selects a family by identity. A family has an ordered parameter vector and operation vector; the operation's position selects its input/output template. FamilyValid requires unique parameter binders, a nonempty API, and every resource name in both ports to refer to a declared parameter. Declaration metadata cannot contain literal runtime activation atoms. checkFamily decides these structural conditions and is proved equivalent to them. It does not check all Core kinds or declaration provenance. In particular, referenced nominal identities and latent effect-family identities, arities, and argument kinds remain unchecked. An explicit example passes this resource scope check while naming an unknown latent effect family.

parameterEnvironment requires the exact argument count and a resource argument at each position. It binds those keys simultaneously to the declared parameters; resource aliases are permitted. Successful construction binds every declared parameter and preserves the parameter/argument count. The selected template's name-scope check therefore supplies all bindings required for structural type realization, proving that its operation ports exist.

DeclaredOperation records the actual family lookup, selected operation, family validity, argument environment, and realization of both ports. Given the same registry and exact dispatch key, two such derivations must select the same declaration, template, and environment. Type-realization uniqueness then proves equality of their ports. A table of these entries is coherent without assuming a separate Coherent premise, and the earlier realized-descriptor lookup theorem now follows from declaration-derived evidence.

Registry extension preserves complete existing family declarations, not merely their presence or identities. Entries derived under the old registry remain valid under that extension. Combining them with entries derived under the new registry yields a coherent table and preserves old successful lookups. This discharges the preceding table-extension obligation within this fragment; fresh resource keys alone are still insufficient for arbitrary descriptors.

The examples derive two aliases of the same operation and reject a forged result type. Fresh callback ports at keys 0 and 1 extend coherently because their declared resource arguments occur in their exact effect keys. The earlier abstract same-key callback counterexample omits the required argument and now fails declaration admission. Other negative cases cover unknown families, unknown operation positions, wrong arity or argument form, undeclared resource names, duplicate parameters, empty APIs, and literal activation metadata.

The current effect typing rule and Core validation boundary remain the language authority. Implementation evidence agrees with their lookup and substitution order: elaboration uses operation_signature, and Core validation uses effect_signature. The latter also checks operation-owner identity, argument kinds, and the selected operation's authenticated identity. The existing test effect_identity_checks_distinguish_argument_and_operation_failures passes for argument-count, invalid-argument, wrong-owner, and unknown-operation failures. It is a focused implementation check, not a simulation theorem.

This model represents family/operation authority by registry key and vector position. It has not extracted that registry from validated Core or proved the extraction correct. General type arguments, kinds, schemes, nominal types, module provenance, sealed provider facts, and full registry closure still need their own bridge. Non-resource arguments are rejected here because this particular parameter fragment only models resource positions; current Ash allows the other argument forms described by the specification. The full goal retains those obligations. The scoped typing layer below begins expression typing and fresh resource entry. Source-derived admission, general progress, and Core correspondence remain open.

Generative scoped expression typing

ScopedTyping.lean types the actual scoped expression syntax used by ScopedExecution, including its lexical resource binders and frozen runtime effect metadata. Typed signature world environment ticket allowed code type retains one sequencing constructor. The finite world records resource names unavailable for fresh allocation. In the execution connection, resourceWorld issued projects these names from the ownership history. A completed resource remains in that history; membership does not grant live access.

The resource rule types the initializer as an integer in the preceding world. It checks the instantiated body for every identity outside that world, in the extended world and under the local cell interpretation plus an outward residual row. Both the result type's resource names and the outward row's resource names must belong to the preceding world. The fresh identity therefore cannot escape through either boundary. This is a declarative binder rule over all fresh openings, not a check of a selected successor's joint invariant. Deriving this premise from finite source checking remains an obligation.

The checked results establish the following:

  • Typing forms result types within the world and survives world extension.
  • Every typed expression is resource-closed. The proof constructs an identity outside the finite world before using the universal body premise, so the resource case does not depend on an empty set of openings.
  • A typed value's resource dependencies are bounded by its type. Result and actual operand types can therefore establish release and payload boundaries.
  • Typed contexts recompose a typed child into a typed expression. Every actual scoped focus transition admits the corresponding typing decomposition.
  • Every identity fresh for actual ownership history yields a typed instantiated resource body, with that identity absent from the result and outward row.
  • A typed resource expression with a returned integer initializer and a valid ownership ledger has an actual fresh RunStep. Its body is typed in the extended history and the step preserves the ledger. Resource closure is derived from typing, rather than supplied as another premise.

Examples type a resource read for every fresh opening and obtain an actual typed acquisition step. The repeated-call program has initial typing and the existing execution with two distinct activations. These two facts do not yet establish typing preservation at every intermediate state. Negative examples reject an unresolved resource reference and return of the newly acquired reference. Another example admits a reference whose identity belongs to the world while rejecting access when no live owner exists.

Two boundaries matter for the next integration. First, bare expression typing does not establish historical issuance of every resource appearing in effect metadata or allowed rows. The joint support, ledger, and formation judgments must supply that relation. Second, the signature is fixed while the resource rule quantifies over every fresh identity. A finite table of exact user-effect instances cannot generally type resource-indexed user operations at every opening. Builtin cell signatures already form a schema over identities; user families need declaration-based lookup that realizes ports for each argument vector, or a proved coherent extension under fresh opening. The declaration results above provide the uniqueness and existence ingredients, but have not yet supplied this integration. This requirement agrees with Core's family parameters and does not introduce operation-local parameters.

The next layer proves scoped typed substitution. Retained-frame and store typing, joint type/effect preservation, and finite source admission remain open. The fresh entry theorem is a bounded progress result for resource acquisition; it is not general progress or a Core simulation theorem.

Scoped typed substitution and ordinary execution

ScopedSubstitution.lean proves closed ordinary substitution for the scoped expression and clause judgments. It preserves the exact result type, immediate effect bound, and declared closure support. The replacement must be a typed ClosedValue: a value with resource-name closure and no free ordinary variables or tickets. Environment relevance permits changing bindings outside the expression's free ordinary variables. A support lemma accounts for the resource dependencies inserted when a lexical variable is replaced by its value; unused variables introduce no extra support.

At a resource binder, the proof opens the original body at each arbitrary fresh identity. Substitution commutes with that opening because the replacement is resource-closed. World weakening transports the replacement's typing into the extended world, preserving its older activation atoms and deferred acquisition templates. The proof does not require source binder numerals to differ from runtime atoms. Its syntax-node measure is unchanged by instantiation, which justifies recursive proof calls on opened bodies. This termination argument concerns the proof function, not program execution.

The resulting local execution theorems produce actual RawStep.bind and RawStep.beta transitions with typed successor expressions. Binding keeps its lexical ticket scope; beta evaluation resets it to none, matching the scoped machine. The exact selected handler clause remains typed after substitution of its closed operand, with the declared operation and continuation ports. Immediate effect weakening and empty-ticket transport preserve latent contracts and independently checked lambda and handler-clause bodies.

Examples retain an older activation atom beneath a same-numbered source resource binder, preserve a closure's resource support after substitution, and type an actual beta step of the repeated-acquisition function. The older reference example checks typing and instantiation; it does not by itself grant live access to that resource.

Those substitution theorems keep the raw steps' lexical readiness conditions explicit. Typing under an arbitrary environment alone does not prove a replacement closed or a binding suffix ClosedExcept its parameter. Nor do these expression results prove the retained stack's type/effect interface correct. Source-derived readiness, retained-frame and store typing, declaration-based signatures across fresh openings, joint preservation, general progress, and Core simulation remain required. The next layer derives lexical readiness in an empty ordinary environment and constructs focus frames from typing.

Lexical readiness and bounded scoped progress

ScopedReadiness.lean derives the lexical conditions required by ordinary scoped execution. BoundDependency checks that a free ordinary variable has an entry in TypeEnv and that a free ticket belongs to the current static TicketType. LexicallyBound applies this check to every dependency. Resource dependencies pass this particular judgment; issuance, live access, and ownership remain separate obligations.

The mutual typing proof establishes this judgment for expressions and closes each handler clause's ordinary parameter and ticket binder. A lambda checks under the empty ticket scope. Resource opening preserves membership of every existing dependency, so a typed fresh opening also bounds the original source body's lexical dependencies. The proof constructs a fresh identity outside the finite world; it cannot use an empty family of openings to justify the body. This dependency lower bound concerns membership, not multiplicity.

Typing a value in an empty ordinary environment now derives ClosedValue: resource-name closure follows from typing, free variables contradict the empty environment, and value transport to the empty ticket scope excludes free tickets. Typing a suffix under the parameter's singleton environment derives ClosedExcept. Therefore the actual bind and application progress theorems need only typing and value-form premises, with no separately supplied lexical closure conditions. Canonical forms also supply an actual branch step and extend typed fresh resource-entry progress to any value-form initializer. The resource case retains its initial ownership-ledger premise and concludes a typed successor body and preserved ledger.

ScopeNamesMatch is a structural relation with two cases: an empty static ticket scope matches an empty runtime scope; a bound static ticket matches a runtime scope with the same lexical binder and a dynamic owner. It does not assert that the owner exists, has particular ports or permissions, or remains available for consumption. Under this relation, lexical typing makes ticket translation total. Given an actual strict Focus position, typing derives both context ports and the pending-owner list and constructs its PlainData and actual RawStep.focus. No caller-supplied pending translation or frame-port annotation is needed for that construction.

Examples derive the repeated-acquisition function's closure and its program's first binding step from typing. Negative cases reject a missing ordinary binding, an outer ticket under an empty ticket scope, and mismatched runtime binders. A focused resume operand yields a unit-to-unit frame whose pending list contains dynamic owner 3, obtained from lexical binder 9. This local raw-focus example has no live boundary for that owner; it tests translation and frame construction, not admitted continuation use.

These are bounded progress cases, not a general configuration theorem. typed_focus_progress takes an actual focus position; it does not classify every possible expression state. Full source admission, runtime-owner and frame-port correspondence, retained-stack effect composition, reachable capture/disposal admission, joint preservation, general progress, and Core simulation remain open. Deriving lexical closure does not establish resource access safety or the legality of abandoning a captured continuation.

Scoped retained typing and configuration transitions

ScopedRetained.lean checks value types throughout the actual scoped configuration. AtType relates current code to its runtime ticket scope and historical ticket ports. FrameTyped checks retained context ports, handler clauses and coverage, cleanup functions, saved cleanup results, and resource non-escape boundaries. StackTyped composes these ports and recursively types dormant captures. ConfigurationTyped connects the current expression's type to that stack. The world index extends the scoped expression world to all retained code. Historical ticket-port facts use the existing ScopeTyped representation; they imply the name correspondence proved above without granting live ownership or continuation permissions.

The checked configuration results now include:

  • Exact handler-cut decomposition preserves the actual captured code, selected handler clauses, and outside stack. Resumption recomposes the full captured stack above the entire remaining clause prefix and spent boundary.
  • Capture constructs an actual transition and a typed successor under a fresh historical ticket-table entry. Operand closure and selected-clause lexical readiness follow from typing. The extension preserves old ticket entries and stored code; this is not arbitrary operation-signature extension.
  • Actual makePlan construction retains typed callback contents and ticket retirement facts. Its materialized close control composes with the remaining clause work. Disposal preserves value-type configuration composition when the actual plan exists; this does not establish plan admissibility.
  • Every raw step whose current expression is a value preserves this configuration judgment. The result covers actual cleanup application, saved results, returned callbacks, scope exits, and owner-retirement frames. Typing derives the current value's closure. A typed return through a cell also derives the resource-dependency exclusion needed at release.
  • Binding, application, and branching with value operands, together with an existing strict focus position, construct typed configuration successors. Focus derives the new frame's annotations; it does not validate arbitrary annotations supplied to a raw transition. Fresh resource entry grows the world throughout all retained frames and dormant captures, then installs its derived cell answer port. That entry also preserves the ownership ledger.

Examples construct typed capture and a resumption with a nonempty remaining prefix. A fresh resource-read entry preserves whole-configuration value typing. A concrete cleanup execution applies its retained function, evaluates its body, completes the cleanup owner, and restores integer 17. All four configurations in that three-step trace are typed, and its actual execution preserves the supplied ownership ledger. These use a supplied abstract operation signature; they do not authenticate a Core declaration registry.

An explicit negative example is value-type consistent but has an unhandled request and no RawStep in its empty stack. AtType retains the immediate row existentially, so this judgment alone does not provide an interpreter. The example is not a source-admitted stuck program or a counterexample to relative progress with outward-request observations. It rules out using this value-type layer alone to claim unconditional machine-step progress.

The following layer connects exact effect requirements across frames. Integration with owner history and availability, capability and usage judgments, and reachable capture/disposal admission remains open. The world index does not independently form every cell annotation or historical ticket port; joint history, support, and formation checks must supply those facts. Source-derived annotation/contract admission, universal joint execution preservation, general progress, and Core simulation remain open.

Scoped entries and connected request progress

ScopedEntries.lean derives the remaining handler and cleanup value-type entries from actual scoped typing. Handler answer ports, clause coverage, and the ticket barrier come from the derivation. Cleanup entry derives a closed callback and stores its latent requests. The chosen handler activation and cleanup owner still need their respective freshness checks in the named execution judgment.

Builtin progress now starts from a typed request with any value operand and successful exact lookup. The fixed cell signature determines whether the operation is a read or write. Canonical forms derive the reference atom and, for a write, the integer payload. cell_selection_of_resolution constructs the actual CellUpdate; handler_selection_of_resolution similarly reconstructs the actual HandlerCut from source lookup. Both traverse the active suffix of live records and preserve their dormant captures. A nearer source override blocks builtin selection. Neither theorem assumes the desired executable selection as a premise.

ScopedEffects.lean connects the immediate row to that ordered stack. Its world-indexed EffectFrame checks each actual context, handler, callback, and saved cleanup value at the frame's incoming and outgoing interface. EffectStack composes interfaces, including separate checks of a live record's dormant capture and historical resume/closing contract. EffectConfigurationTyped joins current expression typing, retained value ports, and those connected effect interfaces. The existing historical EffectScope representation ties static ticket effects to the runtime owner; it does not establish availability or permission to consume that owner.

The checked results include:

  • Effect-interface decomposition at the actual handler cut and recomposition of the entire captured stack above the full remaining clause prefix.
  • Capture construction with a fresh historical ticket slot, preserving connected typing and every old ticket contract. The selected handler's residual row supplies both resume and closing effects. Operand closure and clause substitution readiness follow from typing.
  • Connected typing preservation for resumption, builtin reads and writes, binding, beta reduction, and every raw transition from a current closed value. Cleanup start checks the actual application; cleanup completion restores the typed saved value.
  • request_effect_progress: a request with a value operand either has no local interpreter and belongs to the outward row, or takes an actual raw step with a connected typed successor. Lookup is inspected before choosing the observation alternative, so an outward row cannot bypass a local handler. With an empty outward row, closed_request_effect_progress derives a step.

The request theorem requires a fresh historical ticket slot for its source capture branch; its standalone builtin case needs no such premise. Historical table absence does not imply freshness in the ownership ledger. These are raw-transition results: resource access, exact ticket usage, disposal permission, and name-history admission are still independent obligations. The live effect interface requires both resume and closing rows at its boundary, regardless of usage rights. This is a sufficient conservative interface. It neither infers the minimal effects of an actual disposal plan nor proves that the plan exists or is safe.

The nested-handler example checks a four-step capture/resume/plug/bind execution. The resumed suffix reaches the outer handler through the reinstalled inner handler and spent ticket. Connected typing follows through those successors, and the concrete execution preserves the ownership ledger. Further examples execute typed reads and writes. A request with no local interpreter is rejected under an empty outward row and admitted with its effect exported. An inhabited dormant-handler example confirms that a saved handler cannot interpret an active clause's request.

This proves the value-operand request case of relative progress. The following layer checks connected entry and disposal interfaces. The scoped joint layer below connects those local cases to ownership, access, and usage history. Complete source admission, universal admitted-execution preservation, general progress, and correspondence with validated Core remain open. These examples use an abstract user signature plus fixed builtin ports; they do not authenticate or simulate a Core declaration registry.

Scoped effect entry and structural closing readiness

ScopedEffectCompletion.lean completes the local connected effect interfaces for focus, handler entry, cleanup entry, branching, and fresh resource entry. Focus and entries derive their stored annotations from typing. Resource entry constructs a fresh activation, grows the world in all retained frames and dormant captures, and preserves both connected typing and the ownership ledger. The world-weakening lemmas also transport callback and saved-result typing without changing existing resource atoms or contracts.

The closing layer now uses actual scoped callbacks and materialized frames:

  • PlanTyped checks each callback's function type and bounds its requests by the builtin cells in its remaining plan suffix plus the outward closing row. InvocationAt identifies that actual suffix. The callback application is typed there, and every suffix-provided request has a corresponding actual builtin lookup even with arbitrary surviving outer control appended.
  • CloseReady is a structural judgment on the captured stack. Plain contexts and source handlers are removed. Cells are retained until their release position. Armed callbacks are checked against their future suffix. A nested live record closes its capture, retires its ticket, then closes its outside suffix; that outside suffix's resources remain available to the inner callbacks. Running cleanup, closing, and retirement frames have no readiness constructor.
  • close_ready_constructs_plan derives both a successful makePlan result and its ordered PlanTyped derivation. It does not take plan existence as a premise. Plan composition preserves execution order, and readiness survives extension of the resource world.
  • close_plan_has_effect_interface joins callback effects with retained value types and historical retirement entries. Disposal then composes the actual close control with the full surviving clause prefix. The resulting configuration preserves connected value/effect typing.
  • ready_disposal_effect_progress combines structural readiness with an existing live boundary, its matching runtime binder and historical contract, and a supplied ownership ledger. It constructs the plan, chooses a fresh close owner from finite history, and derives an actual RunStep, connected successor typing, and the successor ledger.

These judgments prove effect readiness and one-step disposal progress at the supplied boundary. They do not establish resource access, disposal permissions for the selected or internally retired tickets, or agreement between original and surviving interpretations. Source admission still has to derive the boundary and readiness conditions and preserve them for future captures. Readiness does not imply termination or eventual cleanup completion.

An eleven-step example disposes a captured callback and cell. It starts the actual callback, evaluates its body, reads integer 17 from the still-live cell, completes cleanup, releases the cell, completes the close owner, and leaves the spent clause. All twelve configurations have connected value/effect typing, and the actual execution preserves the ownership ledger. Negative examples reject releasing the only cell before its callback and abandoning a running cleanup. A nested plan checks the exact order: callback invocation, inner-ticket retirement, resource release.

A separate example makes the remaining interpretation obligation explicit. Its captured code has valid value/effect interfaces and structural closing readiness. Disposal removes a source override, so the callback's request now resolves to the builtin cell instead of the original source handler. SameRequests rejects that change. Effect availability alone therefore cannot supply the independent interpreter-agreement check. This is not a source-admitted execution or a claimed Core defect.

The following layer joins these local effect cases with access, usage, and lifetime history. Source establishment and preservation of interpretation agreement and future readiness remain open, along with general progress and Core correspondence. The concrete cleanup trace does not substitute for a universal admitted-execution theorem.

Scoped joint invariants and derived progress

ScopedJoint.lean checks seven facets of the same actual scoped configuration: the ownership ledger, handler/ticket name history, live resource support, connected value/effect typing, structural ticket usage, historical registry domain, and resource-name closure. It reuses the historical TicketRecord representation from the administrative model. Its execution, expression, stack, access, and usage judgments are the scoped ones; the old joint theorem is not transported by erasure.

Initial checks establish these facets independently for a closed expression with empty histories and no ambient resources. Each issued ticket has one record with two projections: its continuation contract and its independently checked resume/dispose rights. Type-directed capture derives both projections for the same selected clause binder and fresh runtime owner. Resumption recomposes the entire captured segment, current clause prefix, spent boundary, and caller tail. Disposal constructs the actual closing control under the registered closing interface.

Focus, handler entry, cleanup entry, branching, binding, beta reduction, builtin operations, and all current-value events preserve the joined judgment or construct annotations which do. Resource entry derives a fresh activation from finite issued history and grows the world throughout retained typing. The helper for this event uses the successor resource world; other events use proved world weakening. Neither helper is a source-admission rule.

Several local checks are now derived. Result typing proves release exclusion; a focus cannot perform an evaluated request or discard; builtin selection excludes a competing source-handler cut. Capture still requires the operand to be supported outside the selected segment. Disposal still requires structural access and interpreter agreement. CloseReady supplies the executable typed plan, and the ledger supplies a fresh close owner. The selected-boundary disposal theorem does not derive that boundary or preservation of readiness.

value_progress proves that a current value either has empty control or takes an actual named/access-checked step preserving all seven facets. Canonical forms supply unit at cleanup/close/retirement frames. Independent usage rejects returning through an unconsumed live ticket. resume_value_progress derives lexical resolution and an actual live boundary from current usage and active accessibility; dormant captures are not searched. It then constructs a resumption preserving the same registry and all facets. Neither theorem assumes a next step, supplied live boundary, or access certificate.

At empty control, terminal_ledger_settled derives a permutation between issued and discharged owners, with no duplicate discharge. It does not assert that arbitrary execution terminates. The concrete fresh-read example checks all four states of the actual three-step acquisition/read/release execution under one joined judgment. A nested-handler example checks type-directed capture and usage-derived resumption with a pending bind and two ordered source interpretations. That fixture starts with two existing handler activations; it is not an empty-source execution.

These are local preservation and completion/resumption progress results. The following layer classifies every current expression and proves progress under structural prestate checks. Those checks still need source establishment and preservation over retained code and captures. Current usage authorizes explicit ticket consumption but does not check the dispose permission of an internally retired ticket. The delegated-retirement layer below explains why current Core authorizes that completion through the selected outer discard; an inner direct-dispose flag is not required. Declaration authentication, complete Core type/kind coverage, and operational simulation remain open. No result in this layer changes current Core or its specification.

Scoped progress for every expression form

ScopedProgress.lean proves relative progress at any current scoped expression under explicit structural prestate checks. CurrentForm classifies a typed expression as a value, a strict focus, or one of the evaluated head forms. Its constructors contain syntax and value/focus evidence, never an execution witness. Ordinary value forms use canonical forms and typed substitution. Finite histories supply fresh handler activations and fresh owner identities; registry history then rules out an existing record at a newly captured ticket.

ClosingInterfaces recursively checks active and dormant control. At a live ticket it reads the historical record and requires CloseReady only if that record permits disposal. A resume-only capture may therefore retain a running cleanup. A capture with disposal permission must be structurally closable, including its actual callback effects and plan order. This is a sufficient prestate condition over all existing captures, not a checker for future code. The separate AccessChecks judgment retains the operand-boundary support and actual-plan Discardable obligations, including interpreter agreement.

For discard, structural usage derives the actual owner, its resolution, its active boundary, and its explicit disposal permission. The closing interface uses the same historical record as connected effect typing. Only then does the proof construct the plan and fresh close owner. An implication in AccessChecks.discard cannot hide a failed makePlan: the independently required CloseReady constructs that plan.

current_progress has three outcomes: a value with empty control, an outward operation observation, or a named/access-checked step preserving all seven ScopedJoint.Valid facets. The step also preserves every existing ticket record through RegistryExtends; only fresh capture can add a record. An outward observation requires both membership in the declared outgoing row and absence of a local interpreter. Local interpretation always takes precedence. The theorem fixes builtin signatures with withCellSignatures users; it is parametric in the user signature and does not authenticate Core declarations.

closed_current_progress removes the observation alternative when the outgoing row is empty. Here “closed” concerns the effect row, not ambient resources. Neither progress theorem assumes a next step or a valid successor. The conclusion preserves Valid and historical records, but not AccessChecks or ClosingInterfaces. Repeated application still needs a source-established, transition-preserved readiness judgment. Current internal retirement authority remains outside this guarantee, as described in the preceding layer.

Empty control and an empty runtime ticket scope establish the initial local access checks directly. Together with independent expression typing, usage, and resource-support checks, initial_progress derives a first step or an initial value. It does not prove safety throughout that source execution. Examples exercise fresh resource entry and nested resumption through the general theorem. A permitted outward request is forced to be an observation because it has no actual internal step. Separate positive and negative derivations show that a protected running cleanup satisfies the conditional closing interface for resume-only rights and fails it when disposal is allowed.

Current Core semantics require static checking and Core validation to exclude unsafe discard, invalid capture boundaries, missing owners, and repeated completion from accepted source. An internal failure is not a substitute for proving those obligations. This layer adds neither a source failure alternative nor a Core semantic change. Correspondence still needs source establishment, preserved readiness, authenticated declarations, and simulation of the selected Core fragment.

Scoped preservation of closing readiness

ScopedPrepared.lean proves that existing structural closing interfaces survive scoped execution. Registry extension preserves the entire old ticket record, including permissions and effect contracts. Resource-world weakening preserves callback typing in CloseReady. Stack append and decomposition retain the actual saved captures; resumption restores those captures with the whole clause prefix and surviving caller tail. Materialized closing control has no live capture boundaries. Its callback access and internal retirement authority remain separate checks.

AllocationClosing isolates the newly created obligation. Its non-capture constructor proves that the event allocates no ticket. Its capture constructor checks the new historical record and requires structural CloseReady for the actual captured stack when that record permits disposal. It contains neither a step witness nor the complete successor invariant. Under this local check, registry extension, and world growth, raw_step_preserves_closing_interfaces covers every scoped raw transition, including source capture, builtin updates, resource entry, cleanup start/completion, resumption, and disposal.

Ready combines ScopedJoint.Valid with the existing closing interfaces. For non-request expressions, nonrequest_ready_progress derives a terminal value or a named/access-checked step preserving Ready. It also derives exact registry equality: without ticket allocation, registry-domain history and extension leave no room for a changed or extra ticket record. Resource, cleanup, and close-owner allocation remain possible. The theorem still takes the current AccessChecks derivation explicitly. ready_value_progress derives those checks from value typing. Neither result establishes access checks for future requests.

Capture constructs its selected clause, contract, fresh record, named step, and joined valid successor before asking for new readiness evidence. capture_constructs_ready_obligation exposes the remaining implication: the new capture must satisfy CloseReady under its chosen closing interface if its policy permits disposal. Existing captured interfaces are preserved independently. This implication is not a theorem that source checking has already supplied the certificate.

A checked counterexample makes the distinction concrete. A source expression installs a handler around a cleanup whose callback performs that handler's operation; the clause only resumes. Four actual named/access-checked steps enter the handler, acquire cleanup, start its callback, and reach the request. Both the initial source expression and that running state satisfy Ready. If the supplied policy grants both resume and disposal, actual capture preserves Valid but cannot establish the new closing interface: it has captured a running cleanup. With a resume-only policy, the same code and actual capture preserve Ready without a disposal plan. Initial Ready alone therefore does not imply preservation of readiness for new captures under an arbitrary supplied policy.

This is a model admission and policy-mapping issue, not a demonstrated Core defect. Current static rules check actual discard and inferred control summaries and allow capture/resumption of running cleanup; they have no source capture annotations. The cleanup tests exercise the corresponding positive and negative cases. cargo test --test cleanup_typing passes all 14 cases, including captures_resume_armed_and_running_cleanup_in_structural_order and armed_cleanup_closes_but_running_cleanup_cannot_be_abandoned. These tests ground the comparison; they are not a formal simulation theorem.

A Core-to-calculus mapping must derive or validate the required continuation actions instead of assigning all rights by default. A clause that can discard still needs the capture-specific closing and interpreter obligations; narrowing its action set does not prove those obligations. The following layers derive action contracts and conditional retirement authority. New-capture closing certificate derivation, future access preservation, and formal Core correspondence remain open. No Core or normative specification change is justified by this counterexample.

Least enclosing continuation actions

ScopedActions.lean computes the least resume/dispose permission bound for an enclosing ticket in the existing structural usage judgment. Strict sequencing joins the requirements of its operands; a branch joins its condition and both arms. A resume adds the resume flag, and a discard adds the dispose flag. Function bodies cross the existing no-enclosing-ticket barrier. Nested clauses check their own tickets separately, so their actions do not contribute to the enclosing ticket's bound. Handler bodies still contribute.

usage_requires_actions proves necessity for every Syntax.Uses derivation. usage_repermission reconstructs that derivation under any sufficient enclosing permission bound, preserving the binder, input/output usage states, and the original nested policy. Together, least_enclosing_actions proves that the computed bound itself suffices and that every alternative valid bound covers it. The scoped-code counterparts use usageShape only for these structural facts. Value substitution and resource instantiation preserve the computed bound exactly, including substitution into the selected clause at capture.

“Least” refers to this structural checker, not dynamically reachable actions. Both arms count even when the condition is a literal. The sufficiency theorem takes a prior usage derivation: the flags alone do not check binder identity, single consumption, function barriers, or nested policy. Checked negative examples retain rejection of a wrong binder, sequential double resume, capture through a function, and a nested discard denied by its own policy. A mixed resume/discard branch requires both flags; a nested discard followed by an outer resume requires only resume for the outer ticket.

The running-cleanup example has exactly one clause whose required bound is resume-only. derived_resume_contract_preserves_ready connects that bound to the existing source-prefix execution and actual capture preserving Ready. It removes the unnecessary disposal obligation in that example. It does not derive closing safety for a clause that actually discards.

A separate checked example exposes the boundary of global policy synthesis. The current administrative TicketPolicy uses a natural-number binder key. If an outer resume clause and its nested discard clause reuse that number, ClausesUse forces the shared policy entry to grant both actions, although the outer clause's own bound is resume-only. The local repermission theorem keeps the nested policy unchanged and therefore does not justify updating that global entry. A source mapping must distinguish clause occurrences, for example by proved resolution to unique identities. Taking a union at a reused numeral would retain the excess-permission problem. This is a model representation and mapping obligation, not evidence for changing Core semantics.

Current name resolution already assigns a clause-owned hidden ResumeId, with a separate scope for each nested clause. Effect Core lowering retains handler and resume-owner identities. The resolver allocates checked fresh continuation identities, and Core validation looks up continuation contracts by (HandlerId, ResumeId). This gives the mapping a concrete existing target. The extraction and its preservation proof are still required; the local action theorem does not prove resolver or validator correctness.

These results derive local action requirements. Core-to-calculus policy mapping, new-capture closing certificates, future access checks, and formal Core simulation remain separate obligations. Conditional retirement authority is proved in the delegated-retirement layer below.

Synthesized clause action policies

ScopedPolicies.lean collects a finite profile of clause keys and their local action requirements from the entire expression. Unlike the enclosing-ticket bound, this traversal includes clauses inside functions and other clauses. The policy at a key is the join of all entries for that key; an absent key receives neither action. It concerns the clause declarations contained in the expression. An externally supplied enclosing ticket keeps its own scope and permissions.

usage_covers_profile proves that every valid structural usage derivation covers the collected requirements. usage_change_policy reconstructs the entire derivation under any policy covering them. It rechecks nested clauses under the new policy, then changes each clause's own ticket permissions using the local repermission theorem. least_whole_policy combines this with executable policy synthesis: the inferred policy supports the same derivation, and every other valid policy covers it pointwise. A prior derivation still supplies scope, barrier and consumption validity; synthesis alone is not a usage checker.

The distinction between a least global policy and exact local contracts matters. Conflicting entries at one key force a join. Coherent requires entries sharing a key to agree on their action flags. Under that explicit condition, inferred_exact proves that the synthesized policy equals each entry's local requirement. Distinct keys imply coherence. Identical repeated entries are also coherent, which matters when substitution copies a function containing handlers. Coherence establishes action precision; it does not authenticate a clause's identity or prove capture safety.

Resource instantiation preserves the complete profile and inferred policy exactly. Value substitution instead preserves a membership bound: every resulting entry comes from the original expression or the substituted value. Its profile can contain more copies. Coherence of their combined profile therefore implies coherence after substitution. Separate coherence of the two inputs would be too weak if they assigned different requirements to the same key. The checked function-copy example has repeated keys, retains coherence, and keeps distinct resume-only and dispose-only contracts for its two clause identities. A conflicting-key example computes both permissions and fails coherence.

initial_ready_with_synthesized_policy connects policy synthesis to initial expression typing, structural usage and empty runtime resource support. The running-cleanup example now computes its policy from the actual entire source expression, establishes initial and pre-capture Ready, and takes the actual capture step preserving Ready. Its four-step source prefix is the existing named, access-checked execution. This is a concrete source-to-capture example, not a theorem establishing new-capture certificates for every source program.

Keep the synthesized source policy fixed during execution. Recomputing it from the current expression could forget contracts still needed by retained closures, pending code or historical ticket records. The following provenance layer preserves profile coverage across current and retained code in the represented machine. Connecting resolved Core clause identities and external callable inputs to that profile remains open. Capture-specific closing certificates and future access checks are also required before general progress or Core simulation follows.

Source contract provenance through execution

ScopedProfiles.lean tracks clause key/requirement pairs through actual scoped execution. Its runtime profile includes the current expression, pending plain contexts, handler clauses, cleanup callbacks, saved cleanup results and recursively dormant captures. Cells contain integers in this fragment and contribute no code. Historical ticket records are separate from this profile; their permissions retain the fixed source policy.

raw_step_profile proves that every profile entry after a raw transition was already present before it. It covers every current transition constructor. Focus and plug redistribute code. Binding, application and capture use the proved substitution bound. Capture selects an actual clause retained by the exact handler cut. Resource opening preserves its profile. Cleanup-plan generation and materialization retain only callback code already in the captured stack. Resumption includes the full clause prefix and saved capture. The proof requires no additional typing, usage, access or freshness premise beyond the structural evidence carried by RawStep.

The invariant is membership, not multiplicity. An actual beta step copies a function containing two clauses: the profile grows from two entries to four, but each pair comes from the original profile. Another example retains those clauses inside a materialized cleanup callback. A branch example drops all current clause entries while the fixed source policy still retains its original contracts, demonstrating why recomputing the policy from current code is wrong.

The bound composes through raw traces and finite run, named and access-checked executions. From an empty initial machine, source_profile_provenance places every later runtime entry in the original expression's profile. Consequently, the fixed synthesized source policy covers all current and retained entries; source coherence also gives exact local contracts throughout execution. selected_contract_exact applies this to an actual selected handler clause, and named_ticket_contract_exact applies it to actual fresh ticket allocation.

source_capture_constructs_ready_obligation connects provenance to the existing type-directed capture construction. It returns the actual named/access-checked step, joined valid successor and new registry record, and proves that the record's permissions equal the selected clause's local required actions. The remaining implication requires CloseReady only when that local action bound contains disposal. Thus arbitrary excess grants are removed from this capture obligation for coherent source profiles. Capture-specific closing safety itself is not derived by action provenance. The running-cleanup example obtains an actual new registry entry with disposal disabled and preserves Ready.

This closes retained-code action-profile transport for the currently represented machine. Coverage is a contract-pair property, not a new structural usage derivation or a safety theorem. There is no transition injecting arbitrary host or imported callable values, and no code-bearing cell payload. Adding such inputs requires a compatible-profile condition and its preservation proof. Mapping authenticated Core identities to source profiles, deriving disposal and future access certificates, and Core simulation remain open. The result does not weaken the specified Core rejection of unsafe discard or add a source-level stuck-state observation.

Delegated internal retirement

ScopedRetirement.lean distinguishes explicit clause actions from completion delegated by an owning discard. Current dynamic semantics recursively consumes contained live clauses when closing a selected capture. The static discard rule checks that owned closure and preserves outside and running completion owners. It does not require each contained clause to have a source discard expression.

The current-Core test discard_closes_direct_and_helper_requests_crossing_an_owned_clause in effect diagnostics makes this concrete: an inner A clause performs B and then resumes; the outer B clause discards the capture containing that still-live A clause. Both direct and helper-call versions execute successfully. The related outside-owner test rejects discarding an unrelated scheduled completion. cargo test --test effect_diagnostics discard_ passes all 11 selected tests. The control analysis also follows contained live captures during close traversal. Requiring an inner explicit dispose flag would therefore reject current accepted behavior. No Core or specification change is warranted by that proposed extra requirement.

plan_retires_exact_live_tickets proves multiset equality between scheduled retirements and the capture's recursively live tickets. A successful plan cannot already contain protected retirement frames. Unique owned tickets give unique scheduled retirements; an outside ticket is never added by that plan. raw_scheduled_origin proves that a scheduled retirement after any represented raw transition either existed before or was delegated by an actual discard of a capture containing that live ticket.

RecordedTrace retains intermediate configurations as data, so an occurrence statement refers to that execution. It projects to RawTrace, and every raw reachability derivation has a nonempty type of corresponding recordings. retirement_has_prior_delegation shows that a pending retirement reached from empty initial control has a delegating discard earlier in its recording. Fresh creation history and the existing ledger theorem separately rule out duplicate completion across the recording.

Structural origin alone is not authority. At a delegating event, delegated_discard_requires_permission derives the selected ticket's dispose permission from its current CodeDemand derivation. Across a recorded execution, initial usage plus fresh creation history and the existing access checks derive the usage premises at later events. source_retirement_has_permitted_delegation then connects a reached retirement to a prior owned discard with selected-ticket permission in the registry at that event. It does not require the nested ticket's direct-dispose flag. The access checks remain explicit for every step; establishing future access and closing safety from source rules is still open.

The administrative example supplies an outer dispose-only ticket and an inner resume-only ticket. Its actual discard schedules the inner retirement, and retirement preserves configuration usage while the inner dispose flag is false. It starts with existing captures and supplied records, so it is not a proof of source-policy allocation provenance or full ScopedJoint.Valid. The independent Core tests provide the accepted-source comparison. This resolves the meaning and conditional derivation of retirement authority for the one-shot target; it does not establish complete source admission, general progress or Core simulation.

Fixed declaration ports and callable support

ScopedSignatureGap.lean proves a source-typing obstruction in the current annotated model. Signature fixes one input/output Ty pair for each exact effect instance and operation. Those types also contain concrete callable-retention annotations. Typed.resource checks its body at every fresh opening while keeping that same signature.

two_openings_confine_support proves that a fixed support list contained in both world ++ [first] and world ++ [second], for distinct identities, must already be contained in world. all_openings_confine_support derives this from universal fresh checking. Actual request typing places both operation ports in its current world, so generative_request_ports_confined applies the argument to a request whose exact instance remains unchanged across openings. This is a theorem about the present fixed annotations. It is not a general source-admission rule for callable payloads.

The inside-owner fixture allocates a cell, installs Send inside that resource scope, and performs Send.send with a closure containing let held = c; 42. Its declaration is send : (Unit -> Int) -> Unit; the clause resumes with unit. The closure retains the cell, but the selected handler is still inside its owner. The corresponding Lean program is resource-name closed, has no initial runtime resource atoms, and satisfies structural one-shot usage. Its seven-step raw execution returns unit and completes the fresh ticket and resource. At the actual cut, the payload's resource is visible outside the capture and is not owned by it.
