Eleven example lemmas include a live owner 5 whose dormant capture must consume outside owner 7. The pending source frame is proved to resolve owner 5; assigning that use to owner 7 or abandoning owner 5 is rejected. A historical spent scope retains no consumption demand. The callable example derives its actual pending frame by focus, resumes without supplying an owner equality, and connects the result to the existing admitted initial-to-capture execution prefix.

The proof applies when the entire active prefix above the selected boundary consists of the plain frames described by Source. Its capture and outside tail may contain other frame kinds and nested owners, checked by the existing runtime invariant. A handler or resource interleaved within the source prefix still requires source-invariant integration. The ownership projection does not itself authenticate protection contexts, capture effect rows or ordinary value ports. Complete source admission, all-transition source preservation and general progress remain open. This evidence changes neither current Core nor the correspondence status, and it does not enter the excluded continuation targets.

Phase-neutral source and derived saved rows

NeutralFrameRows.lean connects the phase judgment to ordinary callable summaries and positional saved-frame requirements. neutral_code_iff and neutral_context_iff prove equivalence when entry and exit phases agree: the ordinary summary retains the full value contract and raw footprint, and interpreting that footprint through the phase context yields the exact phase judgment's exported row. Structural induction uses one-shot phase monotonicity to show that every sequential intermediate phase also agrees. Resume and discard cannot occur along such a phase-neutral derivation.

The equivalence retains protection. An available protected ticket still marks outward requests as protected. After consumption, its own barrier becomes inert; other interpretation layers remain in their positions. Cleanup's invocation footprint retains its explicit protection even at a consumed boundary. Latent function requirements remain part of the full callable contract and contribute when the function is applied.

consumed_chain_rows derives SavedFrameRequirements.Rows from the actual pending contexts of an arbitrary consumed plain-frame chain. No separate row annotation is chosen. consumed_chain_rows_append composes the chain with a remaining interpretation suffix: each plain frame's raw source footprint is interpreted through that suffix, then the suffix's own pending rows are appended. capture_rows_from_neutral_prefix joins this derivation to an actual handler cut. Adding plain frames preserves exact selection and includes their derived rows in the captured prefix. The suffix may contain other frame kinds, for which existing structural Rows evidence is still required.

For a source-checked resume, resume_waiting_rows obtains the consumed caller chain and its positional rows. resume_waiting_checked combines those rows with the outside tail's existing source check. The captured row's acceptance follows from the resume expression's source derivation. resume_joint therefore needs neither a separate waiting-prefix certificate nor a binder-to-owner equality: those are derived from source and ownership evidence. The same named successor preserves CompletionJoint.Valid, checks the recomposed saved frames and retains the caller's full contract and consumed-phase chain.

Eight example lemmas cover protected requests before consumption, nonempty requests afterward, protected cleanup invocation, retained latent callable requirements, and a read whose provider must remain below the pending frame. The callable capture row is derived from the pending bind's phase judgment and its selected handler suffix. The admitted initial-to-resume execution uses that row and derives its waiting certificate from the clause source; it no longer reconstructs the waiting frame's ordinary summary as a separate premise.

This closes the conversion from consumed plain source chains to positional saved-frame rows and joins it to actual resumption. The general captured row still needs structural evidence from the actual capture; handler tables and the older CaptureRows lookup scheme have not been authenticated throughout the calculus. Captured code that changes another continuation's phase, arbitrary interleaved source scopes, ordinary port/contract alignment, complete source admission and all-transition source preservation remain open. A positional check is not a full source invariant for every newly installed captured frame. General progress and Core correspondence remain unproved, and excluded continuation targets remain excluded.

Interfaces for actual capture occurrences

CaptureInterfaces.lean joins resumption and disposal requirements to the actual captured stack. Interface has two structural constructors. A protected capture retains its derived saved-frame row and marks disposal unavailable. A closable capture retains that row, the actual makePlan equation, and source-derived rows for the resulting executable plan. plan_available proves by stack induction that plan availability is exactly the absence of protected frames, including protection inside dormant captures. interface_from_sources constructs the interface from saved-frame rows and retained callback source evidence.

Unavailable disposal is represented by none, distinct from some []. The existing source ticket still has a total disposal-row field, so ticketFor uses an empty placeholder in the unavailable case. unavailable_discard_rejected proves that the actual protected mode prevents a source discard from using that placeholder. When discard is admitted, discard_plan derives a real plan and its exact closing row from the interface. discard_ready joins that plan to the source discard's effect check and derives callback readiness under the actual closing boundary. It does not establish the independent ordinary typing and ownership premises of a full disposal transition.

ClausesAt specializes the existing structural clause derivation to the rows of one actual occurrence. Its compatibility adapter supplies those fixed rows to the older clause rules; callers of the new capture theorem do not supply a key-based CaptureRows oracle. capture_preserves joins this specialization, the actual cut and the interface with the same selected clause, raw port, fresh owner, registry extension and named successor used by the existing joint invariant. It retains the new ticket's source derivation, actual boundary and capture interface.

Twelve example lemmas include two captures whose saved code performs different operations before returning a function. Both cuts select the same actual handler and clause with the same unprotected mode. Their structural saved-frame rows differ. A single old lookup entry, keyed only by operation, clause parameter, continuation binder, clause body and protection mode, cannot equal both exact rows. This does not rule out an explicitly defined common overapproximation or a parametric source handler contract; neither is supplied by that old key alone. These two cuts are structural examples, not full admitted execution traces.

Other examples derive a nested plan that invokes cleanup before releasing its provider, and reject disposal when a dormant capture owns running cleanup. The admitted callable execution reaches capture with an interface whose row comes from its actual pending bind and selected handler suffix. The source and runtime evidence share that occurrence's selected clause and allocated owner.

This replaces the opaque capture-row input at the new local capture proof boundary. It does not yet replace the old scheme throughout source admission. A single handler contract covering all its capture occurrences remains open: the local specialization still has to agree with the handler table used for that occurrence. Phase-changing captured code, ordinary contract/port agreement, all-transition source preservation and general progress remain unfinished. Current Core and its correspondence status are unchanged, as are the excluded continuation targets.

Parametric clause row schemas

ParametricClauseRows.lean replaces repeated concrete clause derivations with one structural schema whose resumption and disposal rows are parameters. A Header fixes the binder, full input and answer contracts, and protection mode. RowExpr describes effect analysis using literal rows, resumption and disposal parameters, concatenation, and the existing ordered residual operation. Its evaluation may fail. These expressions are analysis artifacts for the existing Code; they add no computation constructor or alternative sequencing semantics.

Schema follows every constructor of the current ClauseProtection.Derives fragment, retaining exact source code, phase transitions, full callable contracts and independently checked continuation permissions. instantiate proves by structural induction that successful row evaluation produces the existing concrete derivation. abstract_derivation proves the converse when disposal availability is coherent with the header. The actual capture interface supplies that coherence: unavailable disposal implies protection. This premise prevents the old total ticket field's empty placeholder from being treated as an available plan. The equivalence concerns concrete derivations in this source fragment; it is not a principal inference algorithm or complete Ash source admission.

schema_usage derives the existing one-shot usage judgment before any row arguments are supplied. Specialization cannot grant a new resume or disposal permission, or turn a consumed phase back into an available phase. Application retains latent callable requirements, and cleanup retains protected invocation. Branch footprints combine possible requirements; repeated row parameters in that combined analysis do not imply repeated execution of a continuation.

Offer and ClausesSchema check each source clause under ordinary and protected modes and preserve clause order. specialize_clauses evaluates their row expressions for a supplied capture interface and constructs the existing occurrence-specific certificate. Failed evaluation produces an unavailable offer. One schema-list derivation therefore specializes across different resumption and disposal rows without a separately supplied body derivation for each pair. specialize_at_interface checks agreement between that generated table and the table used by the existing ordered interpreter.

Fifteen example lemmas specialize the same actual clause to both rows from the same-clause capture comparison. The resulting concrete tables differ while the schema and usage derivation remain shared. Other cases reject duplicate sequential resumption, retain one use per alternative branch, reject protected disposal, and refuse to evaluate an unavailable disposal parameter. The admitted callable capture obtains its source certificate by specializing the schema and joins it to the actual capture interface and existing joint runtime invariant.

This closes reusable parametric clause checking for the current source fragment. It does not yet provide a uniform interpreter for such schemas throughout the whole ordered stack. Agreement with the concrete table at an occurrence remains an explicit premise, and capture rows still require structural inference from the actual saved code. Parameterizing ordinary input/answer contracts, integrating phase-changing captured scopes, establishing full contract/port agreement and preserving the complete source invariant remain open. A schema without successful row evaluation and the necessary outside effect check does not establish admission or progress. Core correspondence and the excluded continuation targets are unchanged.

Effect bounds and repeated handling

EffectBounds.lean tests whether an occurrence's exact specialized clause row can also serve as a uniform handler contract. The example clause performs Audit.mark and then resumes. Its exact source row is Audit :: R for resumption row R. If the saved code requests the same handled operation again, interpreting that request through this specialized table gives Audit :: R. Requiring the capture row to equal R therefore demands R = Audit :: R. exact_specialization_rejects_repetition derives this obstruction from the actual saved-frame judgment, and list length proves that no finite row satisfies it. This is an admission obstruction in that experimental formulation; it does not invalidate previously proved conditional lemmas.

Current handler typing instead uses a shared output upper bound and permits effect weakening. The experimental correction defines Covers bound actual as list membership inclusion, preserving the complete demand atom: exact effect instance, operation and protection bit. Repeated requirements may share a bound. The actual ordered interpreter context still determines selection and residual requirements; coverage does not authorize exchanging handlers or providers. It also does not weaken continuation usage.

Offer retains the existing exact source clause derivation and checks that its row is covered by the advertised bound. Certified traverses the actual clause list and preserves first-match selection. Existing exact certificates embed by reflexive coverage. Interface retains an exact saved-frame row covered by its resumption bound and the existing exact disposal-plan certificate. Disposal unavailability retains its existing protection meaning. The capture theorem joins these premises to the same named transition, selected clause, ownership record and joint runtime invariant. The resumption theorem joins the bounded saved-frame evidence to phase-checked waiting frames and preserves both the joint runtime invariant and checked recomposed stack.

For the repeated-request family, structural induction derives the source row for n pending requests and its interpreted row of n audit demands. Every such row is covered by [Audit]. The same clause certificate, actual capture interface, exact cut and outside request check exist for every finite n. shared_bound_condition characterizes this example's admissible shared bounds, and least_shared_bound shows that each contains [Audit]. Separate evidence checks that each clause invocation consumes its continuation once and that an unprotected bound cannot admit a protected audit demand. This is induction over arbitrarily many one-shot invocations, not repeated use of one continuation.

The Core fixture invokes the request twice and counts audit actions in an outer handler. Current Core returns 2 : Int:

cargo run --quiet -- docs/design/direct-effects/one-shot/fixtures/repeated-handler-side-effect.ash

The correspondence judgment here is that exact-row admission was too restrictive in the experiment. This example supplies no evidence that Core needs changing. The Lean family checks structural capture inputs; it does not yet give a fully admitted named execution family or formal translation of the counting fixture. Uniform inference across general ordered interpretations, integration of phase-changing captures and preservation of the complete bounded source invariant remain open. General progress and Core simulation remain unproved. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain separate, excluded targets.

Uniform clause bounds

UniformClauseBounds.lean proves that one advertised clause table can certify multiple actual capture rows. Structural induction first transports coverage through a layer, then through an arbitrary finite ordered interpretation context. Successful interpretation of an upper bound entails successful interpretation of every covered row, with covered residual requirements. Both sides use the same barriers, exact effect targets, provider positions and first-match clause tables. The theorem permits no exchange of interpretations and no change to a demand's protection bit.

SuccessBelow actual bound expresses the corresponding partial-result property: when the bound is present, the actual result must also be present and covered. A failed upper evaluation supplies no admission guarantee. In particular, unavailable disposal cannot cover an available required disposal row. Induction over RowExpr then transports successful schema evaluation to covered resumption and disposal inputs. instantiate_bounded produces the existing exact clause source derivation and its coverage evidence; its phases, full callable contracts and independently checked use permissions are unchanged.

uniform_clauses evaluates the schema table at the shared bounds and proves that this fixed table certifies all covered row inputs. uniform_at_interface checks its agreement with the actual handler's table. capture_preserves obtains the source certificate from that uniform check and the actual capture interface, then preserves the same named transition, selected clause, owner allocation and joint runtime invariant. The ticket retains the actual capture rows. The exact saved-frame and disposal witnesses remain available for the existing resumption and closing theorems.

The different-row captures from the earlier interface comparison are now derived under one shared table, with a bound containing both possible outward demands. Their clause certificates use that same table. A resume-only schema can be evaluated with no disposal parameter; because it never reads that parameter, the resulting table also covers available disposal plans. The example therefore extends to captures containing dormant protected control, where disposal is unavailable, without fabricating an empty executable plan. Separate checks retain rejection of unavailable required disposal and protected demands covered only by unprotected bounds, and exhibit the existing handler-order distinction.

This establishes uniform checking for supplied shared bounds in the current clause fragment. The examples provide structural capture evidence, not complete named executions of all those variants. Bounds are still supplied: principal inference, coverage of each new capture from complete source admission, phase-changing retained scopes, contract/port agreement and all-transition source preservation remain open. Mixed disposal availability must satisfy the stated per-input condition; the uniform theorem does not infer it. General progress and Core simulation remain unproved. Current Core and the excluded continuation targets are unchanged.

Captured segments with pending owner consumption

OwnedPhaseRows.lean addresses saved code that still owes a resume or disposal to an enclosing live owner. The ordinary saved-frame source judgment has no ticket-action constructor. The new example proves that it cannot summarize a pending resume context, then proves that the extended judgment can retain that same context with its owner and effect requirements.

Chain follows the existing phase-aware plain-frame chain. A consuming frame must resolve the source binder to the recorded runtime owner; an idle frame needs no new owner equation. chain_authenticate constructs this evidence from source contexts and scope equations. At a request with a value operand, request_pending_checked derives those equations from the existing runtime ownership invariant using live_source_pending_owner. It also derives the final consumed phase. These are not new assumed ownership predicates or a second owner registry. chain_protocol proves that a consuming chain contributes exactly its actual owner to runtime demand.

The new Rows and Checked extend ordinary saved-frame requirements with an owned phase segment. This constructor retains a contiguous plain chain together with its live boundary, recursively derived rows for that owner's saved capture, and an exact available close-plan row or protected disposal unavailability. The pending chain must return the owner's full source answer contract. Its row is interpreted through the remaining actual suffix. The existing source phase rules account for protection before consumption and its removal afterward. Ordinary saved-frame row derivations embed unchanged.

Structural induction proves the row/check equivalence, append recomposition and capture decomposition. An actual handler cut crosses a segment's plain frames and live boundary together; it can cross arbitrarily many represented segments. capture_joint retains the derived rows with the same selected clause, owner allocation and joint runtime transition. capture_source_joint connects the new capture interface to uniform clause checking at shared bounds, preserving the substituted clause derivation and actual phase boundary. resume_joint restores the captured rows, derives the waiting caller's source checks, and preserves the same runtime invariant and recomposed pending-code check.

The pending-resume fixture uses resume (perform Outer.pong ()) in an inner handler clause. Dispatch to the outer handler captures the pending inner resume and its live owner. Current Core returns 17 : Int:

cargo run --quiet -- docs/design/direct-effects/one-shot/fixtures/captured-pending-resume.ash

The Lean example checks the corresponding pending context, source chain, exact outer cut, actual owner demand and capture interface. Its close effect row is empty, but its plan retires the captured owner; an empty effect row does not mean an empty plan. These are structural source and ownership witnesses, not a fully admitted named execution of the fixture or a formal Core translation. The comparison identifies another experimental admission limitation, with no evidence that Core needs alignment for this case.

This extension handles closed owner segments: the live boundary is inside the saved prefix, and its phase-changing chain contains contiguous plain frames. Captures that leave the referenced owner outside, and phase-changing chains with intervening handler/resource frames, still need rules. Full contract/port agreement, complete initial source admission and source preservation for every transition remain unfinished. In particular, the pending-code check alone is not the complete machine source invariant. General progress and Core simulation remain unproved. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

Outside-owner use interfaces

OpenOwnerUses.lean records which demanded owners are outside a captured stack. Interface carries the existing structural StackUsage derivation and its demand list. externalUses filters out owners physically owned by the capture. These uses remain obligations; the interface does not transfer their ownership to the capture or permit duplication.

capture_interface derives the saved interface from an actual handler cut. capture_linear_interface uses the current configuration's ownership balance to prove that both its total demand and outside interface have no duplicates, and that the outside owners are active in the surviving tail. Restoration preserves the exact demand and outside-use lists while widening access to the actual waiting context. The existing resumption ownership theorem applies to open captures; the example checks both the raw resumption and its resulting configuration usage.

The disposal connection is proved for arbitrary structural usage derivations. Every pending owner is demanded, and its access comes from a recursively live owner in the stack or its outside interface. With the existing ownership separation, external_empty_iff_internal proves that an empty outside interface is equivalent to InternalUses capture.liveTickets capture.pending. discard_usage derives the separation from the prestate and uses the interface to supply that old disposal premise. Physical plan construction, protection, resource support and callback effect compatibility remain separate conditions. A nonempty outside interface rules out the internal-use premise even when a physical close plan exists.

closed_rows_internal proves by induction that every derivation in the preceding OwnedPhaseRows.Rows system demands only owners contained in the represented stack. closed_rows_no_external therefore derives an empty outside interface. This proves the source rule limitation, rather than assuming that another specialization could express an open capture. The new open example has a checked pending source context referring to owner 9, an exact capture leaving that owner outside, and interface [9]. Its physical plan is empty, but disposal would lose the pending outside consumption. Resuming owner 19 restores the capture and retains the obligation to owner 9. The example is structural source and ownership evidence plus a raw resumption step; it is not a complete execution with the joint type, support and phase/effect invariant.

Three Core fixtures distinguish the current comparison outcomes:

  • Open-owner resume binds an effect request's result, then resumes the outside owner inside a nested handler. It returns 17 : Int.
  • Open-owner discard changes the nested clause to discard and return 42. It exits with effect.discard-unsafe, identifying the outside clause whose completion would be skipped.
  • Direct resume operand places the request directly in the outside resume argument under the nested handler. It exits with internal.core-build. JSON diagnostics identify responsibility compiler and cause invalid-payload.
cargo run --quiet -- docs/design/direct-effects/one-shot/fixtures/open-owner-resume.ash
cargo run --quiet -- docs/design/direct-effects/one-shot/fixtures/open-owner-discard.ash
cargo run --quiet -- --message-format json docs/design/direct-effects/one-shot/fixtures/open-owner-resume-operand.ash

The last result is a Core payload-building defect, not a normal rejection of unsafe disposal. Current resume dynamics evaluate the argument before consuming the owner; the earlier outward pending-resume fixture also accepts a direct effectful argument. The nested let form supplies a successful comparison for the open-owner behavior, while the direct-operand failure prevents an execution comparison for that form. This assessment does not locate or repair the internal implementation cause, and is not a formal Core correspondence proof. No Core implementation or specification changed.

The outside-use interface establishes the control/ownership part of open-capture checking. The phase and effect rules must still express consumption of an owner left outside the cut, including the effect of that consumption on later protected requests. Intervening handler/resource frames, full source admission, preservation and progress remain unfinished. An empty outside interface alone does not establish disposal safety or general admission. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

Named owner phases in ordered contexts

OwnerPhases.lean refines the ordered interpretation context with named live and spent owner entries. Ordinary handler, builtin and protection entries retain their existing meaning. A live owner carries the protection of its actual dormant capture; a spent entry projects to no interpretation layer. ofStack derives the entries from the existing runtime stack, and project_stack proves that projection recovers CallableProtectionFrames.contextOf exactly. Dormant interpretations remain inactive. No computation syntax or runtime rule changes.

Consumes is a structural judgment with four constructors: consume the matching live owner, or pass an ordinary entry, a different live owner, or a different spent owner. Induction proves equivalence to consume, uniqueness of the result, preservation of the owner-name list, and rejection of a second consumption. This judgment records a phase change; operation permission, resource support and callback effect compatibility are checked independently.

The stack correspondence uses the existing historical name invariant. Every named context owner occurs in the runtime's ticket-name list, which also counts dormant owners and retirement frames. Runtime uniqueness excludes an alias in the waiting prefix or saved capture. consume_stack therefore updates the exact live boundary selected by the actual resumption, across an arbitrary prefix of plain, handler, resource, cleanup, live and spent frames. capture_context retains the exact ordered split for any handler cut. These induction arguments cover arbitrary finite nesting; they do not enumerate individual stack shapes.

resume_context restores the saved context before the updated caller. resume_requirements proves that checking demands in this restored context is exactly residualizing them through the capture and checking the result in the updated caller. restored_owner_consumed rejects another consumption even after the capture has been restored. resume_joint joins these facts with the same actual named transition and the existing ownership, support, type, callable-result and name-history invariant. The caller update is derived from that invariant, rather than supplied as an unauthenticated phase annotation.

discard_usage_context uses the same structural consumption judgment and installs the actual close plan followed by its closing barrier. It joins the raw discard step with ownership preservation using the preceding outside-owner interface: that interface must be empty, and the plan must exist. Its residual checking equation retains the closing barrier. The theorem covers usage and context correspondence; it does not discharge resource support or callback effect admission for disposal.

The running-cleanup example checks an actual resume step followed by actual cleanup completion. Spending owner 9 removes its protection from the waiting caller, but the restored running cleanup still contributes a barrier. A request to a disposing handler is rejected both before resumption and during the restored cleanup, then accepted by the context checker after cleanup completes. The saved capture has no close plan. These are runtime-step and context-check examples, not a complete source derivation for the example configuration. The previous open-capture example also has the exact context update: spending owner 19 retains the outside owner 9 in the surviving tail.

This supplies the context transition needed when an open capture consumes an outside owner. The general source judgment must still connect pending code to these changes, preserve its phase/effect evidence across intervening frames and all transitions, and derive initial admission and progress. The result does not establish that stronger source invariant or formal Core correspondence. Core is unchanged. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

Source segments with an exposed outside owner

OpenPhaseSegments.lean extends source composition to a segment whose consuming code refers to one owner outside that segment. The existing ClauseProtection.Derives and ContextDerives judgments continue to check direct source expressions and their evaluation positions. No new sequencing syntax or computation model is introduced.

FrameSource has structural cases for all seven ExecFrame constructors. A plain frame carries its existing phase-indexed source derivation and resolves its consuming binder to the exposed owner. Handler and cell returns preserve the full callable contract. Armed cleanup checks its callback and exports its latent effects with running protection; running cleanup preserves the saved value's contract. Closing and retirement return scalar contracts. The independent joint runtime invariant retains ordinary ports, ownership, support and name history; these protection contracts do not replace Core's types.

Segment threads the exposed owner's phase and the full callable contract from one frame to the next. Each frame uses the actual interpretation suffix remaining below it. A separate fixed stack describes the suffix between the represented segment and the exposed owner. Spent boundaries are transparent. The current judgment has no interior live-owner constructor: segment_no_active_owner proves this limitation. It is a component to integrate with owned phase rows, not a replacement that discards their admitted cases.

Induction proves append composition and decomposition at an arbitrary split. capture_segment applies decomposition to an actual handler cut, retaining the intermediate phase, full contract and exact row split. checked_recompose combines the rows at the same outside context. Each component must already be checked at its actual remaining suffix; the theorem does not permit moving a handler across another interpretation or reusing a check at a changed context.

The usage connection uses actual FrameDemand and StackUsage derivations. segment_protocol filters their demand list for the exposed owner. With that owner outside the segment's physical ownership, the filtered demand is empty for an unchanged phase and exactly the singleton owner for available-to-consumed source behavior. Retirement of another owner does not count as consuming the exposed owner. consumed_owner_is_external derives the corresponding outside-use obligation. consuming_segment_not_disposable then rejects the old internal-use premise for disposal, regardless of whether a physical close plan exists. This is source usage evidence; it does not assert that execution terminates.

Source connects current code to the pending segment. Source lemmas preserve its phase and full-contract agreement through focus, plug, bind substitution, application reduction, branch selection, handler return, and synchronous cleanup start and finish. Application reduction follows the machine's reset to the empty current scope. Branch selection retains an accepted row for the chosen branch. Cleanup start introduces the running barrier; cleanup finish returns the saved value under its stored scope. source_current_request derives dispatch checking from the source certificate and the actual exposed-owner boundary.

focus_joint and plug_joint retain the source certificate on the same named step as the existing joint runtime invariant. restore_recompose supports a captured segment followed by a waiting caller segment: the capture's return phase and full contract must match the caller's input. Both are checked at their future suffix, including the spent consumed-owner boundary. restore_joint joins that recomposition to the actual resumption and joint invariant. Its exposed-owner boundary realizes the retained source phase and protection in the actual restored context. This does not authenticate every supplied ticket row against a general continuation registry.

The earlier open-capture example now has a Segment derivation from available to consumed for outside owner 9, as well as a Source derivation for its request. Its source ticket uses the actual saved capture with a checked empty resumption row and an executable empty closing plan. Dispatch is checked at the actual stack. Restoring the capture across spent owner 19 retains the segment and its outside obligation; disposal is rejected from the source-plus-usage evidence. These are source and structural runtime connections, not a complete execution of the example under the full source invariant.

A second example uses an actual protected saved capture whose resumption row is empty and whose disposal is unavailable. Pending code resumes that owner, then performs an operation. The later operation exports an unprotected demand and is accepted by an outside disposing handler. Moving the same requirement before consumption exports a protected demand and is rejected. The preceding runtime cleanup example remains applicable: the restored running cleanup is protected until it completes. The source phase change does not remove that runtime frame.

The next integration must retain these captured phase transitions in continuation interfaces and use them when checking newly selected clauses. Interior live-owner groups, multiple exposed-owner interfaces, authentication of general source contracts, initial admission and all-transition source preservation remain unfinished. Whole-program progress and formal Core correspondence remain unproved. No Core implementation or specification changed; multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

Captured phase contracts and clause checking

CapturedPhaseContracts.lean records a captured segment's outside phase transition in its continuation contract. The contract retains the local binder, full callable input and answer contracts, actual capture protection, outside input and output phases, a resumption effect bound and an optional disposal effect bound. These are source annotations for the existing direct calculus; no computation syntax or runtime transition changes.

Interface connects that contract to the same actual capture in the source and usage judgments. It retains the exact segment row beneath the advertised bound, the outside-use interface, ownership separation, capture protection and a structural Closing derivation. Registry extension preserves the exact source row and outside-use list. Resumption checks may use a shared upper bound; they do not require the exact occurrence row to equal the bound.

Closing has three cases. A protected capture or a nonempty outside-use interface makes disposal unavailable. Otherwise, an actual executable plan, its callback source rows and coverage by the disposal bound establish availability. disposal_preserves_outside_phase proves that available disposal requires equal outside input and output phases: a source transition that consumes the outside owner has an outstanding outside obligation, so it cannot satisfy the closing rule. This separates physical plan availability from ownership permission. Other resource support and callback invocation conditions remain independent.

The new clause Derives judgment threads a pair of states through the existing source forms. One state records the clause's local continuation use; the other records the exposed outside owner's phase. Resumption requires the local owner to be available and the outside phase to match the captured contract's input. It consumes the local owner, imports the resumption effect bound and promises the captured contract's outside output phase. Disposal requires an available closing bound and leaves the outside phase unchanged. The ordinary source forms compose those endpoints and preserve complete callable contracts.

local_usage projects the existing independent one-shot syntax judgment. local_phase_monotone prevents another local use after consumption. The captured segment proves monotonicity of its outside transition, which interface_outside_monotone transports through clause source checking. Closed values preserve both states. Closed parameter substitution retains both states, the full result contract and the exported row. context_realizes connects the two source states to the actual nested owner boundaries, with the fixed interpretations between them in their original order.

capture_clause uses the actual handler cut and selected clause, the captured interface, operation lookup, operand source evidence and an accepted clause row. It constructs the same fresh named capture step and existing joint runtime invariant. Its clause certificate checks the substituted body and retains the captured interface under the extended usage registry. The source entry context is proved to realize the new local boundary and the actual outside boundary. This is selected-clause admission for a supplied structural source certificate; it does not derive that certificate for every initial program or install a general phase-aware contract table in the existing registry.

consumed_to_outer provides the return connection to the preceding source judgment. Once the local owner is spent, the remaining clause code cannot change the outside phase again. Induction converts that code to ClauseProtection.Derives for the outside owner, preserving the full result contract and effect row. This permits reuse of the earlier pending-segment construction; the complete machine handoff from a resuming clause through its restored capture and waiting caller still requires integration.

The main example captures a pending resume of outside owner 9, then checks a clause using local binder 20. The outside owner has an actual protected saved capture. The local capture is itself unprotected and has an executable empty close plan, but its outside obligation makes disposal unavailable. Resuming it consumes the local owner and promises consumption of the outside owner. A later effect exports an unprotected demand and is accepted by an outside disposing handler. The same effect before resumption exports a protected demand and is rejected. The local clause still projects to exactly one syntactic continuation use; a second local resume is rejected.

flat_entry_recheck_rejects_later_row demonstrates why the old flat clause-row check cannot supply this admission: checking all clause effects at entry sees the outside owner as still live. The new source judgment places each requirement at its proper phase. This is a limitation of the experiment's earlier clause-row representation, not evidence that Core needs changing. General ordered handler tables must carry the phase-aware interface before whole source preservation can be established. A separate neutral capture retains available disposal and proves that it preserves the outside phase; the new rule does not ban safe discard.

These examples provide structural capture interfaces and clause source proofs, not complete executions under the full source invariant. General handler-table and registry integration, interior live-owner groups, multiple exposed-owner interfaces, initial admission and all-transition source preservation remain open. Whole-program progress and formal Core correspondence remain unproved. Core is unchanged. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

Resumption into open source

PhaseResumption.lean connects the preceding clause judgment to source evidence for the actual restored configuration. The source language remains ScopedExpressions.Code; the extension adds proof judgments for evaluation contexts and their pending frames, not a new computation syntax.

ContextDerives tracks the local and outside owner states, the hole's full value contract, the context's result contract, and remaining effect requirements. Chain composes arbitrarily many contiguous plain frames. Each frame must accept the states and contract supplied by its predecessor. Structural induction proves chain append, decomposition and expression reconstruction. There is no bound on chain length and no enumeration of concrete captured continuations.

Source combines the current expression derivation with that chain and checks the remaining exported demands beyond the exposed outside boundary. Focusing splits the current derivation into a child and its context; plugging reconstructs it after a closed value returns. focus_joint and plug_joint join these source transformations to the same named runtime steps and existing full joint invariant. context_realizes relates the source interpretations to two actual owner boundaries beneath the plain prefix.

source_resume_parts identifies the exact handoff at a value-operand resume. The local owner is initially available, and the outside owner has the capture contract's input state. The operand supplies the capture's full input contract. The pending clause expects the local owner to be consumed, the capture's outside output state, and its answer contract. Once local use is consumed, chain_consumed_segment converts the waiting chain to the earlier outside-owner segment judgment. Its proof retains both state and full-contract agreement at each inductive step.

saved_at_waiting places the capture certificate above the waiting plain frames and spent local marker. These additions have no residual interpretation effect; the proof does not move a handler, resource or protected frame across the capture. restored_source composes the saved segment and waiting source at their actual future suffixes. It constructs an OpenPhaseSegments.Source certificate for the returned operand and restored prefix. The retained actual capture row is covered by its advertised resume bound, so replacing that bound by the actual row preserves acceptance of the remaining demands.

resume_joint puts this certificate on the same after-configuration as the named resume rule and the full joint invariant. Ownership, closure, runtime types and source restoration therefore concern the same step. The theorem requires the actual captured interface, a source certificate for the clause and waiting chain, an actual outside boundary, and resolution of the local binder. It does not derive those premises for every source program.

The example focuses bind 6 (resume 20 unit) request into an actual waiting frame. Owner 19 holds a capture whose pending code consumes outside owner 9. The outside owner has a protected saved cleanup. The example proves the raw resume step, its exact restored stack, before and after ownership, and a restored source certificate containing the waiting request. Its single handler table resumes local requests and permits disposal at the outside effect handler. The request's unprotected demand is accepted at the final outside suffix and rejected if rechecked against the still-live protected owner at clause entry. This is source and ownership evidence for the fragment, not a complete source-admitted execution.

The handoff is now proved for one exposed outside owner and arbitrary contiguous plain waiting frames; the saved segment may use all seven evaluation-frame constructors and spent markers supported by OpenPhaseSegments.Segment. Interior live-owner groups, multiple exposed owners, and general phase-aware handler-table and registry integration remain open. Resuming the exposed owner itself also needs integration into the common source invariant. Initial source admission, all-transition source preservation, whole-program progress and formal Core correspondence remain unproved. Core is unchanged. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

Shared owner phase transitions

OwnerPhaseTransitions.lean supplies the shared state needed to remove the earlier source judgment's fixed number of exposed owners. Phases maps an owner identity to its available or consumed state. Runtime maps use the finite ownedTickets list, which includes owners retained in dormant captures and scheduled retirement. This is ownership state: it does not imply that a dormant owner is currently accessible to an operation.

Trace before owners after is inductive. An empty demand leaves the map unchanged. A nonempty demand requires its head owner to be available, marks that owner consumed, and continues with the remaining list. Induction proves append, decomposition, a unique result map, availability of every demanded owner, no repeated names, no resurrection, and preservation of undemanded entries. There is no bound on the number of owners. The characterization theorem relates this structural judgment to a duplicate-free available demand and its computed final map; it does not introduce an admission oracle.

A demand trace is a proof of ownership obligations, not necessarily an execution trace. In particular, the trace that consumes a configuration's entire balanced demand does not establish termination. trace_permutation proves that permuting owner consumptions preserves their final ownership map. It permits no permutation of effectful computations or interpretation layers.

trace_restrict projects the same trace onto any selected owners. Applying it to names outside a capture derives that capture's outside transition. The actual handler cut and structural runtime usage determine the captured and surviving demand lists; capture_trace derives their common intermediate map. Interior owners are retained in the full trace and removed only from the outside projection. Thus the full and external interfaces cannot choose inconsistent intermediate states independently.

project evaluates the existing ordered OwnerPhases.Context at the shared map. An available live owner contributes its protection barrier; a consumed owner contributes none. Ordinary handler, resource and protected-frame layers keep their positions. project_actual proves equality with the current stack's interpretation, and consume_project relates a physical live-to-spent update to the corresponding map update under name uniqueness. Capture retains ordered splitting and residual checking at any shared phase map.

resume_phase_trace handles arbitrary waiting stacks, captures and tails, including interior live owners and dormant captures. The restored stack's ownership map differs by exactly the resumed owner. resume_joint joins this map and its interpretation to the same named runtime step and full joint invariant. capture_joint similarly retains the captured phase interface across registry extension and introduces the newly allocated owner into the runtime map. Allocation keeps the existing issued-name freshness premise: an available or consumed map entry alone cannot authorize name reuse.

The new representation is connected to the earlier source work. trace_owner_protocol recovers each single-owner protocol from the shared trace. captured_contract_projection uses source and runtime usage for the same capture to recover its exposed-owner transition. resumption_contract_projection recovers the local and outside states of CapturedPhaseContracts.State. earlier_context_residual proves equality of the corresponding residual effect interpretations. disposal_preserves_external_map strengthens the earlier outside-phase result: an available close contract preserves every outside owner, while internal captured owners may still be consumed.

The example captures an interior live owner 29 together with pending consumption of outside owner 9. The capture owns 29, and its outside interface contains only 9. The actual local resume consumes owner 19, restores the capture and leaves 29 and 9 available. Structural usage and the raw step agree with that map; the complete ownership demand consumes each of the three owners once, and a repeated 19 is rejected. These are fragment proofs, not a complete execution from a fully admitted source program.

old_segment_excludes_live_group proves that this same capture cannot inhabit OpenPhaseSegments.Segment. The new map therefore removes the representational limit but does not by itself add the missing source constructor. The next source judgment must thread this shared map through expression and frame derivations, including live boundaries and saved continuation contracts, and prove capture/recomposition and restoration there. General handler-table integration, complete source admission, all-transition source preservation and whole-program progress remain open. Core correspondence remains unproved and Core unchanged. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

Source with shared owner phases

OwnerSource.lean carries the shared map into the direct source judgment. Derives still describes ScopedExpressions.Code; there is one sequencing syntax. Its indices record the lexical scope, initial and final owner maps, full callable result contract, owner demand and exported effect row. ContextDerives gives the corresponding hole contract, and FrameSource binds a pending plain context to the frame's actual saved scope.

ResumeContract records input and answer contracts, protection, captured owner demand and exported resume requirements. Closing has a separate demand list and optional row. These are annotations at a common outside analysis boundary, not authentication of their own provenance. Resume requires actual lexical resolution, a known contract, the binder's resume permission, an operand derivation and a shared-map transition consuming the owner followed by the captured demand. Discard separately requires disposal permission, an unprotected contract, an available closing row and its transition. The captured or closing demands include obligations executed by that saved work; they are not merely the explicit ticket names in the clause's current syntax.

source_trace derives the shared transition from the expression derivation. Consequently consumed owners cannot reappear and no owner is demanded twice. Both branches must finish at the same map and full result contract. They may consume owners in different orders: trace_same_endpoints proves that their consumption lists are permutations. Effect rows retain both alternatives, and this ownership result permits no reordering of their effects.

Segment now includes every stack constructor. The seven execution-frame rules include a phase change for retirement. A live owner boundary requires the owner to be consumed when the preceding computation reaches it. Its contract protection must match the physical capture, and its answer contract feeds the tail. Spent boundaries also retain the consumed state and answer contract. The physical saved code at a live boundary is retained as runtime data. General agreement between each continuation annotation and that saved code remains an explicit registry obligation.

Each pending frame checks its remaining effects against the exact future suffix, projected at the shared map. Structural induction proves append, decomposition and capture splitting through live boundaries as well as the other stack cases. The split preserves the intermediate owner map and full value contract, with exact concatenation of the demand and effect rows. No finite list of continuation shapes or bound on nesting is used.

Source combines current code with the pending segment and checks their exported requirements beyond the common fixed suffix. Closed substitution preserves the map transition and contracts. Source transformations cover focus, plug, bind, application reduction and branch selection. Application retains the actual reset to an empty ticket scope. The branch result retains the same owner obligations up to permutation and the accepted selected effect row. focus_joint and plug_joint join their source transformations to the same named runtime steps and full joint invariant.

source_current_request_checked derives the earlier callable protection check at the actual current stack from the shared-map source certificate. It checks the immediate request at its entry map and keeps future phase changes in the pending derivation. value_cannot_reach_live proves a local progress exclusion: a value cannot have a source certificate at a live boundary when the starting map is the actual ownership map. The value preserves that map, while the boundary requires its owner to have been consumed. This is not whole-program progress.

The interior-owner example from the preceding module now has a Segment derivation. It consumes interior owner 29 before reaching that live boundary, then consumes outside owner 9. The actual cut splits this source through the interior boundary. Its continuation annotation agrees with the captured source row, protection and runtime demand. The example supplies source certificates before and after the local resume of owner 19, an actual restored-stack equality, and the preceding raw-step and ownership proofs. Neutral discard is admitted, the captured contract's unavailable discard is rejected, and a spent owner cannot be resumed. These remain fragment certificates, not a complete execution derived from a fully admitted initial source program.

The structural source exclusion for this interior live-owner group is removed. Source preservation from runtime records for capture, resume and disposal needs a registry judgment authenticating all saved-source and close-plan annotations at their actual interpretation suffixes. Handler installation and generative resource acquisition also need source rules and integration with their existing runtime proofs. Complete source admission, all-transition preservation, whole-program progress and formal Core correspondence remain unproved. Core is unchanged. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain excluded.

General one-shot source restoration

OwnerSourceResumption.lean proves the general resumption source transformation over the shared owner map. It accepts the before-resume Source derivation and a Segment derivation for the actual capture at its restored suffix. That suffix contains the entire waiting stack, the selected spent marker and the original tail. There is no restriction to plain waiting frames or a fixed number of interior and outside owners.

Interpretation transport uses a precise premise: the selected owner is consumed at the source position being transported. source_inside_spent proves the expression case by induction. Source monotonicity carries that premise through operand evaluation, sequencing and the other children. Context and frame transport follow, including latent calls and cleanup effects. Segment induction then changes the fixed suffix. pending_live_to_spent decomposes the waiting segment, changes just the selected marker and recomposes the source. It retains all ordinary frames, saved scopes, other live boundaries, full contracts, owner demands and effect rows.

resume_source_parts inverts the current value-operand resume. The value has no immediate demand or effects, so the current transition consists of the selected owner followed by the contract's captured demand. The source transition fixes the captured endpoint map uniquely. restored_source composes the saved segment with the changed pending segment at that endpoint. Its new current expression is the original operand value. The resulting demand drops exactly the selected owner; the saved obligations remain pending. The actual saved effect row must be covered by the advertised resume row, preserving the accepted outside check.

resume_joint connects this transformation to the same NamedAccessStep and full CompletionJoint.Valid preservation theorem. The source before the step starts at the actual stack's ownership map. The immediate runtime transition consumes only the selected owner, and the resulting source starts at the actual restored stack's map. The transitive captured demands describe future source execution, not additional immediate runtime consumption.

The interior-owner example now obtains its after-source from its before-source through the general theorem. It retains checked raw execution and ownership: owner 19 is consumed while owners 29 and 9 remain available. Another resume of 19 is rejected. A negative interpretation example shows that live and spent markers can differ while their owner is available; the consumed-phase premise cannot be dropped. A restored protection barrier still qualifies the exported request even though the adjacent owner marker is spent.

The saved-segment derivation is an explicit structural premise. It is not an assumed after-configuration source judgment, but it still requires provenance from the actual captured code and a maintained registry. Checking an advertised row alone does not establish it. In particular, this theorem does not transport a captured source across newly installed handlers without checking their effect on its interpretation. General registry authentication, capture and disposal source preservation, handler/resource source rules and initial admission remain necessary for all-transition preservation and whole-program progress. Formal Core correspondence remains unproved; no Core alignment or later continuation capabilities are part of this result.

Captured source contract provenance

OwnerCaptureContracts.lean supplies source provenance at allocation. SavedSource contains an actual Segment derivation for the captured stack at its surviving suffix, its exact exported row beneath the advertised bound, and agreement between contract protection and physical protection. The derivation checks the full input and answer contracts and the owner demand between its endpoint maps. It authenticates the resume fields; the closing fields still need a separate structural plan check.

capture_contract derives these resume fields from the before-request source and the actual nearest-handler cut. A value operand leaves the entry map unchanged. Splitting the pending source determines the intermediate map, full answer contract, captured demand and row, and surviving tail. The captured input is the request's result contract. The original outside check implies acceptance of the captured row followed by the tail row. Closing annotations are retained explicitly and are not justified by this extraction.

Extends states pointwise retention of existing contract lookups. Induction proves that extension preserves expression, context, frame, segment and complete configuration source derivations. Fresh insertion satisfies this relation. A concrete historical-registration premise maps each source contract name to a runtime record. Runtime issued-name freshness then implies source-name freshness; registration is retained under the paired insertions. This checks name identity, not coherence of the two records' contract contents.

capture_joint joins these results to the same named capture and full runtime invariant. Source and runtime demand lists remain separate: source resume demands include the work of saved continuations, whereas raw syntax demands and dormant captures are represented separately by runtime usage. No unproved equality between the two lists is used.

clause_source constructs the after-capture source from a structural derivation of the selected clause, closed payload substitution, and the surviving tail. The clause starts at the owner map extended by the fresh available owner and finishes at the map expected by the tail; the new boundary checks that its owner has been consumed. General handler source rules must supply this clause derivation and its accepted effect row.

The retained source also supplies the resumption premise. Spending a freshly introduced owner restores the original map when that entry was previously consumed. The captured source determines the subsequent endpoint. Rebase is proved where the actual ordered suffix projections agree at consumed-owner phases. resume_from_saved_source then applies the general restoration theorem to arbitrary waiting stacks satisfying that interpretation check. A spent marker alone is transparent. A negative example shows that a newly installed waiting handler can change the exported row, so this transport proof is not universally available. Different projections require a source derivation checked at the receiving suffix; they do not by themselves prove resumption unsafe. The general restoration theorem accepts such a derivation without projection equality.

The nested-owner example starts with source contracts for owners 29 and 9, and no contract for 19. Its actual cut has a source-derived resume contract. The checked saved source, selected clause and tail construct the after-capture source under fresh insertion. That retained evidence derives the after-resume source. Both raw steps and their existing ownership checks concern the same physical configurations. A separate negative check rejects overwriting a different existing contract as an extension.

This establishes allocation provenance and conditional capture/restoration composition. It does not yet maintain authentication for every saved record through all later transitions. Source operation and callable contracts must also be related to runtime declaration and port records; historical registration alone does not prove that coherence. Closing-plan authentication, general handler/resource source rules and disposal source preservation remain required, followed by initial admission, all-transition preservation and whole-program progress. Formal Core correspondence remains unproved and Core is unchanged. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous integration remain excluded.

Closing source and disposal

OwnerClosingSource.lean connects actual closing entries to the shared-map source judgment. retirements extracts their ordered ticket sequence. It equals the ownership of the materialized closing control, and a successful makePlan gives a permutation of the captured owners. This accounts for nested and dormant captures as well as directly captured owners.

plan_source derives a complete Segment from the existing callback Rows, an owner transition for those retirements, and the exported row at the receiving suffix. Its induction has one case per plan entry. A release preserves the map and carries a cell provider until that entry is reached. An invocation checks the stored callback as a unit-to-unit function and interprets its protected latent row through the remaining plan and suffix. A retirement consumes its available owner and then checks the remaining entries at the updated map. Abandoned expression contexts and source handlers do not reappear in this plan.

The plan contains no live interpretation markers. Its internal retirements leave the suffix projection unchanged when their names are absent from that suffix. retirements_separate derives this condition from the actual runtime stack's name uniqueness. That uniqueness follows from the existing name history and ownership ledger; the runtime join does not require a new supplied separation predicate.

ClosingData retains the exact successful plan, callback source rows, and InternalUses for abandoned syntax. It can be generated from retained callback source, actual captured usage, separation from outside owners, and an empty outside-demand interface. Plan existence alone does not discharge that final obligation. The callback row still needs to be exported at the actual receiving suffix. withClosing installs the actual retirement list and exported row as the continuation's closing fields, preserving its other fields. Successful plan construction and saved-source protection agreement establish the unprotected capability premise.

discard_source inverts the before-discard judgment. Its transition consumes the selected owner followed by the advertised closing demand. The actual plan authenticates that demand and its checked effects. The proof changes the pending selected marker to spent, installs the closing boundary, and composes the planned source with the surviving caller. discard_source_from_data supplies these closing fields from ClosingData and retains the abandoned-use check alongside the resulting source.

discard_joint joins this source transformation to the same named discard and full CompletionJoint.Valid preservation result. It retains the existing plan typing, freshness and access checks. The immediate step consumes only the selected owner. Nested owners remain available until their retirement entries execute; the after-source is indexed by that actual runtime ownership map. Internal retirement has its structural origin in the initiating disposal and does not perform another explicit source-level resume or discard request.

Further source-preservation lemmas cover synchronous callback start and finish, retirement, closing completion and resource release. Starting a callback retains the saved result and its full contract in the running frame. Finishing restores that result and the action's saved scope. Retirement requires an available owner, updates its map entry, and removes just that demand; an already consumed owner is rejected. These local lemmas do not assert callback termination or prove every intervening callback transition from initial source admission.

The example captures pending code for an interior owner together with a callback and its cell provider. The actual plan invokes the callback, retires the interior owner, and releases the cell. Its before/after source judgments and raw discard agree with the checked runtime usage. The selected owner is spent immediately, while the interior owner remains available. The callback's source invocation follows from the after-discard source. Moving its demand after the resource release fails the effect check, as required by the existing close-plan analysis.

These results supply structural closing evidence and conditional disposal preservation. Maintaining that evidence for all continuation records, relating source contracts to runtime declaration/port records, and deriving all handler and resource source rules remain necessary. Initial admission, all-transition preservation and whole-program progress remain unproved. Core correspondence remains an assessment obligation, with no Core changes. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous hooks remain outside this target.

Shared source types and pending contexts

CoherentSourceTypes.lean uses one Value annotation for each binding in the stable callable source component. Its ordinary port projection distinguishes unit, Boolean, integer and reference types. Its protection projection groups those atoms under scalar and retains pair and function structure. A function annotation records both its latent exact-effect instances and its operation/protection footprint. These are annotations on the existing ScopedExpressions.Code, with the same direct sequencing syntax.

Summary checks variables, values, pairs, lambdas, application, binding, branching, requests and synchronous cleanup. Every bound value has the same annotation in both projected environments. Structural induction gives port_typing and protection_summary; checked residual interpretation also gives the stable rule of OwnerSource.Derives. This source judgment is limited to the stated component: it does not yet have handler, resource, resume or discard constructors.

Closed substitution preserves the shared annotation and exact footprint, including higher-order functions. Lambda substitution transports a closed value to the body's environment and latent allowance. Beta reduction then widens that allowance using the application rule's admitted-effects premise. Binding uses the same annotation for the initializer and substituted variable. These proofs preserve the shared derivation itself, so later projections retain its binding choices.

ContextSummary describes the eight stable pending positions. Each hole and result has one shared annotation; previously evaluated values contribute no immediate footprint. Actual focus splits a source derivation into its child and pending context, and plugging reconstructs it. The context projects to ordinary port typing and, after residual interpretation, the owner-phase context judgment. plain_frame checks the shared input/output ports against an actual frame's stored metadata and derives both frame judgments. Ticket and resource positions still need integration with the corresponding source rules.

checkCompatible is a decidable check of callable shape. It deliberately abstracts ordinary atom distinctions, latent effects and stored resource support. checkOperation checks operation presence on both sides and the input/output shapes of present entries. A shared operation annotation always passes this check. A paired Record retains checked source/runtime input and answer shapes; its two registries stay registered and preserve those checks under fresh insertion. These results do not derive a complete record from every capture or maintain its saved-source, effect and support evidence through all transitions.

capture_input_compatible connects the actual source request and checked operation entry to the input contract produced by the capture split. The saved source and tail are retained. Obtaining the captured answer's ordinary type still requires shared annotations throughout the pending segment, including handler and owner boundaries; independent source and port derivations alone do not establish that agreement.

The examples make the boundary explicit. An integer condition has a scalar protection summary but fails ordinary typing and Summary. An unannotated identity lambda separately admits a pair-to-pair protection contract and an integer-to-integer port type; these choices have incompatible shapes. This is an example of independent instantiation, not a Core defect. A shared higher-order application retains its annotation through the actual beta step. A pending bind and application frame gets both judgments from the same source annotations; incorrect result metadata is rejected. Operation shape mismatch and missing declarations are rejected, while separate examples show that a shape check alone does not check latent effects or distinguish integer from Boolean atoms.

The remaining work is to maintain authenticated continuation records, complete structural handler/resource admission, and derive whole-program preservation and progress from that admission. Core correspondence remains an assessment, and the later continuation capabilities remain excluded.

Shared owner source contracts

The Owners namespace in CoherentSourceTypes.lean extends the shared expression judgment to one-shot owner consumption. Its Contract retains one input and one answer Value, with owner demands, protection, source effect rows and the ordinary resume/close effect lists. Both OwnerSource.ResumeContract and ScopedPorts.ContinuationContract are projections of this annotation. The existing exact EffectScope connects the lexical binder to that dynamic owner's complete port contract.

Owners.Derives threads the same value annotations and owner phases through pairing, application, binding, branching, requests, resume, discard and synchronous cleanup. Its stable rule reuses Summary. A resume operand must have the shared input annotation; the result has the shared answer annotation. The rule checks the independent resume permission, the owner transition, the ordinary resume-effect allowance and answer well-formedness. Discard checks disposal permission, absence of protection, the closing row and owner trace, and the ordinary close-effect allowance. Its ordinary result is unit. The resource extension adds a general initializer and stable freshly opened body. Handler installation remains outside this judgment.

Structural induction projects a shared derivation to both ordinary port typing and OwnerSource.Derives. The latter projection gives the exact owner transition and absence of repeated owners. Branches with the same initial and final maps consume the same owners up to permutation. Closed substitution retains the shared value annotations, owner endpoints, demands and effect row. Bind and beta reduction preserve the shared judgment; beta restores the existing empty ticket scope for a callable body. The proof also rejects two sequential resumes of the same resolved owner: the first leaves that owner's source phase consumed, and the second requires it to be available.

Owners.Record pairs this annotation with an actual CallableJoint.TicketRecord and equality of its full ordinary continuation contract. This equality includes the two effect lists, as well as input and answer ports. The record projects to the earlier shape-checked record. Registry projection yields exactly the runtime effect registry and registers every source owner. Fresh insertion extends both the shared and runtime registries; structural induction retains the shared source derivation and its ordinary typing. These are agreement and extension results, not a proof that arbitrary declared effect lists describe the saved continuation or its disposal plan.

The examples use an integer-to-Boolean continuation. Shared checking accepts resume with an integer and rejects a Boolean operand. It rejects a resume from an already consumed phase and two sequential resumes. A conditional chooses between resumption and disposal followed by a Boolean result, consuming the owner once on either path. Substituting an integer into a resume operand and inserting a different fresh record retain both analyses. Protected disposal is rejected by shared source checking even though the ordinary port judgment alone admits its unit result. This demonstrates why permission, protection and value typing remain separate checks within the common derivation.

The shared saved-segment construction below now connects annotations through captured segments and constructs the resume component of records at actual captures. Closing-plan authentication and preservation through every transition and receiving context still need integration. Structural handler/resource admission and whole-program preservation/progress remain unfinished. The Core comparison is still an assessment only.

Source reinterpretation at receiving stacks

SourceReinterpretation.lean addresses the changed waiting-handler case. A residual row has already been interpreted by its outside stack. A source request handled there can disappear from that row. Retaining only the result loses information needed when the continuation is restored at a different caller.

Requirements retains each raw request footprint with its owner phase and position relative to the saved stack. It also has concatenation and literal rows for referenced continuation contracts. It is certificate data on the existing direct syntax. evaluate checks requirements through the ordered receiving context. prepend places the appropriate remaining saved frames before that receiver; its evaluation law preserves their order. Failure remains an explicit none, including a protection/permission conflict introduced by the receiver.

Structural induction gives source_rechecks, context_rechecks and frame_rechecks. Each constructs requirements whose evaluation recovers the original row. Successful evaluation at another context constructs a source derivation there, with the same expression, value contract, owner-phase endpoints and consumption demand, and the recomputed row. shared_source_rechecks retains the shared value annotations and ordinary effect allowances as well. None of these results assumes that the old and receiving contexts have equal projections or that their residual rows agree.

segment_rechecks covers every active stack constructor. A pushed frame's requirements retain its remaining saved frames as a nearer interpretation prefix. Live and spent boundaries preserve their checked source contracts and phase premises. This theorem reconstructs the segment's source derivation; it does not recursively authenticate a live boundary's dormant capture from that boundary rule alone. Referenced resume/close rows remain literal annotations, and the original owner-phase maps remain the indices of the reconstruction. Changing those maps or authenticating the referenced records still needs the runtime invariant.

saved_rechecks retains a saved-source certificate at a new receiver when its computed row fits the advertised bound. restore_rechecked uses that result to construct the saved-segment premise of the existing resumption theorem, without the previous equal-projection transport premise. The same value, capture, waiting stack and owner transition then produce the after-source. This bridge still checks the old advertised bound; it is not yet general call-site admission for every valid reinterpretation.

The counterexample distinguishes this remaining limitation from a proof-tactic problem. One handler discharges a request with no outside effects; a different handler exposes a second effect. An empty computation and the original request both have the cached result [] at the first handler, but different results at the second. cached_row_cannot_determine_reinterpretation proves that no function of the cached row alone recovers every changed-context result.
