The current request's recursive requirement check now supplies the selected offer's export: RecursiveDispatch.cut_residual follows the actual handler cut, and the existing caller-export law retains that result at successor phases. Thus a separate selected-offer export is no longer assumed.

The clause connection takes the existing executable checkClosing check of the exact template footprint through the surviving interpretations, against the request and capture rows. DeclaredCallbackAdmission.checked_template supplies successful closing evaluation and coverage. The exact canonical row and stored template identify these with the clause interface's availability and coverage obligations. This reuses the established checker and proofs rather than adding another admissibility predicate. Choosing a canonical evaluation does not prove that the checker succeeds. Initial source admission and preservation must still establish that success, plan typing and the complete resource/name ownership transition.

Examples.ClosingBudget tests whether the newer contextual checks eliminate the earlier closing-budget gap. Its dependency scope realizes the actual frames of ClosingBudgetGap.capture and its surviving caller. Both Retained checking of the pending source and checking of its scheduled closing callbacks succeed. Resumption interprets the callback beneath the inner handler; disposal drops that handler and interprets the callback beneath the surviving outer handler. The existing normal requirement check has an empty row. The finite closing checker rejects that budget and accepts the nonempty closing row as its budget.

SourceDependencyBudgetGap.lean now checks enriched source typing for that same captured segment and its receiving segment, including rich handler declarations and the callback's latent dependency. The owner demand, recursive requirement tree and resume record store agree with the original fixture. An enriched closing template derives the same closing requirements and footprint from the actual callback. Existing row and contextual proofs then retain the empty normal row and nonempty closing row. Thus adding these source derivations does not establish a general open-segment implication from normal checking to closing-budget coverage.

The fixture's contextual judgments use the nonempty outward interface [effect]. closed_guard_rejects checks that its captured shape fails the empty outward closing guard used by the present enriched Run. It is not a reachable closed initial program or a counterexample to that Run invariant. For open composition, the general normal-row bound is false and requires additional budget evidence or a changed judgment. The closed-source connection now follows with the lambda-interface correction described below: the empty outward guard, rich source and captured support construct a typed plan with an empty footprint. The open fixture does not refute that result. Neither result changes normative Ash semantics.

Closing.Contents retains each actual plan callback's rich source and latent dependency annotation. Closing.plan_contents derives it from the captured segment, including dormant captures. Closing.Contents.template fixes its closing requirements in a structural Closing.Template. Template erasure recovers the existing hereditary template at identical indices, and scope transport reuses the existing closing-context equality. Template.source materializes those fixed requirements without choosing another callback typing.

Closing.Bound is a structural judgment over the dependency scope. Each live ticket records its captured annotation in a separate annotation map; dormant captures are checked recursively. This is proof-level source annotation, not a new operational rule or an extra continuation capability. The source scope and stored template refer to the same map entry, so agreement does not depend on uniqueness of rich typings for the same code. Fresh capture records the actual saved annotation while preserving prior entries. Append splitting, closing-plan materialization, resumption and disposal preserve this structural condition.

Closing.Certified relates a rich template to the actual captured stack, stored requirement body and recorded captured annotation. Its template uses exactly that annotation's closing scope. Closing.Records is a finite list of those certificates; it supplements the existing store layout and ownership invariants. selected_template reuses lookup membership and captured-owner uniqueness to select the exact stored template. checked_plan transports its checked row into the waiting caller after consumption, using the existing phase-normalization lemma. Under Bound and the contextual invocation judgment, it also returns the retained-source check for the selected template's exact captured annotation, plus preservation of Bound on the contextually computed disposal result.

Closing.recompose now uses that selected template and checked row for the actual disposal step. It preserves rich source through an arbitrary caller prefix, including continuations that cannot resume. The result retains the template's callback dependency scope, unique remaining tickets, the ownership permutation and one-shot phase trace. Its evaluation equation relates those closing requirements to the original pending requirements after consumption. An original pending-row check yields a check of the recomposed requirements, with the closing and pending rows concatenated, against the retained store at the new owner phases. Existing record splitting and permutation lemmas identify the removed records. Closing-template evaluation is store-independent, while pending work is checked after retirement of captured owners; existing lookup transport therefore justifies removal even when nested retirements are still scheduled. The proof also reuses closing-guard invariance. The new current expression is unit, so the segment accepts an empty incoming effect interface.

The result includes both the existing structural disposal-store layout and the richer certificates for retained records. Records.after_step recovers those certificates using the post-step layout, record inclusion, and the existing capture-origin and capture-uniqueness proofs. It preserves the old template rather than inferring a new annotation from erased source. This helper applies to steps that create no tickets and retain a subset of the old entries.

Closing-plan effect typing and admission into the waiting interface remain explicit premises. The richer record certificates must be established and preserved by the combined source judgment. The annotation map proves agreement of the selected template's captured annotation with the contextual disposal check. The strengthened extraction proof retains the exact waiting-scope decomposition. prefix_owner_cut shows that a caller prefix without the selected ticket cannot intercept lookup; existing ticket uniqueness supplies that absence. The lookup selection and rich reconstructed waiting scope therefore agree. Closing.recompose now returns Bound and contextual retained-source checking for its actual rich result scope, at the actual new owner phases. Carrying the annotation map and these structural conditions in the complete source-state judgment remains necessary. Integration with the resource/name ledger also remains. This theorem does not establish the complete preserved state or initial-source progress.

Closing.capture_records constructs the captured annotation and disposal record from a supplied rich closing template and its actual handler cut. It preserves that exact template, extends Bound with the fresh owner, and retains both the existing store layout and richer record certificates. Template and record transport reuse existing value typing under contract and world extension. The theorem still assumes a constructed plan, internal-use evidence and a contract extension. allocate_capture_source derives the template from its saved source before contract insertion and supplies it with the same scope decomposition, so allocation, closing-row evaluation and record creation share their annotation directly. This avoids a second source decomposition or an annotation-uniqueness assumption. Closing-effect admission and the complete state transition remain open.

A regression case distinguishes the new source rule from the old route guard. The route guard accepts a disposing capture whose surviving handler would cancel its running finalizer; the strengthened source request rejects it. Existing safe-caller examples still pass, as do rejection of consumed owners and the earlier unsafe caller arrangements.

The projection contains fifteen theorem-dependency reports and the schemes contain seventy-four. All earlier source-check examples remain verified after invocation checking was changed to use projected resulting scopes. Full initial-program progress and preservation remain unproved. No Core implementation or normative specification changes follow from these experimental judgments.

Shared enriched source state

The enriched lambda rule now requires every demand in its latent footprint to name an effect in its declared effect interface. The body, outward-row and world checks remain separate. Before this correction, a checked source fixture could declare an empty interface and a nonempty latent row by conservatively advertising that row at an internal resume-only handler. The same body still types; LatentInterface.inconsistent_function_rejected rejects its inconsistent function annotation, while consistent_function_source accepts the nonempty interface. These tests are in SourceDependencyBudgetGap.lean.

The existing environment, world, contract and substitution proofs carry the new premise unchanged. function_latent_bound reuses canonical forms to expose it for any closed function value. function_empty_latent derives an empty latent row from an empty declared interface. This changes the candidate source judgment only; it does not change runtime transitions or current Ash.

Closing.Template.empty_raw extends this connection to complete closing plans. For a plan typed with no outward effects, every callback's declared effects are provided by its retained suffix. The new lambda premise therefore lets the existing callback-residual filter remove every latent demand. Induction over the closing template proves that its raw footprint is empty; Template.closed_budget derives successful finite checking for any receiving context and budget.

closed_capture_budget constructs that plan and an exact rich template from an actual handler cut, the rich source segment, the checked empty-outward request guard, a disposing selected offer and captured support. It reuses the existing cut, plan realization, interface and ownership-accounting proofs through capture_plan; the older capture_certificate now adds its independent owner-use premise to that result. No supplied plan, successful closing check or extra row bound is a premise of closed_capture_budget. The source owner bound below now supplies internal owner use. Admission of future handler declarations remains a separate obligation.

The obstruction to handler admission is now explicit in SourceDependencyHandlerGap.lean. source_declarations admits a handler clause that performs through an outer interpretation before resuming, including the rich source and advertised-row proofs. checked_with_outer checks its exact dependency tree under an installed outer handler. no_uniform_declarations proves that the current DeclarationSchemes certificate cannot certify this declaration, for any outward effect list. Its universal clause premise includes an empty captured continuation and empty receiving stack; those satisfy CaptureSource but cannot supply the clause's operation. This proves a source-admission limitation, not a reachable execution failure or unsoundness of the conditional capture theorem.

The next certificate revision must retain assumptions about the ordered outer interpretations. Adding the existing universal certificate to source handler typing would exclude this composition. The fixture reuses ContextualClauseChecks.open_checked, the existing resume interface and rich declaration constructors for its row proof; these already retain the actual receiving context and can guide the revision.

SourceContextualClauses.lean now defines FamilyAt, ModeAt and DeclarationsAt at an exact receiving scope. The family remains general over owner names, phase maps, resource worlds and admitted saved continuations. Existing uniform schemes embed unchanged. RequestCapability authenticates nearest lookup at that scope; its source-handler constructor currently requires a resume-only offer with both modes present. The request-prefix proof permits arbitrary saved captures and pending suffixes, while retaining the suffix's independent continuation proof. Repeated requests reuse the operation capability. The earlier rejected declaration has a contextual certificate, and absent or shadowed interpretations remain rejected.

selected_checked_body joins that certificate to the exact rich source family selected by the existing declaration theorem. allocate_declared_clause uses the actual cut and the earlier capture-source and retained-forest recomposition proofs to construct the checked fresh clause and retained live source. Its freshness, pre-capture checks and selected-mode premises have the same scope as the earlier allocation lemma. FamilyAt.project_tail transports certificates across equal spent-marker projections without changing owner phases.

These are certificate and capture-preparation lemmas, not shared-runtime preservation or complete source admission. The stored runtime forest still uses uniform certificates. Replacing it requires source handler entry and certificate transport when resumption inserts caller frames. Equality under spent-marker projection does not justify arbitrary caller insertion: a caller's nearer handler can change lookup. The new request-capability constructor also does not yet cover disposing operation prefixes. These obligations remain open; the existing disposal-continuation scheme itself embeds through of_uniform.

The contextual stored component is now defined in SourceContextualForest.lean. Its Forest judgment pairs actual frames with the existing scope-realization relation. Each handler carries DeclarationsAt for its exact annotated suffix and outside scope; each dormant capture retains that receiving scope recursively. Forest.of_uniform embeds the old stored certificates at any correctly realized annotation.

Forest.append reassociates the same ordered suffix. Forest.cut splits an actual handler cut into contextual subforests, returns the selected handler's certificate at the same tail, and proves exact operation lookup for those scopes. Forest.capture retains both forests beneath the new live owner. These structural inductions cover arbitrary nested captures; their depth is not enumerated. The proofs reuse frame realization, scope reassociation and nearest-lookup lemmas and add no ownership or execution rule.

Forest.project_outside transports every stored certificate across equal spent-marker projections. Forest.resume_boundary uses that result and ordered recomposition when resuming at the captured owner's boundary. It does not cover a nonempty caller prefix. A concrete pair of handler frames now has a contextual forest certificate despite the proved impossibility of its old uniform forest certificate. This is a stored-component example, not a reachable full runtime state. Source admission, caller-context transport and integration into SourceDependencyState.State remain separate obligations.

The actual rich source and contextual stored forest are joined in SourceContextualCapture.lean. Forest.cut_aligned uses successful exact selection to identify both scopes returned by their decompositions. It does not assume uniqueness of arbitrary dependency annotations. capture_checked_interfaces then obtains the typed clause and its contextual certificate from the same actual handler and returns the contextual forest for the new live continuation.

The existing allocation proof is factored as SourceDependencySchemes.allocate_capture_source_from_interfaces. It consumes the constructed source interfaces and carries their certificate payload unchanged. Both exported allocation wrappers construct those interfaces from their respective stored forests; this proof helper introduces no new source-admission rule. The contextual wrapper proves the same actual reduction, exact fresh-owner increment and uniqueness, rich payload substitution, closing records and independently checked resume and disposal interfaces. The original uniform wrapper retains its signature and existing runtime callers.

Contextual allocation still takes the established plan, internal-owner use, freshness, source checks and row checks explicitly. The earlier combined runtime proof derives those inputs for its uniform invariant; that connection has not yet been generalized to the contextual forest. General caller transport, source handler admission and complete contextual runtime progress remain open.

The reconstruction mechanism is now explicit in SourceContextualRequirements.lean and SourceContextualRechecking.lean. A structural Recipe retains explicit resume/dispose permissions, silent prefixes, resource binding and local requests, pure cleanup, external and internally handled request prefixes, and choices. DeclarationRecipes binds those recipes to the actual clauses, dependency families and computed continuation rights. Its former uniform constructor and the arbitrary ModeRecipe.of_uniform and DeclarationRecipes.of_uniform bridges have been removed. Primitive compilation reuses resume_family and dispose_family as proved lemmas; neither lemma is stored as an arbitrary source-admission premise. The actual-plan recipe's erasure now maps primitive actions directly to these constructors.

The resume_declarations example constructs both modes structurally; the rechecking and handler-entry examples use that derivation. mixed_consumption retains branch choice between the two independently permitted actions. pure_semantic_family and pure_not_a_consuming_recipe distinguish the old semantic predicate from this consuming source grammar: a pure family can be checked under arbitrary captures, but contains no explicit consumption path. This is an admission-boundary example, not a claim that pure computations are operationally unsafe or excluded from the expression calculus. Older semantic FamilyAt.of_uniform and forest embeddings remain available for their separate proof layer; they do not reconstruct structural declaration recipes.

This removes an opaque constructor from the active contextual recipe path. It does not complete the consuming declaration grammar. General nested handlers, effectful callbacks and their independent continuation interfaces still require source rules. The present request-prefix recipe uses the earlier resume-only, both-mode operation capability; disposing request prefixes still require a further rule.

check_capability_iff connects the executable nearest-lookup test to that exact capability judgment. check_requirements_equiv proves that equivalent membership sets accept the same scopes even when their lists differ in order or repeated occurrences. This concerns requirements only: it neither exchanges handlers in the receiving stack nor duplicates continuation permission. Compilation of a recipe reconstructs FamilyAt or DeclarationsAt at the checked receiving scope.

checkForest checks each actual handler's finite requirements at its annotated suffix and checks dormant captures at their full receiving scopes. recheck_forest constructs the contextual forest from those checks, existing scope realization and the retained declaration recipes. Full-prefix resumption rearranges existing handler occurrences; disposal removes some and schedules cleanup frames without adding installed handlers. The corresponding membership proofs preserve the recipes without treating interpretation order as irrelevant. resume_rechecked and dispose_rechecked then reconstruct certificates at the actual recomposed stack, given successful finite rechecking. A concrete nonempty caller case passes, and incompatible nearest-handler checks fail.

Successful rechecking is still an explicit premise of these component theorems. It is not yet derived from the initial source judgment or the shared runtime invariant. Source admission must retain the recipes and justify the checks at invocation, including handlers later installed by callbacks. These constructions therefore do not yet establish whole-program progress or preservation.

The finite test now also has a source-only interface in SourceContextualHints.lean. Its proof-independent Hints data is indexed by the existing scope; each handler adds an operation requirement list while all other source annotations remain in that index. The module imports only the existing scope realization layer, so source judgments can use these tests without importing clause recipes or runtime safety proofs. The earlier operation checkers are re-exported from this module; their capability correspondence proofs are unchanged.

SourceContextualHintChecking.lean defines Compatible by scope constructors. A handler checks its finite requirements at the rest of the scope followed by the outside scope. A live boundary checks its saved branch at that same receiving suffix and checks its waiting branch separately. check_iff proves that Hints.check decides this judgment; compatible_append_iff gives its exact ordered composition law.

Matches authenticates requirement lists, tables and dependency families against the same actual runtime handlers. It implies the existing Realizes relation, survives append, and makes the source and runtime checks equal. annotate constructs matching annotations for every realized scope; it does not prove their compatibility. With retained declaration recipes, the source checks reconstruct contextual certificates after full-prefix resumption and disposal. These are stored-certificate component theorems, not complete invocation preservation.

The source example admits the existing nonempty caller. A masking caller gives a sharper negative result: checking the current source scope succeeds while checking the resumed scope fails. The saved handler previously received the outer interpretation; resumption puts the masking caller in that path. Thus initial compatibility alone cannot replace the invocation check. Fabricating an empty requirement list also fails authentication. Source rules must still retain the annotations and their recipes for future handler installation and derive the checks required by actual invocations. The shared Local, State and Run judgments have not yet incorporated this annotation layer.

Annotated invocation now selects its source pieces rather than taking them as separately supplied inputs. SourceContextualInvocationHints.lean defines findOwner on Hints; find_owner_erases proves exact agreement with the existing source lookup. It walks the active spine and retains dormant branches without searching them. selected_cut therefore supplies the existing structural OwnerCut for the same boundary. The selected saved, front and tail annotations determine resumption; forClosing transforms the same saved annotation for disposal. The two executable invocation checks reuse the earlier independent access checks and additionally test handler compatibility at their actual resulting scopes.

SourceContextualInvocations.lean defines structural Resume and Dispose judgments. Each retains the annotated lookup, the earlier invocation-access judgment and Compatible at the recomposed scope. Their checker equivalences reuse the old checker equivalences and exact lookup uniqueness. The consumed-owner rejection lemmas reuse the existing one-shot phase rejection. A source example distinguishes compatibility from permission: its restored handlers are compatible but denied resume permission still rejects invocation. A masking caller instead passes access and fails compatibility. Neither check substitutes for the other.

Matches.find_owner authenticates all selected pieces against the same actual runtime continuation. Matches.forClosing reuses the existing realized-plan construction: scheduled frames contain no installed handlers, so their source annotations authenticate without any new declaration requirement. This does not admit handlers that callbacks might install later.

Resume.step and Dispose.step construct actual RawStep successors from these structural invocation judgments and retained handler recipes. Both preserve annotation matching and reconstruct contextual handler certificates. They reuse the existing ownership permutation and phase-trace lemmas: the invoked owner is consumed exactly once, while other owners remain accounted for. Disposal constructs its plan from the selected capture and returns the existing plan-owner accounting. The handler-membership lemma allows the actual saved return scope on the spent marker independently of the current cleanup caller; runtime metadata is preserved by the existing transition.

The nested disposal fixture combines a callback using cell 4, dormant owner 6 and invoked owner 8. It instantiates the actual step theorem, including the contextual certificate and ownership trace. These invocation proofs cover the annotation, stored-handler and ownership components. They do not yet preserve the complete rich source record or derive all invocation judgments from initial program admission. Retaining annotations and recipes throughout source typing, including future handler installation, remains the principal source obligation.

SourceDeclarationPlans.lean now supplies recursive annotation data indexed by the existing dependency syntax. A handler plan retains its actual clause syntax, dependency families and required capabilities. Clause plans retain both offered modes; cleanup plans retain the callback as well as the body. Resource plans retain a family indexed by resource identity. splitHints recovers the exact annotation split at an existing scope append.

SourcePlannedChecks.lean defines structural Local and Pending judgments using these plans. Handler admission requires the same declaration recipe, recursively certified clause plans, a successful requirement check and a checked body under the installed annotation. Pending code and callbacks retain their plans. Invocation admission requires the annotated Resume or Dispose judgment and pending checks at the consumed owner phase. A disposing request requires its closing schedule to check at the exact saved and waiting annotation split; Local.request_schedule extracts that premise.

The mutual erasure theorem reuses the earlier local and pending rules. Projected invocation results agree after projection, since the older checker introduces a fresh spent marker. Local.certified retains declaration recipes throughout the plan; fresh resource bodies extend the world only for fresh identities. CertifiedClauses.selected retains the plans for the actual selected clause and mode. This certifies recursive recipe retention, not full clause admission.

Local.handler_entry supplies the installed contextual certificate from the source handler rule. Local.resume_step and Local.dispose_step reuse the existing actual-step, matching and ownership proofs and retain the strengthened pending check. The examples cover a forwarding handler, that handler in a cleanup callback, and rejection when the required outside interpreter is absent. Full expression and value typing still needs to authenticate these plans against actual code and retain them through substitution and instantiation. Capture must then establish the stronger local judgment for its selected clause. The existing recipe compiler produces the older local judgment and does not establish this connection. The shared State and Run integration remains open.

Literal clause code cannot serve as a stable function-type annotation: value substitution changes that code. SourcePlanSignatures.lean therefore projects an actual plan to a signature containing clause order, required continuation actions, requirement lists and recursive annotations. It omits clause variable names and literal bodies. substitution_signature reuses the existing preservation of requiredActions under value substitution. The examples distinguish changed code with an unchanged signature from a change in required actions, which equality of signatures rejects.

SourcePlanSignatureChecking.lean proves recipes_congr, the three certification congruences and local_congr. These reuse the same structural recipes and invocation checks for any actual plan with the same signature. Pending checks retain their existing witnesses and actual receiving scopes. actual_handler_checked uses the source annotation's actual clauses and transfers the structural handler check to that witness. Signature equality does not identify source programs or excuse checking their actual clause bodies.

SourcePlannedTyping.lean defines annotated values, environments, operations and continuation contracts. Function values retain stable body signatures. Its mutually recursive Annotation, Offer and Declarations judgments check actual source syntax, including both offered modes, latent function bodies, callbacks and fresh resource families. Typed pairs this derivation with the existing hereditary Expression at the same root code, erased environment, result type and dependency tree. The earlier proof retains its complete demand and requirement indices. Typed.erase reuses the existing erasure proof; it does not reconstruct those obligations. lambda_body recovers the actual source body at its declared signature, and handler_declarations recovers the actual clause witness.

SourcePlannedTransport.lean preserves annotations under agreement on free variables, larger resource worlds and extended continuation registries. It follows the existing transport structure and reuses syntax dependency and resource-instantiation bounds. SourcePlannedSubstitution.lean proves closed substitution for annotations and their paired typing judgment. Clause substitution retains stable signatures, including beneath functions and callbacks. The resource case reuses commutation of closed substitution and resource instantiation. Typed.bind_expression and Typed.beta_expression reuse the existing reduction results: owner demand and requirement evaluation remain unchanged, and the resulting source retains the exact body signature. Typed.resource_body reuses the old instantiated source at a fresh identity. The higher-order cleanup example checks successive bind and beta substitutions.

These are source typing and reduction components, not a shared machine-state preservation theorem. Typed pairs the derivations at their roots; their intermediate type choices have not yet been synchronized for machine-frame storage. Capture still must derive the stronger Local judgment for the selected clause, and State/Run must retain the annotated values and source derivations. Existing ownership and closing proofs remain reusable components.

SourcePlannedSources.lean addresses the intermediate type-choice gap with one mutually recursive Expression, Body, Offer and Declarations derivation. Its rules choose refined value types, stable signatures, requirement trees and ownership demands together. Each child uses the same intermediate type selected by its parent. Declaration modes retain their actual clause plans and universally checked fresh-owner bodies. The existing port, usage, coverage, row and resource premises are retained; no constructor accepts a pair of independently chosen complete derivations.

expression_erase projects to the earlier dependency-annotated source judgment without changing its requirement or owner indices. expression_annotation projects to the stable annotation judgment. Expression.paired derives the earlier root pair from these projections, rather than using that pair to construct the stronger derivation. refine_contract_erase reuses all fields of an existing contract at the selected refined input and answer types. handler_body recovers the actual full body and declaration derivations and their exact signature and requirement equations.

SourcePlannedContexts.lean defines synchronized evaluation contexts. context_erase preserves the selected intermediate types; Context.plain_frame supplies the earlier frame certificate for the same actual input/output metadata. focus_decompose follows every existing Focus rule, retaining a stronger child derivation and context with matching input type. Existing value-demand and requirement-evaluation lemmas supply its accounting. focus_step reuses prepare_plain to construct the actual frame and RawStep; the retained context, old frame certificate and child typing refer to those same choices. Focusing adds no owner, so the existing empty phase trace applies. This theorem does not yet transport the strengthened Local check.

SourcePlannedSourceTransport.lean retains the stronger derivation under environment agreement, larger resource worlds, extended continuation registries and larger allowed-effect interfaces. Its proofs follow the earlier transport structure and reuse dependency, port, resource-support and registry lemmas. SourcePlannedSourceSubstitution.lean preserves the stronger derivation under closed substitution, including both declaration modes and fresh resource bodies. It reuses the earlier clause usage, port-substitution and instantiation results. Stable signature preservation retargets each substituted actual clause witness. Value summarization and its legacy projection reuse existing proved results.

SourcePlannedSourceReduction.lean uses this stronger substitution theorem for bind and beta reduction. Successors retain the full synchronized derivation and exact body signature. Existing value-demand, outward-row and evaluation laws prove unchanged ownership demand and requirement evaluation. context_plug constructs the synchronized recomposed expression using the same context input type. actual_handler_checked connects the full source body and declarations to the local check at their actual clause witness. bind_checked and beta_checked retain that stronger local check at the same receiving scope and owner phase. The cleanup/function/bind examples verify two successive substitutions with full synchronized successors.

The intermediate type agreement now has structural source and ordinary-frame evidence. The shared runtime invariant still needs to retain it in every frame and continuation record. The stronger clause check at capture and the combined execution induction remain open.

SourcePlannedRecomposition.lean supplies the stronger pending-stack split/join theorem. It reuses scope associativity and retains the exact plan witnesses under ordinary, cleanup and dormant frames. pending_capture packages an already checked split under a live boundary at unchanged phases; it does not prove fresh allocation or phase transport. Installed-handler compatibility through spent markers reuses operation-selection projection. Closing removes installed handlers, but callback source checks stay separate from that compatibility result.

resume_clause and dispose_clause construct head invocation checks from the saved and waiting source pieces checked at the spent owner phase. They derive the combined successor check by composition and reuse the independent access, permission, availability, protection and closing-route judgments. request_prefix reuses the existing builtin or resume-only operation capability; it does not consume that capability or grant disposal. In the existing nested disposal fixture, callback_source authenticates the complete callback at the retained plan signature, including its bind and operand evaluation. This refines the older fixture's request-only dependency annotation; stack matching alone does not authenticate a callback body. nested_closing_pending checks that complete plan under the scheduled scope. nested_disposal_source_step retains that check through the actual runtime step and reuses the owner permutation, phase trace and nested retirement-plan accounting. These results do not yet derive the piece checks from arbitrary source captures or compile every retained declaration recipe to the stronger judgment.

SourceNeutralScopes.lean supplies structural transports for inserting plain frames whose pending dependency is pure, spent-history markers, or armed pure callbacks with no effect requirements. Inserting a history marker does not itself change the independently checked owner phases. The right-pair focus case needs plain-frame transport: its child was checked at the waiting scope, while evaluation adds the frame that retains the left value. Expansion inserts only along the active spine and preserves every existing dependency, handler requirement and dormant program. Prefix and append composition retain this relation. Protection, normal and closing interpretation contexts, closing checks, source-owner lists and pending owner bounds are preserved. Closing annotations are related by Expansion.forClosing: new callbacks remain in the closing schedule, so equality of those annotations is not assumed.

find_owner retains the exact saved continuation and relates its caller and waiting suffix. OwnerExpansion.resumed and disposed reconstruct the corresponding expansions of the invocation results. Operation capabilities and installed-handler compatibility are unchanged. SourcePlannedNeutralFrames.lean uses those observations in Expansion.resume and dispose to reuse the independent invocation rules with the same permissions, phase and captured closing route.

SourcePlannedCuts.lean reconstructs a structural annotated cut from the existing nearest-handler lookup. It retains the exact handler table, modes, requirement lists and dormant branches. Its reconstruction and split-uniqueness proofs identify the actual saved and waiting hints; expand preserves their cut through pure-frame, pure-callback and history insertion. Builtin selection is also preserved. No second lookup algorithm is introduced.

SourcePlannedNeutralChecks.lean uses the cut to rebuild a request check. The captured closing annotation and its receiving scope both expand structurally; recursively transported checks cover the new callbacks and retain the existing ones. Existing guard and owner-bound results supply the legacy projection. The mutual Local/Pending induction covers every constructor; a nested induction on target hints handles additional pure frames, pure callbacks and history markers without assuming a checked successor. Public local, outside-pending and full pending transports retain the same plans, permissions, phases and world.

SourceProviderInsertion.lean proves the primitive checking properties for adding a builtin resource scope. Its Insertion judgment inserts exactly one cell along the active spine and keeps dormant saved branches fixed. Normal and closing projections both gain that cell. ContextInsertion.route transforms a matching exported route into a local builtin route; both sides of an existing route agreement use the same transformation. closing_contexts and Insertion.closing_checked then reuse the recursive closing judgment, including callbacks in dormant captures. These are preservation implications, not equalities of interpretations.

Insertion.cut identifies the two possible request outcomes: the new builtin is selected, or the same source handler and mode table remain selected. In the latter case, Split records whether the captured segment or the waiting tail gained the cell. The capture guard, finite operation requirements and installed handler requirements remain checked. Owner lookup retains the same dormant program, permissions and phase; the resumed and disposed results retain the cell in their corresponding caller or waiting scope. This establishes independent access, not the full pending-source check after invocation.

The examples prove that builtin insertion can change handler selection and can turn exported routes into local routes. They also reuse the existing newly-visible-cell counterexample to reject insertion into a dormant saved branch. No new resource-support premise is needed for these primitive checks. Actual resource allocation still uses the existing runtime freshness and ownership proofs; these checking lemmas do not replace them.

SourceDependencyProviders.lean now transports the full lower Local and Pending judgments. Its mutual induction tracks exactly one inserted cell on either side of a pending schedule. Requests retain the same handler cut and transport its closing schedule, or select a builtin and have no source-handler closing schedule. Resume and disposal reuse the independent access lemmas and recursively check the projected recomposition. The owner bound is preserved using the existing pending-owner theorem. A saved branch remains fixed and is rechecked when its receiving outside gains the provider.

SourcePlannedProviders.lean uses that result for erased checks while retaining the actual declaration plan. It also transports invocation compatibility and installed-handler requirements. The request proof identifies the uniquely selected annotated pieces before transporting their schedule; it does not assert equality of handler lookup.

SourceScheduledProviders.lean lifts insertion to the actual retained Forest. It reuses the existing handler and owner cuts, retains each pending expression and callback plan, and keeps the selected owner's dormant forest identical. A split records insertion in the captured or waiting segment. For invocation it records insertion in the caller or waiting segment, and recomposition retains that provider past the spent-owner marker.

SourceScheduledProviderChecks.lean transports the full scheduled Local and Pending judgments through those pieces. It reuses the existing owner-cut authentication and invocation alignment lemmas. Handler requirements are preserved at the actual receiving suffix, including in saved branches. The permissions, phases and world stay fixed during insertion; resource-world extension remains the existing separate judgment. This completes retained-check transport for active builtin insertion. The resource recipe rules below now reuse this result.

The provider examples include a local resource body that requests its own newly acquired provider before resuming. The new operation is not required from the original waiting tail. Other cases check interpreter preemption within resumed source, a disposing request that captures an armed callback, and disposal with an effectful saved callback. These local checks do not establish complete initial admission. The consuming resource declaration rule is now integrated as follows.

Both contextual recipes and actual-plan recipes carry an explicit list of locally available resource identities. The existing declaration interface uses the empty list. A resource rule checks its body with the bound identity added; localRequest requires membership in that list and contributes no outer operation requirement. Existing external request rules retain their finite requirements. Resource capabilities may be used repeatedly, while resume and dispose still check the independent one-shot permission and phase.

providerScope, providerHints and providerForest interpret that annotation as the ordered caller prefix at the three checking layers. Their transport lemmas reuse the proved single-provider insertion. Compilation proceeds by induction on the recipe, not by enumeration of captured continuations. The resource case extends the world of the retained source using existing weakening laws, then compiles its body under the actual new cell. The operation is thus supplied locally, rather than falsely required from the original waiting tail. Neither the contextual nor the actual-plan recipe judgment has a uniform whole-success constructor.

Erasure, certification and signature transport cover both new rules. Signature transport decomposes resource-body signatures for every bound identity; it does not assume literal equality of plans. Scheduled compilation retains the same actual saved and waiting forests. Existing declaration selection and capture then derive the body check without an additional resource-body check at the call site.

The ResourceRecipes examples in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean check a source clause that acquires a cell, requests its operation and disposes its continuation with no outer operation requirements. They derive the selected body at capture, retain the declaration after payload substitution, admit two nested resources with repeated local requests followed by one resume, and reject a local request without an enclosing provider. These are declaration and selected-capture checks, not a complete initial runtime fixture. Handler and effectful-cleanup declaration rules, complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation remain open.

Exact handler interference during closing

SourceHandlerInterference.lean characterizes one handler inserted in the original context of a closing computation. Its surviving context is unchanged: the inserted handler is removed on closing. route_insert_iff proves that an existing route retains its exact target if and only if its requested effect differs from the inserted effect or a builtin in the preceding context already supplies it. The theorem concerns the existing Route judgment; a matching source handler cannot supply a closing route.

Shielded is a structural judgment over the finite Shape. At a cleanup node, it checks whether a callback requesting the inserted effect has a builtin in its original receiving suffix. At a live node, it checks both the dormant saved shape and the waiting shape; the saved branch includes the waiting shape's normal interpretation context. Other constructors recurse. No future execution or whole-body success is a premise.

closing_insert_iff proves an exact equivalence: closing after insertion holds precisely when closing before insertion and these shielding obligations both hold. check_sound and check_complete connect a finite Boolean checker to the structural judgment. In SourceDependencyCapture.lean, check_closing_handler_insert factors the existing executable closing checker into its old result and the new check. This is an equality for all inputs; the specialization for an accepted old check needs only the shielding result.

exposed summarizes the same obligations as a finite effect list. Each callback contributes requirements not supplied by builtins in its own original suffix. Dormant captures contribute their summary after accounting for their receiving suffix. check_summary says that every occurrence of the inserted effect in this summary must be supplied by the context before the insertion. Only membership matters, so duplicate effects require no usage count. The ordered original shape remains necessary for computing the summary and for the pre-existing closing judgment.

exposed_bound proves that existing closing evidence bounds the summary by the original context's builtins and the outward closing-effect row. captured_row_separation therefore derives handler noninterference for a closed capture when the inserted effect is absent from its existing row. This is a sufficient declaration-level check, not a restriction imposed on general admission. The exact checker also admits overlapping effects when an existing builtin shields them.

realized_interfaces reuses Realizes.interfaces and Realizes.owner_accounting for the same stack and generated plan. It supplies typed closing, the operational closing interface and exact owner accounting; ordinary support and typing remain independent premises. Examples accept both active and dormant callbacks shielded by a receiving cell, and reject exposed callbacks in both positions.

This result discharges the closing-interference prerequisite for the represented insertion. It does not transport operation-table selection, protected clause capabilities, or the full retained Local/Pending source judgments through a handler. General handler-bearing consuming recipes still need those rules. Effectful-cleanup recipes, complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation also remain open.

Finite operation requirements at handler insertion

SourceHandlerRequirements.lean derives an exact interface for the existing installed-handler requirement checks. reaches follows a scope's active interpretation spine. A matching handler or builtin stops lookup; an incomplete matching handler still stops it. Dormant saved branches are excluded from this lookup path. capability_append proves that a prefix either supplies the existing operation capability or passes the request to its outside scope. It retains the selected table's ordinary and protected mode checks and does not assert identity of handler behavior.

outwardRequirements filters a finite list of operation requirements using that traversal. exposed computes the outside interface of actual Hints: each installed handler contributes requirements that pass its waiting suffix, and each dormant capture contributes exposed requirements that pass its receiving suffix. The construction does not inspect or replace clause bodies. exposed_requirements derives this interface from the existing recursive checker. check_transport reconstructs that checker at a replacement outside scope from the old check and the new interface. check_replace_iff combines the two directions: given established internal checks, the finite exposed interface exactly characterizes an acceptable replacement outside scope.

check_handler_insert specializes this result to a handler inserted after any preceding receiving scope. It filters exposed requests again by that scope, then by the inserted effect. The inserted table must supply precisely these intercepted operation capabilities. Other operation requirements retain their previous evidence. These capabilities retain the current requirement discipline: a provider must be resumptive and offer both ordinary and protected modes. This theorem does not impose that discipline on every handler in the calculus; it decides the requirements represented by the existing checker.

SourceContextualHintChecking.lean connects both replacement and handler insertion to its independently defined structural Compatible judgment and the existing RequestCapability constructors. SourceProviderInsertion.lean now specializes the general interface transport, replacing its former separate induction for retained outside requirements.

Examples accept an overriding handler supplying the required capability, reject missing operations, reject missing protected modes and disposal where a resumptive capability is required, and retain dormant requirements. A nearer active builtin shields its operation, while a dormant builtin does not. Another negative case has an empty exposed interface but invalid internal lookup at an incomplete handler; this demonstrates why the established internal-check premise cannot be omitted. These are finite requirement-checking examples, not complete initially admitted source programs.

The closing-interference and installed-handler requirement prerequisites now have exact finite checks. Full Local/Pending transport must still track the actual selected clause, capture and continuation checks through changed interpretations. General handler-bearing consuming recipes remain open, as do effectful-cleanup recipes, complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation.

Exact selection and capture pieces at handler insertion

SourceHandlerSelection.lean retains the capture information omitted by the operation-capability interface. select_append proves an exact equation for the existing select algorithm. If lookup passes the preceding scope, an outside handler's selected capture gains that entire scope. If lookup stops inside it, the selected capture remains fixed and its waiting scope gains the appended outside. Builtin results remain builtin results. An internal missing operation remains failure, because a matching incomplete handler stops lookup.

The insertion corollaries identify three cases. inserted_selected gives the new matching handler's exact capture and waiting scope from its operation and dependency-family lookup. inserted_bypassed keeps an outer handler's contract and modes while adding the inserted handler to its captured prefix. inserted_after_selection keeps an inner handler's capture, contract and modes while adding the inserted handler to its waiting suffix. inserted_missing proves that either a missing operation or a missing dependency family blocks an exposed matching request.

inserted_cut, bypassed_cut and inside_cut reuse SourcePlannedCuts.of_lookup to authenticate these pieces against the actual whole Hints. They introduce no second cut algorithm or replacement handler annotations. Existing cut uniqueness remains available to identify the same pieces in subsequent recomposition proofs.

guard_same_capture and inside_guard_transport preserve the independent local capture guard when the capture, contract and mode families stay fixed and only the waiting scope changes. This does not preserve code retained in that waiting scope. In SourceContextualRequirements.lean, capability_prefix reuses exact outside selection to transport the existing operation capability through any prefix that passes its effect. The previous sequencing and live-owner capability proofs now specialize this result.

Examples retain a plain frame and a recursively saved cleanup/resource scope while checking interception, outer-capture extension and inner-waiting extension. They distinguish active builtin blockers from dormant providers and reject missing operations at both the inserted and preceding handler. The existing running-completion counterexample is reused to show successful selection of a disposing handler together with rejection by the capture guard. Selection and continuation permission remain independent judgments.

These results establish the selection transformations needed by general handler insertion. The connection to closing interference follows below. Full Local/Pending transport must still combine these results with installed-handler requirements, continuation invocation and source typing. General handler-bearing consuming recipes, effectful-cleanup recipes, complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation remain open.

Closing checks on selected captured scopes

SourceHandlerClosingInsertion.lean connects the original-context interference theorem to an insertion inside an actual captured source scope. normal_append and closing_append project source-scope composition into its interpretation contexts. closing_append_iff splits the recursive closing judgment into the prefix checked at those tail contexts and the tail checked at the original outside. Dormant saved branches remain in place and retain their full receiving suffix.

inserted_closing_iff then reuses the previous exact interference theorem. Closing after a handler is inserted between a prefix and a tail holds exactly when closing held before insertion and the prefix satisfies Shielded for the inserted effect. The tail's own callbacks are unaffected. The theorem allows arbitrary original and surviving outside contexts. check_closing_inserted proves the corresponding equality for the existing Boolean checker: its old result is conjoined with the finite prefix check.

inserted_held shows that insertion does not change physical protection. bypassed_guard_transport combines this result, the exact outer-selection law and the closing equivalence. The selected contract and modes remain the same. Its local capture guard is preserved if its disposing mode implies that the prefix passes the interference check. No such closing premise is required for a non-disposing mode, and no whole-source successor check is assumed.

Examples accept a disposing capture whose callback is shielded by a builtin before the new handler, and reject an exposed callback that the new handler would intercept. The latter inserted handler is complete and resumptive: operation availability alone is insufficient. These are checks of actual source capture guards. The full request connection for this insertion case follows below; general pending-source transport remains open.

Source request transport with an unchanged closing schedule

SourceHandlerRequests.lean proves the full lower source request case when a different-effect inserted handler becomes part of an already selected outer handler's capture. forClosing_inserted shows that the inserted frame is removed and leaves the same closing source schedule. owners_inserted preserves the recursive live-owner inventory, and pending_owners_inserted transports the existing structural owner bound.

bypassed_request reuses the exact selection and conditional guard theorem, then fills every field of Local.request_selected. The scheduled-source field uses the old schedule by equality; the owner-bound field uses structural transport and equality of owner inventories. The only additional condition is the finite prefix-interference check when the selected contract permits disposal. The theorem does not assume a checked replacement schedule. checked_bypassed_request connects this result to the source checker used by the stronger layers. It reuses the existing spent-marker projection and proves that projection preserves lookup reachability and the interference check.

SourceScheduledHandlerRequests.lean retains the actual plan-carrying forests. It proves that removing the inserted handler during closing produces the same hints and forest, including every callback plan and dormant branch. cut_prefix lifts an authenticated existing cut through an effect-passing prefix. The stronger bypassed_request identifies the actual post-insertion pieces with existing cut and forest uniqueness, then reuses the old scheduled Pending proof through the closing equality. Existing generic congruence lemmas are made public and reused without changing their proofs.

The handler_inside_disposing_capture example in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean derives the new request from the existing disposing-cleanup example. It retains its armed callback without constructing another schedule proof. handler_preempts_builtin_request uses the existing resumptive capability rule and generalized capability-prefix proof for a new handler beneath a pending sequencing frame. These are local source-checker examples, not full initially admitted executions.

This completes the represented request-transport case through the scheduled source layer. It does not yet provide the mutual Local/Pending theorem for arbitrary insertion. Insertion in the waiting scope, recursive continuation invocation, and a newly selected disposing handler require their corresponding source obligations. General handler-clause recipes and the other admission and finite-run obligations remain open.

Continuation invocation under handler insertion

SourceInterpretationInsertion.lean generalizes the existing provider insertion proof to two interpretation frames: a builtin cell and a source handler. Insertion.find_owner retains the same active owner and dormant saved hints. OwnerInsertion records insertion in either its caller prefix or waiting suffix. Its resumed and disposed theorems follow the existing recomposition, including the spent-owner marker and running-completion boundary. Independent access retains the same ticket permission and phase. Disposal also retains the selected saved scope's protection and closing checks. The provider module reuses these proofs through structural conversions; its public relation and operation-selection proofs remain unchanged.

SourceHandlerInvocations.lean keeps the separate installed-handler compatibility obligation explicit. check_inserted proves an exact characterization at a given prefix and suffix, assuming the original compatibility. The two conditions are:

  • The new handler's declared operation requirements are supplied by its waiting scope and outside context.
  • Its table supplies the matching operations in the preceding prefix's finite exposed requirement list.

Interface is a structural version for insertion anywhere on the active spine. At the insertion it checks the new declaration's list. At an existing handler it checks that handler's requirement list in the changed receiving scope. At a dormant branch it checks its finite exposed list in that scope. Other frames recurse. Interface.check proves sufficiency using the original compatibility; interface_of_check proves necessity for the actual insertion. No constructor asks for Local, Pending, an execution invariant or a proof that the replacement whole program succeeds.

resume_selected and dispose_selected combine the existing owner access with this finite interface on the actual recomposed hints. resume_admitted and dispose_admitted reuse an existing contextual admission. Examples cover insertion in caller and waiting scopes, nested disposal with a retained callback and owner, a masking handler that preserves independent access but invalidates resumption compatibility, and rejection of an already spent owner. These examples prove contextual invocation admission, not initial-program admission or pending-source preservation.

SourceScheduledInterpretationInsertion.lean generalizes the existing scheduled-provider owner-cut proof. Its insertion relation retains every actual plan and saved branch. Insertion.owner_cut returns the existing authenticated cut with the identical saved forest and a changed caller or waiting piece. Split.resumed and Split.disposed carry that same forest through recomposition. Split.owner connects those plan-carrying pieces to the shared source selection. The scheduled-provider module reuses this result rather than keeping a second owner-cut induction.

The results above provide exact pieces and independent finite compatibility checks. The retained-site theorem below now handles pending traversal through changed scopes, conditional on transport of affected local checks. It does not establish the full mutual theorem. General handler-bearing and effectful-cleanup recipes, complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation remain open.

Retained code sites and handler transport

SourceScheduledPendingSites.lean separates the recursive pending traversal from local operation and invocation checks. Site selects an actual stored plan and its receiving forest. A sequencing frame checks its plan at the suffix; a callback receives an additional running frame; a dormant continuation receives its complete original waiting suffix. No source or runtime plan is replaced by an existential substitute.

Site.checked extracts an existing subderivation. pending_iff proves that a pending check is exactly finite installed-handler compatibility together with local checks at every retained site. It reuses Pending.compatible for the forward interface and reconstructs the existing structural constructors for the reverse direction. This is a decomposition of the current judgment, not a new accepted recipe or a presumed whole-program safety property.

Site.outside and Site.inside track insertion through these positions. A site keeps its identical plan and either its identical receiving forest or that forest with the same interpretation inserted. New interpretation frames create no retained code sites. Site.transport combines inside and outside insertion. The proof handles live saved branches and callbacks structurally, without limiting nesting depth or requiring those plans to be pure.

pending_transport reuses unaffected checks and applies a local proof transformer at affected sites. pending_outside derives compatibility from the old forest's finite exposed operation list; pending_handler_inside uses the exact finite Interface established above. The transformer is an explicit proof obligation for the remaining local transport theorem. It is not stored in syntax, accepted by a declaration rule, or replaced by a target Pending assumption. Both provider pending-transport theorems now instantiate this shared traversal with their already proved local transformer.

The waiting-side request helper in SourceScheduledHandlerRequests.lean uses the same machinery. replace_waiting retains an authenticated captured prefix with another waiting forest. request_same_capture preserves the original independent guard and owner bound; erasure of the actual transported schedule supplies the lower checker. waiting_request reconstructs that schedule from the old request, the finite exposed-operation check and the local site transformer. It covers either builtin or handler insertion in the waiting piece. The concrete handler_in_disposal_waiting example reuses the original captured pure callback and supplies no replacement schedule.

SourceScheduledHandlerInvocations.lean closes the corresponding scheduled resume and disposal cases relative to the same local transport obligation. Existing invocation decomposition supplies the original pending checks; shared owner splits supply exact recomposition; the finite handler interface supplies contextual compatibility. Affected code is transported at the spent-owner phase. The examples handler_resume and handler_dispose retain an armed pure callback. They now use the structural adaptation compiler below to discharge those recursive obligations.

This factors the pending traversal and supplies the waiting-request and invocation induction cases. It does not close the full mutual source-transport proof. The next section gives a structural prefix rule for newly selected disposing handlers; operation availability alone remains insufficient. General clause admission must establish those prefix judgments and discharge the finite checks and recursive local obligations before it can use these helpers. The four overall admission and preservation obligations remain open.

Newly selected disposing handlers

A previously builtin or resumptive request need not carry a disposal schedule. The fresh selection therefore needs additional source information. Existing counterexamples in SourceDependencyChecks.lean and SourceDependencyOwners.lean already separate the capture guard from ownership: effect_guard_accepts_outside_owner holds, but source_request_rejects_outside_owner rejects pending invocation of a continuation absent from the capture. The new rules retain that distinction.

SourceScheduledClosingCallbacks.lean introduces the structural Callbacks judgment on the original retained forest. Plain computations, installed handlers and spent markers recurse without adding closing work. Resource and running frames preserve their position. An armed cleanup checks its actual callback plan under running protection with the closing suffix. A live capture checks its saved callbacks before the closing tail, using the same running boundary as Forest.forClosing. No constructor requires a checked replacement schedule.

Callbacks.schedule builds that schedule by structural induction and the existing ordered pending-append theorem. callbacks_of_schedule proves the converse. callbacks_iff_sites reuses the retained-site decomposition: closing contains no installed-handler requirements, so exactly the local callback-code checks remain. These callback plans are actual stored source, and their local judgments retain the existing operation, invocation and nested-source rules.

SourceScheduledFreshRequests.lean combines three independent parts at the authenticated selected cut:

  • The existing structural capture guard checks selected contract, mode, protection and closing routes.
  • PendingWithin checks captured pending code against recursively captured owners, reusing the existing syntax-directed invocation-membership rules.
  • Callbacks checks the actual retained callbacks at their closing positions.

request_from_callbacks compiles these into the full scheduled request rule. The generated schedule supplies the lower source checker by erasure. Owner projection reuses the existing pending_owners_project proof, now exported without changing its body. Existing cut and forest uniqueness authenticate the schedule against every selected witness.

For a selected disposing contract, disposing_request_iff proves necessity and sufficiency of all three parts. Thus the rule does not accept a request merely because an operation exists, and it imposes no extra blanket exclusion of overlapping effects. installed_request authenticates a new handler's capture through the existing prefix-cut theorem, without an old request proof.

callbacks_at_handler reuses the proved equality of actual closing forests: adding the selected handler at the end of the prefix adds no callback. installed_request_from_prefix uses this equality and the existing structural owner-insertion theorem to derive the captured obligations from checks of the preceding prefix. The handler adds neither owners nor closing callbacks.

The FreshDisposal examples in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean first check a builtin request, then introduce a disposer for the same effect. Its capture contains a pending resume of owner 19, that live owner, an effectful cleanup and builtin resource 7. The owner bound follows by membership in the actual captured inventory. The callback's request reaches resource 7 at its closing position. Both checks are constructed from the prefix; no original disposal schedule or target Pending certificate is passed.

This establishes the fresh-disposal request rule at the structural-judgment level. It does not yet derive its prefix judgments for arbitrary declaration recipes. Closing the mutual handler proof, integrating general handlers and effectful cleanup into clause admission, and proving complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation remain required. These are local source examples, not a claim of complete admitted executions or Core correspondence.

Exhaustive request transport under handler insertion

SourceScheduledHandlerSelection.lean proves cut_origin by induction on the structural insertion and the actual selected cut. Every target selection has one of three origins:

  • The new handler intercepts the request through an effect-passing prefix.
  • The original selected handler remains, with the insertion inside its capture.
  • The original selected handler remains, with the insertion in its waiting suffix.

The latter two cases retain the original contract and mode families. The Intercept judgment records the first case structurally. Its cut projection reuses the existing authenticated selection judgment; entry identifies the inserted table's operation and modes. prefix extracts the exact preceding forest, its hints, and its original waiting suffix. Dormant saved branches are retained, not searched for an operation. A missing operation yields no selected cut and cannot enter this classification as a successful request.

SourceScheduledHandlerTransport.lean assembles the request proof. handler_context recovers the exact prefix and suffix of an arbitrary insertion. closing_same and owners_preserved then reuse the existing prefix-based equality and owner-bound proofs. In particular, an insertion inside a capture does not change any actual closing callback or its order, and does not add or remove a continuation owner.

closing_transport handles both retained-selection cases. An insertion in the capture reuses the original closing schedule through equality. An insertion in the waiting suffix reuses pending_transport and the existing closing_check: closing has no installed-handler requirements, so no additional finite handler-compatibility premise is needed there. Each affected callback still requires its local source check at the changed receiving suffix.

request_transport combines this with exact selection. Its inputs are the old request check, structural insertion, an independent target capture guard, fresh interceptions' structural owner and callback checks, and the recursive local transformer for affected old callback sites. Builtins use the existing capability theorem. Fresh handlers use request_from_callbacks; retained handlers obtain their owner bound and closing schedule from the original request. No replacement Pending or target request proof is supplied.

The examples in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean now use this theorem for insertion inside a disposing capture and insertion in its waiting suffix. FreshDisposal.transported_disposing_request also uses it when a new disposer takes over a builtin request. Its pending resume, live owner, retained resource and effectful callback receive explicit structural checks; the earlier target request theorem is not used as an input.

This closes the request-case assembly relative to those source checks and the recursive callback transformer. The following structural judgment discharges recursion by mutual induction when its constructor-level evidence is supplied. Uniform derivation from general clause admission remains open.

Structural source adaptation and mutual compilation

SourceScheduledHandlerAdaptation.lean replaces the recursive proof-transformer parameter with two mutually inductive source judgments. Adapt relates checks of the same actual plan at two receiving forests. Retained describes adaptation of actual stored code and callbacks, with both receiving suffixes explicit. Context changes are still established separately by Insertion, Split and authenticated cuts; an adaptation derivation is source-checking evidence, not a runtime transition.

The local rules follow the plan constructors:

  • Identical contexts reuse their existing check. Pure code and directly supplied operation capabilities use the existing primitive rules.
  • Fresh request checking supplies the structural capture guard, pending-owner bound and actual callback checks. Retained requests instead carry an inductive adaptation of the old closing forest and waiting suffix, conditional on disposal permission. Their exact cuts and split reuse the old owner proof.
  • Resume and disposal retain the selected owner, saved forest and independent permission checks. Their recursive Retained premise describes the actual recomposition at the spent-owner phase, including the running boundary for disposal.
  • Sequence retains the second plan as the first plan's pending frame. Choice checks each arm. Handler entry preserves the actual declaration plans and checks their finite requirements at the new suffix. Cleanup checks body and callback separately. Resource entry quantifies over the existing fresh activation rule and extends the resource world.

The retained rules walk every frame. Plain frames adapt their actual stored plan at the changed suffix; cleanup adapts its callback under running protection. Live frames recursively check their saved forest against its complete receiving suffix and check the tail. Handler insertion checks only its finite requirements and reuses the original retained source. Existing handlers retain their declarations and recheck their requirements at the new suffix. Cells, running markers and spent history preserve their structure.

sound_all proves both compilation results together by induction on these judgments. Adapt.sound takes the original local check and constructs the new one. Retained.sound does the same for pending source. There is no assumed function from an old callback check to a new check, and no whole target Local/Pending or successful runtime successor is an annotation field. Fresh requests still check actual callback source through the previously established structural Callbacks judgment.

The invocation rules do not require a separate finite compatibility certificate. Their recursively compiled pending check supplies compatibility; the existing interface_of_check theorem extracts the handler interface along the actual recomposition insertion. Existing resume_admitted and dispose_admitted then transport access. Thus permission and phase remain independent checks, while the source traversal establishes the interpretation requirements. Retained.owners_preserved proves equality of the retained owner lists, including order and multiplicity. It does not count the separately indexed outside scope as captured ownership.

The examples in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean include the earlier resume/dispose cases, a waiting request, and a nested resume-19/dispose-23 derivation with an effectful callback using resource 7. The nested derivation traverses a stored invocation and its closing callback, with both owner phases updated. shadowing_adaptation_rejected reuses the existing missing-operation counterexample: the new judgment cannot justify resumption through that shadowing handler.

This establishes mutual compilation for explicit structural adaptations. General consuming declaration recipes still need rules that produce these derivations for their actual captures and context changes. The adaptation theorem alone does not extend declaration admission. The bounded internally handled prefix rule below extends the recipe grammar; complete initial admission remains open. In particular, this module depends on the scheduled checker, whose handler constructor already uses recipe declarations; it cannot simply be imported back into the earlier recipe definition. Integration must expose the required structural annotations at the declaration boundary without replacing them with an opaque whole-body success premise. General handler and effectful-cleanup recipes, complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation remain open.

Source contexts before declaration checking

SourceRetainedPlanData.lean exposes the existing retained forest, append, closing construction and append injectivity before recipe checking. SourcePlanRequirementSites.lean exposes the existing primitive requirements, actual source sites and selected clause plans at that same earlier boundary. Their namespaces and definitions are preserved. This data layer imports neither contextual recipes nor the planned or scheduled checker; interpreting its requirements remains in SourceScheduledRequirements.lean.

Site.context derives a structural caller context from source traversal. Sequence adds the actual pending plan; handler, resource and cleanup entry add their corresponding frames; callback traversal adds running protection. Context.trans composes these traversals. Context.owners preserves the exact owner list, including order and multiplicity: lexical entry does not allocate a continuation owner. Context.owner_cut then transports an authenticated owner cut through that context, retaining the identical saved forest and waiting suffix. The existing Site.owner_cut theorem now reuses this result.

These contexts include bodies whose operations become available only after handler entry. In SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean, LocallyHandledClause.request_site locates such an operation beneath its actual new interpreter. prefix_checked proves a local composition for any effect, resource world, permission map, owner phase map, receiving forest and checked remainder: install the single-operation disposer, perform its operation, then continue with that remainder.
