Only the new handler boundary is captured; the pending remainder remains outside. The proof reuses request_from_callbacks and the existing declaration recipe for disposal.

followed_by_outer_resume instantiates that rule with an outer continuation. body_before_installation_rejected proves that the same operation body fails checking without its new interpreter. Thus adaptation of an already checked body cannot be the only rule for admitting general handlers. These are local source checks, not a complete execution or admission theorem. The earlier data layer permits declaration rules to refer to actual sites without an import cycle; deriving their capture obligations and compiling general consuming recipes remain outstanding.

Source-local requirement templates

A source-local requirement template is an existing Site derivation whose initial receiving forest is empty. Its resulting forest contains the caller frames contributed by that source position. It does not contain the actual saved continuation or waiting tail. The existing Site.context and Context.owners results establish that this caller forest has no live owners. Resource templates retain the fresh-identity premise and extended world; they are parameterized source derivations, not an enumeration of runtime identities.

Site.append in SourcePlanRequirementSites.lean instantiates such a template by appending any actual receiving forest. Conversely, Site.factor in SourceScheduledRequirements.lean extracts a template from every actual source site. It proves equality of the receiving scopes and heterogeneous equality of both hints and retained plans. The induction reuses the existing append-associativity proofs. It accounts for pending sequence bodies, branches, installed handlers, armed cleanup, callback running protection and fresh resource scopes.

satisfied_iff_templates proves that checking all instantiated source templates is equivalent to the existing site judgment. compile_from_templates reuses the existing whole-plan compiler; it adds no checking or runtime rule. resume_clause_scopes in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean now uses this interface to compile a handler/resource/cleanup body with resumption inside those scopes. It supplies only installation and invocation obligations and reuses the previous exact resumption proof.

This separates the source caller context from the eventual capture without assuming the body checked before handler entry. The template checker still has to establish primitive capture, callback, invocation and declaration obligations at the actual receiving forest. Neither this equivalence nor its universal premise is added as an opaque consuming-recipe constructor. General declaration rules must derive those obligations; their integration and initial admission remain open.

Internally handled request recipes

Recipe.handledRequest in SourcePlannedClauseRecipes.lean turns the internally handled prefix into a consuming declaration rule. The plan first installs a single-operation handler, performs that operation, and then continues with another consuming recipe. The installed clause disposes its own capture. That capture contains only the new handler boundary; the pending remainder and its continuation owner stay in the waiting suffix. The rule therefore adds no operation requirement to the outer declaration.

SourceDeclarationPlans.lean records the canonical plan, table and clause family in HandledRequest. The recipe accepts an actual prefix plan for each owner whose signature equals this canonical signature. That equality retains the effect and operation, empty handler requirements, clause dependency family, required continuation actions and body shape. It permits different bound names and substituted source witnesses. It is not a local admission proof; source typing must still authenticate the actual code.

The dependency compiler derives the selected request's guard, empty closing schedule and owner bound directly. The planned compiler reuses that result, the established disposal family and existing signature transport. The scheduled compiler reuses strong declaration-signature transport and request_from_callbacks at the actual retained plans. All three reuse their existing induction for the remainder. Recipe.signature_congr handles the new constructor by composing the prefix signature equalities and recursing on the remainder; the existing capture and substitution theorems need no new runtime case or ownership proof.

HandledRecipes.declarations in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean admits a clause with an inner disposer for the same effect instance as the outer handler. HandledRecipes.captured derives the actual clause-body check and retained live-capture check through declaration_capture, starting with the original request and capture premises. substituted_declaration changes an outer resumption payload and preserves the recipe. The earlier generic local prefix_checked theorem now uses this compiler instead of repeating request assembly.

This closes admission and compilation for internally handled request prefixes. It does not admit arbitrary handler bodies or a handler enclosing the outer continuation use. Those cases still require structural demands on the actual saved and waiting code. General effectful-cleanup clauses, complete initial admission and universal finite-run preservation also remain open.

SourcePlannedPhases.lean proves strong local and pending transport under the existing phase-extension and permission-extension relations and resource-world inclusion, retaining the actual plans. The mutual declaration-certification proof retains every nested witness in the larger world; the original world-preserving interfaces are specializations. Invocation access reuses the independent permission and availability rules; continuation checks recurse under the existing spending law.

SourcePlannedCapturePrep.lean splits the pre-capture pending and compatibility judgments at the authenticated handler cut. captured_checks derives the pending live continuation, saved code after spending, waiting suffix and disposing callback checks from the pre-capture request and pending judgments. Fresh permission insertion and OwnerCaptureContracts.spend_introduced supply the permission and phase changes; history transport supplies the actual receiving scopes. Disposal protection and closing routes reuse the existing request guard. The theorem still requires the fresh owner's prior phase to be consumed and its permission entry absent. It does not assume post-capture pending checks, but admitting the actual clause bodies and integrating the result into the shared runtime invariant remain open.

SourcePlannedClauseRecipes.lean replaces the opaque uniform-proof constructor for a consuming-clause fragment with rules indexed by actual plan families. Resume and disposal check their permissions independently; silent prefixes, operation prefixes and choices use the existing sequencing and choice constructors. Recipe.cleanup adds pure cleanup around a consuming body and derives its callback check from the local transport rule. Recipe.compile reuses the checked recomposition rules. Recipe.capture derives their saved-code and callback premises from the pre-capture request, pending and compatibility judgments, freshness and the finite supplied operation requirements. Erasure reconstructs the earlier contextual recipe, and certification retains the same actual plan. Request prefixes currently require a builtin or non-disposing handler through the established RequestCapability judgment.

SourcePlannedRecipeDeclarations.lean retains recipes at both actual mode plans. Selected follows the existing clause order, parameter, continuation binder and body, and chooses the actual offered plan. Its syntax and dependency projections agree with existing lookup; selected_of_lookup recovers this witness from those lookups. Declarations.selected extracts the selected recipe and its requirement subset. Capture fixes the mode to the captured scope's protection flag and identifies the offered family from the same dependency lookup. Handler entry reuses erasure and certification of the stronger annotation. The existing contextual-handler example provides an inhabited declaration which still has no uniform scheme.

SourcePlannedSelectedSources.lean extends the established selected-body induction to the synchronized source indices. It retains the selected plan witness and returns the hereditary source body at that plan's stable signature. capture_body combines this source witness with the declaration recipe, pre-capture checks and existing clause-mode permission theorem. The output shares one plan between source typing, the local clause check and selected dependency family, and retains the live pending check. The source body remains under its ticket binder; capture substitution and runtime storage are not asserted by this component theorem.

These recipe rules do not yet cover general handler-bearing clause bodies, and the shared source and runtime invariants do not yet require their hereditary retention. The fragment is an intermediate proof component, not a restriction of the intended one-shot calculus or a completed source-admission theorem.

SourcePlannedCaptureSubstitution.lean uses the existing synchronized substitution theorem to retain the clause's actual signature and row judgment after payload substitution. Registry extension transports the payload at the same refined argument type. Port typing of the synchronized body supplies ClosedExcept, so body_step constructs the actual raw capture without a separately assumed lexical-readiness predicate. It reuses RecursiveCapture.capture_owned and OwnerPhaseTransitions.capture_map, and derives successor owner uniqueness from the original uniqueness and freshness. These are physical stack properties; they do not identify a supplied contract's demand with the saved source demand.

SourcePlannedRuntimeCuts.lean follows the actual HandlerCut through the original Matches witness. It constructs the exact annotated cut and matching saved and waiting hints, retaining each dormant branch and history marker. The selected handler's requirement check at the waiting scope follows from original compatibility. This adds annotation authentication to the established cut induction; it does not change lookup or stack composition.

SourcePlannedCaptureEntry.lean joins the physical cut, synchronized source declaration, selected structural recipe, pre-capture local and pending checks, compatibility and closed payload. The selected protection mode comes from the physical captured stack. The output uses one clause plan and one saved/waiting annotation pair for the actual live successor, its matching hints and its stronger checks. Its owners are exactly the fresh owner followed by the original owners, with no duplicates. For each fresh matching continuation contract it constructs the raw capture step and substituted source body at the same plan signature. Contract freshness and its matching input, answer, effect interfaces, protection and demand balance remain explicit premises. The following allocation connection constructs that contract from the saved and closing records. Retaining the richer source forest and preserving the shared runtime invariant remain open.

SourcePlannedAllocationData.lean retains ClauseData at the allocator's exact answer, dependency family, captured and waiting scopes, and resume/closing effect interfaces. Its constructor shares one actual plan between synchronized source typing and the stronger local check; the pending check and Matches witness use the same saved and waiting hints. capture_data derives this data from the actual handler cut, selected structural recipe, source declaration and pre-capture checks. This is retained proof data, not a new source-admission rule.

erase_checks and erase_body supply the existing allocation interface. For an old contract, the latter instantiates the synchronized body at refineContract and proves its erasure equals that exact contract. allocated_body substitutes the payload under the same refinement while retaining the actual plan and runtime-matching checks. Ownership demands, rows, protection and effect interfaces are unchanged by refinement.

SourcePlannedAllocation.lean specializes the shared allocate_capture_source_from_interfaces theorem with this data. The shared theorem's proof-data parameter now retains the selected answer, family and effect interfaces as well as both scopes; the allocation proof and both earlier callers remain valid. The stronger wrapper derives the old checking and body premises from ClauseData, then uses the returned contract's input, answer, protection, effects and proved demand balance to recover the synchronized substituted body. It retains the full existing allocation result, including the saved and closing record extensions, template, owner uniqueness, row split, invocation checks and conditional combined-budget result. It does not assume a separately chosen matching contract.

The allocation input still needs the annotated saved/tail decomposition and the same selected clause data. It does not derive a hereditary strengthened source forest or a complete State/Run successor. Those structures still use the earlier source annotations, and handler-bearing clause bodies still need the remaining structural recipe rules. The combined-budget conclusion retains its existing explicit checker premise; this connection does not prove that premise for every initial source program.

SourcePlannedFrames.lean strengthens source frames and segments with actual plans, synchronized handler declarations, and structural recipes for both offered modes. Plain frames and callbacks retain their source plans; live segments retain the stronger dormant source. Erasure recovers the earlier source judgments, and matching derives the relationship between hints and the actual stack. SourcePlannedFrameCuts.lean decomposes these segments at a physical handler cut, preserving the selected stronger frame, saved and waiting source, records, and requirement-evaluation equation. SourcePlannedFrameInterfaces.lean obtains the selected declarations and recipes from that frame. The exact selection equation returned by capture_data aligns its clause data with the same scope split. Its allocate theorem derives the earlier allocator's interface and retains the stronger substituted body under the constructed contract.

This removes separate stronger-declaration and decomposition premises from capture entry. It does not yet retain stronger saved and closing source in the successor. That reconstruction must share the refined answer type between the selected clause and saved source; equality after erasure is insufficient. Moreover, separate source segments and pending checks on the same hints do not ensure that their hidden plans coincide. A joint structural judgment must share the actual plan between each frame's source and check. These obligations, the remaining clause recipe rules, and the closing-budget premise precede complete State/Run preservation and initial-source progress.

SourcePlannedCheckedFrames.lean supplies the joint structural frame and segment judgments. The plain-frame constructor shares an actual plan between its typed context signature and Local check; the armed-cleanup constructor does the same for its callback. Other frame constructors retain the existing source obligations. A segment checks each frame against the rest of the stack appended to its explicit outside hints. A live segment checks its dormant source against that same receiving suffix. Frame.source, Frame.pending, Segment.source and Segment.pending project the existing judgments without choosing independent plans.

SourcePlannedCheckedRecomposition.lean proves joint segment concatenation. Equality of annotated receiving suffixes reuses hints_append_assoc; the requirement-evaluation calculation reuses the existing stack, phase and merge equations. The result retains source and local checks together throughout dormant captures. SourcePlannedCheckedCuts.lean splits the joint judgment at the physical handler cut. Its result shares one refined answer between the selected handler, saved segment and waiting segment, and includes heterogeneous equality between the original hints and their recomposition. Requirements and owner records satisfy the existing exact split equations.

TypedClauseData in SourcePlannedAllocationData.lean now indexes the selected refined answer directly. ClauseData is its existential projection at an erased answer, preserving the earlier allocation interface. capture_typed_data derives the indexed data from source selection, and TypedClauseData.allocated_body preserves that fixed answer through the actual contract refinement and payload substitution. The older theorems reuse these proofs. No equality of refined types is inferred from equality after erasure. SourcePlannedCheckedInterfaces.lean joins this data to the joint handler cut. Saved source, waiting source and selected clause data share the same refined answer; the pending check is derived from the joint segment rather than supplied independently.

The shared allocation wrapper still returns the older saved and closing source. Its adoption of the joint segments must retain the fixed answer witness and transport the source and checks through contract insertion and phase changes. These component proofs do not yet preserve the joint invariant in every State/Run transition. The remaining clause recipe rules and source-derived closing budget remain separate prerequisites for initial-source progress.

SourcePlannedCheckedTransport.lean proves registry extension for synchronized bodies, offers, declarations and contexts using the established expression-extension proof. Joint frame and segment transport combines this with the existing Local phase/permission transport. Plans, refined values, hints, demands and requirement records remain identical; dormant source is transported recursively.

SourcePlannedCheckedAllocationData.lean retains CaptureData indexed by the allocator's saved and waiting demands and requirement bodies, in addition to its answer, scopes and effect interfaces. The shared allocation theorem's certificate parameter now includes those exact indices. Its proof is unchanged, and the older wrappers remain valid. matched_hints_unique proves that matching the same actual stack at a fixed dependency scope determines the handler hints. CaptureData.allocated uses this result to align the clause's local check with the joint saved/waiting hints. It refines the returned contract, substitutes the payload using the existing theorem, and builds the joint live segment through fresh registry, permission and phase extension. The original source records supply the exact resume-store entry and remainder.

SourcePlannedCheckedAllocation.lean derives CaptureData from the joint handler-cut interface and calls the shared allocator once. The result retains its actual capture step, exact owner increment, owner uniqueness, saved and closing record checks, and conditional combined-budget conclusion. It additionally retains the synchronized clause and joint live stack under one refined contract, answer and set of runtime hints. The joint checks use the introduced-owner phase; capture_map identifies that phase with the actual successor's owner map. No separate matching contract or successor source premise is supplied.

The closing template and disposal-record source annotations remain at the older layer. Strengthening them requires checking the actual retained callback plans at their closing receiving suffixes. A scheduled Pending check currently retains an existential plan at each dependency index; pairing it with stronger callback source does not by itself prove that the plan is the same. This is a source/checking obligation as well as a record-transport obligation. The joint allocation result does not yet establish complete State/Run preservation or initial-source progress, and retains the existing closing-budget premise.

SourcePlannedClosingPlans.lean introduces proof-independent Plans annotations on the existing close-entry list and closing hints. Release and retire entries preserve that list; each invoke entry records its actual callback plan. Contents types the callback at that plan's signature, and Checked checks the same plan at the running closing suffix. Thus source and scheduling cannot silently select different plans with equal dependency indices. This adds annotation data, not runtime instructions.

plan_contents extracts these annotations and their synchronized source from the actual joint captured stack, including callbacks inside dormant captures. Contents.template retains them in a template indexed by its raw footprint and requirement body. Template.erase supplies the established closing-template judgment. Template.source combines source and scheduling at the same annotation to materialize a joint closing stack with the exact template requirements. It still requires the established plan typing and caller-scope interface.

SourcePlannedClosingRecomposition.lean proves that checks split and join across annotated plan concatenation. The invoke case reuses running_append_assoc and retains the original callback plan. Template registry transport reuses source expression extension; caller-scope transport reuses plan_context_scope. Template.recompose materializes and joins the actual waiting stack using joint segment concatenation, retaining its source/checking witnesses and the existing requirement-evaluation equation.

These results provide the stronger scheduling judgment and its materialization consequence, but do not derive it from the current request/disposal rules. Those rules must retain the actual closing annotations instead of merely an existential plan at each dependency index. Strong disposal-record allocation must also preserve the template at the exact raw footprint and requirement body selected by the shared allocator. Independently extracting strong and erased templates cannot prove that their requirement witnesses coincide. The following allocation connection supplies one template to both layers. The remaining source-admission/progress obligations remain open.

SourcePlannedClosingAllocationData.lean connects the stronger template to allocation. capture_closing extracts planned closing source from CaptureData's actual saved segment, constructs its template, and supplies the erasure of that same template. Its Certificate retains the planned source at the exact captured scope, raw footprint and requirement body. Registry transport preserves those indices and callback plans.

The shared allocator now exposes allocate_capture_source_from_closing_interfaces. Its additional input constructs a closing template from the selected saved source and retained certificate; its result retains closing evidence at the actual returned requirement indices. The existing ownership, requirement and allocation proof uses the supplied template. allocate_capture_source_from_interfaces keeps its earlier interface by constructing the older template and calling this shared entry point. This is proof factoring, not a new source-admission premise about future execution.

SourcePlannedClosingRecords.lean retains the stronger certificate in each disposal record, tied to the actual captured stack, recorded scope and exact stored requirement body. Erasure supplies the existing record judgment. Registry and annotation transport retain the planned template; capture uses the existing captured-location split to move older records and adds the newly allocated record.

Records.after_step retains these same certificates using the established post-step record layout, retained-entry inclusion, capture-origin theorem and owner uniqueness. It requires that the step create no ticket and keeps the same registry and world. selected_template uses exact lookup membership and capture uniqueness to select the stronger template for the actual stored record. These are component preservation and selection results, not a proof that every source execution supplies their premises.

SourcePlannedClosingAllocation.lean derives the supplied template from the actual joint saved source and retains it through the single shared allocation call. The resulting strong template and disposal records use the same refined contract as the clause and joint live stack. The actual capture step, exact owner increment, owner uniqueness, row checks and conditional closing-budget result remain those of the shared proof. Thus allocation no longer needs to identify independently chosen strong and erased closing requirement witnesses.

The allocation wrapper still uses the earlier planned source judgments. The following retained-plan judgments derive stronger scheduling locally, but their annotations and checks must still be preserved through allocation, records and all runtime transitions. Complete initial-source progress and the source-derived closing-budget obligation remain open.

SourceRetainedPlans.lean introduces Forest, a scope annotation that retains each actual pending context and callback plan. Its closing operation preserves callback plans and flattens dormant captures using the existing closing order. split_cut lifts the established handler cut; Forest.append_injective proves uniqueness at fixed annotated scopes. Neither lemma treats equal dependencies as equal source signatures.

SourceScheduledChecks.lean defines structural Local and Pending judgments over that data. Sequencing places its actual second plan in the pending frame; cleanup places its actual callback plan in the armed frame. A request checks the retained closing plans at its selected cut. Resume and disposal retain the exact selected front, capture and tail, reuse independent capability checks, and check the recomposed forest under the spent owner phase. Both judgments erase to the earlier planned checks. Pending.closing_checked and Pending.closing_prefix_checked produce the existing strong closing check for the same callback annotation. Local.dispose_schedule authenticates the supplied pieces against the exact selected owner and the unique retained forest split.

SourceScheduledFrames.lean ties source typing and scheduling to a single explicit forest. A plain frame's typed context and an armed frame's typed callback use the same plan retained in that forest. Frame.source and Segment.source project to the established joint source judgments; their pending projections keep the actual plans. The local handler rule now retains the same structural recipe declarations required by installed frames. This closes that evidence mismatch, but does not extend the consuming recipe grammar to all scope-bearing clauses or settle hereditary admission.

SourceScheduledClosing.lean proves plan_contents: closing-plan extraction from the scheduled source produces callback source evidence and an equality between the extracted annotation and the retained forest's closing image. This includes nested dormant captures. request_template derives a template and its scheduling check from a request, its annotated cut, the matching forest split and the captured source. dispose_template derives the corresponding result at the actual selected owner and spent phase. Neither theorem takes a separate closing-check premise. They still require the captured source segment; full transition preservation must construct and retain that segment and the same annotation at runtime.

SourceScheduledRecomposition.lean lifts the established scope and hint associativity equations to retained plan forests. pending_append_iff splits and joins the same checks at the same receiving suffix. segment_append retains both typed source segments, their actual plans and records, and the established requirement-evaluation equation. The dormant-capture case transports its saved source to the same reassociated suffix. resume_clause and dispose_clause construct head invocation checks from retained pieces, permissions, phases and the existing compatibility and closing-route judgments. They do not assume a check of the entire successor.

SourceScheduledCuts.lean proves capture_segments for the physical HandlerCut. It returns typed captured and waiting segments, their actual forests, the same refined answer, exact demand and record splits, dispatch agreement and requirement evaluation. The whole forest equals the concatenation of the returned forests up to the existing scope indices. This is stronger than erasing to the earlier cut theorem and trying to recover plan witnesses afterward.

SourceScheduledCaptureClosing.lean connects that physical cut to scheduling. capture_closing takes the whole scheduled source, its request check, the selected handler's lookup facts and disposal permission. It derives successful plan construction using the existing SourceDependencyCapture.checked_cut, and internal owner use using SourceDependencySchemes.capture_internal_uses. It also derives the captured and waiting source segments and a closing template with a check for those same callback plans. The theorem retains demand and record splits and reuses handler_cut_reconstructs with owned_tickets_append for ownership accounting. It requires neither an independently supplied captured source, a successful-plan premise nor a separate closing check. This theorem covers disposal-enabled capture; it does not allocate the new owner or establish closing effect budgets.

SourceScheduledTransport.lean preserves the same plans under registry, permission and available-phase extensions. SourcePlannedPhases.resume_transport and dispose_transport expose the existing independent access transport for reuse; source expressions and contexts use the established registry-extension proofs. Phase extension preserves existing availability; actual allocation must still supply freshness and consumption invariants. These results support allocation but do not yet prove its stronger clause check or integrate all transitions into State and Run. Full structural clause recipes and source-derived closing budgets remain open.

SourceScheduledNeutral.lean adds a structural expansion relation over actual plan forests. It erases to the established annotated-scope relation; existing interpretation, protection and compatibility results remain reusable. Closing erases plain frames and history markers, retains inserted pure callbacks, and preserves every existing callback plan. Expansion.forClosing proves a relation between the resulting schedules, replacing the stronger equality that held before callback insertion was added. Plan-carrying handler and owner cuts lift existing lookup results. Expansion preserves the selected handler and its modes, or the same selected dormant continuation while expanding only its caller and waiting suffix. These are structural evidence relations, not alternative dispatch rules.

SourceScheduledNeutralChecks.lean proves transport for all stronger Local constructors and their recursive Pending checks. Request transport reuses the previous guard proof, expands the exact plan-carrying cut and authenticates the requested split by uniqueness before rebuilding closing checks. Invocation transport similarly authenticates the actual owner pieces, reuses existing access and compatibility, and transports the recomposed schedule. The outside-only theorem keeps each pending plan fixed; pending_transport also permits the retained forest to gain pure callbacks. The pure_cleanup rule wraps any locally checked body using those proofs. It covers resumption, disposal and disposing requests without a successful future state as a premise. The regressions in SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean check an effectful saved request, an effectful saved completion, repeated cleanup around a disposing request, and the fact that cleanup changes the closing schedule. This local rule is now used by Recipe.cleanup in the consuming declaration grammar. SourceDependencyNeutral.lean uses the same scope relation and cut lemmas at the erased checker, with a structural Local/Pending induction for retained code and callbacks. Keeping the scope relation below declaration admission avoids a circular import. Erasure, certification, recipe compilation, capture and signature transport all cover the new constructor. The declaration examples also derive its checked body at capture and retain a cleanup/resume recipe through a substitution that changes the actual resume argument. Runtime cleanup allocation and completion keep their existing owner-ledger obligations; transport does not erase the new cleanup ticket.

SourceScheduledCapturePrep.lean derives fresh capture preparation from the request, its retained-plan cut, the pending forest and freshness. Fresh permission insertion uses the existing extension lemma. Spending the newly introduced owner restores the original phase map; inserting its spent-history marker then uses the stronger inert-frame transport. Disposal protection and route evidence come from the existing request guard, while callback checks retain the actual saved plans. No entire successor check is an additional premise.

SourceScheduledClauses.lean reuses the existing structural Recipe constructors. compile builds the stronger clause check from retained pieces; capture derives those pieces from pre-capture checks. declaration_capture selects the actual recipe and its finite requirements. capture_body reuses the established source-body selection proof and returns the stronger clause and pending checks with that same body's plan and contract family. Substitution and allocation are connected below. The recipe grammar includes resource binding with locally supplied operations and pure cleanup. General handler-bearing and effectful-cleanup recipes and complete hereditary source admission remain required work.

SourceScheduledScopedInvocations.lean generalizes the invocation component beyond the head-only recipe case. For an actual OwnerCut, resume_iff and dispose_iff characterize the existing Local judgment using independent access and three structural pending checks. For resume, those check the saved forest at front ++ spent(tail), the caller prefix at spent(tail), and the waiting tail. Disposal replaces the first with the saved closing forest at running(front ++ spent(tail)). All use the spent owner phase. The equivalences reuse forest append decomposition and selection uniqueness; they do not assume a complete successor state. The introduction rules retain explicit permission, phase, protection, route and handler compatibility obligations. No restriction is placed on the caller prefix's frame constructors. request_from_capability supplies a resumptive request check at an arbitrary actual receiving scope. The existing recipe compiler uses the general invocation rules for its initial empty caller prefix, then derives the locally acquired resource prefix by provider insertion.

SourceScheduledScopeExamples.lean checks complete local clause plans that install a handler, enter a fresh resource, arm cleanup, and invoke the captured continuation from inside all three scopes. Resume restores an effectful pending computation; disposal checks an effectful retained callback under running protection. The resource examples quantify over the fresh identity rather than testing one chosen allocation.

The same file refutes blanket transport from the existing head invocation check. A pending request for F works at its original outer handler. Inserting a nearer F handler with no matching operation blocks it. A second example has the operation but permits disposal: placing running cleanup before that handler makes the restored request attempt a protected capture. The original pending forest and independent resume/handler-requirement check pass in both examples; the full scheduling check rejects them. These are local annotation examples, not claims about complete typed Core programs or reachable admitted runs.

SourceScheduledRequirements.lean represents that context sensitivity explicitly. Site is a structural position in a plan, indexed by the plan's starting forest/world and the forest/world at that position. Its rules cover both sides of sequencing and choice, handler entry and body, cleanup body and callback, and every fresh resource identity. It retains the actual suffix and callback plans when crossing their scopes.

There are four requirement forms: request, resume, disposal and handler installation. Check expands them into the established request guard and closing schedule; exact owner selection, independent access and the three recomposed pending checks; or the declaration and installation checks. Satisfied universally checks these structurally generated positions. It is not an uninterpreted admissibility predicate and has no complete future-state premise. Resource annotations produce a family indexed by fresh identities; this construction does not claim a finite enumeration or decision procedure. Nested handler installation still uses the existing declaration certificates.

necessary follows the position derivation to recover each check from Local. compile recurses on the existing Plan, reconstructing Local for every constructor. Their equivalence establishes that these contextual requirements neither weaken nor strengthen the local judgment. Separate composition equivalences expose how sequence, choice, handler, cleanup and resource obligations combine, with the correct receiving context at each branch. The calculus still has one sequencing operation.

Site.owner_cut is a separate induction on source positions. Starting from an actual owner cut, it derives a cut at every source position with the identical saved forest and waiting tail. Sequence, handler, resource, cleanup body and callback traversal add their actual caller frames; none chooses a replacement capture. The proof needs neither local validity nor a continuation permission. Site.resume_requirements and Site.dispose_requirements combine this result with the established invocation equivalences. They derive the exact access, saved-segment, caller-prefix and waiting-tail obligations at the source site's resource world. Deriving this formula does not prove its obligations: source admission must still justify the saved computation under each new interpretation.

SourceScheduledClauses.capture_body_from_requirements combines actual source-clause selection with this compilation. The older recipe-based capture_body derives these requirements from its stronger, restricted premises and calls the general rule.

SourceScheduledCaptureEntry.capture_entry_from_requirements connects that rule to the physical handler cut, closed payload substitution and the actual capture transition. The previous entry theorem is now a specialization through the old recipes.

The source-admission gap remains. The old flat operation list checks the waiting tail; it does not derive all contextual requirements for saved code under a clause-local caller prefix. The new rules expose those requirements and prove the relative capture result when they hold. They do not establish that initial source admission supplies them at every request. Their structural erasure, recomposition, capture-cut and transport proofs accept arbitrary declaration evidence; scheduled local checks remain unchanged. The scheduled allocation interfaces now accept arbitrary declaration evidence, preserving it in both typed continuation pieces and the reconstructed live segment. Their separate requirement premise checks the actual selected plan at an authenticated cut. Deriving that premise from general source annotations and preserving contextual requirements through all source and runtime transitions remain necessary. Supplying the desired whole successor invariant as a new premise would not discharge this work.

Shared scheduled state and capture preservation

SourceScheduledState.lean defines a single state indexed by the retained source-plan forest.
