Finite-prefix existence is not preservation for every arbitrary machine trace: raw transitions can carry unchecked annotations. A final checked-execution interface and its universal finite-run preservation still need to be stated and proved. General scope-bearing consuming recipes and complete initial-source admission also remain open. These theorems do not change Core or establish a Core correspondence theorem.

SourceDependencyState.capture_preserves now constructs the complete enriched source successor for a supported disposing capture with no outward effects. It uses the same actual cut, selected clause, contract, annotation, closing template and updated continuation records. The closing budget follows from the typed plan; existing consuming-clause and phase lemmas supply demand balance and the pending check. The successor demand is a permutation of the old demand with the fresh owner added, and its row is contained in the old row. Captured support and freshness of the three registries remain explicit premises at this source-only layer; internal owner use follows from the local request rule. The result also identifies the exact substituted clause and live boundary and supplies a disposal certificate for a runtime record with the same source annotation.

check_capture_outward_weaken preserves the actual selection when the outward effect interface grows. Its two structural proofs retain the same target for each route and the same original/surviving route pair for each closing callback. This lets the empty-outward guard supply a certificate at the new contract's closing interface without changing the order of interpretations.

SourceDependencyState.lean defines a candidate State judgment that shares the current expression, pending segment, recursive requirements, owner records and dependency scope. It retains both closing-store representations, the captured-annotation binding, stored declaration schemes, current and pending contextual checks, ticket uniqueness, and the checked combined requirement row. Erasure recovers the existing connected-source state without selecting another source derivation or changing its indices.

Run connects this enriched state to the existing runtime invariant through an explicit equality between the rich contract registry's erasure and the runtime source registry. The existing invariant supplies resource accounting, name history, access validity, completion contracts and usage evidence. The enriched invariant additionally requires each stored annotation's owner to appear in the issued-name ledger. This finite support condition holds for the empty initial map and is preserved by capture insertion and disposal. Its erasure recovers the earlier connected-source Run.

Run.capture_preserves now joins the actual source successor to the existing coherent completion-record constructor and generic runtime preservation proof. The new runtime record has exactly the rich contract's erasure. Capture provenance retains older disposal certificates, while the source capture proof supplies the new one. The same successor retains source checks, ledger, access, usage, completion contracts and annotation history. The selected disposing cut and ready operand describe the actual operation; no independent capture-safety premise remains. Freshness for all three registries follows from freshness in the name ledger.

Run.capture_progress chooses that fresh owner using the existing finite-ledger proof, then applies preservation. It proves a step and successor invariant for the disposing cut, including demand balance and row containment. This closes the disposing runtime allocation connection. Preserving the richer invariant through the remaining transitions, including non-disposing capture, and complete source admission remain open.

SourceDependencyOwners.lean defines Within by the dependency constructors: invocations require membership in an owner list, sequencing and branches check their components, and resource bodies check each fresh resource instantiation. This membership condition does not count or consume uses; the existing one-shot judgment still does that. PendingWithin checks plain retained frames and both regions of live boundaries. Handler and cleanup frames have no pending ticket actions of their own.

The source-to-usage proof shows that a context whose annotation excludes an outside owner cannot refer to that owner. It reuses closed function usage, resource-instantiation preservation, scope translation and the existing free-ticket/consumption theorem. Rich segment typing authenticates the scope's recursive owner list and supplies the exact runtime InternalUses judgment.

The Local.request rule now requires PendingWithin for the exact selected capture whenever its offer permits disposal. This is a structural source-rule change, with no future-execution premise or runtime transition change. Projection through spent markers preserves owners; world extension preserves the bound. capture_internal_uses connects the rule to the actual typed cut, so neither source nor runtime capture preservation takes InternalUses as an extra input. A regression shows that the effect guard accepts a scope with pending work for an outside owner while the stronger source rule rejects it. Another accepts an invocation whose owner belongs to the retained capture. These are checking examples, not a claimed reachable counterexample to the earlier full invariant.

capture_resource_support derives captured support at the computed outside interface from the existing access invariant and unique resource ownership. The established cut decomposition supplies support in the enclosing tail; ownership separation prevents any tail resource from also belonging to the capture. The new supported_restrict induction removes ambient resources that are not retained dependencies, while keeping each dormant capture's enclosing visible suffix. supported_outside_interface combines that restriction with ownership separation. Thus resource support is no longer a caller-supplied premise of runtime capture progress or preservation. The source-only capture lemma retains it because its source state does not carry the runtime ledger.

initial_run derives an empty initial owner demand and constructs this joined runtime state from rich source typing, an initial contextual check, the existing recursive requirement check, row acceptance, result typing and support evidence. It reuses the earlier initial-runtime proof. Transport from the empty permission map supplies the contextual check for the same action map selected by that proof. This establishes the initial candidate invariant; it does not prove admission of every later handler installation or capture.

Bind and beta reduction preserve the enriched State using the existing rich substitution and silent-dependency lemmas. The shared replacement proof changes the current expression and its check while retaining the exact pending segment, stores and annotations. Its all-store evaluation equality preserves the combined requirement check. These are source-state preservation results; runtime preservation for all transitions and the complete execution induction remain open, together with the remaining source-admission obligations.

discard_preserves now constructs the whole successor State at the actual closing stack. It decomposes the original combined check, obtains the selected action from contextual disposal checking, and reuses Closing.recompose for the matching pending source, reduced stores, annotation binding and contextual checks. Existing forest decomposition retains the handler certificates. The new current expression is unit; its empty requirement check recombines with the returned pending check to preserve the original row. The result includes the actual disposal step, the equality between the old demand and the selected owner followed by the new demand, the ticket-ownership permutation, and the one-shot phase trace.

This theorem assumes a constructed plan typed at the selected contract's closing interface. The current expression supplies admission of that interface into its allowed effects.

Run.discard_preserves now preserves the joined runtime invariant for every actual access-checked disposal step. It extracts the selected action permission and the retained certificate for that same owner and capture. Registry coherence identifies the rich contract's closing interface with the certificate's interface; equality of the constructed plans supplies the plan typing required by source preservation. The existing completion theorem preserves the result contract on that exact successor. assemble_entry then reuses connected-runtime assembly, usage and history preservation, and capture provenance to retain the resource ledger, names, source checks and closing certificates together. No new ownership or execution induction is needed.

Run.discard_progress uses the existing structural disposal-progress theorem to obtain an actual step and applies this preservation result. Its only premise is the current enriched Run; a supplied plan or successful-disposal check is not an additional premise. This closes the disposal runtime connection. Initial admission of the retained certificates and preservation for the other transitions remain open.

Finite coverage of an intercepted operation interface

SourceHandlerCoverage.lean adds an executable sufficient check for a new resumptive handler to cover the operation interface of the nearest existing interpreter for the same effect. operationDomain stops at that interpreter. A matching handler contributes its declared table keys, including any conservative extra keys without dependency annotations; a matching cell contributes its typed read and write operations. An incomplete nearer handler blocks lookup instead of exposing an outer handler's keys. Dormant captures do not participate in the active lookup path.

check_iff connects the finite Boolean test to the existing independent RequestCapability judgment for every key in that domain. Both ordinary and protected modes must be available, with resumptive control use. Requirements use membership rather than use counts. selected_in_domain proves that every previously selected typed operation belongs to this interface; selected_capability then supplies its capability under the replacement. This is a sufficient coverage condition, not a claim that every individually safe interception must cover the whole old interface.

The builtin typing premise is explicit. The abstract dependency selector can return a builtin for any operation number, while ScopedPorts.withCellSignatures permits only operations 0 and 1. builtin_typed_of_signature derives that finite bound from the existing typing signature. The proof therefore does not assume that all untyped selector results denote executable operations, and it does not alter builtin selection.

The typing premise is now derived at actual source requests. selected_builtin_effect authenticates the requested instance from exact lookup, including lookup beneath arbitrary intervening scopes. builtin_typed_of_source in SourceScheduledFreshRequests.lean projects the operation signature from the existing structural Expression derivation. request_from_source_coverage uses that fact without a separately supplied BuiltinTyped premise. Its operand may still require evaluation. The negative example invalid_cell_operation_rejected rules out operation 2 under the declared cell signature for every operand and resource world.

SourceScheduledRuntimeCells.lean supplies the corresponding Run.request_builtin_typed projection from retained source typing and the declaration registry. Run.request_covered then admits the primitive request beneath a covering caller handler. These proofs reuse the existing port projection and request inversion. They do not authenticate every latent dependency signature in an abstract callable type: that still requires the callable-contract admission work, and no global latent-signature validity claim follows from typing one actual request.

SourceScheduledFreshRequests.lean uses the coverage result in request_from_coverage. The request may lie beneath any caller prefix through which the effect passes. The proof reuses capability prefix transport and the existing request constructor, without a previous whole-body check or a future schedule premise. Checked examples cover a same-effect replacement under running protection, both cell operations under an arbitrary passing prefix, and rejection of missing operations or a missing protected mode. A read-only replacement does not cover a cell's full interface.

This follows the research principle that control-use obligations belong in operation contracts and must constrain their handlers; see Tang et al., Soundly Handling Linearity, section 2.2. The paper does not establish this experiment's disposal or cleanup rules. The coverage proof is local evidence for one request obligation, not reuse of the paper's complete soundness theorem.

General handler-bearing consuming declarations still need to derive and retain these and the other primitive obligations at their actual source templates. Requests supplied only by the new handler use the existing direct capability or selected-capture rules at that new scope; they need not have checked before installation. Rechecking an outer continuation additionally requires its actual saved code and callback schedules. This coverage result alone neither proves that transport nor extends the consuming-recipe grammar. It also makes no observational-equivalence claim about old and new providers.

Constructing handler-bearing clauses at capture

SourceScheduledClauseHandlers.lean separates two obligations that cannot share a before-installation check. The original consumer has a structural recipe whose check follows from the pre-capture request and retained forest. Its saved computation must be adapted to the new handler. Newly introduced requests are then checked in the installed scope, where their provider exists.

capture_handler performs that construction using the existing recipe capture and structural Adapt.sound theorems. The new handler's declarations retain their existing recipe checks, and both its external requirements and the added requests use finite capability checks. requestPrefix is an abbreviation for ordinary sequencing plans. Duplicate requests reuse the same operation capability; continuation use remains checked separately. The theorem takes no old check of the complete new body and no replacement Local or Pending certificate.

selected_capture_handler authenticates the full wrapper against actual clause selection. source_capture_handler joins its scheduling result to the existing source declaration theorem. Selection uniqueness makes the two proofs refer to the same plan, including its handler declarations. The resulting source body retains the established type, effect, ownership-row and fresh-contract premises.

Checked examples exercise three cases: a clause installs a previously absent provider, requests its operation twice and resumes beneath it; a saved request is reinterpreted by a new handler for the same effect as its former waiting provider; and disposal runs a saved effectful callback under the new handler and running protection. These are source-checking examples, not complete machine executions or observational-equivalence proofs. They reuse the existing capture, owner-cut, recomposition and callback proofs. The request and callback cases now generate their retained adaptation with the compiler below.

This does not complete general declaration admission. The existing declaration recipe grammar still rejects the full wrapper, as old_declaration_recipe_rejects_wrapper proves. General admission must generate the adaptation certificate from retained source interfaces at every capture and retain the resulting declaration evidence through execution. Arbitrary handler nesting, new effectful cleanup scopes in clause bodies, initial-term admission and full execution preservation remain open. The rule is a capture component for the intended calculus, not a smaller replacement milestone.

Compiling adaptation from source interfaces

SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean removes two parts of handwritten adaptation. outside, inside and split construct the retained derivation by induction over the actual forest or insertion. They retain the source plan at each affected position, move callback checks under running protection, and traverse dormant continuations at their new waiting suffix. Unaffected suffixes reuse their existing derivations. The inputs are finite handler-requirement checks and adaptations at affected code positions, not a replacement whole Pending judgment. Each position is authenticated in both the original and resulting forest.

resume and dispose use this traversal at the existing owner cuts. They generate the recomposed or closing derivation under the spent owner phase. The existing Adapt.sound theorem still supplies independent access and ownership reasoning. No execution or declaration rule accepts a universal successful-body transformer as a field.

RequestFootprint supplies the code-position adaptation for a useful class of stored code. It applies the structural signature interface described below to the existing plan, with a finite list of operation requirements. Sequencing and choice concatenate lists. Cleanup combines the callback and body requirements. A handler checks the operations it intercepts and exports its own declaration requirements together with the body's unhandled requests. A resource binder checks its body under its local read/write interface and the outer requirements. Weakening permits a larger finite annotation. These lists do not count operation uses.

RequestFootprint.adapt generates an entire code adaptation from this annotation and one checkRequirements result at the new receiving scope. Nested handler declarations retain the original source evidence through Adapt.sound; the footprint does not establish their admission. External request capabilities here require resumptive handlers in both protection modes. The internal-disposer source rule below adds a separate case. Other code needing the general disposing-request or continuation-invocation rules still uses those rules. RequestFootprint.no_invocation proves that an operation footprint cannot silently discharge an explicit continuation use.

The capture examples now compile retained adaptation for a reinterpreted saved request and an effectful disposal callback. Further checks cover repeated requests in cleanup surrounding a nested handler and choice, a resource's read/write footprint, and reinterpretation inside a dormant saved branch. These results generate adaptation for the stated source annotations; they do not derive those annotations for every typed source program. General consuming declarations must still generate the appropriate interfaces, including explicit continuation uses, and retain them through source and runtime frames. Complete initial admission and full execution preservation remain open.

Request interfaces through source substitution

SourceRequestFootprints.lean places the request interface on SourcePlanSignatures.Signature. Callable source types already retain that signature, whereas literal clause witnesses may change after substitution. The plan-facing RequestFootprint is now an abbreviation for this same judgment applied to signature plan; it is not a second interface definition. The annotation imports neither runtime forests nor source-success judgments.

The adaptation compiler's signature_adapt consumes a signature interface, an actual plan with that signature, and the finite operation check at its new receiving scope. Structural induction produces the same Adapt derivation as before. RequestFootprint.adapt specializes this theorem to a known plan, and all previous callback, disposal and resource examples retain their statements. Actual declaration typing remains independent of this interface proof.

SourceRequestInterfaceRetention.lean reuses the existing rich-source substitution and beta-reduction theorems. Substituting a closed value preserves the checking signature. Beta reduction returns the function's declared body signature together with the established ownership-requirement evaluation equality, so its interface is retained without another substitution induction. The existing higher-order source example now carries a finite interface through both bind and beta substitution, including its effectful cleanup body.

Handler decomposition authenticates the actual clause plans from the rich source derivation. Equality of their clause signatures transfers the interface from a reference plan to this actual witness. A separate checked example changes a literal clause by value substitution and retains its interface using the existing declaration-signature theorem. The negative signature example shows that changing a handler's external requirements changes its signature even when the dependency index stays equal.

This resolves interface retention for these source transformations. It does not produce an interface for every source signature, validate phantom latent operation signatures, prove general declaration admission, or extend runtime preservation. In particular, explicit continuation uses still require their own structural interfaces. The new source representation keeps those remaining obligations separate from literal plan-witness bookkeeping.

Compiling disposal from callback interfaces

SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean now compiles the retained-request case as well as continuation invocation. request takes the original and resulting selected cuts, their structural insertion relation, and the finite target capture-guard check. It generates closing adaptation from the original callback positions. When the inserted handler lies inside the capture, request_inside needs no callback adaptation premise: the established equality of closing forests reuses the old schedule. Insertion in the waiting suffix rechecks affected callback code using the shared retained traversal. The selected disposer and captured owners retain their original evidence through Adapt.sound.

A newly selected disposer cannot assume that its predecessor had a disposal schedule. SourceScheduledCallbackInterfaces.lean instead annotates the actual retained forest with Interfaces. Each cleanup position stores a finite operation list and a RequestFootprint of its actual callback plan. Ordinary pending computations contribute no callback obligation; live continuations retain annotations for both their saved branch and tail.

Interfaces.compile consumes the original normal Pending derivation and rechecks each callback at its closing position. Its inputs contain no target callback Local proof or complete closing Pending proof. Existing source evidence supplies each callback's original check, and footprint adaptation changes its receiving context. Saved branches acquire the running boundary required by the existing closing construction.

Interfaces.exposed computes one finite list for the whole captured forest. Interfaces.check_iff proves that checking this list at the receiving scope is equivalent to checking all annotated callbacks at their closing positions. The proof reuses ordered capability lookup and requirement filtering. Closing prefixes contain builtin providers but no source handlers, so they either provide an operation or pass it to the outside; no previously successful disposal check is assumed. A builtin in a live continuation's closing tail can therefore discharge a requirement of its saved callback. Repetition in the list does not count operation uses.

installed_request combines that finite list with the separate capture guard and captured-owner bound. Checked examples replace a resumer with a disposer for the same effect, reinterpret an existing disposer's callback through a new waiting handler, and reuse callbacks when an unrelated inserted handler is captured and removed. Negative checks distinguish missing callback providers from a changed closing route: callback capability checks can pass while capture must still be rejected. The source-connected disposal example in SourceScheduledClauseHandlers.lean now derives its callback evidence from the pre-capture retained source through this compiler.

These are local request and callback-admission results. Callback bodies covered by Interfaces use RequestFootprint; explicit continuation invocations and more general internally disposing callback code still need their appropriate structural interfaces. The new requested operation itself may dispose, and the retained-request compiler accepts general structural callback adaptation. General consuming declarations must generate and retain these interfaces. Complete initial-source admission remains open. Universal execution preservation is connected later in the common event relation; no Core alignment or later continuation mode is included.

Direct callback and initial scheduling admission

SourceScheduledSourceInterfaces.lean adds Declared, a structural annotation over the checking signature. Its rules follow pure terms, requests, invocations, sequencing, choice, handlers, cleanup and fresh resource bodies. A handler retains its actual declaration recipes; no rule stores a Local, Pending, or successful future-body transformer. Declaration annotations are independent of the receiving forest and operation availability. Signature equality preserves them, including when substitution changes literal clause syntax.

compile_signature combines this annotation with Footprint and one finite operation check at the receiving scope. Induction constructs the existing scheduled Local judgment directly. It reuses declaration-signature transport, exact request selection, and requirement propagation through handler, cleanup and resource scopes. declared_of_local extracts the annotation for existing clients without changing their accepted programs. Direct continuation invocations remain outside Footprint; they still require independent access and recomposition evidence.

The interface now has a separate handledRequest rule for the established internal-disposer pattern. This handler supplies its own operation and disposes its empty capture. The adaptation compiler reuses the same exact cut, guard, captured-owner bound and callback rules as the existing source proof. It needs no outer resumptive provider. Existing sequence, choice, cleanup and resource interface rules compose this case. This extension does not claim to cover every internally disposing handler.

SourceScheduledCallbackInterfaces.lean retains these declaration annotations structurally at callback positions. Interfaces.compile_declared constructs closing callback checks from those annotations and the finite operation check, without a previous normal pending schedule or a checked target callback. installed_request_declared uses the result for a newly selected disposer; capture routing and captured-owner bounds remain independent checks. The old interfaces derive annotations from normal source evidence and reuse the new compiler.

SourceScheduledInternalCallbacks.lean checks nested effectful cleanup and choice whose callbacks handle operations internally and dispose their own captures, including when the enclosing callback runs under closing protection. Its declarations are supplied structurally; its callback and closing checks are compiled. A negative check confirms that the internal disposer is not an external resumptive capability, and a second rejects using an operation interface to justify an arbitrary outside disposal. These are source-plan examples, not fully admitted Core programs.

SourceAnnotatedInitialInterfaces.lean uses a closed operation interface and structural declaration annotations to derive the initial scheduling premise. It then reuses existing annotated runtime assembly and common-event proofs: every supplied finite trace can finish or extend, and every terminal endpoint has exact-once owner discharge. The theorem still takes annotated expression typing, the finite initial check, structural completion, and signature agreement separately. General consuming declarations and complete initial-program admission remain open. This is a partial admission connection within the original one-shot target.

Retained operation interfaces at invocation

SourceScheduledRetainedInterfaces.lean annotates every ordinary pending plan and cleanup callback with its finite operation requirements, structural footprint and source declarations. The annotation follows all retained frame constructors, including both branches of a dormant capture. It stores no checked Local or Pending premise.

Interfaces.check checks each plan against its actual receiving suffix. A callback runs under the additional running boundary; a dormant saved segment receives its own waiting tail. Interfaces.compile derives the normal pending schedule by structural induction, reusing the direct source-interface compiler. The same annotation supplies closing-only callback interfaces and their source declarations. Closing still requires a separate finite check because removing saved handlers can change operation availability.

SourceScheduledInvocationInterfaces.lean uses these annotations at an actual owner cut. Resumption checks the saved segment, caller prefix and waiting tail at their recomposed receiving scopes. Disposal checks only saved callbacks, followed by the complete caller prefix and waiting tail. The existing recomposition theorems assemble those schedules and derive compatibility. Known continuation rights, the required permission and owner availability remain independent premises. Disposal additionally checks protection and the existing finite closing route. No old or target schedule is an input to either invocation theorem.

SourceScheduledInvocationInterfaceExamples.lean checks a caller-installed handler supplying a saved request and effectful cleanup without an outer provider. A complete local clause plan installs both scopes around resumption; another example uses the caller handler during disposal. Negative checks reject a nearer handler missing the operation, a missing provider, denied permission and a consumed owner. A further example passes normal scheduling but fails closing after its provider is removed.

These results discharge primitive invocation scheduling for the operation interface class. They do not complete general consuming declarations: the retained plans covered by Footprint still exclude free continuation invocations, and the runtime declaration discipline still uses the existing recipe grammar. Generating broader annotations from declarations and retaining them through selection and runtime execution remain required. These are source-plan proofs, not a claim of complete expression admission or Core correspondence.

Recursive continuation capability annotations

SourceScheduledCapabilityAnnotations.lean removes the operation-only restriction from retained source scheduling. The mutually inductive Code and Retained annotations follow the existing plan grammar and every retained-frame form. They retain actual owner cuts, request cuts, code and callbacks; they are independent of the action and phase maps. Neither annotation stores a Local, Pending, or successful whole-body transformer. Existing operation interfaces are reused as leaf annotations.

Code.Valid and Retained.Valid validate these data structurally. Invocation validation checks the selected owner's permission and availability separately, then checks recursively retained source with that owner spent. Resumption uses the actual saved, caller and waiting pieces. Disposal uses the actual closing source and additionally checks protection and the closing route. Selected requests keep the existing structural captured-owner bounds, capture guard and recursive closing checks. Handler requirements are checked at their actual receiving scopes. Resource bodies retain the universal fresh-identity rule; this is not a claim of a finite executable checker for arbitrary source families.

The mutual compilation theorem constructs the existing Local and Pending derivations by induction on these annotations. It reuses selected-request compilation, the invocation rules, recomposition and compatibility theorems. Recursive annotations can therefore contain further outside continuation uses at any finite depth. No new operational transition or ownership axiom is added.

SourceScheduledOutsideInvocations.lean checks resumed code that invokes a distinct outside owner, including a mixture of resumption and disposal. The same annotation is rejected when the owner is reused or the outside action lacks permission. A closed plan also checks a selected disposer capturing armed effectful cleanup; this is broader than the earlier special empty-capture pattern. These examples establish source scheduling, not rich expression typing or reachability of an initial program.

SourceAnnotatedInitialInterfaces.lean now accepts validated recursive annotations when assembling the initial runtime invariant. Its generalized finite-progress and terminal-accounting theorems reuse the common-event proofs. Earlier closed operation interfaces are wrappers around this connection. initial_atPackets_from_annotation also constructs the stronger packet-aware execution invariant for general declaration policies. It compiles the same validated annotation under the supplied policy laws, constructs its admitted initial snapshot from the checked bounds, and derives admission of the empty packet stack. Existing initial assembly and AtPlan.empty_packets supply the runtime result; no runtime invariant is an input. Rich source typing, the finite initial check, completion typing and signature agreement remain independent inputs.

General declaration admission remains open. These annotations are indexed by actual receiving forests; the declaration rules must generate them and retain their meaning through source transformations, selection and runtime use. In particular, the earlier finite-safety specialization uses the existing declaration recipe discipline; the general packet-aware construction exposes declaration policy laws. Both retain the separate rich source, finite initial check, completion and signature-agreement premises. Neither complete source admission nor general Core correspondence follows from this connection.

Reconstruction and transport of general capability annotations

SourceScheduledCapabilityCuts.lean splits a validated retained annotation at an actual forest boundary. The saved source retains its real receiving suffix, including recursively dormant source, branches and outside-owner calls. retained_at_cut authenticates both pieces against the actual handler cut. Resumption and disposal decomposition reuse the same split; disposal retains the closing callback annotations. The proofs reuse existing scope, hint, forest and operation-interface equations.

SourceScheduledCapabilityReconstruction.lean proves the converse of the existing annotation compiler by mutual induction on Local and Pending. Requests recover the selected source cut; invocation cases decompose the recursively reconstructed retained annotation. All other constructors reuse their induction hypotheses. The only translation premise concerns declaration evidence. This covers every current structural scheduling constructor, not only operation interfaces or resumption chains.

local_annotated_iff and pending_annotated_iff establish equivalence between these structural scheduling judgments and existence of validated annotations, under the stated declaration laws. retained_append_iff reuses established ordered recomposition. annotations_at_cut constructs both captured and waiting annotations from the current whole-source derivation and the actual cut. It does not require annotations or scheduling checks for a successor.

SourceScheduledCapabilityTransport.lean reuses neutral expansion and structural handler adaptation to obtain validated annotations at changed receivers. Neutral expansion and handler adaptation retain generic declaration policies with the stated laws. The generalized SourceScheduledHandlerAdaptation.sound_all_with preserves the supplied declaration evidence by the same mutual induction. Retained requests use the policy-independent schedule rule directly; newly intercepted requests transport their existing callback evidence through the source-level declaration laws. Structural adaptation is still required. The retained result reuses the established equality of owner lists, preserving order and multiplicity.

These are scheduling results. Reconstruction may omit optional handler bound metadata, so it is not preservation of Snapshot.Admitted or StackBounds.Admitted. An existing scheduling derivation is still needed; this is not complete initial source admission. Generating the broader bounded capture input, deriving every reachable input check, and integrating the broader declaration policy through execution remain open. In particular, the annotation grammar is general, but the current bounded capture-input generator still has operation-only and resumption-chain branches.

Capability phases preserve the actual annotations

SourceScheduledCapabilityPhases.lean proves permission and phase transport for the same Code and Retained values. Permission extension retains existing entries. Phase extension need retain availability only for live owners in the actual receiving forest, including recursively dormant captures. Mutual induction reuses the existing selected-owner, resumed-owner, closing-owner and spending lemmas. Operation requirements remain independent of these capability checks.

Fresh allocation preserves validation when the new permission entry was absent. Spending that new outer owner also preserves the earlier annotation when the owner is absent from its receiving forest's live-owner inventory. These results cover general branches and outside-owner calls. They do not reconstruct the annotation, so every optional bound field remains the same data.

This closes the permission/phase transport obligation for general annotations. Changing the actual receiving forest is a separate obligation: the current reconstruction-based receiver transport can still omit bound metadata. Neither phase transport nor the generalized adaptation policy establishes the broader captured-source validity proof or complete initial source admission.

Capture bounds independent of source scheduling

SourceConsumingCaptureSnapshots.lean separates bound-data construction from captured-source scheduling. The selected bounded declaration supplies an admitted SourcePlanBounds.Annotation for its actual clause plan, using the existing nested-bound admission proof. The actual capture cut then moves the original saved and waiting metadata into a live continuation through capture_snapshot and Captured.admitted.

Bounded.capture_snapshot therefore constructs an admitted successor snapshot for arbitrary captured forests and the stated nested declaration policy. Its result is indexed by the exact selected plan and exact saved/waiting pieces. It assumes neither a successful captured-source check nor validation of a future clause annotation. This is bound-data admission only; it does not prove that the selected clause can execute safely at that receiver.

The current-plan bound projection intentionally excludes saved/caller continuation annotations. General capture integration can carry the declaration's admitted current bounds beside the independently derived scheduling annotation, while retaining the original pending snapshot. It need not first prove that reconstruction preserves every optional annotation field. The existing bounded runtime wrapper for operation-only and chain inputs still uses the narrower GeneratedCapture evidence with an ofCode projection. The general certificate connection below uses the independent construction directly.

Certified capture with independent bound snapshots

SourceAnnotatedStoredCertifiedCapture.lean connects an existing structural Capture certificate to the actual allocator. The certificate names the exact source cut and selected clause and contains recursive capability annotations. Its Valid check remains an explicit input. Cut and clause uniqueness derive the allocator's legacy requirement premise; no universal successful-body function is supplied by the caller.

CapturedBounds packages current-plan and retained bound data independently of capability annotations. The selected installed packet supplies the bounded declaration; Bounded.capture_snapshot supplies its actual admitted snapshot. capture_from_certificate_retaining reuses both existing allocation branches and returns the exact annotated successor, joint source/packet typing, physical packet movement, ownership balance, owner inventory and effect-row inclusion. It imposes no operation-only or resumption-chain restriction on captured source.

capture_from_certificate_snapshot exposes the admitted successor snapshot and installed packet admission in the same result. Existing cut recomposition and StackBounds.Admitted.capture supply those proofs. The raw step and successor shape are retained explicitly, without equating targets through erasure.

Capture certificates, typed allocation data and both raw allocation branches are parameterized by declaration policies. Capture.requirements_with uses DeclarationLaws to compile the certificate's structural declaration evidence into the scheduling admission and certification policies. DeclarationProjection connects admission to certification when source checks are erased. These laws concern declarations; they contain no future execution or successful clause-body premise. The original recipe certificate compiler is a specialization of the same proof. Contract refinement, substitution, ownership and packet movement reuse the existing proofs under these policy parameters.

SourceAnnotatedStoredCaptureAssembly.lean factors the common completion, ledger, usage and ownership argument out of the recipe and bounded capture proofs. It combines an actual raw transition and its typed successor with one current action/source witness. It is an internal preservation lemma, not a new source-admission rule. The existing disposal certificate extracted from current source is now generic in declaration policies.

SourceAnnotatedStoredCertifiedExecutionCapture.lean uses that shared assembly for general structural capture certificates. capture_certificate_retaining pairs validation with the same existential action map, usage, source and retained-completion proofs. It returns the combined successor with exact packet movement, ownership balance and effect-row inclusion. capture_certificate_snapshot_admitted also retains the actual admitted snapshot, installed packet admission, exact forest and successor shape. It does not require an operation-only or owner-chain shape for the captured source.

This does not derive every certificate's validation from initial source, change the common finite-event theorem's policy, or establish complete initial admission. The concrete policy laws below instantiate the static interface. Broader finite execution must still derive the checks at reachable captures; adding a successful capture premise to each event would not discharge that source-admission obligation.

Concrete consuming declaration policies

SourceConsumingDeclarationCertification.lean derives declaration certification from the existing consuming-clause syntax. Operation prefixes and callbacks reuse recipe certification and signature transport. Handler cases use the supplied static declaration laws; resource cases follow the existing fresh-binder derivation. No receiving forest, owner phase, successful capture or future body check occurs in the premise.

SourceConsumingDeclarationPolicies.lean defines a concrete cumulative family of policies. Layer zero is the existing recipe policy. Each next layer retains earlier evidence and admits a bounded consuming declaration whose nested declarations use the preceding layer. Its source derivation starts in the empty resource world, so existing world weakening supplies certification in every actual world. This is a condition on declaration evidence; completeness for arbitrary source annotations has not been proved. The index counts evidence layers. It adds no computation form or runtime interpretation layer.

Induction proves DeclarationLaws at every finite layer. Admission and capability reconstruction use the same judgment, and projection supplies the required connection to certification. The laws use the existing structural Bounded judgment; they do not replace missing capture validation with a future-success predicate. They can instantiate the generic capability compiler and raw capture interface, while continuation permissions and phases remain separate checks.

SourceConsumingDeclarationTransport.lean translates the existing syntax derivations along a pointwise implication between declaration policies. The proof follows the existing world-weakening induction. It preserves actual clause plans, rights, operation requirements and recorded bounds, including nested bounds beneath resources. The transformation is a structural function on the annotation data.

SourceConsumingPolicyInstallation.lean combines policy inclusion and world weakening. bounded_at_world keeps the same bounds when the declaration is used under the next policy. handler_admitted checks the actual installed packet with those exact bounds and plans. The existing typed-frame install theorem also accepts general scheduling policies.

SourceConsumingDeclarationPolicyExamples.lean checks a handler-wrapped resumption accepted by the new policy and rejected by the old recipe grammar. It also derives certification for every resource world, compiles a handler installation through the existing source scheduler and retains the original bounds at runtime worlds. This is evidence of broader static admission, not a complete initial-program or finite-execution theorem. General captured-source generation and derivation of every reachable capture check remain outstanding.

Direct consuming clauses over general captures

SourceConsumingDirectCapture.lean removes the operation-only and owner-chain restrictions on captured source for clauses that retain the receiver or add builtin resource scopes and pure cleanup at consumption. Body.Direct follows the existing clause syntax: resume, dispose, operation-prefix sequencing, choice, resource allocation and cleanup whose callback checking plan is .pure and whose callback dependency list is empty. Prefixes retain the existing operation-footprint grammar; the restriction still excludes handler and effectful-cleanup wrappers around consumption. It does not restrict the syntax or owner references in the captured continuation.

Bounded.selected_direct extracts the exact selected body's structural admission, direct-source derivation and declared bounds. capture_direct then constructs a validated Capture certificate from the current request annotation and whole retained-source annotation. The actual cut supplies saved and waiting pieces. Disposal scheduling and its protection/route checks come from the current request, using the selected clause's permitted disposal action. The handler's outer operation requirements, permission-map freshness and absence of the new owner from the current inventory remain explicit premises.

The proof reuses existing neutral receiver transport and capability phase transport. Inserting the new spent-owner marker preserves recursive calls to older owners, including owners outside the captured prefix. Source induction handles choices and prefixes. Resource cases extend the resource world and insert the actual cell into the caller context, including beneath running protection on disposal. The cleanup case reuses neutral expansion for the actual callback frame, including under running protection on disposal; the caller's operation interface and callback requirement check come from the original clause-local judgment. No new cleanup transport assumption is introduced. The internal generate helper receives the transported pieces; the public capture theorem derives those pieces and assumes no validated future clause or successful capture event.

SourceScheduledCapabilityProviders.lean constructs retained annotations after resource-world extension and provider insertion. It reuses the existing scheduling transport and annotation reconstruction. The provider and pending-site proofs now accept declaration policy parameters without changing their induction arguments. No target-source validation or provider-specific declaration law is a premise. As with general reconstruction, this does not promise identity of optional bound fields.

SourceConsumingDirectCaptureExamples.lean checks a captured choice whose two branches resume an owner in the waiting tail. That owner is absent from the captured inventory. An operation-only interface for the saved branch is impossible, while the new generator produces its outer capture certificate. Spending the outside owner makes the original source validation fail. A resource-wrapped clause allocates and reads a cell before resuming that same general captured source; its annotation is generated from the original source checks. A pure cleanup wrapper now composes with that resource case, and a separate disposal example generates the same cleanup frame around abandonment of the saved branch. A negative admission theorem confirms that cleanup does not grant disposal to a resume-only continuation. These are source-checking examples, not complete runtime traces.

This closes the resource-wrapper and pure-cleanup cases of general captured-source generation. Handler and effectful-cleanup wrappers still need their general transport derivation; the chain-specific generator is not a proof for those arbitrary captures. Complete initial admission and broader finite-execution preservation remain open. The full one-shot milestone is incomplete.

Handler boundary obligation for general captured source

SourceConsumingHandlerInterference.lean identifies a necessary condition for extending the general capture generator through handler wrappers. It reuses the existing closing-interference proof and the capability compiler; it does not add a new operational rule.

The example has a saved G request and an armed callback that reads cell 4. G's handler, in the waiting suffix, may dispose. The original source validates: cell 4 survives G's capture and continues to supply the callback. The consuming clause installs a resumptive handler for that cell effect before resuming. Operation availability still holds, and owner 19 has its resume permission and an available phase. The clause's local operation-bound judgment also holds. Nevertheless, the next G capture would include the new handler. Disposal removes that handler, changing the callback's original route to the surviving cell.

restored_source_rejected and clause_annotation_rejected rule out every valid target annotation for the respective retained source and consuming clause. The rejection holds under every declaration policy satisfying the stated static compilation laws. This is stronger than failure of one attempted generator. It is a source-level boundary example, not a counterexample to the existing runtime preservation theorem: operation_route_rejects confirms that the earlier generator rejects the input. G is disposing and is omitted from the clause's declared F-only operation bound. The example rules out replacing that authentication with old general source validity and local clause admission alone.

selected_disposal_requires_shield derives the existing finite shield check from any validated selected disposing request. closing_iff_boundary_exclusion factors the exact insertion check through SourceHandlerInterference.exposed: given the old closing judgment, the installed effect must be absent from that boundary's exposed callback list. closing_from_boundary_bound permits a declared over-approximation authenticated against the actual list. bypassed_guard_from_boundary_bound uses that evidence to construct the new capture guard for a request handled beyond the inserted handler. Neither construction assumes a successful target schedule.

The list records callback-routing dependencies. Its multiplicity does not count continuation uses. A nearer builtin can shield an overlapping effect, as the positive example checks. This closing condition does not discharge new operation selection, declaration requirements or recursive retained-source scheduling. Carrying and preserving boundary evidence through the general consuming-source judgments remains open, alongside the cleanup-wrapper case. Existing source admission has not been broadened to accept the rejected example.

Callback boundary composition and consumption

SourceHandlerBoundaryComposition.lean proves composition and extraction for the existing exposed summary and Shielded structural judgment. It introduces no second callback analysis. For a prefix followed by a tail, an effect is exposed exactly when it is exposed in the tail, or it is exposed in the prefix and the tail supplies no builtin for it. Dormant captures receive the same tail in this calculation.

boundary_append_iff therefore splits a whole-scope bound into a tail bound and a prefix bound enlarged by the tail's builtin providers. The enlargement is necessary: an empty whole-scope summary does not imply an empty prefix summary. The checked example has a dormant callback reading cell 4, supplied by the receiver; detaching the prefix exposes that dependency. boundary_at_cut derives these two bounds at the actual selected handler cut, using the existing cut reconstruction theorem. boundary_recompose transports the prefix bound to a replacement receiver with sufficient providers and its own authenticated boundary bound.

The same module proves that resumption and disposal introduce no new exposed callback effects. Closing retains normally visible builtins and may reveal additional ones from dormant captures. The closing proof uses that inclusion; the consumption proofs then reuse prefix composition. shielded_resume and shielded_dispose preserve the existing structural judgment, and boundary_resume_at_owner and boundary_dispose_at_owner preserve a finite bound at an actual selected owner cut. The saved scope can contain arbitrary recursive captures. Permission and phase checks remain independent.

bypassed_guard_from_composed_boundary connects these bounds to the existing handler guard transport. Its separation check includes the receiver providers, so a whole-scope bound cannot conceal a dependency exposed at insertion. This is a sufficient bound rule; the exact local shielding check still allows overlapping effects when a nearer builtin supplies them.

These results establish boundary-summary preservation for the stated scope transformations. They do not establish preservation for every execution step: code may register further callbacks, and newly intercepted operations require their own declaration and capture checks. Generating general handler and cleanup annotations from source declarations, carrying their evidence through all execution families, and complete initial admission remain open.

SourceCleanupClosingInsertion.lean identifies the exact additional closing obligation when a clause registers an effectful callback around a captured computation. inserted_closing_iff proves that structural equivalence, and check_closing_inserted factors the executable check into the old check and a finite check of the new callback effects. check_capture_inserted gives the corresponding exact capture-check equation at a selected outside handler: non-disposing requests add no closing obligation. guard_transport derives the new guard from the old guard and the primitive route evidence; guard_requires_routes proves necessity. request_requires_routes derives the same requirement from any validated request annotation under declaration policies satisfying the existing compilation laws.

The source-level counterexample validates the original disposing request and the callback separately. Inserting the callback still invalidates the request: its selected capture contains a handler that supplies the callback operation, but disposal removes that handler. request_annotation_rejected rules out any validated request annotation for the resulting scope. inserted_owners retains the exact continuation-owner inventory, and pending_within preserves existing pending-code bounds. This supplies the route condition and ownership connection for general effectful-cleanup transport. It does not yet generate callback schedules through every recursive invocation or authenticate the route evidence from consuming declarations. SourceScheduledCleanupInsertion.lean adds structural insertion for an actual callback plan and its declared effect list. Prefix and suffix composition retain that plan. route_capability relates existing source routes to capability lookup. Matching routes preserve the operation check through two prefixes with a shared outside receiver. A negative example has an available callback operation and a vacuous closing guard because its declared needs omit the operation. Closing removes its handler, so the callback check fails; Covered rejects the missing declaration. General cleanup insertion still needs to preserve these source interfaces, coverage and normal checks, and to derive the primitive guards while transporting arbitrary existing local code. Another example retains an existing dormant effectful callback while inserting the cell-reading callback. The conditional generation theorem below supplies an enclosing induction for arbitrary existing annotated code. Source admission must still discharge its generated primitive checks at later requests. SourceScheduledCleanupGeneration.lean constructs annotations after insertion of one actual cleanup callback by mutual induction over the existing Code and Retained annotations. A caller does not supply an adaptation derivation or a successful target source judgment.

Checks has only operation-requirement leaves, closing-route leaves, conjunction, an empty case and the existing fresh-resource quantification. Generation is proved as existence of annotated results, using classical choice for families and exact cut witnesses; no executable annotation-inference algorithm is claimed.

The induction covers operation interfaces, selected requests, resume, dispose, sequencing, choice, handlers, cleanup and resources, together with every retained frame and recursively dormant source. Existing operation requirements are preserved through cleanup insertion. A new callback contributes its operation requirements at the actual registration receiver. Selected requests retain their exact handler modes and owner bounds, while generating a new closing-route check and recursively transforming their actual closing source. Owner invocation uses the existing owner-cut and full-prefix recomposition proofs; the selected saved forest remains identical. Rights and consumed phases are inherited from the original validation, rather than added as new obligations. Handler construction copies its existing declaration evidence and optional bound data.

Old callbacks may contain recursive continuation uses: their existing capability annotations are traversed, so this theorem does not restrict them to operation footprints. The newly inserted callback uses the existing footprint and source declaration interface of consuming cleanup clauses. Its source typing and effect coverage remain admission obligations. CodeResult.scheduled and RetainedResult.scheduled reuse the existing compiler to derive the actual local or pending schedule once the returned checks hold.

The regressions preserve the earlier safety boundary. Every sound generated result for the removed-handler example rejects its additional checks. A concrete result for an effectful cell-reading cleanup around an owner resumption preserves validity with one satisfied operation check. The same check cannot make a consumed owner resumable. The concrete result witnesses the constructor pattern; it does not assert that an opaque existential choice computes that exact tree.

This closes the constructor coverage of conditional cleanup annotation generation. It does not prove that the new checks pass for arbitrary previously valid source; that unconditional claim is refuted by the existing counterexample. The contextual cleanup rule below incorporates these structural obligations. Uniform declaration admission and derivation of every reachable condition remain open. General nested-handler generation, complete initial and reachable capture admission, preservation of admitted bound snapshots under broader execution, and the final milestone audit remain open. The earlier conditional generator and Context.cleanup remain separate sound evidence. This completes the contextual rule and its soundness connection for these clause forms. It does not prove that a declaration can be checked once for every future capture or derive all reachable conditions from initial source admission. The handler rule below extends this contextual judgment. The older Body.Direct fragment remains unchanged. Broader finite execution must still retain admitted bound snapshots and packets; resource transport here does not establish that metadata invariant. New interception from original source

SourceScheduledCleanupGeneration.lean now strengthens its existing mutual generation proof with structural rechecking. The proof covers all source constructors, including selected disposing requests, recursive continuation uses, dormant captures, cleanup callbacks and fresh-resource families. It reuses the existing cut, owner-partition, operation-lookup and closing transport lemmas. The result's old target-validity guarantee remains available, but clients no longer need to infer structural rechecking from target validity.

SourceScheduledCleanupReceiverPlans.lean defines ReceiverPlan over the original retained source and a new receiver. It keeps every retained frame. Operation interfaces and installed-handler requirements carry lookup-preservation equalities; pending and callback code carry the generated expression plans. Its check tree contains only the existing primitive operation and closing conditions, with resource quantification where needed. receiver_plan constructs such a plan for cleanup insertion over the full retained grammar, reusing the mutual expression generator for code sites. ReceiverPlan.rechecking derives the existing, metadata-preserving ReceiverChange judgment from the original validity and successful primitive checks.

At.cleanup_planned is a derived theorem for the existing cleanupSource constructor, not a new admission axiom or a replacement source grammar. It constructs both permitted-action receiver changes from supplied plans and their checks, then reuses the existing recursive cleanup rule. The outside-owner example in SourceConsumingStructuralCleanupExamples.lean checks an explicit plan with a cell-reading callback, derives contextual admission and scheduling, and compiles the resulting receiver judgment while retaining exact original metadata. Owner permissions and consumed phases still come from the independent source validation.

These results reduce cleanup rechecking to the generator's primitive conditions; they do not prove that every generated plan passes. The existing extra-false-check counterexample still holds for the strengthened result type. Inference completeness, derivation and retention of those conditions from initial source admission at all reachable contexts, and the corresponding general construction for handler insertion remain open. No broader finite-execution claim follows from this local generation result.

Structural admission descent and entry

SourceConsumingAdmissionDescent.lean proves At.descendants by induction over the existing structural admission judgment. Its Descendants definition inspects the immediate source constructor; it is an inversion result, not an additional admission premise. A sequence exposes its rest and a choice exposes both branches at the same receiver. Handlers and cleanup expose a child context with the exact installed frame and caller interface. Resources expose a child for every fresh identity in the extended resource world. Saved and waiting forests and owner permissions and phases keep their original indices.

The induction covers structural cleanup and any number of sameReceiver rules. Descent transports through a witness change using equality of the caller interface and agreement of retained metadata. It neither chooses a replacement conditional check tree nor reconstructs a child admission proof from a successful target annotation. The checked handler, cleanup and resource projections inherit the child's Body.BoundCheck from the corresponding part of the parent's check. The handler declaration check and cleanup callback completion check remain separate parts of that parent check.

SourceConsumingAdmissionEntries.lean connects these projections to the existing EnteredHandler, EnteredCleanup and EnteredResource relations. It takes an actual entry relation whose source snapshot contains the source body's exact boundAnnotation, derives the child's structural admission and finite check, and identifies the same event's successor snapshot. Handler entry retains the exact body bounds even when the installed clause-plan witness differs with equal signatures. Cleanup entry queues the exact callback annotation. Resource entry uses the event's fresh identity and retains the existing world-weakened pending annotations. These are connections to the established relations, with no new machine transition.

SourceConsumingAdmissionDescentExamples.lean reuses the existing two-handler example and descends through cleanup, a fresh resource, a sequence and a choice. The two resulting consumption branches are schedulable for every fresh identity and every valid initial annotation witness at the same receiver. Another example descends through explicit cleanup over a nonempty saved outside-owner invocation. An existing handler entry relation also yields scheduling and exact successor bounds through the new connection. No child At derivation is supplied separately in these examples.

SourceConsumingBoundTransport.lean separately transports the finite clause-bound check. Resource-world extension reuses Body.world_weaken, Interfaces.world_weaken and the existing interface check invariance and composition lemmas. Permission and phase transport need preserve only the bound owner's permission entry and availability. Other owner entries can change because this finite judgment does not check the saved continuation's code. A separate induction proves that every checked consuming body requires its bound owner to be available, including resource bodies: the existing fresh-name theorem supplies a fresh identity, so their universal check cannot become vacuous.

The example finite_checks_do_not_validate_saved_source checks that distinction. The original finite bound check survives world extension from [4] to [4, 8] and spending outside owner 37. The original saved invocation of owner 37 rejects that spent phase by the existing negative theorem. This does not exhibit a reachable-program failure or refute the ownership invariant. It establishes that finite bound transport alone cannot supply contextual source preservation; the existing retained-source and ownership evidence must also be used.

This closes immediate source descent and its connection to the three entry relations. It does not prove preservation during execution of a sequence prefix: that execution may allocate resources or change continuation phases. The entry lemmas require structural source admission and finite checks at the actual entry state; deriving those facts for every reachable entry remains open. Broader-policy finite execution, complete initial-program admission and the milestone audit remain outstanding. Core remains a correspondence assessment; no Core alignment or excluded continuation target is included.

No new induction or ownership proof is introduced.

Expression.waiting_selected covers the complementary case where the selected capture stays fixed and its waiting suffix changes. It reuses replace_waiting and guard_same_capture to derive selection and the guard, and retains the original owner bound. Only receiver rechecking of the original closing annotation remains as a recursive premise. The theorem accepts no target guard or independently valid target callback. It permits arbitrary changed waiting forests for which that structural recursive premise is derived.

SourceScheduledBypassedRecheckingExamples.lean checks insertion of a handler sharing an armed callback's effect after the callback's original builtin provider. The derived rule admits that overlap, and the whole saved source is rechecked with exact retained bounds. Moving the same handler before the provider fails the capture guard. A second example retains an original closing callback that resumes another live owner, beyond operation-only callback footprints. The original closing compilation is reused; no target callback validity is assumed after insertion. Another example uses waiting_selected with an actual effectful closing callback and generates the request at the changed waiting suffix.

This discharges the bypassed selected-request case. It does not yet derive all expression or retained rechecking judgments from initial source admission. Requests intercepted by the new handler, recursive closing-source transport for waiting changes, and reconstruction through other source constructors remain parts of that proof. The one-shot milestone remains incomplete.

Rechecking requests at non-disposing interpretations

Expression.capability in SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean reuses the existing SourceContextualClauses.RequestCapability judgment. It accepts any original annotation of the same atomic request when the new receiver supplies a builtin or a resume-only handler with both ordinary and protected modes. Exact nearest lookup authenticates that capability. A missing operation does not fall through a nearer same-effect handler.

The earlier Expression.operations rule could recheck only an original operation-only annotation and retained its requirement list. The new rule also accepts an original selected request whose old interpretation could dispose. Its target annotation uses the singleton operation requirement. The existing mutual compiler proves validity and preserves current-plan bounds: an atomic request has no current-syntax handler-bound annotation. This does not discard retained callback code or assert equality of saved request-closing proofs. World extension and phase restriction follow the same existing inductions. The rule grants no continuation permission and does not restore a spent owner.

ReceiverChange.request in SourceScheduledReceiverRechecking.lean handles a retained atomic request independently of the annotation constructor chosen by an earlier compilation. Case analysis on its original annotation reuses either the operation interface or Expression.capability. The existing receiver compiler then preserves the complete retained bound snapshot.

SourceScheduledBypassedRecheckingExamples.lean checks a selected cell disposer changing to a builtin, a saved disposing request changing to a resumptive handler while its effectful cleanup remains checked, and protected request rechecking. Negative proofs reject missing operations, disposing targets for this capability rule, and omitted protected modes. Disposing requests remain available through the separate selected and fresh capture rules with their closing obligations.

SourceConsumingWaitingRecheckingExamples.lean composes two non-neutral waiting reconstructions. The first changes a saved request from a resumptive interpretation to a disposer. The second installs a resumptive handler before that disposer. It accepts the actual existentially generated first context, derives rechecking without assuming its annotation constructor, reconstructs the queued source record, and generates valid resumption code. Saved metadata agreement composes across both changes; waiting metadata follows structural provenance.

These results extend request and source-context reconstruction. They do not prove a typed execution of the examples or derive all rechecking obligations from initial source admission. General recursive capture-source generation and broader-policy finite execution remain open.

Fresh capture from structural closing

Expression.reinterface in SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean permits an original operation-only annotation to use another structural request footprint for the same plan. The new footprint must pass its finite operation check at the new receiver. The original declaration annotation remains intact. The existing mutual compiler preserves the original current-plan bounds, and the world-extension and phase-transport proofs include the new rule.

This matters when an annotation conservatively lists an operation that its actual syntax does not need. Removing a handler during closing may remove that operation capability while leaving every actual request supported. Reusing the old requirement list would reject this source. A new footprint proof justifies changing the list; merely omitting a failing requirement does not.

Closing.at_fresh_handler and Expression.fresh_closing in SourceScheduledStructuralClosing.lean connect the original normal prefix's structural closing derivation to a newly intercepting handler. They reuse the existing equality of closing scopes, hints and actual forests: adding the delimiter contributes neither callback code nor an owner. This equality includes dormant saved branches. The existing fresh-request rule then consumes the derived rechecking judgment. No new closing traversal or ownership proof is introduced.

SourceScheduledFreshClosingExamples.lean checks a prefix with an effectful resource callback and a callback that resumes an outside owner. Its original operation annotation contains a conservative requirement supplied by an internal handler. Closing erases that handler, and the old requirement list fails. A precise footprint for the same callback passes; the outside continuation is separately rechecked using the original resumption annotation. Structural closing generates the fresh request and preserves exact canonical callback metadata. Negative proofs reuse the existing source compiler to reject omission of the actual request, and the original phase check to reject invocation of an already-consumed outside owner.

The input still includes original normal-source validity, the finite capture guard and pending-owner bound, and structural closing of that original source. The example constructs its closing derivation recursively; no valid target callback annotation is supplied. Deriving such closing and source-rechecking derivations for every reachable capture remains open. These are source/context proofs, not an initial-source typed execution theorem.

Separate ownership bounds for disposal callbacks

SourceScheduledClosingOwners.lean defines CallbacksWithin by the retained scope structure. It checks every cleanup body, including bodies in dormant saved branches, and omits ordinary pending code that disposal discards. Each body uses the existing Within judgment over source dependencies, including nested computations and fresh-resource families. The new judgment checks owner references independently of effect requirements, permission modes and one-shot phases.

Local.disposal_owner_bounds derives two bounds from the existing scheduling judgment for a request and its actual disposing handler cut:

  • PendingWithin bounds ordinary pending-code references by the captured segment's owners. This reuses checked_request_owners.
  • CallbacksWithin bounds callback references by the surviving receiver's owners. This follows from the request's actual closing schedule.

The distinction is necessary because closing recursively removes every live owner from the captured segment. owners_closing_empty proves that fact. Pending.closing_owner_bound reuses the existing ordered pending decomposition and invocation checks to derive the callback bound. Closing.callback_owners and CaptureSource.callback_owners connect it to structural source closing and the authenticated original capture. None adds a successful-target premise to source admission. Callback bounds split and recompose over ordered append, survive resource-world extension, and are equivalent before and after the closing traversal.

An owner inventory also contains dormant owners, so membership alone does not establish an active invocation target. OwnerCut.closing_prefix preserves an actual active cut in the surviving receiver when any closed prefix is added; the selected saved body and tail remain exact. Closing cannot shadow that selection because its owner inventory is empty. The mixed-callback example in SourceScheduledFreshClosingExamples.lean now uses this general cut lemma when rechecking its outside-owner invocation. Permission, phase and recursive restored-source checks remain independent.

OwnerCut.survives_closing also derives the target cut from the original active cut, membership in the surviving receiver and the existing unique-owner invariant. Uniqueness separates the prefix's owners from the receiver's owners; OwnerCut.drop_prefix then locates the original selection in the receiver. Closing preserves that selection with its exact saved body and tail. The target cut is a conclusion, not an input. This resolves the active-selection part of callback transport under those premises; it does not establish the recursive source checks required after invoking the selected continuation.

SourceScheduledClosingOwnerExamples.lean checks a contrary case. A normally valid callback resumes owner 37 inside the segment that a fresh disposing handler captures. The request passes its capture guard and ordinary pending-owner bound, but the surviving receiver has no owner 37. The callback bound fails, and the general request theorem excludes every valid target annotation, not just a particular generator result. A positive example retains the earlier mixed callbacks using a surviving outside owner.

This is a source/context obstruction, not an unsafe typed execution. The new bound is necessary, not sufficient: it does not derive active owner cuts, permissions, phases, operation compatibility or recursive source rechecking from membership. Incorporating sufficient callback conditions into initial structural admission and proving their preservation remain open.

SourceScheduledClosingTransport.lean now connects canonical closing compilation to captured-owner retirement. Closing.compile_retiring first derives the actual closing annotation from the original source and structural closing judgment. It then reuses the general annotation phase theorem, restricted to owners in the surviving receiver. The existing pointwise spendAll_at equation supplies their unchanged availability. Permissions use the same action map, and the exact canonical callback metadata remains unchanged.
