CaptureSource.compile_retiring derives the required separation from the original capture's actual cut and unique-owner invariant, then transports the original request's checked closing annotation. It accepts any retired subset of captured owners, including an intermediate subset. Neither proof assumes a valid target annotation or requires the discarded normal source to remain valid at the later phases. This is phase stability of closing source; the existing operational trace and ledger proofs still govern when retirement occurs and whether each owner is consumed exactly once.

The retirement example in SourceScheduledClosingOwnerExamples.lean includes ordinary code that resumes captured owner 19, plus the resource and outside-owner-37 callbacks. The original source is valid before retirement and provably invalid after owner 19 is consumed. Structural closing drops its ordinary code and generates a valid annotation at those later phases, retaining both callbacks and their exact metadata. Thus retirement transport is applied to the generated closing source, not to the discarded normal source. General closing generation and recursive receiver rechecking remain the missing source connection; the retirement phase change introduces no additional condition beyond the proved owner separation.

Protected-mode request rechecking

A request crossing a running callback captures its protection marker. The existing capture guard therefore excludes disposal of that segment. SourceScheduledProtectedRechecking.lean proves this by reusing disposing_capture, including for an arbitrary bypassed prefix before the running marker. protected_capture_check characterizes the remaining finite check exactly: disposal is disabled, the protected effect row is present, and the matching protected source-body family is present. Nearest selection is still the actual selected cut; an unavailable nearest operation cannot fall through to another handler.

The existing reusable RequestCapability deliberately requires both ordinary and protected modes. It is stronger than this local request check. The new Expression.nonDisposing source rule in SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean checks the actual cut, capture guard and disabled disposal. Its compiler creates the existing selected-request annotation: the disabled permission eliminates both disposal obligations. It retains the exact original request bounds and adds no source-computation or runtime rule. General permission/phase transport and resource-world transport include this source-rechecking rule.

Expression.protected_request derives disabled disposal from the selected protected segment. Expression.crosses_cleanup authenticates that segment using the existing prefix-cut theorem and any prefix bypassed by the request. Neither theorem needs a target closing annotation or a successful target schedule. Builtin requests continue to use the existing operation-capability rule. A request intercepted by a handler before the running marker does not satisfy this crossing case and retains its recursive source obligations.

SourceScheduledProtectedRecheckingExamples.lean checks a callback under a changed outside interpretation offering only the protected mode. Its original source is valid; rechecking generates valid request and closing annotations with exact original bounds and callback metadata. The uniform capability correctly rejects the same target because its ordinary mode is absent. Additional negative cases reject ordinary use, a missing protected body family and disposal across the running marker.

These are source/receiver proofs, not authorization to exchange interpretations or ignore the existing capture-route checks. Initial admission must still supply the actual protected-mode availability after a receiver change. For this crossing case, however, the recursive fresh-disposal branch is impossible rather than a further ambient-source obligation. The following request and caller sections supply further structural cases; general reconstruction must still derive their recursive premises from admission.

Requests selected inside an unchanged prefix

SourceScheduledInternalRechecking.lean handles selection before a callback's running boundary. Cut.suffix appends an outside receiver while retaining the exact saved forest, contract and mode families. It reuses waiting replacement, cut reconstruction and associativity. Cut.drop_suffix recovers the actual internal cut from an existing whole-source cut when lookup stops in the prefix. The proof uses the existing lookup-append equation, hint uniqueness and forest uniqueness to identify both the saved forest and the waiting decomposition. A new local cut is a conclusion, not an independent source premise.

An atomic request has two source annotation forms, handled separately:

  • Expression.internal_operations derives the precise target capability from the original operation footprint and validity. Footprint.request_member proves that even a weakened footprint includes the actual request. The same selected contract retains its two-mode capability when only its waiting receiver changes. Extra conservative requirements need not survive.
  • Expression.internal_selected retains the original selected capture, guard and owner bound. Only the original closing annotation is recursively rechecked at its new waiting receiver. This annotation is already a child of the original selected-request source; no new normal captured-source witness or independently validated target annotation is required.

The latter proof reuses Expression.same_capture_selected in SourceScheduledBypassedRechecking.lean. The existing waiting_selected entry point now delegates to that generalized two-cut theorem, so guard transport and receiver rechecking have one proof. The selected capture need not be syntactically the entire receiving prefix.

SourceScheduledInternalRecheckingExamples.lean checks both cases. An operation-only annotation lists a real internal request and an unused outside requirement; after removing that outside receiver, the old list fails but the actual request rechecks from its original footprint. The second example selects a local disposing handler before the running boundary. Its captured callback uses an outer effect, whose receiver changes to a handler offering only the protected mode. The original closing callback is reconstructed with crosses_cleanup, and the local request reuses its original capture guard and owner bound. The recursive receiver compiler also preserves exact callback metadata.

These results identify the request cases needed by general source reconstruction. They do not yet supply the whole mutual source-generation theorem. The selected case still requires structural receiver rechecking of its original closing child; callback owner invocations likewise require their original saved/caller source children to be reconstructed. Initial source admission and runtime retention must supply those recursive premises. No handler-exchange law follows from changing a receiver in these source/context examples.

Partial caller closing during continuation invocation

SourceScheduledPrefixClosing.lean defines PrefixClosing on the original retained caller and an explicit prefix boundary. It discards ordinary pending code, handlers and spent frames inside that prefix; retains cells, cleanup callbacks and running frames; and closes each dormant saved branch before the running remainder. At the boundary, receiver rechecking retains the suffix. The protected stopping rule also inserts the running marker introduced by disposal. No rule accepts a replacement caller or a valid target annotation as its premise.

PrefixClosing.rechecking embeds the traversal in the existing retained-source judgment. Its proof reuses Closing.rechecking, ReceiverChange.rechecking and forest associativity; it adds no runtime transition. surviving_owners proves that the resulting caller has exactly the suffix's live-owner list. Closing removes the prefix's owners, and the optional running marker adds none. compile_admitted reuses the general compiler and its structural metadata provenance theorem. The stronger compiler described below also proves exact canonical snapshot equality and carries original source-record payloads.

Expression.resume_closing_caller and dispose_closing_caller share this caller traversal. They take the original outside owner selection and the source annotated with its prefix extension. The existing owner-cut theorem supplies the new selection after closing. The selected saved forest and tail stay fixed; resumption rechecks the original saved-body child at its changed receiver, and disposal rechecks the original stored closing child. The original tail is reused unchanged. Permissions, availability and disposal guards remain obligations of original source validity and the existing compiler.

SourceScheduledPrefixClosingExamples.lean checks resumption with a nonempty saved body, a retained caller suffix and a closing prefix containing a dormant callback. Ordinary caller code requests a handler that cleanup removes; the traversal drops that code. The saved body requests a surviving handler, although its original conservative interface also listed the removed handler. Rechecking narrows that interface using the actual request footprint. The resulting source is valid, saved metadata is identical, and caller metadata remains admitted. A second case disposes an outside owner with a nonempty stored closing body and preserves that body's exact metadata. A spent outside owner remains rejected.

The negative case changes the saved body's actual request to the erased handler. The original body is valid, but lost_no_target excludes every valid annotation at the closing receiver, and lost_no_rechecking excludes receiver rechecking. This is a necessary source-admission distinction: unused conservative requirements may be removed; actual requests in a resumed saved body must remain available. The proof reuses the existing compiler and necessary request guard.

These are structural invocation cases, not a complete initial-source preservation theorem. The saved-body/closing-body receiver derivations and callback obligations must still follow from initial admission and remain available recursively. The original caller decomposition and exact metadata retention are connected below. Derivation from initial admission and integration into the broader runtime invariant remain open. These examples are source/context evidence, not complete initial executions or Core simulation.

Canonical partial closing and original caller decomposition

SourceScheduledPrefixRetention.lean strengthens partial closing to exact canonical metadata. The compiler splits the original snapshot with the existing Retained.splitAt, closes its prefix with forClosing, and appends the original suffix. BoundaryBounds has exactly two structural cases: the same suffix, or that same suffix wrapped in the disposal running marker. It cannot supply another suffix's code bounds.

PrefixClosing.compile_retaining constructs the source annotation and its exact snapshot together. Callback and dormant-body cases reuse the existing expression and closing compilers. The suffix reuses receiver compilation, and the dormant case reuses ordered retained recomposition. Retained.append_assoc proves the corresponding metadata associativity using the existing scope, hint and forest laws; it moves every recorded bound unchanged. Admission follows from the original snapshot's split, closing and append laws. No successor validity or successor metadata-admission premise is introduced.

SourceScheduledCallerDecomposition.lean connects an arbitrary original owner cut to this traversal. caller_unique uses deterministic owner lookup and forest append injectivity to identify the caller's scope, hints and actual forest. drop_prefix_retaining strengthens the existing outside-cut recovery with those equalities. prefix_cases then eliminates the original caller at that authenticated split, without a second cut induction.

Code.resume_caller_source and dispose_caller_source apply this elimination to the original source children. The resulting saved or closing child and caller child are heterogeneously equal to their original values. The entire rebuilt invocation annotation is equal to the original Code, not just its current bound projection. Thus the prefix traversal receives the original stored source, with only its dependent indices rewritten; no replacement source witness is chosen from validity alone.

SourceScheduledPrefixRecords.lean carries actual queued payloads through the same transformation. Records.forClosing drops ordinary pending prefix records, retains callback records, and visits dormant branches before their running tails. Its entry list is exactly the original list filtered to callback positions, preserving payload values, order and multiplicity. Record splitting reconstructs the entire original payload tree. Boundary protection leaves suffix entries unchanged. compile_records joins this record movement with the exact source compiler: the resulting caller contains the prefix's original callbacks followed by all original suffix entries. This is more than finding some records with compatible metadata indices.

The existing partial-closing examples now check exact canonical snapshots with and without the boundary marker. Both retain explicit nested-handler bounds in the dormant callback and caller suffix. A payload example assigns 11 to the discarded pending source, 22 to the dormant callback and 33 to the retained pending suffix. The generated caller carries exactly [22, 33] in that order.

These results close the caller-decomposition and canonical-retention obligations for a supplied structural PrefixClosing derivation. They do not derive that derivation from initial program admission. In particular, the checked erased- handler counterexample still requires admission to ensure that actual requests in a resumed saved body remain available. The general mutual source-generation and preservation theorem, adoption of the generated annotations and records by the broader execution invariant, and complete initial admission remain open.

Independent recursive admission checks

SourceScheduledAdmissionFactors.lean factors the existing recursive source validator into two structural projections. InterpretationChecks checks operation requirements, selected capture contracts and cleanup effects. It takes neither the external continuation permission map nor the one-shot phase map. ContinuationChecks checks invocation permissions, availability before consumption, and the unprotected-capture condition for an explicit disposal. It takes no outward effect row and checks no operation list. Selected capture guards still check their selected contract and protection mode; the factorization does not remove those contextual conditions.

The mutual theorem admission_factors proves that their conjunction is exactly the existing Code.Valid and Retained.Valid, in both directions. It follows the existing source recursors through every constructor, including saved and closing bodies, caller and tail annotations, dormant branches, and all fresh resource instances. Each invocation checks its owner before spending that owner in all of its actual continuation children. The projections retain the original validator's scheduling structure; this theorem does not independently prove a trace property such as absence of repeated consumption.

Code.compile_factors and Retained.compile_factors reuse the existing source compiler to produce Local and Pending from the two checks. No successful target judgment is an input. Source declaration evidence, actual cuts and owner bounds remain in the original annotation. The result is a factorization of that annotation's validation, not a claim that an effect list alone admits a program. Because resource annotations range over arbitrary fresh-name families, this is not a new whole-program decision procedure.

SourceScheduledAdmissionFactorsExamples.lean checks a resumption whose saved body resumes a second owner. Both the current source and its retained form compile from separately proved factors. With the interpretation factor unchanged, missing permission for the second owner, consumption of that owner, or consumption of the first owner rejects the control factor. Conversely, an unprovided effect has a trivial control factor but fails the interpretation factor and full validation.

This makes the two recursive obligations explicit for the full annotated source grammar. It does not construct the contextual rechecking derivations needed after closing, nor establish that a transformed source preserves either factor. Those transformation proofs and their connection to initial source admission remain necessary for the general one-shot milestone.

Source-only recomposition and independent checks

SourceScheduledSourceJoin.lean constructs Retained.joinSource directly from the actual prefix and suffix annotations. Construction takes no interpretation check, continuation permission, phase map or successful validation. An operation-only prefix is expanded far enough to retain the suffix's explicit metadata. Structured source follows its existing constructors. Current code, callbacks and dormant saved code are transported through the existing receiver associativity laws; heterogeneous equality proves that this transport retains the original source value.

The two validation factors characterize this one output independently: joinSource_interpretations equates its interpretation check with the conjunction of the two original interpretation checks, and joinSource_continuations does the same for permissions and phases. Both are equivalences, so a rejected input cannot become accepted merely through joining. joinSource_bounds separately proves exact snapshot append. joinSource_valid combines the factors through the existing admission equivalence.

This strengthens the earlier existential recomposition interface, which required successful validation before returning a source witness. The data constructor exists even for rejected inputs, and both factor proofs concern the same output. It does not choose separate source witnesses for interpretation and control checks. The main structural rechecking compiler, the closing compiler and the partial-caller retention compiler now use this constructor when joining a closed dormant segment with its running tail. Their earlier exact metadata conclusions remain checked.

SourceScheduledSourceJoinExamples.lean retains explicit handler metadata in callback, dormant and suffix positions, and checks a compact prefix followed by a rich suffix. A suffix with nested owner invocations remains rejected when its second owner's permission is missing or that owner is already consumed. A source with an unprovided effect is also constructible but remains rejected by the interpretation factor.

This removes the validation prerequisite from the recomposition constructor. It does not yet make every rechecking compiler branch independent of original validation, derive its contextual transformation from initial admission, or complete broader-policy execution safety.

Rechecking compilation before full validation

compile_factors_retaining_all in SourceScheduledSourceRechecking.lean constructs one target annotation from a structural Expression or RetainedChange derivation without a blanket original Valid premise. For that same output, it proves that original interpretation checks imply target interpretation checks, original continuation checks imply target continuation checks, and the existing metadata conclusion holds. Current-code bounds remain equal; retained bounds follow the existing structural provenance relation.

The proof strengthens the existing mutual compiler induction. It retains the original constructor cases, uses the existing fresh-interception compiler, and uses the source-only join for closed dormant branches. Invocation cases transport the saved or closing source, caller and tail separately, preserving the original permission and phase facts when the control implication is applied. Resource cases choose one output family, shared by both implications and the metadata proof. They do not choose separate witnesses for effect and control checking. The earlier validity-preserving compiler API now follows by combining these two implications for the same annotation through valid_iff_factors.

These implications are not equivalences for every rechecking rule. Dropping ordinary pending source can discard a failed check. SourceScheduledFactorCompilationExamples.lean exercises construction when full original validation is unavailable: a request with a missing original provider still transports its control factor, and a branch containing an unpermitted nested invocation still transports its interpretation factor. A fresh-resource example checks both factors for one output family. A discarded invalid ordinary frame leaves a valid empty target. None of these examples admits the rejected original as an executable program.

The structural transformation derivation remains a premise. In particular, freshRich still carries validation of its original normal prefix; the new compiler does not manufacture that evidence or remove it from the rule. Deriving and retaining the contextual transformation evidence from initial source admission is still open, as are broader-policy execution integration and complete initial callable/resource contracts. Compilation before validation closes a construction dependency, not the whole admission theorem.

Original source at fresh interception

SourceScheduledInterceptSource.lean recovers the normal prefix captured by a newly inserted handler from the original whole retained source. InterceptSource.recover combines the existing interception decomposition and retained-source split: the recovered prefix and waiting suffix are valid at their original receivers, and their ordered metadata append is exactly the original snapshot. recoverAt retains a prefix index already known by a syntax traversal. Neither requires a separately supplied valid normal-prefix annotation.

For whole source constructed from its actual prefix and suffix, recoverJoined reuses joinSource_valid to derive the child checks. It retains the actual prefix annotation up to receiver equality, including invocation children and fresh-resource families. It does not choose a replacement source annotation. This distinction lets clients reuse proofs about those original children rather than reconstructing them from a metadata equation. The proof uses the existing join and receiver-transport laws; it adds no split induction.

InterceptSource.rechecking supplies the recovered normal prefix to the existing fresh-disposal rule. Three independent obligations remain: the capture guard, the bound on owners referenced by discarded pending code, and structural closing for callbacks at the surviving receiver. Whole-source validity alone does not imply these obligations. The primitive Closing.request_callback derives closing for a single actual request callback from an outside uniform operation capability, for either compact or structured original annotation. It supplies no continuation permission.

SourceScheduledInterceptSourceExamples.lean checks a nonempty callback prefix recovered from whole source and compilation of the newly intercepted disposing request with unchanged current-code metadata. A second example retains the actual prefix from the existing mixed-callback fixture, reuses its closing proof for an outside-owner invocation, and obtains the same compilation result. The existing consumed-owner rejection transfers to the joined whole source. A separate negative check rejects the primitive callback capability at an empty outside receiver.

This establishes original-prefix recovery for fresh interception. It does not derive the residual closing obligations for arbitrary callbacks, construct a general handler-insertion traversal, or retain initial admission through every runtime transition. Those remain part of the open initial-source and execution integration work. Core correspondence and the excluded continuation modes are unchanged.

Handler admission from original operation interfaces

SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceAdmission.lean derives handler-entry receiver changes for original retained source whose code positions carry operation footprints. OperationSource relates that actual source to its interface. It covers compact annotations and every expanded retained-frame constructor, including callbacks and dormant captures. Its valid_iff theorem identifies the interface check with the original source's validation. It does not erase or replace the source annotation.

OperationSource.extract traverses the original annotation and returns its interface together with this structural evidence. Extraction is complete for the view and retains the exact requirement lists, including duplicates. It returns no result when a code position uses a richer selected-request or continuation-invocation annotation. This is a representation distinction, not program rejection. Such source retains the existing richer rechecking rules.

The new Interfaces.check_handler_insert theorem composes the existing exposed interface and ordered-scope replacement proofs. Assuming the original interface checked, its check after insertion is equivalent to checking only the operations that pass the unchanged receiver prefix and match the newly installed effect. That check runs against the inserted table alone. A nearer matching handler with a missing operation cannot fall through to an older provider. Internal providers discharge requirements before this boundary; dormant providers do not supply active sibling requests.

OperationSource.receiver derives the existing ReceiverChange rules for all retained frames. handler_receiver, handler_here and handler_running then use the finite insertion criterion, reusing original validity for unrelated operations. At.handler_interfaces applies these results to the actual resumption and closing source in a continuation's context. The rule takes their source views and primitive table checks instead of supplied receiver-change derivations. The recursive clause-body admission, declaration evidence, and independent permission and phase checks remain the existing obligations. Metadata preservation follows through the existing receiver compiler.

SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceExamples.lean uses extracted source evidence to admit a handler over a nonempty saved request, followed by a choice of resume or dispose. Another example derives both paths with a nonempty cleanup callback, retaining the protected closing receiver. Negative and boundary checks cover masking, unrelated effects, consumed owners, dormant requirements, active builtin shielding, and dormant cells that do not shield siblings. A disposing override that fails this uniform-interface test is still admitted by the existing richer fresh-capture proof. A valid callback invoking an outside continuation likewise remains valid when extraction returns no operation-only view.

The source views now persist across entry. OperationSource.bounds proves that compacting source represented by this view retains its complete snapshot. This is limited to positions already carrying operation footprints; it does not erase richer continuation annotations. Context.OperationSources packages the views of the actual saved and closing source. Its handler and cleanup constructors create explicit successor annotations from those interfaces, retain the waiting tail, and prove BoundsAgree with the original context. after_handler and after_cleanup retain the same extracted interfaces for the next entry. Resource entry retains their existing world extensions: OperationSource.world_weaken transports the structural source view, and Context.OperationSources.resource uses the established provider-insertion law to check the new builtin receiver. resource_bounds proves equality with the original continuation metadata's world extension, including its waiting projection. after_resource supplies the extended source views for subsequent entries. Freshness remains a premise of the existing resource-body rule.

This source-shape fact is stronger than the previous compiler result, which promised a valid annotation and matching metadata but did not promise that the chosen annotation had an operation-interface view. The new At.handler_retaining_interfaces, At.cleanup_retaining_interfaces and At.resource_retaining_interfaces rules connect explicit successors to the existing admission constructors using sameReceiver and their established metadata preservation proofs. They do not change those constructors or bypass their checks. Cleanup receiver transport reuses the existing insertion theorem; the newly registered callback still has its separate footprint, coverage, and clause-side capability check.

SourceConsumingInterfaceNestingExamples.lean uses induction to admit every finite nesting depth of the supplied resumptive table and derive the existing Generated source correspondence and scheduling results. The same induction applies to saved paths containing an actual cleanup callback. A consumed owner is rejected at every depth. Further examples put an unrelated disposing table around the nesting and interleave an outer handler, effectful cleanup registration, and arbitrarily many inner handlers. The resource examples quantify over every fresh identity and perform an actual builtin read before the nested consuming body. The combined example composes all three entry forms and generates source with the original continuation correspondence. These results reuse the existing source-generation compiler; they are not runtime all-transition safety or general Core correspondence theorems.

This closes interface-based handler receiver derivation for that structural source class. It is not a complete generator for arbitrary recursive continuation annotations or fresh disposing interceptions. Those cases still need the general closing and receiver derivations, followed by retention through execution and complete initial-program admission.

Initial interface admission at continuation use

An entry-by-entry interface check can demand saved-source validity too early. The checked example in SourceConsumingLeafInterfacesExamples.lean installs an empty E handler, then an E handler supplying the saved request, then resumes. The initial Admitted judgment accepts it and the existing scheduling compiler validates it. The saved interface fails at the intermediate empty handler, where it is still dormant. This proves an obstruction to that eager interface construction, not an impossibility theorem about every At derivation.

SourceConsumingLeafInterfaces.lean provides a direct route from initial admission to generated source for this source class. Body.generate_leaf_interfaces follows the existing consuming body grammar and checks saved or closing requirements at the consuming leaf's actual caller. It reuses Interfaces.check_from_bound, the original source views, permission/phase checks and disposal protection. Handler, sequence, choice and cleanup constructors retain their order. Resource entry reuses world extension for the interfaces, original waiting annotation and bound snapshots.

The waiting annotation is arbitrary and is retained verbatim, except for its existing resource-world extension. Saved and closing annotations are compacted only where OperationSource.bounds proves exact metadata preservation. The result includes the existing Generated correspondence for every consuming leaf, including actual owner cuts and the original saved/closing/waiting projections. Context.OperationSources.initial_source obtains its local checks from Admitted.at_capture; it needs no future At, receiver-change derivation or target-validation premise. Original validity and authentication of the saved/closing interface bounds remain explicit inputs. The construction is a proof of generation; resource-family witnesses use classical choice, so it is not advertised as an executable inference algorithm.

SourceConsumingLeafCapture.lean connects this route to the actual selected stored clause and its recorded offered-mode contract. Existing selection and snapshot lemmas derive a valid capture certificate, admitted canonical capture metadata and canonical metadata for every permitted disposal. An actual request example instantiates that boundary. Other examples retain a waiting computation whose handler-bound snapshot is provably different from the absent snapshot, extend it through a fresh resource with an actual read, and reject an already-consumed owner.

This removes eager intermediate checking as an obstacle for saved and closing operation-source views. It does not generate views for richer saved annotations that invoke other owners or contain selected disposing requests. Deriving those cases from initial admission, retaining evidence at every reachable request, and broader-policy finite-execution integration remain open. No operational rule, normative Ash semantics or Core implementation changes here.

Rich source rechecking at continuation use

SourceConsumingUseAdmission.lean defines AtUse, a structural judgment over the existing consuming body and the original captured source. Its sequence, choice, handler and cleanup rules accumulate the actual caller without recompiling dormant saved code. Cleanup retains its explicit dependency-coverage premise. The resource rule extends the world of the original annotations and adds the builtin frame to the caller. It does not validate saved source at intermediate handler contexts.

At a resume or dispose leaf, AtUse requires the existing ReceiverChange derivation from the corresponding original source to the full caller at that leaf. Those rules recursively inspect actual source, including other owner invocations and fresh disposing requests. They take primitive checks and structural recursive evidence, not target Valid, Local or Pending proofs. The original context supplies original validity; Body.BoundCheck separately supplies clause operation checks, rights and owner availability. Disposal also retains its independent protection and closing-route requirements.

AtUse.generate_source reuses ReceiverChange.compile_retaining at the leaves and assembles the existing Generated correspondence through the body. Saved, closing and waiting snapshots remain exact. initial_source derives the clause-side checks from initial Admitted evidence while retaining AtUse as an explicit additional structural obligation. AtUse.world_weaken reuses receiver-world transport; composition of the original context maps handles the resource binder without choosing a replacement source annotation. AtUse.provide now proves that structural provider insertion anywhere in the caller preserves an existing use derivation for arbitrary captured source. Its induction follows all consuming-body constructors. Resume and disposal reuse the new receiver rule and the original context's checks; nested handlers, cleanup and resource binders lift the same insertion. This discharges provider transport without a second capture or scheduling proof. Handler and cleanup interference still require their own source-derived conditions.

Local clause admission alone cannot discharge that additional obligation. MissingCaptureContract in SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean proves a counterexample using the existing compiler: a clause installs an empty E handler and resumes, declaring an empty continuation interface. Admitted accepts that declaration, but the actual saved source requests E. The masking clause has no AtUse derivation for that valid original source. Declaring the actual E requirement makes the existing clause checker reject it. This is a failure of the implication from clause-local admission to contextual admission. empty_handler_not_source_typed also proves that full SourcePlannedSources typing rejects this empty handler whenever E's signature contains operation 0: the existing coverage premise requires a clause for it. Thus this example cannot refute admission based on the full source judgment, or justify adding a new source contract on its own.

The stronger source premises also have an admission limitation. ClauseRowAdmission.UncheckedTemplate in the same example module proves that Expression types a handler for E operation 0 around resume, with complete operation coverage, port typing, one-shot use and hereditary declarations for both modes. The former unrestricted Body rule rejects it for the stated continuation contract, regardless of its checking signature; nested_unrestricted_body_rejected retains that exact old-rule result. Unrestricted Rows quantifies over every template store. Its invocation interface accepts a stored E operation 1 when the original caller supplies that operation; the newly installed operation-0 handler then masks it. The actual source signature has no E operation 1. This is a proved admission restriction caused by an unauthenticated template, not a reachable well-typed program violating safety.

Consequently, unrestricted Rows cannot supply the intended general admission of nested handlers around continuation use. The source connection must constrain its template quantification by authenticated source information, or supply a replacement structural interface with that information. The existing recursive requirement checker and its soundness proof remain reusable. This evidence does not establish that operation-signature authentication alone suffices for cleanup-route preservation or general AtUse; those remain separate parts of the same admission obligation. Finite interface inclusion already supplies the operation-source case.

Rows now has an explicit template-source parameter. Its default retains the unrestricted rule. Rows.instantiate requires evidence that the actual store satisfies a relative certificate's source parameter; the existing finite contextual derivation still supplies the checked requirements and row bound. AuthenticatedTemplate in the same example module constructs such a relative certificate for the handler-around-resume case. Its source contract requires lookup of the exact saved template, an existing structural Outward derivation, and a finite bound containing only E operation 0 in both protection modes. The valid operation-0 store instantiates this certificate. The earlier operation-1 store cannot satisfy its source contract. There is no target-body validation or future execution premise. Outward excludes further owner invocations, so this is a local repair, not general recursive admission.

The hereditary source judgments now use Rows relative to SourceStore for their operation signature. This includes declared, dependency, planned and annotated source bodies; their offers retain the same source-relative premise. SourceStore witnesses structural StoreModeSource, exact normal resume-body certificates and StoreClosingRecords, together with StoreAnnotation relating those resume and disposal lists to the actual checking store. These judgments retain legacy source evidence and admit mixed value/unwind boundaries and lexical closing summaries. It is indexed by the clause header's owner and contract, and the witnessed source registry must contain that exact contract. This ties input and answer types, demands, rows, protection and effect interfaces to the same owner. It does not require successful checking or future execution. SourceStore.resume_template reuses record certification to recover the selected saved source at the header's exact input and resumption demand, its relation to the actual annotated body, and an exit boundary equal to its answer or unwinding. The capture proofs obtain the registry equation from the same fresh-owner insertion that constructs the source and closing records, including the path without a new closing record. Erasure preserves the owner contract as well as the operation signature.

The contract index matters: the former store-only predicate could use a source segment expecting a function argument when checking a header that accepts unit. That function's latent row could contain an operation absent from the source signature. Thus existential source provenance alone did not establish the intended connection to the clause's continuation type. The registry equation repairs that missing connection; it does not assert that all remaining latent operation or receiver checks follow from it.

The local interface also excludes an active occurrence of its newly allocated owner from the receiving tail. Without that condition, consuming the owner can change an unrelated protection marker in the abstract tail. The CleanupTailFreshness regression in SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean uses an authenticated empty saved continuation and a typed effectful cleanup around resumption. A tail that repeats the allocated owner passes the old resume and advertisement checks, then fails the callback export after consumption. The fresh concrete tail succeeds. cleanup_resume_rows now supplies a general row certificate for that requirement form when the saved continuation has no additional owner demand; the literal clause receives hereditary body admission. Actual capture interfaces derive the new condition from their existing allocation freshness and ownership decomposition. This changes source checking, not the operational stack or Core semantics.

This connects source-relative row contracts to actual allocation. It does not prove that every intended nested-handler body has such a contract, or that operation-signature authentication suffices for receiver preservation. General initial admission still has to derive AtUse and preserve its evidence through all transitions. The row interface has not been substituted for that obligation.

For an outside-owner call whose saved or closing annotation has an authenticated operation view, Expression.resume_from_bound and dispose_from_bound in SourceScheduledHandlerInterfaceAdmission.lean derive the receiver-change premises from finite interface inclusion and caller checks. They reuse the original permission, phase and disposal-route evidence, and retain the arbitrary waiting annotation. The existing outside-owner, resource and closing-callback examples now use this derivation. This covers operation-interface callees; recursively richer callees and general selected disposing requests still require the broader admission connection above.

SourceConsumingUseCapture.lean connects this judgment to the selected stored clause, existing capture certificate and canonical capture/disposal snapshots. It reuses stored-source selection, nested-bound admission and the existing snapshot theorem. It adds no new operational capture or ownership proof.

SourceConsumingUseAdmissionExamples.lean checks captured code that requests E and then resumes outside owner37 under the previous temporary-mask arrangement for owner19. Its saved annotation has no operation-source view and has a provably non-absent snapshot. A fresh resource with an actual read precedes the same consuming body, reusing that body's existing initial admission. A separate closing callback resumes owner37 during disposal of owner19; the callback also has no operation-source view. The existing fresh-disposer example reuses its original structural rechecking proof. A consumed outside owner is rejected, and an actual request instantiates the stored-clause theorem to produce an allocator certificate.

This removes operation-only compaction and eager intermediate checks from the structural clause compiler. It does not derive all AtUse leaves from initial program admission. Queued source and actual focus/return integration are provided below. General derivation at reachable requests, reconstitution after arbitrary receiver changes and broader-policy finite execution remain open. The earlier At APIs remain unchanged; neither a general translation between At and AtUse nor full initial-program safety is claimed.

Queued consumption-time source at focus and return

SourceConsumingUseQueued.lean connects AtUse to source records with explicit current owner cuts and caller interfaces. UseQueuedBody retains the original captured-source context separately from that current receiver. Its fields are the actual body, exact bound origin, structural use-site admission, nested declaration admission and independent clause checks. This permits an intermediate masking caller without demanding that dormant saved code validate there.

Source inversion and Body.plug reuse the existing focus/recomposition syntax. UseQueuedBody.focused covers the existing Focused relation: an operation prefix queues its consuming remainder, while a pure pending frame leaves the consuming body current. UseFocusedSource.child_valid constructs the actual child annotation, using existing neutral code expansion for the latter case. Return constructs the plugged source record and its bound equality from the record on the actual plain frame; successor admission is not supplied anew.

SourceConsumingUseTransport.lean transports AtUse through permission extension and phase changes by induction, reusing ReceiverChange.transport and its phase specialization at consuming leaves. World extension commutes with both context maps, including fresh-resource bodies. UseQueuedBody.transport composes permission, phase and world changes on the retained source, nested declarations, finite checks and bound index. The finite check derives equality of the selected owner's existing permission entry. Phase transport preserves availability of every owner in the original source scope; preserving only the selected owner's availability is insufficient.

UseQueuedBody.generate obtains source validity, exact current bounds and the original continuation correspondence from the consumption-time compiler. CanonicalPayload adapters reuse existing code normalization to compile these records at canonical indices and recompose them on return. They retain the original source payload and prove expanded code, exact canonical current bounds and bound admission. Normalization is not asserted to preserve an unnormalized Generated index unchanged.

SourceConsumingUseReceiver.lean retains a UseQueuedBody together with a structural Expansion from its recorded receiver to the actual receiver. UseReceiverBody.generate reuses neutral compilation, with exact current bounds. Successive expansions compose by the existing Expansion.trans theorem. Focus retains the same path for queued source and adds the actual pure frame when the consuming body remains current. Return reconstructs the source record at that actual receiver. This closes the local neutral-receiver connection without reconstructing AtUse at every administrative frame. It does not allow insertion of a different handler or assert equality of every saved annotation after neutral compilation.

SourceAnnotatedStoredUseQueued.lean connects the record to actual typed focus and plain-return steps. It reuses the existing snapshot focus/return proofs and execution assembly, including owner accounting and completion preservation. All ten runtime focus forms share the same existing focus relation. The result records source evidence at the same actual successor as the typed execution theorem; it does not define a new operational transition. These theorems now take UseReceiverBody and retain UseReceiverFocused, so the source cut can differ from the actual receiver by the recorded neutral expansion. An unchanged receiver uses .at_receiver.

SourceConsumingUseHandlerEntry.lean adds source-directed handler entry. AtUse.handler_body inverts the parent's structural rule. The child retains the same original captured context, extends its recorded cut and caller by the entered handler, and inherits the parent's nested declarations and finite checks. UseReceiverBody.handler_body lifts the existing neutral path under that handler. The EnteredHandler relation then fixes the child's exact bound snapshot, even when actual installed clause plans differ from checking witnesses by their existing signature equality. This derivation does not require saved-source validity at the intermediate caller or a newly supplied admission proof for the child.

SourceAnnotatedStoredUseHandlers.lean connects that descent to actual typed packet installation and execution. The execution theorem takes the same explicit action witness for the initial typed state and source record, and returns both at the same successor. Runtime ownership, access, name and completion accounting reuse the established handler entry assembly. The existing declaration-retention law remains a premise; this does not prove it for arbitrary declaration policies or establish source coverage for every pending position.

SourceConsumingUseTransitions.lean reuses the four Body.Reduction rules for binding, application and branch selection. Body.reduced_source determines the actual surviving source; the new judgment and finite check follow by inversion. UseReceiverBody.computed retains the original captured context and neutral receiver path at the exact computation snapshot. SourceAnnotatedStoredUseComputation.lean connects this result to typed computation and full execution with the same initial action witness, ownership multiset, retained completion evidence and the existing effect-row narrowing result.

The transition module also derives cleanup and resource children. Cleanup descent retains the actual callback footprint and declaration, proves its operation annotation valid under the actual running receiver, and retains coverage by the declared cleanup dependencies. Its callback bound is absent because this Body constructor uses an operation footprint; this is not an extension to arbitrary continuation-consuming callback syntax. Resource descent selects the admitted fresh body, maps the original captured context to the larger world and retains the world-weakened pending bounds. SourceAnnotatedStoredUseEntries.lean connects both descents to the existing actual raw steps and typed successor snapshots. SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionEntries.lean now carries both derived records through full execution. The source context and initial execution use the same explicit action witness. Cleanup returns its checked callback and child record; resource entry returns the child at the fresh world with the original context and pending bounds weakened to that world. Existing entry assembly supplies ownership, access, name and completion preservation. Coverage of every pending record remains open.

SourceConsumingUseCaptureRecords.lean constructs the selected clause's UseQueuedBody from its AtUse derivation and the installed declaration's independent bounds. It retains the exact generated current annotation, saved resumption bounds and canonical disposal snapshots. SourceAnnotatedStoredUseCapture.lean packages that concrete evidence in the existing allocator's ClauseEvidence interface. Exact handler-packet, cut and selected-clause uniqueness identify the source witnesses with the actual allocator's witnesses. Both runtime capture branches therefore return the new source record beside the actual typed successor and exact owner-inventory extension. The theorem does not assume a source invariant for the successor or add a new ownership induction.

SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionCapture.lean connects the same result to full execution through assemble_capture. AtPackets.capture_use_step now chooses the source/action witness already stored in the execution invariant. On the bounded packet route it extracts declaration source and its bounds check from admitted stored packets, then uses Declarations.selected_source to identify the selected body. These are no longer separate caller inputs. StackBounds.Admitted.capture also supplies packet admission at the actual successor; ticket allocation leaves the resource world unchanged. It reconstructs canonical original capture/closing source and derives its snapshot origin, the selected clause's disposal permission, waiting-scope requirements, and owner freshness. The separate initial, freshAction, source, captureSource, permits, supplied, absent and aligned inputs have been removed. Physical allocation freshness and the stored-packet admission, bounded route and physical/planned selection inputs remain explicit. AtPackets.capture_plan derives the offered contract, dependency mode, saved/waiting plan cut and selected body from the current source and physical cut at the exact stored packet. It reuses source splitting, capture-guard inversion and ordered clause lookup; it does not require AtUse.

The same allocator returns the typed and full execution successors with the same owner-inventory result. The event's operation-port lookup now fixes the concrete successor configuration in the theorem statement, rather than returning an existential configuration and a shape equation. It returns one admitted successor snapshot used by both successor judgments, with Captured owner snapshot.normalize nextSnapshot and admitted stored packets. The snapshot is extracted from the existing capture payload; no new admission premise or capture induction is added. Existing normalization preserves incoming snapshot admission. The payload also retains the selected body's source record and resumption/closing metadata. The AtUse premise checks the selected body against the reconstructed context. It remains an independent source obligation, so this theorem does not yet derive request-site admission from an initial program or establish complete source retention through execution.

SourceConsumingUseConsumption.lean activates the saved or closing source at a consuming leaf. Inversion of AtUse supplies the original structural receiver checks, and the independent finite check supplies the permission and caller requirements. Existing receiver compilation and retained-source recomposition construct the whole successor source tree, including callbacks and dormant branches, with exact original bounds. UseReceiverBody also activates source after its recorded neutral receiver changes, using the actual owner cut and a Retained.Neutral relation for the resulting metadata. That neutral relation alone does not identify a particular runtime snapshot.

SourceBoundDisposalRecords.lean completes the record-movement counterpart of capture and resumption for disposal. It reuses the existing source-record split and closing traversal. Saved pending code is dropped; saved callbacks retain their original values, order and multiplicity; caller and waiting records survive. This includes every recursive dormant branch. Discarded.carry_records applies directly to the actual disposal snapshot relation. Its ordered-filter result does not assert that arbitrary payloads are valid at their new receiver.

SourceBoundConsumptionSelection.lean authenticates the consuming source cut against that snapshot relation. Existing owner lookup and forest append injectivity identify the cut's caller, saved forest and waiting tail. A shared elimination proof then identifies both resumption and disposal metadata from uniqueness of the original live owners and equality of the original bound data. The bound split/join lemma concerns data representation; the existing operational ownership proofs are unchanged.

SourceConsumingUseConsumptionSnapshots.lean uses those identities to place the activated source at the exact Resumed or Discarded successor. The input record has a consuming leaf and an exact current cut. Separate premises identify its saved bounds, operation-only caller bounds and waiting bounds with the original snapshot. Disposal additionally uses the original saved snapshot's canonical closing projection. The result is full retained capability source, valid after spending the owner, whose bound projection equals the successor's pending snapshot. It does not construct a new AtUse record for every source position.

SourceAnnotatedStoredUseConsumption.lean connects both activations to actual typed consumption. Source owner uniqueness comes from the existing frame realization and runtime inventory: recursive live tickets are an ordered sublist of owned tickets. The existing consumption trace identifies the spent phase map with the actual successor's available owners. SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionConsumption.lean then reuses full execution assembly for resumption and disposal, sharing the explicit action witness with the original consuming record. Both results retain all moved payloads and construct valid retained source at the same successor, with exact pending bounds. Resumption uses its saved/caller permutation; disposal uses the ordered callback filter. These connections still require original a combined consuming-source/metadata record, as strengthened below. Its structural neutral movement determines the exact destination bounds. Maintaining usable source records throughout arbitrary capture/restoration remains part of the global invariant obligation.

SourceConsumingUseQueuedExamples.lean queues the supplying inner handler under the empty outer E handler, retaining the earlier rich captured code that will invoke outside owner37. The intermediate E requirement is proved false, while the queued source still generates valid code with its exact bounds. Both focus alternatives, ordinary return and canonical return are checked. Existing generic record capture and resumption preserve the payload itself; the recovered record generates code at the restored receiver with its additional spent marker using neutral expansion. It retains that path through return, current-child focus and a second neutral insertion. The transport examples also extend the permission registry, retire unrelated owner88 and enlarge the resource world, then generate and recompose the same queued source. A negative theorem rejects retiring outside owner37, which the original saved code still invokes. Handler-entry examples derive the two successive child records from one parent record, compile both children, and repeat the descent after a neutral restoration. The outer entry has an exact bound-snapshot witness. The record movement example tracks this designated payload, not complete source coverage of every code position or a whole typed execution trace.

These are local computation, focus/return, entry, capture and consumption connections. They do not derive AtUse at every reachable request, prove usable source-record coverage and metadata alignment for every reachable queued position, or establish broader-policy finite-execution safety from initial admission alone. The operational ownership proofs are reused unchanged.

SourceConsumingUseTransitionsExamples.lean reuses the rich masking source for binding and application reductions, two branches with different annotation shapes, and resource allocation after a neutral restoration. The effectful-cleanup fixture checks both its child and callback at the actual receiver and rejects an omitted cleanup dependency.

The current connections for this source-record representation are:

Transition family Checked connection Remaining boundary
Ordinary computation All four reductions, typed state and full execution, sharing the action witness Initial and reachable source coverage
Focus and plain return Source reconstruction at typed and full-execution successors, including neutral receiver paths General capture/restoration of the queued records
Source-directed handler entry Child descent, exact packet installation and full execution Initial coverage and the existing declaration-retention premise
Cleanup and resource entry Child descent and full execution; exact callback check or fresh-world mapping at the same typed successor Initial and recursively retained source coverage
Fresh capture Selected source record and exact capture/disposal bounds at the actual typed and full-execution successor; existing ownership proof reused Request-site structural evidence and original source/bounds alignment remain explicit premises
Resumption and disposal Full execution activates retained source from the combined record at the actual neutral receiver, with exact successor bounds, phase equality and all-record movement Derive usable recursive source-record coverage across arbitrary restoration and at later requests

Consuming source with actual metadata provenance

SourceConsumingUseMetadata.lean records one original captured bound tree, equality of each permitted resumption projection to that tree, equality of each permitted closing projection to its canonical closing, and structural neutral movement from the original caller/live/waiting metadata to the actual pending data. This is a data correspondence invariant. It contains no assumption that a future source or execution is valid.

Source-directed handler, cleanup and resource frames extend both the source caller and actual metadata. Administrative pure frames, pure completion frames and spent history extend only the actual receiver. Permission extension, phase restriction and resource-world extension retain the same correspondence, using the existing context and annotation transport laws.

SourceConsumingUseAligned.lean pairs that invariant with the existing UseQueuedBody. Its at_receiver derives the receiver expansion from metadata movement and the existing owner-cut reconstruction; no separate receiver-expansion field is assumed. Computation and plain return produce a successor with the same pending correspondence. Focus retains the combined record on the consuming remainder, or on the current consuming child beneath its actual pure pending frame. Handler, cleanup and resource descent preserve the combined record, as do independent permission, phase and world changes. The operation-prefix case keeps its existing source interface; it is not falsely treated as a consuming body.

SourceConsumingUseAlignedSnapshots.lean connects these records to actual handler, cleanup and resource entry snapshots. Selected-clause capture initializes the combined record from Context.of_request_bounds, which supplies both original saved metadata and canonical closing metadata. The same original split constructs the actual Captured snapshot, with the generated clause's admitted annotation. The request-site AtUse, capture-source evidence and source/snapshot equality remain inputs. This result does not derive them from an initial term.

SourceScheduledNeutralActual.lean closes a separate metadata transport obligation. Retained.expand_neutral_at takes a given structural movement to the actual destination bounds and constructs valid retained source whose projection equals those exact bounds. The earlier expand_neutral constructs a destination with neutral provenance but does not identify it with a separately supplied runtime snapshot. The strengthened proof follows the given metadata relation, reusing existing code and receiver transport. Its operation-only case uses the proved fact that neutral movement preserves absent bounds. It covers callbacks and dormant saved captures without replacing their original annotation values.

SourceBoundNeutralOwners.lean now decomposes the actual bound data at the selected owner. It reuses the owner-cut reconstruction and metadata split, retaining one identical captured bound tree on both sides. A structural induction tracks only the changed caller and waiting data. Prefix and append composition retain the original annotations. SourceBoundNeutralConsumption.lean uses that decomposition and the existing unique-owner snapshot-cut theorem to prove neutral correspondence through actual Resumed and Discarded events. Resumption moves the original captured data ahead of the changed caller and waiting data; disposal uses its canonical closing projection above the running boundary. No target-source validity or scheduling premise is added.

SourceConsumingUseAlignedConsumption.lean combines those actual movements with the existing consuming-leaf compiler and expand_neutral_at. Both UseAlignedBody.resumed and discarded now construct valid full retained source whose projection equals the actual successor's pending data, even after neutral receiver changes. The runtime integration in SourceAnnotatedStoredUseConsumption.lean and SourceAnnotatedStoredUseExecutionConsumption.lean uses the combined record directly. The source cut belongs to the original source forest; separate exact-receiver, saved-origin and pending-equality arguments are no longer required. Actual owner uniqueness and the successor's phase map still come from existing runtime proofs.

The existing typed and full-execution source connections now retain this combined record for computation, focus/plain return and handler/cleanup/resource entry. Their runtime assembly proofs are reused in place. The capture payload CapturedUseBounds also retains the combined record, through the existing allocator and full-execution capture theorem; its exported resumption and canonical disposal facts are preserved. Focus returns the combined record in its existing current-child/queued-remainder split, with metadata for the exact pending tail. These are local transition theorems, not a proof that every state has all the required records.

SourceCodeRecords.lean now derives concrete code records at every pending body, callback and dormant saved branch of valid retained source. Each record contains its source annotation, current validity, exact bound projection and receiving forest. The structural AtReceivers judgment places ordinary code at its waiting suffix, callbacks at that suffix under a running marker, and dormant saved code at its own waiting suffix. No code slot is optional. Operation interfaces construct operation-only records using their existing checks; richer annotations retain their original code.

SourceCodeRecordPositions.lean proves that positioned records compose and split at the existing forest boundaries. Actual capture preserves the same records at the same receiving suffixes; the proof reuses forest reassociation and the existing record movement relation. SourceCodeRecordCapture.lean additionally applies the existing capability transport theorem to every record when a fresh owner is introduced. The annotations, receivers and bound projections remain fixed while validity moves to the extended permissions and introduced phase. The existing capture payload now includes these complete positioned records, so both typed and full-execution capture retain them without a new input premise. Resumption and disposal also return complete positioned records, constructed from their activated source at the actual successor's available owner phases. Those reconstructed records need not be identical to the old payload values.

SourceCodeRecordReassembly.lean reconstructs valid retained source with its exact original bound projection from positioned code records and a pending schedule. The schedule supplies handler requirements; code annotations and their validity come from the records. Its source_of_schedule_all also reconstructs current and retained source directly by mutual induction on the existing structural Local and Pending checks, at the same receiver and owner phases. It uses the existing normalization to match any prescribed canonical bound spine. Requests with disposal, recursive owner invocations, callbacks and resource families are included; invocation cases reuse the existing retained-source split. CaptureSource.of_schedule then derives original capture and closing source with canonical metadata from the request and pending checks, reusing the actual cut and normalization laws.

SourceAnnotatedCodeRecords.lean derives those checks from the existing runtime state's current code and stored segment. AtPackets.canonical_code_coverage constructs complete source coverage for the normalized snapshot without input code records. At a request, AtPackets.canonical_capture_source also constructs the original capture and closing source and proves its snapshot origin. Neither theorem assumes a successful check under a changed receiver. capture_capabilities recovers the selected clause's disposal permission and waiting-scope requirements from its actual stored handler; fresh_action_absent reuses action registration and the realized live-owner inventory. Full execution capture now consumes these derived facts directly. The earlier AtPackets.retained_source retains the exact unnormalized projection when positioned records are supplied.

SourceCodeDecomposition.lean now recovers valid child code from the existing bound computation and focus relations. Compact operation-only annotations split their original request interface, including conservative weakening; explicit sequence and choice annotations expose their original children. Both forms retain the exact selected bound projections. The pair-right focus case reuses neutral receiver expansion for its pure pending frame. Plain return prefixes the queued code with the pure values prescribed by the existing context grammar.

SourceCodeCoverage.lean combines current code at the actual snapshot receiver with complete positioned pending records. Its computed, focused and returned theorems derive this same coverage at the actual successor. Focus constructs the queued record from the current source and retains the old tail records. Return reads the head record at its proved receiver and reconstructs the current source without a new queued-admission premise. All four computation cases and four focus metadata cases are covered; the latter serve all ten expression focus forms. ordinary_code_snapshot, focus_code_snapshot and plug_code_snapshot in SourceAnnotatedCodeRecords.lean connect those proofs to the existing typed runtime steps, retaining their source typing, ownership, effects and exact snapshot movement. Plain frames add no owner, so focus and return use the same available-owner phase map.

Canonical coverage and original capture/closing source now follow at every state carrying AtPackets; they need no separate source-record invariant for each transition family. This does not derive AtUse: a consuming clause can change the ordered receiver, so source validity at its original receiver is insufficient. Deriving that changed-receiver admission from declarations and preserving the complete execution invariant remain open, as do complete initial admission and the initial-to-finite-execution theorem. Ownership proofs and current Core are unchanged.

Finite requirements at a surviving interpretation boundary

SourceScheduledSurvivingRequirements.lean derives receiver rechecking for operation-only source from finite requirements at the surviving outside interpretation. survivingRequirements first removes requests supplied by unchanged local source providers, then removes requests supplied by cells retained in the closing prefix. User handlers in that prefix are erased and cannot discharge the latter requirements.

requirements_surviving_iff proves an exact criterion for a fixed requirement list, assuming its original internal checks passed. The proof composes the existing replacement and closing factorization lemmas. A running marker does not change this uniform interface check because it already requires both modes. Expression.surviving_operations also permits narrowing conservative metadata, provided a footprint of the same source justifies the smaller requirement list. Actual requests cannot be removed merely to make the check pass.

The retained-source theorem uses Interfaces.exposed, which already accounts for ordinary code, callbacks and dormant bodies. check_closing_receiver_iff factors its receiver check without another traversal. check_any_closing proves a stronger sufficient condition: if the surviving outside supplies a finite bound containing the whole exposed interface, every closing prefix is supported. This bound is checked at the outside, not against a chosen successful target annotation. Repeated requirements are membership obligations, not counted continuation permissions.

ReceiverChange.surviving_operations connects the factored condition to the existing exact metadata compiler. request_any_closing additionally handles an atomic saved request with either original annotation form. The partial caller resumption example now uses that rule instead of checking its target body by hand. SourceScheduledSurvivingRequirementsExamples.lean checks ordinary, callback and dormant source together: a retained cell supplies the callback's request even though the outside handler cannot. A stronger outside bound covers arbitrary closing prefixes. Removing the handler for an actual request rejects the fixed interface. This last result does not quantify over every possible target annotation; the earlier partial-caller counterexample provides that stronger rejection for its own fixture.

Protected-only selected requests use a separate existing contract theorem. These proofs establish finite operation obligations at the changed receiver. They do not establish the general recursive initial-source judgment: continuation invocations, disposal-enabled selections and resource-dependent contracts must retain their independent obligations. Construction of all structural rechecking derivations from initial admission, their adoption by the broader execution invariant, and complete callable/resource admission remain open. Canonical source annotations before rechecking

Exact retention of compact annotation data can prevent a valid change of interpretation. SourceScheduledCompactBoundsGap.lean proves this for sequence(request E, pure): its original operation-only source is valid under a resumptive handler. The same computation with a structured sequence annotation rechecks through the existing fresh-capture rule. SourcePlanBoundNormalization.lean defines a canonical bound tree by expanding absent compound nodes along the actual plan syntax. Induction proves exact equality of every original bound lookup and separately preserves structural bound admission. Lookup equality alone is not used to infer admission.

SourceScheduledOperationExpansion.lean and SourceScheduledSourceNormalization.lean prove normalization for the full mutual current/retained source grammar. Compact Code.operations remains only at pure computations and atomic requests; compact Retained.operations remains only at an empty forest. Every stored branch recursively exposes its source structure, including dormant captures, cleanup callbacks, continuation invocations and fresh-resource families. Operation expansion reuses footprint and declaration-signature proofs; mutual source normalization reuses the existing source induction. The declaration policy must accept the existing recipe declarations.

Expanded is independent of capability validation. A checked counterexample shows why it must be part of the returned witness: an operation-only retained annotation for an atomic pending computation already has canonical bounds but does not expose its retained frame. Bound normalization by itself cannot prove that a classically chosen output has expanded source structure.

SourceScheduledNormalizedRechecking.lean uses the actual chosen normalized source, with all three properties, as input to the existing Expression compiler. Rechecking normalizes the compiled result too, so its returned source remains expanded for subsequent rechecking. Normalization is idempotent for plan bounds, retained bounds and snapshots; this second normalization preserves the canonical tree exactly and therefore preserves every original bound observation. The compact sequence counterexample now rechecks through this generated source and returns an expanded target. This normalizer is a proof-level witness construction using classical choice, not an executable elaboration algorithm.

The same module prepares current and retained source against one admitted normalized snapshot. Both sources retain the original plan, forest, world and owner phases, align exactly with that snapshot, and carry Expanded evidence. Normalization commutes with retained append and closing, and with the existing capture, resumption and disposal metadata movements. These proofs reuse the actual cuts and ordered saved/caller/waiting forests. They neither introduce a new operational transition nor replace ownership preservation.

SourceBoundNormalizedRecords.lean connects normalization to actual queued source records. CanonicalPayload retains the original bound index, the actual original payload, and a proof that its index normalizes to the recorded canonical index. Idempotence proves that this record index is itself stable under normalization. The package does not assert that an arbitrary payload inhabits its old type at a different index. The record traversal preserves original payload values, code positions, order and multiplicity. The existing capture and resumption record proofs then move these packed values at normalized snapshots, preserving the original capture order and resumption permutation. No new transition induction is needed.

For an actual QueuedBody, the packed original structural derivation generates valid expanded code with exactly the canonical record's admitted bounds. Recomposition reuses the existing queued-source plug proof for every return context; an actual plain return yields a generated expanded annotation aligned with the returned snapshot. Generation is at the queued source's recorded context. Moving its payload does not establish validity at a changed receiver.

The broader runtime invariant has not yet adopted canonical annotations and packed records. General derivation of Expression, receiver changes and closing from initial source judgments remains open. Normalization removes the demonstrated representation obstruction and now preserves queued source provenance through capture, resumption and return; it does not establish contextual admission at every reachable request or complete finite safety for the broader declaration policy.

The main proof uses the existing mutual-induction pattern; resource opening reuses Term.erase_instantiate. Thus the established control and ownership results remain available. hint_checked and resource_closed expose the two finite checks. port_unique proves that two derivations of the same annotated term agree on its erased output port, even when their other rich indices differ. It does not assert uniqueness of full effect or continuation contracts.

SourceAnnotatedContexts.lean retains annotated siblings in every evaluation-context form. Evaluated pair/function siblings keep their original source proof and value evidence; the existing value-summary theorem supplies their pure erased summary. Context.erase projects to the old rich context. focus_decompose covers all ten focus forms and returns the actual annotated child and context at one shared intermediate type, together with the existing signature split, owner-demand equation and requirement-evaluation law. The proof reuses the old sequence, value-evaluation and effect-composition laws.

focus_frame_ports connects that child's checked hint to any frame passing the finite guard. focus_prepare reuses the established frame constructor to produce an actual raw focus step, its rich frame certificate, a successful child-port guard and the context's checked result hint. The caller supplies the current scope typing and agreement between the expression result and the stack input. There is no premise asserting successor validity or successful future execution.
