SourceAnnotatedAdmission.lean projects annotated source admission to the existing initial Run theorem. It retains the same five premises: source typing, scheduling, the finite initial requirement/support check, completion and operation-signature agreement. Both unit-parameter and integer-parameter versions of the earlier binding example now have annotated source proofs and establish that initial runtime invariant. A negative theorem rejects changing the initializer type while retaining its annotation. A resource example contains a reference to its locally acquired cell and checks its opened body at every fresh identity, including the body annotations.

This completes the source-authentication and focus-decomposition connection. The substitution and reduction proofs below now preserve that source judgment through ordinary computation. The runtime retention layer below now retains annotated syntax in current/saved records. Preservation across the full runtime and integration with RetainedStep remain open. Its coverage remains six of ten. General consuming declarations, complete initial admission and entry/capture integration remain open. These are informative proof experiments; they do not change current Ash or establish Core correspondence.

Annotated substitution and ordinary reduction

SourceAnnotatedTransport.lean adapts the existing source-transport induction to the finite checked nodes. Agreement on ordinary variable dependencies permits an environment change; resource-world growth, continuation-contract extension and an enlarged allowed-effect list preserve the same source types and signatures. Hint and metadata-closure checks remain unchanged. Fresh resource bodies reuse the old environment-agreement and world lemmas through annotated instantiation erasure.

SourceAnnotatedValues.lean supplies the same pure value summaries as the earlier source judgment. It retains latent function bodies and their annotations. Value context changes, closed-environment changes, world growth and contract extension reuse these transports. Erasing a summary reuses the existing value port and usage proofs.

SourceAnnotatedSubstitution.lean proves closed substitution for the full mutually structural source judgment. Metadata closure of the substituted tree follows from the previously proved instantiation/substitution equation and closure-by-name-coverage equivalence; no additional free-name induction is needed. substitution_hint handles the only root-hint change: replacing a variable. Its environment lookup identifies the exact rich input type authenticated by the replacement value. Every other root hint remains unchanged.

The source substitution proof follows the existing binder, clause and resource cases. substitutePlans retargets clause witnesses to the actual substituted annotated bodies; its signature theorem reuses raw required-action preservation. Clause port typing, continuation usage, coverage and mode checks reuse their existing substitution laws through erasure. The resource case uses full-tree instantiation/substitution commutation and the replacement's checked metadata closure. The conclusion retains the same rich result type, owner demand, requirements and checking signature. No successful successor execution is assumed.

SourceAnnotatedReduction.lean extracts the original annotated lambda body, substitutes it and reuses the existing requirement-evaluation proofs for bind and beta reduction. Beta enters the existing no-ticket scope. Branch selection retains the selected annotated source derivation, preserves the owner-demand multiset and obtains a sublist of the previous checked effect row. reduction_preserves combines these cases for every supplied SourceAnnotatedCode.Reduction: bind, beta, true branch and false branch. This relation does not include resource/handler entry, capture, resumption, disposal, builtin operations or frame returns.

SourceAnnotatedReductionExamples.lean binds and calls a closed function whose body acquires a local resource and refers to that cell. The actual bind and beta steps and both successor source judgments are checked, with unchanged requirement evaluation. The local resource body still has its source proof for every fresh opening; no globally closed replacement for its local resource names is imposed.

This completes annotated closed substitution and source preservation for those four syntax reductions. The runtime retention layer below now adds context recomposition, annotated current/saved records and all ten focus forms at the stronger scheduled-state level. The older combined runtime preservation theorem still covers six focus forms; its connection to that stronger state remains open. General declaration admission, complete initial admission and entry/capture integration remain open.

Annotated runtime retention and focus

SourceAnnotatedRecomposition.lean defines finite context closure by plugging a closed unit placeholder. plug_closed_iff proves that a plugged expression is metadata-closed exactly when the saved context and child are closed. It covers all ten contexts, including the local binder in a saved resource body. Actual focus derives this context property from the parent's source proof. context_plug combines the structural context, its checked result hint and finite closure with any checked child of the same rich input type. The conclusion constructs the complete annotated source and reuses the existing requirement-evaluation and owner-demand equations. It has no premise about successful future evaluation.

SourceAnnotatedRuntime.lean retains annotated contexts, handler clauses, cleanup callbacks and saved callback results as runtime data. All seven frame forms and all four stack forms are represented, including recursively saved live continuations. Erasure projects these records to the existing scoped machine. Stack append preserves erasure. Focus, plugging and the four ordinary syntax reductions project to their existing raw steps; no new ownership or continuation operation is defined. Runtime data carry the existing lexical translation and raw closed-value evidence, not source typing or a successful-execution certificate.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeTyping.lean checks those actual records. A plain frame retains its annotated context source, checked result hint and finite metadata closure. Handler frames retain annotated declarations; armed/running frames retain annotated callback and saved-value source. The segment judgment follows the full stack, including dormant saved segments. Frame.erase and Segment.erase construct the old scheduled judgments at the same rich types, demands, requirements and plan forest. Port projections identify the incoming type from the actual stack. These proofs do not choose a second source typing after discarding annotations.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeState.lean combines annotated current source and those pending segments with the existing closing records, scheduling, resource/owner checks and plan-registry match. Its erasure constructs SourceScheduledState.State. Initial construction, current-source replacement and bind/beta preservation are checked. Their pending annotated stack stays intact; the existing requirement-evaluation proof reconstructs the combined check. Closing records and saved-plan registries still use their old erased interfaces, so retaining annotations through their execution remains an integration obligation.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeFocus.lean proves progress and preservation for all ten focus forms in this stronger state. focus_checked uses the existing signature-splitting theorem to obtain actual child and context plans. focus_preserves accepts any frame matching the actual annotated context and scope whose finite port guard passes. The guard reads the child hint and the retained stack input; source checking and segment typing derive agreement with the same rich intermediate type. The proof constructs the annotated child state, saved plain frame and combined scheduling/effect check. It reuses the existing template transport and row-reassociation laws. focus_progress constructs a passing frame from current source evidence, then applies that preservation theorem.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeExamples.lean constructs an initial annotated state for both parameter-type choices in the earlier ambiguous binding program. Each focuses using its matching frame and then evaluates the inner binding while retaining that same annotated saved frame. Returning reconstructs the outer binding, whose reduction reaches unit with an empty stack and empty owner demand. A finite negative check rejects the other parameter type. No intermediate invariant is supplied independently.

The boundaries are distinct: the stronger annotated scheduled state now covers all ten focus forms, while the older combined RetainedStep theorem below still covers six. Connecting that combined theorem to the stronger state remains open. Capture allocation, including registry extension, resumption and disposal now have the annotated preservation proofs described below; disposal retains its explicit typed-plan interface at the source-state layer. Entry and builtin results below cover the scheduled-state layer; their connection to the common execution interface remains separate. Value returns and retirement are covered by the following results. General consuming declaration admission and complete initial admission also remain open. This work neither changes Core semantics nor establishes a general Core simulation.

Annotated returns and retirement

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeReturns.lean derives value summaries and pending checks from the annotated state. plug_checked reconstructs the actual context plan and source from the saved frame and returned value. plug_preserves restores the saved scope and constructs the successor state, including its transported closing templates and requirement evaluation. It uses the stored context hint and metadata closure, with no successor-source premise.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeComputation.lean lifts branch selection to this state. ordinary_preserves combines it with the existing bind and beta proofs, retaining the annotated pending stack and deriving the resulting demand permutation and effect-row sublist. Its ordinary reduction relation covers binding, application and both branches; builtin operations are separate obligations.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeBoundaries.lean preserves annotated state across handler, cell and consumed-clause returns, cleanup startup/completion and closing completion. Cleanup startup constructs the annotated invocation from the retained callback source and saves the actual annotated return value in the running frame. These proofs reuse existing requirement export and closing-template transport. They do not broaden the current declaration recipe grammar.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeRetirement.lean transports annotated frames and recursively saved segments through phase changes that preserve availability for their retained live owners. It reuses SourceScheduledPhaseRestriction.local_restrict; there is no replacement scheduling algorithm or added future-validity premise. retire constructs the successor after removing a retiring frame, proves that the old demand is exactly the retired owner followed by the remaining demand, and derives the corresponding ownership phase trace. Source annotations and the actual retained plans survive this restriction.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeReturnSteps.lean collects all eight annotated return forms. ReturnStep.erase projects each to the existing raw machine. Conversely, ReturnStep.of_raw lifts every raw step whose current expression is a value to an annotated step with the same erased successor and owner events. This converse uses only runtime data and value shape; it does not assume successor typing. return_preserves then derives annotated successor state, exact retired-ticket demand consumption, no newly allocated owner, and the ownership phase trace. raw_return_preserves combines these results for arbitrary raw returned-value steps.

This closes returned-value preservation at the annotated scheduled-state layer, including retirement. It does not yet connect that layer to the combined runtime ledger/completion theorem or derive complete initial admission. Capture allocation, resumption and disposal are covered below. The following entry/builtin results retain the same boundary on the combined theorem. Core correspondence remains an assessment rather than a general simulation theorem.

Annotated entry and builtin replies

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeEntries.lean derives cleanup entry from the current annotated source and a value callback. It exposes the callback requests and answer port, constructs the actual annotated action for any supplied identity and matching answer type, and derives the body state with that armed frame. Callback source and its latent plan stay together. cleanup_preserves chooses an answer type representing the exposed port. The existing requirement evaluation and callback scheduling proofs supply the successor checks; none are assumed for the successor.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeHandlers.lean transports annotated frames and segments when registry entries agree at every retained activation, including activations in dormant captures. handler_annotations exposes the source table, clause families, declaration requirements and answer port. For any fresh activation and matching answer type, it constructs the annotated handler, registers those source entries and proves the resulting body state. The pending source and plans survive the registry update. This reuses existing registration agreement and activation relocation; it still uses the current structural recipe evidence and does not broaden its grammar.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeWorld.lean transports annotated declaration/context sources, frames and recursively saved segments into a larger resource world. It reuses the existing annotated expression transport, value transport and scheduled-plan transport. Metadata checks and stored type choices remain unchanged.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeResources.lean uses that transport for resource acquisition. resource_annotations derives that the ready initializer is an integer, exposes an answer port and a finite forbidden-name set, and proves entry for every supplied identity fresh in both the world and that set. The actual annotated body is instantiated at the new identity, including its metadata; its erased body executes the existing resource entry rule. resource_preserves chooses a fresh identity and matching answer type. The additional forbidden-name set comes from the existing hidden-requirement support proof. It is not replaced by freshness in the visible world or by the answer type's resource names.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCells.lean retains annotations during builtin selection. Its structural CellUpdate changes only the selected active cell payload, respects a nearer matching source handler, and leaves dormant captures untouched. CellUpdate.erase gives the existing raw update; CellUpdate.of_raw lifts every such raw update while retaining the actual annotated frames and captures. update_segment preserves the same rich source indices and plan forest. read_preserves and write_preserves derive the reply source, remove the request's checked effect row and preserve the owner set. builtin_step_preserves covers every nonallocating raw step from a request with a value operand, assuming the authenticated builtin operation signatures; it constructs an annotated successor erasing to that exact raw successor.

These results cover entry witnesses and builtin replies at the annotated scheduled-state layer. They do not assert that arbitrary raw entry annotations are correct. The common execution interface still needs to obtain and check the exposed entry data, including resource support and fresh handler registration, and combine source preservation with the runtime ledger and completion proofs. Capture allocation and disposal must also preserve this stronger state; resumption is covered below. General declaration admission and complete initial admission remain separate obligations.

Annotated capture splitting and resumption

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeSegments.lean proves append and physical splitting for annotated segments. Both directions retain the actual frame sources, rich intermediate types, plan forests, demands and stored requirement records. The requirement-evaluation equation uses the same ordered receiving suffix as the existing scheduled proof. Reassociation uses the existing scope, hint, forest and requirement laws. Rechecking consumes the structural schedule supplied by invocation rules and retains the same source; it does not recover source typing from erased dependencies.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCuts.lean lifts raw prefix/suffix and live-boundary splits to the original annotated runtime data. Its HandlerCut mirrors exact interpretation selection, including matching builtin blockers and dormant saved segments crossed inside live frames. HandlerCut.erase projects selection to the existing machine; HandlerCut.of_raw lifts every raw selection back to the actual annotated capture, suffix and handler. HandlerCut.reconstructs recovers the complete stack by append. Annotated ClauseAt similarly preserves selection in both directions, retaining the chosen clause body. These are structural data proofs, with no successor typing or capture-admission premise.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCaptureSplitting.lean applies that cut to the annotated segment judgment. capture_segments retains the selected handler's annotated declarations and frame check, the captured source and waiting source, their exact plan-forest split, and the demand and record equations. It also preserves exact operation selection and the existing requirement-evaluation equation. Crossing a live frame keeps its dormant source attached. This proves typed capture decomposition; fresh continuation allocation, contract insertion and selected-clause entry are subsequent obligations.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeResumption.lean reuses the existing invocation-check decomposition and ownership-consumption proofs. replace_live splits the checked stack at the selected live boundary, obtains the captured and caller schedules from the invocation, and reconstructs the annotated saved/caller segments after spending that owner. resume_segments combines those sources with the existing record removal, effect evaluation, closing-record transport and ownership phase trace. resume_cut_preserves therefore constructs the complete annotated scheduled successor for a ready resume, with demand equal to the consumed owner followed by the remaining demand. No successor-source or restored-schedule premise is independently supplied.

raw_resume_preserves removes the requirement to supply an annotated cut: every raw resume step from a checked annotated resume expression lifts to an annotated successor with exactly the same erased configuration. The theorem preserves the checked row, derives the remaining demand and records exactly one consumed continuation owner. It supports arbitrary finite prefixes and recursively saved segments; it does not restrict resumption to an immediate or unnested boundary.

These results complete resumption preservation at the annotated scheduled-state layer. They do not yet supply capture allocation/clause-entry preservation, disposal preservation, complete initial/declaration admission, or the combined runtime ledger/completion theorem. Entry's source-derived annotation and resource support data still need a common execution interface. No multishot, escape or suspension rule is introduced.

Annotated clause selection and allocation components

SourceAnnotatedCaptureSources.lean selects the actual annotated body and plan from the installed declarations. The same operation lookup fixes the argument and resumption input types, and the offered mode fixes the selected body family. capture_body_from_requirements reuses the existing structural requirement compiler and pre-capture scheduling proofs for that plan. Its site obligations remain explicit; capture_body derives them for the current recipe grammar using the existing declaration capture theorem. No additional recipe constructor or whole-future-body premise is introduced.

The module's substitution and payload-extension wrappers reuse the checked annotated source proofs. Lexical readiness comes from the existing erased source theorem. body_step pairs the substituted annotated body with the corresponding raw capture step, exact owner addition, owner uniqueness and phase introduction. These conclusions refer to the same selected body and payload; there is no independent source proof for the successor.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeTransport.lean extends contracts, permissions and phases while retaining annotated declaration and context sources, frames and recursively saved segments. Source extension, port-interface extension and scheduled-plan transport are existing proofs. Finite metadata checks and actual plan choices remain unchanged.

SourceAnnotatedAllocationData.lean retains the selected annotated clause with the actual saved/waiting forests and scheduling checks. capture_typed_data derives that data from physical selection, the installed annotated declarations and the existing structural capture-site obligations. allocated_body refines the allocated contract and substitutes the closed payload at the same rich type and plan signature. Erasure constructs the previous scheduled allocation data, including its source body, instead of assuming a separately chosen old derivation.

SourceAnnotatedCaptureInterfaces.lean connects this selected clause to typed capture decomposition. Exact source operation selection and forest append injectivity identify the same captured and waiting pieces. The selected frame retains its annotated declarations and supplied requirements, and the clause source agrees with that frame's refined answer and operation input.

SourceAnnotatedCaptureData.lean keeps those pieces together through allocation. CaptureData.allocated inserts the refined contract, continuation rights and actual saved-plan registry entry; derives the annotated substituted body; and rebuilds the annotated live segment from the original captured and waiting source. Fresh extension preserves older contracts, permissions and saved-plan matches. The existing owner/protection realization proof establishes the new contract's held mode. The same source data also erases to the earlier scheduled capture certificate for reuse by the allocator.

These allocation components now join the closing certificate, stored disposal records and clause-effect evaluation in the annotated capture theorem below. The closing-source construction retains actual callbacks and constructs their typed closing frames. Annotated disposal is connected below with an explicit typed-plan interface. General declaration admission, complete initial admission and the combined execution theorem remain open.

Annotated closing sources and stored records

SourceAnnotatedClosingRuntime.lean retains annotated callbacks in executable closing entries. Plan construction traverses every stack form, including dormant saved continuations, in the same order as the scoped machine. makePlan_erase proves exact agreement with its plan builder; makePlan_of_raw recovers the annotated plan from any successful raw construction on the same stack. closeControl_erase proves that the annotated closing frames erase to the machine's closing control. Protected running, closing and retirement frames still reject plan construction.

SourceAnnotatedClosingPlans.lean extracts callback sources from the actual annotated saved segment. Its structural Contents and Template judgments retain each original callback, rich function type, latent footprint and declaration plan. plan_contents also preserves the exact saved forest's closing projection, including dormant callbacks. Erasure constructs the older template at those same indices. Contract extension, resource-world extension and handler-table changes preserve the retained source; closing contexts contain no handler frames, so the existing table-independence proof applies.

SourceAnnotatedClosingRecomposition.lean materializes the template's callbacks as annotated armed frames. Scheduling and port-level plan typing remain explicit premises, and both check the template's actual erased plan. Template.scheduled_source derives the annotated segment; it does not assume successor typing or reannotate an arbitrary erased callback. Template.scheduled_recompose reuses annotated segment append and retains its exact retirement demand and requirement-evaluation equation under the waiting stack. Changing the caller scope reuses the existing closing-context equation.

SourceAnnotatedClosingRecords.lean stores this stronger template certificate at the existing raw plan and exact saved-forest indices. Record transport reuses captured-origin and unique-owner proofs. It preserves annotated templates through capture relocation, ordinary steps, contract extension, resource-world extension and handler registration. The annotated runtime state's templates field now uses these records. State erasure projects them to the older records; the previously established annotated transition proofs preserve the strengthened invariant.

SourceAnnotatedClosingData.lean connects capture data to this certificate. capture_closing recovers the annotated plan from the actual raw construction, extracts its source once, and retains it in the allocator's capture witness. The older allocator certificate is a projection of this witness. selected_template connects actual record lookup, unique capture location and saved-plan matching to the stronger stored certificate. Certificate.materialize uses that certificate, its schedule and plan typing to construct an annotated closing segment whose erasure is exactly the machine's closing control.

This closes the callback-source retention and materialization gap. The capture theorem below joins that witness to clause-effect evaluation and the complete annotated successor state. The disposal theorem below joins the constructed closing segment to caller recomposition, record consumption and the same state's accounting. The general handler-admission and initial-admission obligations are unchanged. These results remain experimental proof evidence; they do not change current Ash or establish full Core correspondence.

Annotated capture preservation

SourceAnnotatedAllocation.lean joins the annotated clause, captured and waiting segments, stored closing certificates and source-plan registry at one fresh continuation contract. allocate reuses SourceDependencySchemes.allocate_capture_source_from_closing_interfaces with the annotated capture and closing witnesses. The generic allocator supplies record insertion, invocation checks and ownership accounting; annotated substitution and segment reconstruction retain the original rich source types. Existing disposal records keep their original annotated callback certificates.

allocate_without_closing covers captures whose plan builder fails or whose pending owner uses cannot be internalized. Existing checked-cut and clause-mode proofs derive disposal denial. The branch installs the resume record, retains older disposal certificates, and derives the substituted clause's effect check from the same structural row instantiation. This branch is part of the complete capture classification, not a restriction to resumptive clauses.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeCapture.lean connects both allocation branches to the annotated runtime State. capture_preserves constructs the actual substituted annotated clause and live stack, proves their raw capture step, and retains source typing, the shared schedule, annotated closing records and the combined effect check. The new owner is added exactly once; the successor demand is a permutation of that owner followed by the previous demand, and its effect row is included in the previous row. Ownership completion, phase transport, row bounds and footprint checking reuse established proofs.

The theorem applies to every supplied physical handler cut and selected clause under its stated premises. It uses the operation-derived input annotation for the allocated continuation; it does not validate arbitrary annotations supplied to the raw capture rule. The general theorem retains explicit capture-site requirements and captured resource support. Its combined statement uses the existing empty outward guard needed by closing-budget admission; the branch without closing also supports a general outward guard.

SourceAnnotatedRecipeCapture.lean derives the capture-site requirements for the existing structural recipe grammar. capture_from_recipes uses the actual pending source, request schedule, selected clause mode and installed requirement check; it adds no successful future-body premise. Resource support and registry freshness remain explicit, for later connection to the full runtime invariant. General nested-handler consumption and effectful-cleanup declaration admission are still separate open obligations; this specialization does not enlarge the current recipe grammar.

Capture preservation at this annotated source-state layer is now connected. Annotated disposal is connected below. The milestone still requires complete declaration and initial-source admission, the common execution interface, and the combined progress/preservation and finite-execution result. Core correspondence remains a status assessment; no Core alignment is included.

Annotated disposal preservation

SourceAnnotatedDisposal.lean connects the actual stored annotated closing certificate to caller recomposition and record consumption. disposal_parts splits the annotated caller at the selected live owner, obtains the certificate from the actual store lookup, and rechecks the waiting frames under the spent owner phase. The resulting waiting segment keeps its original source annotations. The invocation schedule supplies the closing and caller checks; no successor source or scheduling judgment is assumed.

discard_segments materializes that certificate's annotated callbacks and joins them to the waiting caller through the closing frame. The reconstructed stack erases exactly to the scoped machine's closing control. Existing record permutation, lookup transport and consumed-owner proofs remove the discarded continuation's resume record and the records owned by its captured stack. The remaining records retain their annotated certificates. Existing phase and requirement-evaluation equations establish the successor's effect check and unique ownership.

discard_cut_preserves constructs the complete annotated successor state for a ready disposal at the supplied live cut. It produces the machine step, preserves the checked effect row, removes exactly the selected owner from current demand, and proves the owner permutation and phase transition. Cleanup entries still carry the captured owners until their retirement steps consume them; disposal does not silently remove those owners from the accounting.

The source-state theorem retains an explicit typed-plan interface, together with the actual closing-plan construction and owner resolution. It does not claim progress from this source state alone. The existing SourceScheduledExecution.Run.discard_preserves derives that interface from the runtime's retained continuation certificate. Connecting the annotated state to the same runtime invariant must reuse that derivation. Captured source admission, initial admission and the common execution theorem remain open; this proof adds no multishot, escaping or suspending continuation behavior.

Annotated runtime integration

SourceAnnotatedExecution.lean joins the actual annotated configuration to the existing runtime invariant. Its Run retains one action map, owner registry, issued-name history, completion result and annotated source forest. Run.erase constructs the older scheduled run from those same witnesses. It does not assume an unrelated source derivation for the erased program. Initial assembly still requires separate source, scheduling, finite initial-check, completion and signature premises; it is not complete program admission.

SourceAnnotatedRuntimeDisposal.lean proves Run.discard_preserves for every actual named/access-checked disposal step from this state. raw_discard_shape recovers the actual annotated live cut from the raw step through the existing stack decomposition lemma. The retained runtime certificate supplies plan typing for the same contract and plan. Annotated source preservation then constructs the restored cleanup and caller, with exact erasure to the raw target. Runtime assembly reuses completion, ownership, access, usage and name-history preservation. The result consumes exactly the selected owner from the source demand. Run.discard_progress derives an actual step and this successor from the invariant alone; neither theorem takes a separate typed-plan or successor-validity premise.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionCapture.lean connects both capture allocation branches to the same runtime. For the supplied physical handler cut and selected clause, retained access and unique ownership derive captured resource support. The issued-name history supplies freshness for contracts, actions and saved annotations. The source-selected operation result annotation and clause substitution determine the actual successor, and the existing completion proof constructs its owner record. Existing certificate allocation preserves disposal evidence. Run.capture_progress chooses the new owner from the finite ledger. The result adds exactly that owner, retains the annotated captured and waiting pieces, and produces an effect row contained in the previous row.

This capture result uses the existing structural declaration recipes. It still takes handler selection, clause selection and the offered operation lookup as premises. It does not cover arbitrary raw capture input annotations or complete general declaration admission. Its source-derived annotation is the one already used by the annotated capture theorem.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionFocus.lean lifts all ten annotated focus forms into Run. Run.focus_preserves handles every supplied frame satisfying the existing finite port guard. Run.focus_progress constructs such a frame from the retained source hints. Both reuse source focus, completion and runtime assembly; the frame and guard carry no successor typing. This includes function position, application argument, binding initializer and cleanup action, in addition to the six forms in the older retained-event theorem.

The other annotated transition families and exhaustive progress now join this Run below. The checked annotated event relation separately proves universal preservation for every transition family. Exact annotated disposal and progress within that relation are now connected below. General consuming declaration admission and complete initial-program admission remain open. The older retained-event theorem continues to have its stated six-focus scope. This is proof-experiment evidence, with no change to current Ash or Core correspondence.

Annotated progress and finite execution

SourceAnnotatedExecutionStable.lean connects every raw returned-value step, including cleanup completion and ticket retirement, to the annotated runtime. The actual successor erases to the supplied raw target. The source demand loses exactly the tickets retired by that step. Returned-value progress is terminal at an empty annotated stack and otherwise constructs such a successor. Ready builtin replies reuse the retained operation signature and exact cell-selection proof; they preserve owner demand and may reduce the checked effect row.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionComputation.lean recovers an annotated reduction from every raw ready bind, beta or branch step. The selected body or branch is the actual retained term. Existing source substitution and completion proofs then preserve Run, with the same owner multiset and a sublist of the previous effect row. Ready progress reuses the existing raw source progress theorem and this preservation result.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionResumption.lean joins full-prefix resumption to Run for every actual annotated live cut. Existing usage and accessibility locate the live owner for progress. Stack lifting recovers the original annotated capture and waiting caller. Resumption consumes exactly the selected owner; it does not assume a new caller source or restrict nesting depth.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionEntries.lean connects resource, handler and cleanup entry to the same invariant. Resource annotations expose a finite forbidden-name set, including requirement support, and an answer port; all supplied identities and types meeting those conditions are admitted. Handler annotations retain the source-selected capability table, clause families and declaration requirements, and register them under a fresh activation. Cleanup annotations retain the original callback, request list and answer port. Existing completion and ledger proofs establish the corresponding runtime successors. Each entry theorem also constructs a fresh choice for progress. These are source-derived annotation witnesses; a final event interface must still authenticate its metadata choices independently of successor validity.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionProgress.lean proves Run.progress for every configuration satisfying the annotated invariant. It reuses the existing typed current-form classification and lifts raw focus, handler cuts and clause selection to the actual annotated syntax. Request coverage derives both the selected clause and its offered capability entry; these are no longer premises of the combined progress theorem. Every case returns either an ordinary terminal or an actual named/access-checked step and a successor Run, including updated owner and interpretation registries.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionFiniteRuns.lean reuses the existing counted machine steps and finite-prefix induction pattern. For any fuel, Run.finite_prefix constructs that many steps unless an ordinary terminal is reached first. The endpoint retains the annotated invariant. Run.terminal_accounting reuses the owner ledger to prove that every issued owner has been discharged exactly once at termination. initial_finite_prefix starts this construction from the current explicit source, scheduling, finite initial-check, completion and signature premises.

This is exhaustive progress and existence of finite checked executions. It does not establish preservation for every trace of the final event interface, and it does not combine the initial premises into complete admission. That interface must authenticate annotation and registry choices without carrying intermediate or successor Run proofs. General handler-bearing and effectful-cleanup consuming declaration admission remains open. No multishot, escape, suspension, async or Core alignment is included.

Checked annotated events

ResourceRowNarrowing.lean proves that inserting a builtin interpretation can narrow a successfully checked effect row while preserving the owner demand. It reuses ordered residual composition and the existing requirement-checking rules. The new resource source theorem therefore accepts every identity fresh in the resource world; equality of the old row no longer requires excluding additional hidden requirement names.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionResourceEntry.lean checks a supplied resource answer annotation against the source node's finite hint and derives the successor for every historically fresh resource owner. SourceAnnotatedExecutionCheckedEntries.lean does the same for the concrete handler and cleanup records. The handler's clauses, effect and scope are the actual source fields. Cleanup checks both the enclosing answer port and the callback's request list. The existing handler and cleanup source proofs now expose these exact witnesses; preservation constructs the handler tables, clause families and requirements. An event supplies none of those proof registries. Positive and negative examples check wrong answer ports, unresolved resource hints and fabricated cleanup requests.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionExactControl.lean reuses ordinary, returned-value and builtin source preservation at the supplied annotated successor. Existing runtime completion and ownership proofs assemble the shared invariant. This avoids treating equality of erased successors as equality of annotated syntax. Capture preservation now also exposes its existing exact substituted clause, saved stack and operation input type witnesses.

SourceAnnotatedExecutionEvents.lean defines a common Step relation for all ten focus forms, ordinary reduction, all eight return forms, full-prefix resumption, builtin reads and writes, resource/handler/cleanup entry, both capture branches, and disposal. Its fixed parameters are the operation port signature and result port. Constructors carry actual syntax and structural selection, finite port checks and name freshness. They do not carry source judgments, proof registries or successor validity. Capture uses the canonical embedded result port of the selected operation; preservation derives the corresponding rich contract and owner record.

step_preserves proves preservation for every supplied event in that relation, with an exact annotated target. steps_preserve applies induction to every supplied finite trace. It constructs all intermediate invariants and threads changes to contracts, owner records, handler tables, declaration families, requirements and saved annotations. The final effect row is a subset of the initial row. terminal_accounting derives exact-once owner discharge for every terminal endpoint of such a trace.

Disposal now retains exact annotated-plan provenance. SourceAnnotatedCaptureIdentity.lean lifts capture location to the annotated stack and proves uniqueness under the existing one-shot ownership invariant. Closing certificates are indexed by the actual capture and retain its makePlan equation. Record transport reuses structural capture-origin proofs through cell updates, resumption and disposal. Run.discard_at therefore preserves the supplied annotated closing control; the common disposal event needs only resolution, actual plan construction and freshness. Existing ownership, access and completion proofs are reused.

SourceAnnotatedClosingIdentity.lean retains a regression for the former erased-only certificate representation: two well-typed callbacks can erase identically while carrying different internal annotations. Its ErasedCertificate witnesses explain the need to retain provenance; they do not apply to the strengthened Certificate index.

SourceAnnotatedEventSelection.lean reuses existing source progress, exact entry witnesses, physical capture selection and hint agreement to select common events. SourceAnnotatedEventProgress.lean reuses the typed current-form classification to prove progress: every runtime state satisfying Run is terminal or has a Step of the same relation used by preservation. finite_progress applies steps_preserve and this theorem to any supplied finite trace, deriving endpoint progress from just its initial runtime invariant. General consuming declaration admission and complete initial-program admission remain separate obligations. This evidence concerns the DN-0033 experiment; it does not change current Ash semantics or establish general Core correspondence.

Universal preservation for retained events

SourceScheduledRetainedRuns.lean establishes universal preservation for an explicit part of the final execution interface. RetainedStep operations contracts result has five constructors: the existing CallableRuns.StableEvent, an actual named/access-checked disposal step, focusRequest, focusResume and focusContext. The fixed result is the erased initial result type, not a new type chosen at each step. Stable events include value returns and their cleanup/closing transitions, ready bind/application/branch computation, builtin reads/writes, and resumption. Disposal may allocate a closing owner; the source contract, handler and saved-plan registries remain unchanged.

focusRequest takes a nonvalue operand, the actual request context, and checkRequestPorts = true. This executable guard compares the frame's erased input/output ports with the fixed operation signature. Its soundness theorem exposes exactly that equality. The event requires no source typing or runtime invariant at the intermediate node. Run.request_frame_ports extracts the same port equality from a retained typed request frame. request_focus_preserves uses that fact and the earlier focus_annotations theorem to admit every supplied matching frame. It applies to any operation and retained stack; the cell-read example is not a restriction on the rule.

RequestFocusExamples.focus_bind_plug constructs a three-event trace: focus a cell-read operand, evaluate its ordinary binding, then return the reference through the plain request frame. focused_trace_preserves applies the common finite-execution theorem to this mixed trace. Separate executable checks reject wrong input and output ports. The example assumes the starting Run for its preservation result; it does not claim new initial-program admission.

focusResume resolves the lexical continuation binder, looks up its retained contract, and checks both erased ports with checkResumePorts. The Run.resume_frame_ports lemma extracts those ports from the actual typed frame; resume_focus_preserves reuses focus_annotations. The guard grants no resume permission and cannot revive a consumed owner. The resume examples check unresolved binders, missing contracts and wrong ports, construct operand binding/return followed by full-prefix resumption, and reuse the common finite preservation theorem.

focusContext uses checkContextPorts for four context forms. stackInputPort reads the incoming port of the actual annotated stack; for an empty stack it uses the fixed execution result port. The existing source-to-port erasure and StackTyped constructors prove this agrees with the source derivation. contextInputPort then projects the appropriate component for a pair, returns boolean for a branch condition, or integer for a resource initializer. Run.context_frame_ports combines these facts, and context_focus_preserves applies the same generic focus theorem. No new substitution, capture or ownership induction is needed.

The context guard rejects reversed pair ports, wrong result ports, and forms whose input types these data do not determine. Its local stack-head examples are guard checks, not claims that arbitrary whole stacks are well typed. ContextFocusExamples.nested_resume_branch supplies a seven-event mixed trace: resume focus, branch-condition focus, binding, condition return, branch choice, resume-argument return and one-shot consumption. The caller prefix and saved continuation are arbitrary finite stacks. nested_resume_preserves applies the common finite theorem from an assumed initial Run; the example does not add initial-program admission. None of its intermediate nodes carries a Run.

No constructor contains the successor invariant or successful checking of future code. Stable events carry their existing raw transition and local syntax premises. Disposal carries the existing freshness and access checks; Run.discard_preserves derives its closing-plan typing and source successor from the current retained evidence. The event interface does not accept an arbitrary raw disposal without those checks.

The runtime computation layer now exposes ready_preserves for any supplied ready raw step. It reuses the source substitution/branch theorem and the result contract theorem. ready_progress selects a source step and applies that preservation result. stable_preserves then reuses the value, ready, builtin and resumption proofs; retained_step_preserves adds the existing disposal and focus proofs. No capture, recomposition, ownership or substitution induction is duplicated.

retained_run_preserves uses Relation.TransGen and its ordinary induction. For every supplied nonempty finite RetainedStep sequence and one initial Run, it derives the actual named/access-checked execution, an endpoint Run with its retained forest and owner demand, and an endpoint effect row that is a sublist of the initial row. Intermediate invariants are conclusions of the induction, not fields of the execution trace. The empty sequence retains its initial invariant directly. Existing endpoint progress and terminal accounting apply to the derived Run.

This is a universal theorem for the stated event forms, not the completed one-shot execution theorem. Six of the ten focus cases are integrated; the four remaining cases are function position, application argument, binding initializer and cleanup action. Their source type choices are not determined by the current context/stack guard. Resource/handler/cleanup installation still requires authenticated source annotations; capture additionally changes the contract and saved-plan registries. Those events must be integrated into the final interface. General consuming declaration admission and complete initial-term admission remain separate obligations. No Core semantics change or general correspondence theorem follows from this result.

Remaining proof construction

The one-shot milestone remains incomplete. The selected execution model is lexical unwinding, described below. Earlier plan-dependent source theorems are reusable components, not a safety theorem for this changed machine.

Connection Verified components Outstanding obligation
Runtime typing and interpretation Local port proofs cover capture, resume, discard, all value/unwind transitions, ordinary computation and scope entry. Effect checking reuses the existing ordered interfaces through a lookup-preserving projection. Source focus and plug now construct matching runtime and source frames. Finish authenticating annotations at the other constructing transitions and join the port and effect facets throughout execution; construction of a typed successor does not prove preservation for arbitrary raw annotation choices.
Structural source admission Existing expression typing, capability annotations, completion bounds and structural receiver checks; lexical source capture/append, resumption, focus/plug, cleanup entry/return and fresh-environment transport, with the local premises described below Preserve source evidence for continuation use, interpretation availability, release exclusion and outward operand support in reachable states. The recorded protection bit now agrees with actual captures and supplies the source discard guard; source expressions and callback annotations still need preservation. Integrate the lexical source checks in place of legacy plan-routing checks throughout admission and preservation. Preserve rich captures, outside-owner calls, branches, callable/resource bodies, effectful cleanup and disposing interpretations.
Common event preservation Generic ownership preservation; resource-support preservation with two local pre-step checks; local typing and effect results; exhaustive use-accounting and continuation-access preservation for structurally checked events, joined with ownership and ticket history; capture-protection preservation under source-registry extension and authenticated allocation Assemble a common invariant and derive its successor for every admitted event, including callback execution and return to unwinding. No event may assume its successor invariant or safety of future execution.
Initial-source safety and progress Legacy initial-source construction, finite-trace induction, progress components and terminal ledger accounting Establish the new common invariant from sufficient source admission, propagate it through finite execution, and prove progress and terminal accounting. Run the final combined verification.

The existing AtUse.provide, structural receiver rechecking, cleanup obligation checks, AtPackets.capture_use_step and initial annotation theorem are evidence to reuse where their premises still apply. Completing their old plan-dependent variants is not a prerequisite for the selected semantics. Their intended source coverage remains required; a smaller grammar or an assumed future-safe state would not complete the milestone.

Source admission may combine independently checked expression types, capability annotations, their structural validation, completion bounds and signature agreement. Deriving every check from plain expression typing is not a separate requirement. The missing connection is from these source checks to the new runtime invariant, not from a supplied runtime invariant to itself.

Core correspondence remains a status assessment: report proved relations, unproved obligations and demonstrated mismatches. Aligning Core or its specification is outside this milestone. Multishot, escape, suspension and asynchronous continuations remain separate targets whose integration is deferred.

Lexical cleanup and local unwinding

The selected design direction is local unwinding of an abandoned continuation. Its captured scopes retain their structure: run each scope's cleanup before leaving that scope, while enclosing interpretations and resources remain available. A handler installation has a distinct identity. Cleanup bound to an installation does not choose another finalizer when a nested scope is installed. This does not by itself pin every effect performed inside that finalizer. Closure capture must preserve the referenced scope's lifetime; explicit early finalization is not introduced by this change.

The existing experimental makePlan does not implement this rule. It extracts callbacks, releases and ticket retirements, but drops captured source handlers before any callback executes. InitialCleanupRouteGap already contains a small source example exposing this difference. The local-unwind work replaces this planning dependency; it does not require repairing or extending the planner. This is a change to the experimental calculus, not current Ash or Core.

SourceResourceRoutes.lean, under LexicalUnwind, now defines the administrative fragment. It removes only the top ordinary frame, handler boundary, cell or spent boundary. A live captured owner exposes its saved scopes with a retirement marker after them. It cannot skip an armed or running callback. append proves that each local step leaves an added enclosing suffix unchanged. accounting, preserves_ledger and no_double_completion reuse the existing ownership representation, ledger and list-permutation laws. They do not require a generated plan or assume a valid successor.

The example disposal_scope_mismatch checks that the original callback scope resolves to handler installation 101 and the old plan has lost it. cleanup_runs and cleanup_run reuse the current ordinary scope-exit rules and trace-to-run proof: the callback invokes its enclosing handler, resumes once, completes, and only then leaves the handler scopes. This verifies reference behavior for the small example; it is not a proof of general disposal or source admission.

LexicalUnwind.Machine now distinguishes ordinary evaluation from unwinding. The existing stack has one additional internal unwinding frame. Starting a cleanup replaces its armed frame with that return marker and calls the same closed callback. When it returns Unit, evaluation switches back to unwinding. The enclosing handler records, including their original answer types, remain unchanged. cleanup_entry_ports reuses the existing Unit-to-Unit callback typing; it does not invent an ordinary return value for the abandoned scope.

Transition.discard enters unwinding on the captured stack itself, with a close boundary delimiting the disposing caller. At that boundary it returns Unit to the caller. It constructs no cleanup plan. The reused ordinary evaluator excludes RawStep.discard, so the old planner is not an alternative disposal rule in this machine. Running cleanup remains protected from abandonment by the existing protection check. Capture and resumption carry the new return marker through the same stack operations; callback_cut reuses the existing handler cut unchanged. Ordinary pending computation encountered during unwinding is abandoned; its registered cleanup is still executed before its scopes are left.

Normal return through a retirement marker preserves the returned value. Normal return through a disposal boundary produces Unit for its caller. These two local exits generalize the old plan's Unit-only boundary behavior; unwinding itself still produces no ordinary result.

transition_accounting covers every new machine transition. The event wrapper checks fresh owner allocation against lifetime history. execution_preserves_ledger and execution_no_double_completion use the existing ledger and the library's finite-trace induction. DisposalExample.execution executes the earlier small counterexample in eleven transitions, including disposal, an effectful callback, one resumption, local scope exit and return to the caller. Its final ledger and exactly_once show that all issued owners are completed exactly once.

FramePorts, StackPorts and MachinePorts give structural local port rules for ordinary evaluation and unwinding. Ordinary stack typing embeds through ordinary_stack_ports. Composition is explicit at each adjacent frame. The administrative steps, cleanup call/return and both boundary exits preserve these ports; retirement carries the same port through, and a close boundary returns Unit regardless of the abandoned answer port. Existing callable typing is reused.

handler_cut_ports, capture_ports, resume_ports and discard_ports extend the existing stack decomposition and recomposition proofs to the new marker. They reuse ordinary clause selection, substitution, scope typing and historical ticket extension. Capture constructs an actual transition and a typed successor; resume restores the typed capture and clause prefix; discard enters unwinding without changing the captured handlers or constructing a plan. These are port results, independent of whether requests have an available interpretation or whether continuation use and resource access are permitted.

value_transition_ports covers every transition starting from a value, including ordinary frame returns and the new cleanup return marker. unwind_transition_ports covers every transition starting in unwind mode. Both derive successor typing from predecessor typing and the transition; neither assumes it. Existing value, context plugging and substitution proofs supply the expression cases.

ordinary_step_ports handles bindings, application, branching and builtin cell reads/writes through the existing ordinary step family. focus_ports, handler_entry_ports, cleanup_entry_machine_ports and resource_entry_ports construct typed transitions using the existing focus elaboration, clause typing, callback typing and fresh resource instantiation proofs. World extension checks every retained frame and dormant capture. These construction results do not admit arbitrary raw annotation choices.

effectView is a proof-only projection that reads an unwind return marker as its retained armed action for effect checking. It keeps every handler, cell, callback, and dormant capture. effect_view_resolve proves identical nearest-handler lookup; effect_view_cut preserves the selected handler record. Execution, port typing, ownership and protection use the original stack. This projection neither builds a disposal schedule nor fabricates a saved result.

MachineEffects reuses the existing effect interfaces through this projection. machine_request_provided_or_exported derives interpretation availability or membership in the outward row. unwind_transition_effects covers every unwind-mode transition, while capture_effects and resume_effects reuse the existing effect decomposition, substitution and recomposition proofs. discard_effects requires the captured outward row to be covered by its closing row. Capture allocates equal resume and closing rows; closing_rows_insert preserves that coverage in the historical registry. initial_machine_typing derives initial port and effect typing from source expression typing alone, without claiming the other source-admission facets.

MachineAccess reuses structural retained-resource support. discard_access uses the existing resumption support proof because the disposer restores the same enclosing scopes. The close boundary has no resource payload or visibility. transition_access covers every new transition, requiring only local release and capture checks for ordinary evaluation. Those checks exclude a released resource from a returned value and establish outward support of a captured request's operand. Unwind-mode steps need no extra access check, and disposal has no plan-based access premise. Source derivation of the two ordinary checks remains necessary.

UnwindPrefix structurally checks the scopes before a disposal delimiter, including recursively owned captures and locally introduced retirement markers. It has no case for skipping an already running cleanup or crossing another disposal delimiter. unprotected_unwind_prefix derives it from the existing protection guard at discard; UnwindReady places this prefix before the actual closing boundary and an unrestricted ordinary caller suffix. Every actual discard constructs this evidence, and administrative unwinding preserves it.

unwind_progress proves that such a state has a next transition: pop a scope, enter a callback, expand a dormant capture, or finish at the delimiter. checked_unwind_progress joins that result with port, effect, resource-support and ledger preservation for the same actual event. Callback evaluation remains an ordinary successor; its success or termination is not assumed. Preserving readiness through callback capture/resumption and return still requires the source/runtime connection. Neither this branch theorem nor its structural readiness premise establishes full source progress.

checkUnwindPrefix and checkUnwindReady decide the structural boundary judgments. Their soundness/completeness proofs inspect the existing stack, without building or executing a cleanup plan. unwind_ready_append_iff gives an exact open-stack interface: a composed stack is ready precisely when the boundary is already in its first fragment, or that fragment is unwindable and the enclosing suffix supplies the boundary. A capture is therefore not required to be independently ready.

handler_cut_unwind_boundary applies that interface to the existing handler cut. callback_resume_ready recomposes the scopes behind a captured cleanup return marker. If the boundary is captured, inserted clause frames are outside it; otherwise the proof requires those inserted frames to be unwindable. The theorem retains the same selected handler and derives readiness of the restored suffix. Deriving this local compatibility condition from admitted source, and covering arbitrary ordinary callback prefixes, remain obligations of the runtime/source connection; the theorem does not assume the restored successor is ready.

The old FrameTyped and source judgments deliberately do not admit the new internal marker. FrameUse and StackUse now distinguish ordinary evaluation from unwinding, with entry and exit modes for each open fragment. Ordinary frames reuse FrameDemand; unwinding skips their pending code and counts only internal retirement. A live boundary in unwind mode additionally counts its own eventual retirement. The callback-return marker changes ordinary evaluation to unwinding; the closing delimiter changes unwinding back to ordinary evaluation. These are proof interfaces, not additional runtime modes or cleanup plans.

MachineUse balances current and pending ticket demand against ownership. It is an accounting facet, not a replacement for lexical accessibility, protection, or source admission. The checked results cover all administrative unwind steps, cleanup entry and return, closing and retirement, evaluation focus, and capture. Capture retains the saved fragment's actual exit mode and reuses clause-use substitution and historical registry extension. Initial accounting follows from the existing source use judgment.

prefix_use_unwind converts an abandonable fragment to its owned-ticket demand. Resume and discard recomposition have checked event-level accounting results. discard_machine_use derives exact capture-demand balance from predecessor accounting, unique ownership, the existing protection guard and finite bounds on pending uses in the three affected fragments. capture_demand_balance reuses balanced_middle_demands; exact balance is no longer an admission premise.

returnMode computes the captured fragment's exit mode from its actual lexical boundaries. ReentryBounds distinguishes ordinary return, which imposes no abandonment condition, from return into unwinding. The latter checks that the inserted caller fragment is unwindable, its pending uses are internal, and the saved and outer fragments do not demand its owners. reentry_from_bounds derives exact caller accounting with the same existing disjoint-demand lemma; resume_machine_use then proves accounting after actual recomposition. checkReentryBounds has a soundness/completeness theorem and inspects only finite predecessor fragments. The same bounds establish the earlier callback boundary compatibility through callback_resume_ready_from_bounds, including open captures whose delimiter remains in the enclosing suffix.

SourceDependencyOwners.PendingFrame and PendingStack connect these pending-use checks to source dependency annotations for actual retained code. Plain frames reuse the existing typed context and Within judgment; frames with no pending invocations contribute no pending-use obligation. This includes the new cleanup-return marker, without pretending that it is an armed callback for protection or execution. segment_pending_stack projects existing source segments and their PendingWithin evidence. Append, decomposition, administrative unwinding and callback-marker insertion preserve this annotation with its fixed owner bound.

source_discard_use and source_resume_use derive event accounting from these source annotations and predecessor accounting/uniqueness; ReentrySource supplies the local resumption bounds. These judgments check only retained pending code. Callback bodies, protection and the other runtime facets remain separate obligations. Establishing and preserving all required source annotations through arbitrary execution, and joining them in the common invariant, remain unfinished. None of these theorems assumes a valid successor or safe future run.

UseTransition now joins all transition families for continuation-use accounting. Ordinary evaluation reuses the established value-demand, substitution, context-replacement, scope-entry and resource-update proofs; resumption and disposal carry the structural bounds described above. Focusing a nonvalue resumption operand remains ordinary evaluation. Every checked use transition erases to the existing Transition; this introduces no alternative runtime semantics. The source invocation constructors build its resume/discard cases from ReentrySource and PendingStack evidence.

UseTransition.preserves is exhaustive for this accounting facet. UseEvent adds fresh allocation and the actual historical ticket registry. UseEvent.preserves combines ownership, registry history and MachineUse; uniqueness and registry freshness follow from the existing ledger and history. use_execution_preserves reuses finite-trace induction, and the initial use judgment establishes this combined accounting invariant. An event carries no successor invariant. This theorem concerns checked event sequences: deriving and preserving their source evidence, combining typing/effects/access/protection, and proving that a next event exists remain necessary for source safety/progress.

TicketAccess now supplies structural continuation accessibility at the same entry/exit modes as StackUse. Ordinary pending code must refer to live tickets in its enclosing suffix or explicit outside interface. A dormant capture is checked against the outer tail, excluding its own live owner. Unwinding skips pending code; internal retirement requires ownership rather than a visible continuation. The judgment reuses the established pending-name/demand correspondence, admits every old ordinary StackUsage derivation, and introduces no restriction to nearest-clause invocation.

Append, decomposition, capture, resumption, disposal and administrative unwinding preserve these interfaces. Removing access to a consumed owner uses existing uniqueness and demand balance. MachineTicketAccess additionally checks the currently evaluated expression. UseTransition.ticket_access and UseEvent.preserves_ticket_access cover every checked transition, including ordinary callbacks and callbacks entered from unwinding. use_execution_preserves_ticket_access combines accessibility with the existing ownership/history/use invariant over finite checked executions; initial accessibility follows from the existing source use judgment.

live_clause_cannot_return reuses the existing ownership contradiction to rule out a value returning past an unconsumed live continuation. This discharges that specific progress obstruction; it does not by itself prove progress for other heads or construct the source evidence required at every invocation. Preservation of source expressions and annotations, and the common typing/effect/resource invariant remain outstanding. The protection connection below supplies the discard guard from those source expressions.

CaptureProtection records a separate fact for each live continuation: its source contract's protection bit equals the protection of its actual saved scopes. It recursively checks dormant captures and their tails. It does not identify disposal permission with absence of protection. The projection captureModes reads these bits from the existing source contracts; there is no additional runtime registry.

transition_capture_protection covers every actual lexical-unwinding transition. It requires that existing records are retained and that a newly allocated continuation records the protection of its actual capture. Source contract extension supplies the former; source_protection_allocation supplies the latter from the contract's capture equality. segment_capture_protection extracts the initial correspondence from the existing source segment, and source_capture_protection reuses fresh insertion and the exact handler cut to preserve older records while introducing a new capture.

source_discard_unprotected inverts the existing source discard rule and uses the recorded correspondence to establish the runtime protection guard. source_checked_discard_transition combines that guard with the existing pending-owner bounds to construct the checked disposal transition. It assumes neither a successful cleanup plan nor a safe successor. These results do not establish preservation of the current source expression or of callback bodies; those remain necessary to apply the rule throughout execution.

SourceDependencyFrames.LexicalFrame retains every existing rich source-frame derivation and adds the actual unwinding return frame plus the general answer interfaces of internal closing and retirement markers. Its ports and interface theorems derive both runtime interfaces from the same source frame. The unwinding rule retains the callback's full function and dependency annotations without inventing a saved result value.

LexicalFrame.start_cleanup constructs the actual callback application using the existing source application and value-transport rules, preserving its latent body annotation. LexicalFrame.finish_cleanup recovers the Unit input, original answer interface, saved scope and unchanged effect boundary. The source-stack lift below reuses these local results. Preserving source expressions throughout callback execution and deriving contextual checks for callback requests remain necessary.

LexicalSegment lifts these frames to the actual recursive stack with the existing enriched values, requirement indices, dormant continuation records and dependency scopes. Segment.lexical embeds every existing source segment. Its ports, connected, capture_protection and realizes results derive coherent runtime interfaces and physical protection from that same source. The effect projection uses the existing permission-sensitive Connected judgment: a dormant continuation does not acquire a resumption obligation when its clause denies resumption. This is not an unconditional MachineEffects derivation for disabled actions.

lexical_capture_segments and lexical_segment_append adapt the existing structural inductions, reusing the same phase, append and requirement-evaluation lemmas. They preserve the enriched intermediate type, exact dependency scopes and continuation records, including captures containing unwinding markers. LexicalSegment.start_cleanup constructs the callback source application and retains the typed suffix; finish_cleanup recovers that same suffix and saved scope. lexical_segment_pending_stack connects finite pending-owner bounds on these scopes to the existing invocation checks. These results preserve source structure at these boundaries; they do not assert that every resulting contextual requirement is satisfied or establish a whole-machine source invariant.

The existing dependency-scope realization now recognizes .unwinding as a running, protected frame. Stored contextual handler declarations recognize it as a frame with no handler of its own. Their structural checker still checks each actual handler at its exact suffix; it does not check callback bodies. SourceContextualForest.Forest.start_cleanup and finish_cleanup preserve the suffix's stored handler declarations when changing or removing this marker. Callback body typing remains the separate source-expression obligation.

lexical_extract_live and lexical_replace_live adapt the existing source extraction proof to the lexical stack. They retain the saved enriched source, replace only the selected live boundary, preserve the continuation-record permutation, and reuse the existing requirement-evaluation equality after that owner is consumed. Other captures in the caller prefix remain intact.

lexical_resume_source starts from the current source resume expression and the same retained source stack. It derives the closed operand, constructs the checked runtime resumption, and constructs the resumed value's rich source type and recomposed stack derivation. The new stack retains the saved and waiting records, with the consumed owner's resume entry removed. The theorem still takes the existing finite reentry bounds and the selected action permission; it does not establish preservation of all contextual requirement checks or infer those bounds throughout arbitrary execution.

UnwindRecords.resume_split now reconstructs the cleanup records from the actual saved and caller scopes. UnwindRecords.resume uses existing owner uniqueness and record-filter laws to show that the new records are exactly the old records with the consumed owner's entries removed, up to order. Summaries for nested captures remain unchanged; no cleanup plan is constructed.

SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.resume_segments joins this result with the rich source extraction and append proofs. Existing recursive transport checks the saved and waiting requirements in the recomposed stack, preserving their combined effect row. The old owner-lookup proof identifies the same source scopes used by Local.resume, so pending-source checks also survive at the actual new owner phases. Source ownership balance accounts for every remaining continuation.

resume_source derives those invocation and waiting checks from a typed current resume expression and the combined pre-step requirement check. It returns the actual checked runtime step, closed value source, rich recomposed stack, both record collections, unchanged combined effect row, pending-source checks and exact ownership accounting. It retains the finite reentry-bound and action permission premises. Stored handler-declaration certificates, resource-support checks and cleanup-effect annotations still need to join this result before it constitutes the full common invariant.

UnwindRecords.discard reuses the same record-removal result and inserts the actual closing delimiter. selected_template combines lookup provenance with physical owner uniqueness to identify the stored summary with the capture being discarded. It does not choose another handler or infer a fresh cleanup summary.

SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.discard_source now starts from the typed current discard, its combined requirement check and its local source check. It retains the rich saved and waiting source fragments, actual stored cleanup summary, both record collections after owner removal, callback and waiting checks at the new owner phases, and exact ownership accounting. The existing finite pending-owner bounds construct the actual checked disposal transition. The saved fragment remains evidence for its retained scopes; its abandoned ordinary computation is not asserted to execute or to have a checked row.

The effect conclusion uses ClosingEffects for that exact summary at the surviving closing delimiter followed by the actual waiting stack. It derives the combined cleanup-and-waiting check and bounds its row by the original row. The annotation is a finite pre-step obligation; this theorem does not derive it from ordinary typing or from the earlier capture-time cleanup check. closing_delimiter_changes_check reuses the existing handler-row example to show why this distinction is necessary: a retained handler can export an unprotected request, which the surviving closing marker protects again before it reaches a disposing outer handler. The check without that marker succeeds; the check with it rejects the request. This is checker evidence, not a claim that the complete source admission accepts the example.

These disposal results do not yet constitute common preservation. Initial admission must supply the actual-context cleanup annotation and preserve it, and handler-declaration and resource-support evidence must accompany callback execution and subsequent unwinding.

SourceDependencyProviders.Lexical.local_transport now preserves the mutual lexical checks for expressions, pending scopes and unwinding scopes when a builtin provider is installed. It reuses the existing exact handler and owner lookup laws, including the case where the builtin handles a request previously served by a source handler.

SourceContextualRequirements.Lexical compiles the existing structural clause recipes into lexical declaration certificates. The same finite operation requirements and ordered receiving scopes are checked; there is no new source syntax. SourceContextualRechecking.Lexical.resume_rechecked and discard_rechecked reconstruct stored certificates from these recipes and a finite check at the actual restored scope. Lexical discard retains the captured handlers above the closing delimiter. Verified examples include a nonempty caller stack and a retained handler delegating to an outer interpretation. These invocation results still require the actual receiving-scope check; they do not prove that initial admission supplies it at every use.
