For these finite handler requirements, advance_checked proves preservation through all six administrative unwind transitions: ordinary-frame pop, handler pop, resource release, spent-marker pop, entering a live capture and retiring its owner. The live-capture case reuses capability lookup through the retirement delimiter and stack-append factorization. It derives the successor check from the current check. advance_rechecked reconstructs the resulting lexical handler certificates from retained recipes. This transport concerns operation capabilities with both protection modes; it does not make the closing delimiter transparent to arbitrary cleanup-effect checks.

SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.local_restrict and unwind_restrict now reuse the existing finite AvailableOn relation and owner-cut laws. They preserve lexical checks when phase changes retain availability for the live owners those scopes can reach. The independent relation, cut laws and realized_available proof were moved upstream with their existing names and proofs so both lexical and legacy checks can reuse them. No invocation right is inferred from an effect occurrence.

SourceDependencyFrames.unwind_owner_phases projects the existing runtime owner-accounting permutation onto continuation owners. The established phase-consumption theorem then identifies the resulting map with availability in the actual successor stack, and preserves owner uniqueness.

SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.advance_unwind_components joins these results for an active unwind prefix and an arbitrary retained caller suffix. From the current authenticated source summary, cleanup-effect annotation, callback checks, finite handler checks and recipes, resource support and unique ownership, it derives the corresponding successor evidence for all six administrative transitions. Callback and effect checks use the actual successor owner phases. The new summary still accounts for precisely the owners in the remaining prefix, and the cleanup-effect budget is unchanged. The proof reuses administrative resource support, source-summary preservation, finite handler rechecking and ownership accounting; it assumes no successor certificate.

The same theorem now retains the rich waiting source and its continuation records. unwindStore states the exact administrative record update: opening a live capture removes that owner's callable entries; other administrative steps keep the store unchanged. It is a proof-level store projection, not a cleanup schedule. The existing record-removal laws preserve all surviving payloads and unique keys. UnwindRecords.advance preserves the structural disposal-record collection, and resume_records_advance preserves each surviving resume record's actual-capture provenance and rich source certificate. No replacement record is inferred.

The active summary's ownership permutation and the existing phase laws identify the caller's phase map after cleanup with precisely its retained owners. unwind_waiting_checked then reuses removal of a consumed owner's records to preserve the caller's requirement check. The combined theorem derives the cleanup-and-waiting requirement check in the updated store at the actual successor phases, with the same cleanup budget and waiting row. The waiting source's own resume records are unchanged. opening_before_retirement verifies that opening removes both modes' records while the retirement marker still owns the ticket; only its later pop discharges that ownership.

UnwindSource now retains the summary and dependency scope in one structural derivation. Its cleanup rule uses one typed callback for both the effect row and dependency annotation. LexicalSegment.unwind_source constructs this witness from the actual unprotected captured source. Append, registry extension and administrative unwinding preserve it. Scope.afterUnwind names the resulting source scope; the runtime Advance rule still determines which pop is legal. The combined administrative theorem now retains this shared witness instead of independently choosing a summary and a stack realization.

The handler rule also retains the installed handler's original rich Frame derivation. A callback may still request that interpretation while its scopes are being abandoned. UnwindSource.handler_source retrieves this declaration at the actual handler cut. unwind_selected_body joins it with the contextual forest's certificate at the same remaining suffix, then reuses the established clause-selection theorem to recover the rich typed clause body and dependency family. Append, source-registry extension and unwinding preserve this evidence. No ordinary pending-code effect composition is required for the abandoned suffix. This supplies selected clause source; it does not yet prove the complete mixed callback state is preserved through dispatch and resumption.

allocate_disposing_capture constructs that witness from the same saved source used for the selected clause. It retains the exact witness under the fresh continuation contract. start_unwind_cleanup_components then joins actual callback application typing, its checked effect row and budget, its lexical dependency check, retained handler certificates and resource support. The remaining abandoned source and its cleanup budget are retained separately from the callback being evaluated. Both continuation-record collections remain unchanged, with their capture provenance intact, and the owner ledger is preserved. The caller suffix is arbitrary.

finish_unwind_cleanup_components joins the existing return-marker, record, support and ledger proofs at an actual Unit return. It resumes unwinding at the callback's saved scope and discharges precisely its cleanup owner. It does not assert that a callback terminates, or establish the intervening evaluation.

UnwindAnnotated connects each stored disposal body to its actual captured source and recorded dependency scope. It reuses the existing structural Closing.Bound judgment to connect the recorded scope to the live boundary. selected_unwind_source combines record lookup, that bound and capture uniqueness to recover the exact UnwindSource checked at disposal. It does not assume that independently chosen annotations of the same callback are equal. Bare UnwindRecords remains the structural store layout; these certificates supply the additional source evidence for its exact payloads.

capture_annotated_records records the annotation with the fresh capture, and allocate_disposing_capture now returns that bound and all resulting record certificates. resume_segments and resume_source retain them during actual recomposition. discard_source now returns the selected authenticated source, the bound for the actual closing marker and caller, and certificates for every surviving record. The proofs reuse record-removal permutations, capture provenance and annotation splitting. Administrative unwinding and both callback boundary theorems retain these same facts. No extra runtime lookup or cleanup schedule is introduced.

allocate_resuming_capture now returns the same recorded-scope invariant. Its lower allocation proof chooses any optional disposal body from the actual saved UnwindSource: protected captures add no disposal entry, while unprotected captures retain the chosen body's exact dependency annotation. Both cases preserve all earlier certificates under the fresh contract.

UnwindRecords.ordinary_step derives the surviving disposal collection for ordinary evaluation without continuation capture. It includes resource and cleanup allocation, cell updates and resumption. Resumption reuses the existing owner-removal permutation; the other cases keep the entries unchanged. The legacy plan-based discard is excluded by the lexical machine's ordinary-step condition. annotated_records_ordinary_step then reuses saved-capture origin and uniqueness to preserve each retained entry's source witness. It assumes no successor record collection.

The thirteen ordinary source-boundary theorems in SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical now also preserve Closing.Bound for the same source scopes: focus and plug; cleanup registration, normal callback entry and return; handler entry and exit; resource entry and exit; cell read and write; spent-clause return; and value return through a closing delimiter. They reuse the existing bound constructors and recover the retained suffix from the same source frame. No transition chooses a fresh annotation for an existing capture. The judgment's declaration moved to SourceDependencyChecks, retaining its name and constructors, so these earlier source proofs can use it without an import cycle. Capture, resume, discard and unwinding retain their existing bound proofs.

These results cover the stored-certificate facet of ordinary evaluation; they do not yet preserve the complete machine invariant. Expression typing, actual-context effects and the recorded-scope bound must still be joined across callback body execution, including a running prefix above abandoned scopes. Sufficient initial admission and the complete preservation/progress chain remain unfinished. The administrative theorem's handler-recipe premise has the same coverage limit as the rechecker above.

The lexical forest also now has append, cleanup-entry and cleanup-return proofs, reusing the corresponding structural inductions. These results concern stored handler certificates. Callback expression checks, resource support and cleanup effects remain separate facets to combine. The existing recipe language covers a useful structural subset, including only pure cleanup in its cleanup constructor; it does not yet provide the full source admission required here.

LexicalFrame.transport and LexicalSegment.transport reuse ordinary source transport to preserve the exact rich annotations when fresh continuation contracts, action records or resources extend their environments. This includes callbacks and dormant non-resumable captures. Neither transport changes the existing requirements, dependency scopes or effect boundaries.

rich_focus_decompose and rich_context_plug adapt the existing declared source context proofs to enriched dependency annotations. All ten strict focus positions are covered. Their requirement-evaluation equations reuse the existing sequence, value and phase laws. FocusDependencies records the exact dependency-tree transformation: ordinary sequencing, a pure pair, removal of a silent left value, or removal of a silent function prefix. Latent bodies remain in the same enriched function type.

lexical_focus_source chooses one actual plain frame from the source derivation and constructs both the checked runtime focus step and its typed source stack. lexical_plug_source restores the scope stored in that frame, transports the returned value's rich annotation, and constructs the checked plug step and remaining source stack. focus_dependencies_checked and plug_dependencies_checked connect the same dependency transformations to the existing local contextual checks. The former reuses neutral-scope transport only when inserting a pure waiting frame; the latter uses the returned value's silent dependencies. These are preservation components for ordinary evaluation, not a proof of all lexical-disposal admission checks or whole-source progress.

SourceDependencyChecks.UnwindPending checks an abandoned source prefix against a separate enclosing suffix. It drops requirements for ordinary code that will not execute, retains each callback check at its actual running scope, and checks a nested live capture with its pending retirement marker. Callback checking is an explicit parameter, not an assumption that future execution is safe. The append_iff proof adapts the existing pending-source induction. advance connects this judgment to all six actual administrative unwind rules, using the existing scope realization and append proofs. Actual runtime rules still determine which protected markers may be removed.

The strengthened lexical cleanup-entry theorems identify the exact stored callback dependencies and source suffix. UnwindPending.start_cleanup uses these equalities to construct the typed callback application and recover its check at that same suffix; finish_cleanup retains the suffix checks when the actual unwinding marker is removed. cleanup_application_checked reuses the existing silent-prefix law. Positive and negative resource examples show that a callback can use its still-enclosing resource, while removing that resource first invalidates the callback check.

SourceDependencyChecks.Lexical now supplies concrete mutual Local, Pending and Unwind judgments for these boundaries. Its capture guard retains operation selection, clause-row availability and protection checks without a closing plan. Its disposal rule checks the actual accessible owner, independent disposal permission, available phase and unprotected capture. It then checks the abandoned callbacks against the actual closing delimiter and waiting caller, and checks that caller's ordinary retained code. Both checks use the phase in which the disposed owner has been consumed. A disposing request also carries a structural Unwind check of its captured callbacks at the actual enclosing suffix, under a closing marker. This supplies the callback premise used when admitting a disposing clause. It inspects retained source syntax; it does not extract a plan or assume successful future execution. The old plan-dependent judgments remain available for legacy proofs; they are not the selected lexical rules.

Local.discard_step reuses source owner lookup and scope realization to construct the actual lexical discard transition. It retains the capture and caller annotations separately, together with their respective checks. Local.resume_step reuses the existing resumption correspondence and retains pending-source checks for the actual recomposed stack. These are transition connections, not rich-expression preservation or whole-source progress proofs.

The mutual Unwind judgment converts to and from UnwindPending with its concrete Local callback predicate. This allows administrative popping and cleanup entry/return to reuse the preceding generic proofs. The mutual form avoids Lean's restriction on nested inductive parameters containing local phase indices. The ordinary silent-source, sequencing and pending-scope append/capture proofs use the existing structural inductions unchanged. Examples accept disposal whose captured cleanup still needs a captured handler, reject a handler that would cancel a running callback, and reject both resume and discard when the owner is already consumed.

SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical.local_transport adapts the existing mutual scope-expansion proof to all three lexical judgments. It reuses the existing operation-cut and owner-cut transport results. The disposal case transports its captured callbacks and waiting caller separately; no plan projection is used. Pure waiting frames, pure cleanup and spent markers preserve checks, including checks nested in callbacks and dormant captures.

The lexical focus/plug bridges now retain the exact dependency-tree relation from the rich source proofs. focus_preserves_source constructs the same actual runtime frame, typed child, typed pending stack, child check and retained caller check. plug_preserves_source obtains the waiting check from that exact frame and proves the recomposed expression checked. The strengthened lexical_plug_source conclusion explicitly equates the original source scope with the returned context and suffix annotations; an unrelated existential context annotation cannot supply this check. Both combined theorems return the actual checked runtime step. Existing substitution, bind, beta and branch proofs also retain the new lexical checks, reusing their original rich-source and requirement-evaluation lemmas.

The lexical scope connections now also cover cleanup registration, normal cleanup invocation/return, and handler installation/exit. Cleanup registration constructs one actual action from the source callback value, retaining its rich body annotation and the body check under the armed frame. Normal invocation retains the returned body value in the running frame and obtains the callback check from the actual pending source. Return restores that same rich value and saved scope. Handler exit similarly recovers the existing checked suffix. Each theorem constructs the corresponding checked runtime transition.

frame_registries and segment_registries adapt the existing handler-table transport proof to preserve both tables and rich clause families. They cover dormant captures as well as the active stack. enter_handler_source chooses an installation identity fresh for the supplied activation history, registers the exact table and families obtained from source inversion, and constructs the typed installed frame and body checks. Existing installations keep their table and family annotations. This does not yet prove contextual admission of a selected clause when a later operation invokes it.

The support connection reuses the independent finite support environment in ScopedPorts.Support. substitution_preserves_source_support retains rich source typing, the lexical dependency check and the support calculation for the same substituted body. Its closed instance reuses the existing parameter-binding support theorem and applies equally to a local binding or selected clause parameter. Neither theorem infers physical captures from a function port.

Scope.visibleResources follows only active lexical resource scopes. Realizes.visible_resources identifies that list with actual runtime visibility; dormant captures remain ownership without caller access. source_payload_at_cut reuses the existing handler-cut correspondence to show that an operand bound checked at the selected source handler's outer suffix supplies the actual runtime payload condition.

source_request_access packages that result into the ordinary machine's local access conditions. It reuses the same source selection for every actual runtime cut of the request; operand and effect identities follow from the concrete request expression. The value-release case is impossible for an operation request. The result adds no restriction on operation ports or callable values.

leave_resource_source combines a finite value-support annotation excluding the released identity with rich source typing and the actual cell frame. It derives the local access checks, constructs the checked resource-exit transition, and preserves the source suffix and runtime resource-access invariant. This applies to closures as well as scalar values. The existing escaping-closure example cannot satisfy such an annotation excluding its captured resource.

These are connections from explicit support annotations, not a proof that initial admission supplies and preserves every required annotation. Existing finite template and completion-contract analyses remain reusable where their premises hold; their unknown application results or finite operation-port restrictions are not adopted as restrictions on the target source grammar. The lexical world-extension proofs now cover Local, Pending and Unwind by mutual structural induction. Resource-body checks instantiate only identities still fresh in the enlarged world. Checks in callbacks and dormant captures retain their exact scopes; extending the historical world grants no new resource access.

enter_resource_source constructs the actual opened body and cell frame at a supplied fresh identity. It preserves the checked pending suffix in the enlarged world, derives the body's lexical check from the source resource rule and retains the exact requirement-hiding relation for effect checking. The body, frame and runtime allocation use the same identity. This construction does not yet join fresh lifetime-history accounting or requirement-row evaluation to a common state.

cell_update_segment adapts the existing cell-selection induction to rich lexical segments. Read and write preserve the exact dependency scope, demand, requirements and stored continuation annotations of the pending segment, including dormant captures. read_cell_source and write_cell_source derive the reply's rich type from the operation signature and construct the checked runtime step. They take an actual cell selection as input; deriving selection at every reachable builtin request remains part of the common progress proof.

leave_clause_source restores the caller stored in an already-spent boundary, preserving the returned value's rich summary and the checked suffix. close_value_source produces Unit at a disposal delimiter and restores its actual caller. Neither boundary consumes a continuation owner; these proofs do not replace the outstanding transport across resume, discard or retirement phases.

SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical now adapts the existing fresh-owner admission proofs to these lexical checks. Its CaptureSource contains finite checks of the saved computation, waiting caller and abandoned callbacks after consumption of the newly allocated owner. capture_source_from_request derives those premises from the current request and pending source: fresh permission insertion preserves old permissions, and consuming the newly introduced owner restores the original phase map. This does not establish preservation when consuming an existing owner.

The uniform ClauseFamily rule supplies reusable proofs for simple resume and discard families. Both follow the existing owner-cut, append and neutral-history transports. This uniform rule is not the general clause-admission requirement: the existing outer-handler counterexample shows why the enclosing interpretation scope must be retained.

SourceContextualClauses.Lexical.FamilyAt instead checks each dependency family at its actual enclosing scope. Its DeclarationsAt judgment selects the family of the actual clause and protection mode; value substitution and resource-name instantiation preserve these certificates. The existing exact-tail operation capability supplies reusable nondisposing requests. Positive examples admit a clause that calls an outer handler before resuming, including repeated calls; the corresponding absent-handler case remains rejected.

The lexical stored Forest in SourceContextualForest attaches each handler's certificate to its exact annotated suffix and checks dormant captures recursively. Its cut and alignment proofs reuse the existing structural handler-cut induction. Successful selection aligns stored and typed source decompositions; no uniqueness of arbitrary annotations is assumed. Capture retains both certified subforests.

SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.capture_checked_interfaces joins the actual lexical runtime cut, rich source segment and contextual forest. It authenticates the handler, captured segment, caller, source family and requirement decomposition, and derives the selected family's local check and retained live-scope check at the fresh owner. Its typed body remains parametric in a matching fresh continuation contract. Constructing that contract's complete resume/disposal requirements, substituting the operand and joining the resulting runtime capture remain open. Initial construction and preservation of the contextual forest through the other execution families are also outstanding. The positive disposing-request example retains the captured handler needed by cleanup, so the new request premise does not restore the old planner's scope loss.

SourceDependencyFrames.UnwindTemplate now describes disposal requirements by structural traversal of the actual captured stack. It drops abandoned ordinary computation, retains each callback's actual enclosing interpretation context, and places a nested owner's retirement after its saved scopes. Its demand is a permutation of the stack's recursively owned continuations, with multiplicity. The construction follows any unprotected rich source segment and does not use makePlan. This is proof data; runtime unwinding still inspects only the top scope.

UnwindTemplate.append preserves callback contexts under stack recomposition. Its evaluation does not depend on the continuation-template store. Contract and resource-world extension preserve the same summary. advance_checked covers all six administrative unwind cases and spends exactly the continuation owners discharged by the actual step. start_cleanup extracts the typed callback application, its checked effect row under the actual unwinding marker, and the checked requirements for the remaining scopes. These results do not establish preservation during the callback's intervening evaluation.

UnwindRecords collects disposal entries from the rich source stack, including dormant captures. A protected capture contributes no disposal entry; its nested records are retained. Each entry is certified against an actual saved capture. lookup_ownership identifies that capture and proves that the looked-up demand accounts for exactly its owned continuations. Collection requires no successful future execution or pre-existing closing plan. Record composition and extension reuse the existing structural inductions; uniqueness of combined resume/disposal keys reuses the existing ownership and list laws.

The retained-handler example uses the callback and captured stack from InitialCleanupRouteGap. Its structural summary checks with an empty outward row and supplies an authenticated disposal record. Removing the callback's handler leaves an outward requirement, so the same callback cannot check as a closed disposal. This checks the scope distinction that the old planner lost.

SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.disposing_capture_summary connects construction to the actual selected request: its lexical capture permission establishes that the typed saved stack is unprotected, and that stack supplies its disposal summary and ownership equation. This construction does not itself show that the ordinary source demand accounts for those owners or that the closing row checks in the receiving context.

SourceDependencyOwners.Lexical now supplies the ownership-balance connection. Its ResumeCertified retains the exact rich saved derivation behind each resume entry, including lexical cleanup return markers. Ordinary frame retirement and pending-call bounds reuse source erasure and the existing proofs. The additional markers have no direct invocation; retirement contributes its actual owner. Mode-specific lookup combines these resume certificates with UnwindRecords.

The existing checked-derivation inductions now use these lexical certificates. checked_capture_spines connects consumption of an owner to consumption of its saved immediate owners. checked_internal_demand keeps demands within an actual captured region when its pending uses are internal. Both reuse the established capture inclusion and uniqueness lemmas; disposal uses the structural summary's ownership equation instead of a plan's retirements.

captured_segment_balance reuses ownership_tree_consumed unchanged to prove that a checked rich capture's ordinary demand is a permutation of its recursively owned continuations. Its premises are an authenticated source/record store, unique physical owners, the actual capture location, internal pending uses, a check of the saved requirements, and availability of the captured owners. captured_modes_balance therefore equates that demand with any authenticated lexical disposal summary. captured_closing_requirements constructs such a balanced summary for an unprotected capture. Neither theorem assumes budget equality or successful future execution.

The whole-stack instances derive ownership balance and consumption of every owned continuation from the current check. source_ownership_balance includes the present rich expression and pending lexical segment; balance is a consequence of their checked requirements, not an additional admission premise.

LexicalSegment.owned_registered and fresh_unowned connect contract-registry freshness to actual ownership, including pending retirement markers. Capture uniqueness then reuses the existing ownership equation. UnwindRecords splits at the actual lexical cut and constructs the new disposal entry from its chosen summary. A protected capture preserves its nested entries without gaining a disposal entry.

SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.allocate_split constructs the fresh rich contract, live source segment and extended disposal records from the typed split. It preserves the saved and caller requirement checks with the existing generic fresh-record insertion lemmas. The new source uses the same input, answer, dependency scopes, interfaces and requirement indices as that split. The proof also derives the fresh resumption invocation check and the exact phase equation.

allocate_disposing_split specializes this construction to an unprotected capture with internal pending uses. Its closing row is the evaluation of the actual lexical summary. The constructed source and records supply the premises of captured_modes_balance, so allocation derives owner-demand agreement without assuming that the two demands match. The disposal invocation check follows whenever that row evaluation succeeds. closing_invocation_from_record reuses the established invocation construction, replacing only plan ownership and store independence with the lexical summary lemmas. These are allocation connections from the present split checks; they do not assume an admitted successor.

ClosingEffects supplies the remaining finite cleanup annotation. Its four structural rules cover callback requests, retirement, spent boundaries and sequencing in the exact closing requirement tree. A request carries an upper footprint, its export through the actual nearer and receiving interpretations, and inclusion of that export in the declared budget. Sequencing advances the owner phase by the first part's demand. A spent boundary checks consumption; retirement readiness follows separately from actual ownership.

ClosingEffects.checked reuses uniform residual coverage and owner-trace composition to construct the existing requirement check. UnwindTemplate then derives the required trace from physical ownership, uniqueness and availability. The converse effects_of_checked and effects_iff show that this annotation accepts every successfully checked lexical closing row within the budget. The existing finite evaluator can therefore check it. There is no new runtime evaluator, generated cleanup plan or restriction on the callback's source syntax. The retained-handler example constructs the annotation; removing that handler still rejects an empty budget.

advance_effects preserves this annotation through all six administrative unwind cases by reusing advance_checked. start_cleanup_effects derives the actual callback application, its checked effect budget and the annotation for the remaining scopes using start_cleanup. Both use the current ownership trace. Neither repeats the runtime case proof or assumes a checked successor; callback execution and the combined source invariant remain separate work.

Given this annotation with budget requestRow ++ capRow, allocate_disposing_split now constructs the complete clause invocation interface. Closing-row success, its advertised coverage and caller owner freshness are conclusions. The proof derives retirement availability from the actual cut and uses the already constructed resume and disposal invocation checks. Establishing and preserving the annotation from initial source admission remains a source-invariant obligation; it is not a claim that ordinary saved-row typing alone supplies the cleanup budget.

SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.disposing_capture_summary also derives the actual capture's pending-owner bound from the selected request's structural source check. It reuses lexical_segment_pending_stack, PendingStack.internal and the realization equation for live owners. The allocation theorem's internal use premise therefore has a source derivation at this same cut; it is not an independently assumed fact about the runtime capture.

ClauseRowAdmission.SourceStore accepts structural source evidence for lexical completion frames and disposal records. Legacy StoreSegment evidence embeds in StoreModeSource; the mixed constructors distinguish value results from unwinding. StoreClosingTemplate retains each typed callback and its actual interpretation suffix. Legacy stores embed through SourceStore.of_source; this proof compatibility does not add a runtime disposal path. Resume-record certification recovers the registered header's exact input and owner demand, and a return boundary equal to its answer or unwinding.

LexicalSegment.row_store constructs that evidence from the actual rich lexical segment, its UnwindRecords and the same registered contract. The existing Rows checker and its instantiation theorem are unchanged. A clause's source certificate now ranges over lexical stores as well as the earlier stores; it does not assume arbitrary stores are authentic. No successful row evaluation or valid successor is part of store authentication.

LexicalSegment.instantiate_clause joins this store evidence with the selected rich clause and actual operand. It reuses substitution and Rows.instantiate to derive the substituted expression and its check at the same requirement index, with the advertised effect bound. Its local invocation interface is now constructed by disposing allocation from the structural cleanup annotation. The selected clause, allocation and actual runtime capture results are now joined at their exact shared inputs by the two allocation cases below. These source checks are not yet preserved through every execution step or assembled into initial-source safety.

SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.allocate_disposing_clause_from_split combines allocation, the structural cleanup annotation and clause instantiation. It returns the actual raw capture step, the exact new owner list and its uniqueness, the live source stack and records, and the substituted clause with its checked effect bound. complete_allocated_clause reuses clause-usage substitution, consuming_usage_completed and consuming_clause_balance to derive the selected clause's consumption and demand permutation. Both allocation cases now join the clause and waiting requirements at their actual successive owner phases, then reuse source_ownership_balance to account for every owner in the new stack. The combined check and ownership permutation are conclusions, not extra admission premises.

SourceContextualCapture.Lexical.allocate_disposing_capture derives the split, selected clause factory and cleanup summary from the same pre-step source witnesses. It also retains the selected clause's local check, pending checks and contextual forest. Cleanup-effect coverage remains an explicit finite annotation; this result does not infer it from ordinary typing.

The corresponding allocate_resuming_clause_from_split and allocate_resuming_capture cover clauses without disposal permission. They handle protected and unprotected captures without an internal-use restriction or a successful cleanup-effect premise. For an unprotected capture, the stored cleanup summary is structural bookkeeping; it grants no disposal permission. Both cases use the existing allocation and substitution proofs. Neither assumes a successor invariant or changes runtime unwinding.

Remaining source integration must cover support propagation, selected clause execution, continuation phase changes and the other control boundaries, then establish the combined invariant from initial source admission. No preservation result for the legacy plan-dependent checks discharges those obligations.

General progress for this machine is not proved. Earlier plan-dependent source theorems do not prove it. This work replaces the disposal part of the handler/cleanup connection in the remaining proof construction above; it is not a new milestone. The scope-exit mechanism is intended to be shared by later continuation targets, but only the one-shot ownership policy is being implemented and proved here.

The earlier ExplicitCleanupReference experiment in the same module proves installation identity binding and unchanged operation ports. It remains only binding evidence: lookup by identity does not keep a removed scope alive, and its reference type is not a new dispatch rule. Retain these lemmas only where the local scope representation uses them. The retained-plan prototype remains scratch comparison evidence and is not part of the selected execution design.

Pending checks across cleanup returns

SourceDependencyChecks.Lexical.ModePending retains the actual runtime frame alongside its dependency scope and the existing ordinary/unwind usage modes. Ordinary plain frames retain their local source check; abandoned plain frames are skipped. An unwind-callback return marker changes ordinary execution back to unwinding, and a closing delimiter restores ordinary execution. Armed callbacks retain their local check in either mode. Opening a live capture for unwinding checks its saved scopes behind the actual retirement marker.

Recomposition joins the first fragment's exit mode to the second fragment's entry mode. Splitting at an actual handler cut derives that intermediate mode, including cuts across a callback return marker. The judgment agrees with the existing runtime returnMode; it adds no runtime mode or evaluator. Existing ordinary Segment checks and authenticated UnwindSource checks embed into it. The ordinary embedding does not assert that every LexicalSegment has an ordinary exit mode.

The existing advance_unwind_components, start_unwind_cleanup_components and finish_unwind_cleanup_components now take these structural checks for the current actual stack and derive them for the successor stack. Administrative unwinding also derives their restriction to the actual successor owner phases, reusing local capability restriction and realized_available. Cleanup entry checks the callback in ordinary mode; Unit return exposes the retained suffix in unwind mode. No successor mode check is a premise.

These results preserve contextual pending-code checks at those boundaries. The mixed source judgment below supplies rich source composition and selected expression boundaries. Local.resume still uses the existing restored Pending premise; replacing that connection and joining the remaining source facets remain necessary. Complete initial admission, common preservation, progress and terminal accounting are still unproved for the lexical-unwinding source calculus.

Rich source across ordinary execution and unwinding

SourceDependencyFrames.ModeSource composes source at a ModeValue boundary: either a rich value is expected, or execution is unwinding and no abandoned result value is supplied. This is a source judgment, not a new runtime mode. Its return mode agrees with the existing runtime returnMode.

Ordinary frames reuse the rich Frame derivation, including higher-order value and callback annotations. In unwind mode, skipped plain frames contribute no ordinary requirements. Installed handlers retain their typed declarations and armed callbacks retain one typing witness for their latent requirements and dependencies. An unwind-return marker changes a Unit boundary to unwinding; a closing delimiter changes unwinding back to Unit. Dormant captures retain their source, while opening an abandoned capture contributes its cleanup requirements and the existing retirement requirement. Continuation permissions, stored-record certificates and physical resource support remain separate checks.

Segment.mode_source embeds ordinary source with the same rich values, demand, requirements and scope. UnwindSource.mode_source embeds abandoned source with the same demand and scope; additional empty sequencing nodes have exactly the same requirement evaluation. The mixed relation does not impose an ordinary effect-interface inclusion across abandoned frames. Its executed requests must still pass the contextual Checked requirement judgment and local dependency checks; the relation alone is not source admission.

ModeSource.append and split preserve the complete requirement-evaluation equation for arbitrary stores, receiving interpretations and owner phases. handler_cut reuses the split and retains the selected handler declaration from the same derivation. The captured boundary is either that handler's rich answer or unwinding. This covers cuts across callback return markers without assigning ordinary requirements to abandoned code. mode_selected_body reuses the existing contextual clause proof at the actual selected installation; the older unwind_selected_body now follows through the abandoned-source embedding.

ModeSource.start_cleanup, finish_cleanup, advance_checked and finish_close derive the successor rich source and its checked requirements at the actual control boundaries. Callback entry reuses the factored cleanup_application_checked calculation also used by UnwindSource, including protection at the real unwinding marker. The existing SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical.focus_preserves_source and plug_preserves_source now use ModeSource and ModePending, preserving the same recorded-scope bound while ordinary expression evaluation proceeds over a mixed suffix. Their rich expression decomposition and substitution proofs are reused.

ModeSource.unwind_source now derives the caller fragment's cleanup source from its retained source and the existing UnwindPrefix check. It keeps the same dependency scope, handler declarations and callback typing witnesses; it skips ordinary code and includes retirement markers. The resulting demand accounts for precisely the fragment's owned continuations by the existing UnwindTemplate.ownership theorem.

reentry_unwind_balance factors the existing usage-accounting proof so source reentry can reuse it. ModeSource.reentry_from_bounds derives the caller's source at the actual captured return mode. resume_recomposition then joins the saved continuation, the derived caller fragment and the spent-owner suffix, with total demand equal up to permutation to the physical owned continuations. The source-demand and usage-demand lists are related by explicit permutations; identical order is not required. These are source and ownership results. They do not yet establish that the new cleanup requirements pass their effect check in the actual receiving scope, or preserve all contextual capability checks.

ModeSource.extract_live obtains the three fragments from the predecessor source. It derives exclusion of the invoked owner from pending demand using checked_once on the current resume requirement and pending requirements. That owner therefore cannot be in the implicit-retirement case. The live boundary retains the exact contract input and answer types and the saved return mode.

ResumeAnnotated pairs a stored resume body with its chosen ModeSource, contract and recorded dependency scope. selected_resume_source recovers that exact body through lookup, capture identity and Closing.Bound. The contract fixes the rich answer and the actual returnMode distinguishes ordinary return from unwinding; the proof assumes no general uniqueness of typing annotations. extract_recorded_resume joins this lookup to predecessor-source extraction, replacing the saved witness with the exact recorded requirements. Fresh capture, registry extension, administrative unwinding and removal of the resumed owner's records preserve the paired certificate. The existing capture-location and source-transport proofs are reused.

ReturnEffects gives the caller's additional check two structural cases. Ordinary return reuses its existing source and requirement check. Unwind return carries its lexical UnwindSource, a demand permutation and ClosingEffects at the actual receiving interpretations and owner phase. The demand permutation checks that abandoning the caller accounts for the same outstanding owners. The effect budget is explicit and must cover the ordinary caller row as well. This annotation contains no successor machine or quantification over execution. ReturnEffects.unwind_iff proves that, for the retained cleanup source, its effect obligation is equivalent to the existing finite requirement evaluator succeeding within that budget. It does not establish whole-program inference.

ReturnEffects.source_checked derives retirement readiness from the predecessor's checked owner trace, using the existing trace-permutation and cleanup-effect lemmas. It produces the caller's source and effect check for the actual return mode. ModeSource.append_checked and resume_checked_recomposition then derive the check for the complete restored stack. They retain the declared caller budget and the saved-body and tail rows. They do not assume a checked successor.

resume_checked_fragments joins the strengthened extract_recorded_resume to requirement checking: it obtains the exact saved body's check from the actual invocation, splits the caller and tail checks from the predecessor, and removes the consumed owner's records. Context transport reuses normalization of the actual live-to-spent boundary. The extraction result also retains its requirement-evaluation equation and the restored recorded-scope bound.

resume_mode_segments uses those results with ModeSource and ResumeAnnotated. Given a matching cleanup branch in the annotated predecessor when the capture returns by unwinding, it derives the restored source, bounded effect row, actual successor owner phase and exact physical owner balance; surviving resume and disposal certificates are preserved. Ownership derives the predecessor's whole-state demand balance from its checked source and exact records, then uses the established physical resumption permutation. This checked route does not require the three source-versus-usage fragment permutations of the earlier source-only theorem. Its conclusion exposes the exact caller source and the structural branch coverage still required. It does not prove that every previously admitted resume site supplies that coverage.

capture_mode_segments now constructs the mixed source, exact resume and cleanup certificates, recorded-scope bound and checked resume interface from the actual predecessor handler cut and a selected checked annotation branch. A normal branch is always supplied. The allocated contract has no advertised disposal row, as in the existing resume-only allocator. Protected captures retain their nested cleanup records; unprotected captures derive their cleanup source through the existing structural unwind-prefix proof. The result retains the selected handler declaration and the actual capture step. It proves fresh physical ownership, uniqueness and demand balance, using an explicit fresh physical owner and a predecessor balance derived from the mixed stack's checked source and exact records. It does not infer physical freshness merely from contract freshness: mixed source includes retirement markers without such a contract premise.

This source/store allocation result does not check the selected clause body or its local capabilities and resource support. The main capture allocators and the source-step connection still need to join those facets.

mode_source_ownership_balance and mode_stack_ownership_balance establish those predecessor balances without a separate balance premise. They use the actual ResumeAnnotated and UnwindAnnotated records, physical owner uniqueness, and the existing requirement check starting with exactly those owners available. The expression case also uses the established fact that source expressions introduce no direct retirement requirements. Both main mixed-mode capture and resume results now call these proofs.

The mixed-mode argument retains the earlier ownership-tree, capture-identity and trace-endpoint proofs. Its additional structural case is opening a dormant capture during unwinding. Such source checks the saved cleanup before retiring the still-present owner, so its direct retirements cannot all be classified as already installed retirement markers. mode_segment_retirement_spines proves that the saved capture's spine is consumed before that retirement completes. mode_checked_capture_spines combines this fact with authenticated resume and disposal lookups; the existing ownership-tree induction then accounts for all nested owners. No new ownership axiom, future-execution premise or restriction to empty caller demand is introduced. This removes the two balance assumptions; it does not establish the remaining source cleanup-coverage invariant.

Clause-row admission now accepts the actual mixed source through StoreModeSource. Its frame rules retain normal values or an unwind boundary, and its live-capture rule retains the selected contract's input and either its answer or unwinding. SourceStore separately authenticates the active source, every exact normal saved resume body at its physical capture location, and the cleanup record collection under the same registries. A structural StoreAnnotation relates these normal records to the actual checking store. Ordinary source certificates still construct this interface through SourceStore.of_source, using the reflexive annotation. This broadens the stores quantified over by declaration row certificates: they must justify the advertised row for mixed stores and annotated bodies. It does not assert that an arbitrary old certificate automatically meets the stronger obligation.

ModeSource.row_source and ResumeAnnotated.row_source erase existing rich source witnesses into this interface without changing their normal requirement trees. mode_row_store combines them with the actual StoreAnnotation. capture_mode_segments preserves existing annotations and stores the selected relative annotation for the fresh resume body, while retaining its exact normal source record. It returns the resulting store relation and source certificate. instantiate_mode_clause reuses source substitution and Rows.instantiate against the annotated checking store and that store's actual continuation interface. It returns both the annotated clause check and its projected normal-source check in the same annotated store, within the advertised bound. No checked successor or substitute normal store is assumed. The earlier ordinary LexicalSegment.row_store uses the reflexive case of the same interface. These are source-provenance and clause-row results; caller cleanup reentry, local capabilities and physical support remain independent obligations.

Capture projects the predecessor check only to reuse the normal-source ownership proof. Its actual saved and tail checks remain in the annotated checking store. StoreAnnotation.split preserves the existing resume/disposal partition; StoreAnnotation.append rejoins it around fresh closing entries. The predecessor certificate is normalized around the actual handler cut. A checked choice retains both the original annotation and the normal split into captured and tail requirements, within the original bound. Explicit paths retain both branches, so the normal case remains available without another admission premise.

A structural path in this normalized certificate selects a sequence whose first part is a relative captured annotation with the actual tail interpretations prepended, and whose second part is the tail annotation. Each part must annotate its corresponding exact source fragment. The path supplies both checks at their correct owner phases; no separately checked captured body or successor is assumed. The fresh record stores only the relative body. An explicit lookup equation identifies that selected body, and its checked row becomes the resumption advertisement. The pending tail retains its annotation through the spent marker. The selected split's row stays within the predecessor bound, including the effects of previously annotated nested records.

This is a local source rule for a structurally identified branch. It does not infer a relative body from an arbitrary annotation whose leaves may already contain the outer interpretations. Initial source admission must supply the appropriate branch and establish that its extra paths cover the required cleanup executions. The normal fallback alone does not establish that coverage.

ModeSource.unwind_checked_empty derives the lexical cleanup source and its checked effect row from existing mixed source and requirement checks when the caller's remaining continuation demand is empty. It uses the structural UnwindPrefix and availability of physically owned continuations. A dormant live continuation would require its owner both consumed and available, so that case is excluded by the existing checks. Nested handlers, resource frames, spent boundaries and typed effectful finalizers retain their original metadata; ordinary pending code is skipped. The cleanup row is contained in the original caller row at the same receiving context and phase.

return_effects_of_empty consequently constructs ReturnEffects from that source evidence. resume_checked_recomposition_empty uses it to derive checked resumption within the original saved/caller/tail effect budget, without a separately supplied cleanup certificate. These results discharge one local admission case. They do not establish initial-program admission or remove the cleanup obligation for callers with nonempty continuation demand.

SourceDependencyBudgetGap.Lexical checks the remaining budget question against lexical unwinding itself. It reuses the existing typed nested-capture fixture: normal execution resumes its saved callback beneath an inner handler, whereas abandonment skips the pending resume, pops that handler, then opens the saved continuation. Cleanup consequently exports through the outer handler. The normal row is empty and the lexical cleanup row is nonempty. The exact cleanup requirements reject an empty row and admit the explicit cleanup budget through ReturnEffects. No global cleanup plan is used in these proofs.

This fixture has a rich ModeSource and finite requirement checks; it is not a reachable closed initial execution. It establishes that a proof for arbitrary typed callers cannot simply bound their cleanup by their normal row. Initial admission must either establish an additional invariant that excludes this mismatch or retain and check the separate cleanup bound. Handler identities and callback metadata are already unambiguous in the fixture; the issue is the bound for the alternate lexical execution path.

The same module's Lexical.Admission.authenticated now establishes that the source-relative SourceStore predicate includes the example inside an enclosing continuation. It supplies exact normal resume records and structural lexical closing records for both owners. body_admitted constructs the current enriched Body.typed judgment for a normal-only resume of the enclosing continuation. admitted_normal_cleanup_gap instantiates the existing hereditary Rows proof at that authenticated store: the normal resume has an empty row, while lexical cleanup of its saved body has the nonempty row above. Thus source provenance and the existing normal-only row rule do not alone imply that cleanup fits the normal budget. This reuses the existing source, registry-extension and row proofs; no runtime plan or execution rule is added.

This evidence still does not establish closed-program reachability, or that this particular resume must unwind its caller. It does not require a resumption-only clause to budget an unused explicit disposal. The remaining source-admission obligation is to establish coverage at the boundaries where lexical execution actually requires cleanup, and preserve it through capture and resumption.

ModeSource.return_choice_admission supplies a local admission rule for arbitrary caller demand. Existing lexical source, an unwind prefix and owner balance construct the cleanup requirements and their demand permutation. The annotation uses the existing requirement-tree choice constructor to check normal execution and cleanup from the same owner phase and interpretation suffix. Both alternatives consume the same outstanding owners; the check does not execute or sequentially consume both alternatives. Its row covers both paths, so the cleanup row need not fit the normal row alone.

UnwindSource.choice_return_effects proves that this single finite check yields the ordinary caller check and ReturnEffects for either return mode. It reuses ClosingEffects and the existing alternative-check rule. The lexical budget fixture checks this rule with a nonempty owner demand. No evaluator, runtime annotation or source grammar restriction is introduced. This is a sufficient local rule; hereditary source admission must still establish and retain these alternative checks at each applicable caller boundary. The theorem does not claim that the earlier normal-only check already supplies them.

The hereditary SourceDependencyAnnotations.Body judgment now has an annotated constructor. It retains the original expression derivation, a structural RowAnnotation relating its normal requirements to the annotated tree, and a Rows certificate for that annotated tree. The relation permits additional alternatives beneath sequencing, emission and choices; all paths retain the original owner demand. It does not identify an arbitrary extra path as lexical cleanup. Rows.alternatives composes independently certified paths under the same advertised bound using the existing checker.

RowAnnotation.checked projects a checked annotation to a bounded check of the original source. RowAnnotation.prepend retains that relationship when ordered interpretations are installed. Environment, world and contract transport and source substitution preserve the actual annotation. Handler declarations carry it through their existing Offer families, so no separate annotated-body hierarchy or runtime registry is introduced. Normal erasure remains available through Body.normal_rows; the mixed clause instantiator retains both trees through Body.row_annotation.

StoreAnnotation relates checking-store bodies to their exact normal source bodies, entry by entry with identical keys, order and owner demands. Its checked projection recursively reuses RowAnnotation.checked at invocations, preserving owner phases and deriving a normal effect row within the annotated bound. Both lookup directions retain the actual body annotation. Removing a consumed owner preserves the relation. These are proof certificates; no runtime store or execution rule is added. Normal source records continue to justify ownership without attributing an added annotation branch to the source syntax.

RequirementPath records a structural position inside the complete annotated requirement tree and the owners consumed before that position. Its checked lemma extracts the selected check at that owner phase, within the root effect bound. Paths compose and survive installation of ordered interpretations. RowAnnotation.focus locates an annotated child without removing alternatives from the enclosing tree. The ten strict source-focus forms return the exact child's path. RequirementPath.remainder constructs a remaining certificate from any selected path: it retains the selected subtree and following requirements, removes the preceding demand, and derives the check at that later owner phase within the original row bound. Its proof is structural induction on the existing path; enclosing choices follow that path. This is a static certificate transformation, not a runtime cleanup plan.

focus_preserves_source and plug_preserves_source now retain an annotation of the complete current expression and waiting stack in the same format. Their source decomposition proofs establish equality of the old and new normal requirement evaluations, reusing the existing neutral-frame and value lemmas. RowAnnotation.rebase_checked then uses the existing choice constructor to check the rebuilt normal tree alongside the entire prior annotation. The old annotation remains an exact subtree, so its stored alternatives and their paths remain available. Both alternatives consume the same owners; the rule does not execute both paths. Its effect row stays within the previous bound, even though the checking tree and row may contain repeated entries.

Both source transitions also preserve the exact UnwindSource requirements in both directions: a plain evaluation frame adds no cleanup action. This connects a retained cleanup branch to the actual successor stack and dependency scope, rather than just retaining an unrelated checked tree. Neither transition consumes an owner or changes the checking store or phase. This argument does not yet cover computation, capture, resource or handler entry, or transitions that consume owners; it does not establish complete source admission.

ready_preserves_source uses the same complete certificate for ordinary bind, beta and boolean-branch reduction. Existing port typing supplies the actual raw step and closed-substitution readiness; the existing rich substitution and branch proofs supply its successor source and local capability check. The pending source stack, cleanup requirements and physical owners remain the same. Bind and beta retain the normal effect check exactly. Selecting a branch uses its previously checked effect subrow and the established permutation of owner demand; the existing phase-permutation lemma preserves the pending check. The successor annotation retains the entire predecessor certificate as an alternative within its previous effect bound. The theorem assumes no checked successor and proves local progress for these ready forms, not progress for arbitrary admitted programs.

Handler installation and normal exit now retain that same complete certificate and the exact cleanup-source association. Installation reuses RecursiveHandlerTables.checked_activation to replace the static checking label with the fresh installation identity. unwind_source_registries transports the unchanged lexical cleanup requirements through the registry extension, including callbacks and dormant captures. Existing installations keep their tables and clause families. Pushing the new handler adds no cleanup action of its own; normal exit recovers the unchanged suffix certificate after the returned value and handler frame contribute empty rows. Both results construct the checked annotation for the actual successor, retain the predecessor annotation as a subtree, and preserve its effect bound. These results do not establish that source admission supplied every required cleanup alternative before entry.

UnwindSource.clause_return_effects connects a static clause-row certificate to a caller obligation at any structural path to choice normal cleanup. It checks that alternative at the owner phase after the path's preceding demand, and requires the cleanup branch to match the exact lexical UnwindSource requirements. It then supplies ReturnEffects for either mode within the clause's advertised bound. The earlier sequence-prefix case is the path into its second operand; nested sequences and surrounding alternatives use the same rule. The theorem assumes the source certificate and authenticated invocation interface, not a checked successor machine. Existing source rules still admit normal-only bodies: this extension does not prove that every applicable caller boundary has the required alternative. Establishing that coverage and preserving its association with the actual caller remain source-admission obligations.

resume_mode_segments now takes the typed ready resume expression and its whole expression/stack certificate. Source inversion, the resolved owner and value silence derive the invocation requirement check and its exact demand. Projection of the same certificate supplies the pending requirement check after that demand; neither requirement check is a separate premise. The result retains the operand's rich value source for the resumed computation and exposes the exact caller requirement tree selected by source decomposition.

For an unwind-returning capture, the theorem now constructs the caller's UnwindSource and its owner-demand permutation before requesting effect coverage. mode_reentry_unwind_balance derives the caller's ownership from the checked saved, caller and tail fragments, authenticated surviving records and the existing reentry dependency bounds. Recursive demand membership stays within each preserved region; the saved region includes the outer tail, so outside-owner calls remain supported. The proof reuses Syntax.balanced_middle_demands and ModeSource.unwind_reentry.

The remaining obligation is only a structural path to choice normal cleanup for that derived cleanup in the same enclosing certificate, after the invoked owner's and capture's demand. Both branches carry the caller's actual outer interpretation context. Cleanup source and its owner balance are results, rather than additional premises of the effect-coverage obligation. Ordinary-return captures require no cleanup branch. Keeping the enclosing tree allows alternatives above the pending subtree to remain usable.

The proof extracts the cleanup check from that path and reuses the existing consumed-owner normalization and record-removal proofs to transport it to the spent caller boundary. It derives the internal ReturnEffects evidence, then reuses checked mixed-mode recomposition and ownership accounting. There is no separately supplied invocation requirement check, pending requirement check, ReturnEffects or caller budget. The successor row stays within the original certificate's effect bound.

The resume theorem accepts a checking store structurally related to the exact normal source records by StoreAnnotation; reflexivity admits the previous unannotated case. Lookup supplies the selected saved annotation and its checked body at the actual caller context. Projection derives the normal saved-source check and its effect subrow. Projecting the predecessor and fragment checks to the normal store allows reuse of the existing ownership proofs. The successor retains the store relation after removing the consumed owner.

The successor also carries a checked RowAnnotation for its rebuilt source. RowAnnotation.focus extracts the pending annotation from the predecessor; consumed-owner record removal preserves its check. For unwind return, RequirementPath.remainder also retains the selected normal/cleanup choice and the requirements following it, even when that choice lies above the pending subtree. Owner-demand cancellation aligns these remaining requirements with the caller suffix. The saved continuation's checked annotated requirements precede both retained alternatives. An explicit path retains that saved annotation with its actual receiving interpretations. Further paths locate the pending annotation and the selected cleanup choice in the successor after the saved demand. The annotated row remains within the predecessor bound.

This proves retention of these concrete subtrees through the actual resume step. It does not prove that initial source admission supplies matching cleanup branches at every applicable site, or that every future coverage obligation can be recovered from the retained trees. Capture now constructs the fresh annotated record and its StoreAnnotation from a relative split branch in the predecessor certificate; resume checks and retains that stored annotation. Clause admission accepts the resulting annotated checking store.

capture_mode_segments also joins the allocated capture to its actual clause and pending tail. Its predecessor premises now include source typing and a requirement check for the ready operation request. The existing request-evaluation and cut-residual proofs identify the selected handler's offered row and its export through the receiving suffix. The source declaration at that handler supplies the exact dependency family, clause body and continuation effect interfaces through selected_body; the operation signature aligns the operand and continuation input types. Operand closure follows from its source typing. No clause certificate, continuation effect interface or advertised export is supplied independently. Both resumption-only and disposal-capable offers use this same allocation and clause-joining theorem.

The theorem instantiates that hereditary clause certificate in the actual annotated allocation store. Substitution retains its normal expression and RowAnnotation. complete_allocated_clause supplies the existing consumption argument: the clause demand is a permutation of the fresh owner followed by the saved continuation's demand. This aligns the annotated tail check with the phase where the clause finishes. The combined successor annotation checks within the actual request row plus the predecessor pending certificate's bound, and its whole demand is a permutation of the successor's physical owners. The normal combined check follows by the existing annotation projection. No independently checked successor or new ownership induction is assumed.

For a disposal-capable offer, the existing structural request check now supplies the protection guard and PendingWithin owner bound. The capture theorem no longer assumes an independent physical InternalUses bound. The same physical cut and complete lexical annotation identify the exact saved scope through Realizes.append_scopes_unique. Bound.captured_pending carries its source owner bound to every stored continuation referenced inside that scope.

mode_source_calls_within bounds the calls that the mixed source executes; skipped frames contribute no calls. It does not reconstruct typing or pending uses for abandoned raw code. mode_capture_ownership_balance combines these source bounds with the existing checked-demand, ownership-tree and retirement proofs to show that the saved demand accounts for exactly the captured owners. The exact UnwindSource supplies cleanup's demand over the same owners, deriving the permutation between the two demands. This removes the separate owner-bound premise without claiming preservation of the whole mixed local judgment.

A structural path identifies those lexical cleanup requirements in the checked saved annotation. Reading that path supplies cleanup's successful row and its bound within the saved row; no independent cleanup row bound is assumed. The existing record-insertion and closing-invocation proofs then construct the fresh disposal interface, including row availability and coverage. The result retains that interface alongside the source, records, normal resume interface and actual clause check. Resumption-only offers still require no cleanup path or usable disposal interface. Their allocation retains structural closing records where lexical abandonment permits them.

Capture now derives the successor ReturnHints.Recursive.Pending from the same recursive judgment for its predecessor, with matching annotations on the actual stack. Pending.handler_cut reuses Realizes.cut and the existing physical-prefix split to identify the captured and waiting annotations. Pending.split keeps the exact receiving suffix for executed code and callbacks; annotation associativity transports only equality of scopes. The rich source and annotation return-mode results identify the same captured boundary. Recursive.local_transport and pending_transport reuse the existing phase-spending and permission-extension laws through every recursive check. The live-boundary constructor then yields checks for the actual allocated stack. No separately checked successor stack is supplied.

The capture theorem also takes the recursive check of the whole perform expression. Local.ready_request uses rich-source inversion and sequencing to extract the request check, replacing its separate primitive-request premise. That check supplies the existing protection and owner-bound arguments for a disposing offer. Both capture and resumption now use the same recursive retained-stack judgment.

This result covers the retained stack, not the selected clause's current recursive Local judgment. The existing ClauseFamily interface takes ordinary Pending checks for saved and waiting scopes. It does not supply the required recursive clause check when the capture returns into unwinding. Joining that check remains part of the same M1 obligation; the existing clause source, row, usage and support results do not establish it implicitly.

The ready-resume rule now retains the missing return-mode information in SourceDependencyChecks.Lexical.ReturnHints. Each annotation follows the existing lexical scope and distinguishes normal callback return, unwind callback return, closing and retirement markers. Matches relates it to the same runtime stack and erases to the existing Realizes; it does not introduce a new runtime operation. ReturnHints.Pending is a finite source traversal with explicit entry and exit modes. Ordinary code is checked when executed and skipped during unwinding; cleanup callbacks retain their lexical receiving scopes.

The earlier ReturnHints.Resume rule checks a ready primitive against retained code using the old Local judgment. It remains a local comparison result; resume_mode_segments now uses the recursive source judgment described below. ModePending.annotate_return reconstructs annotations for the earlier retained judgment. The main capture theorem now transports recursive checks directly. The local ReturnExamples establish that returning into cleanup accepts a skipped dependency on an unavailable owner which ordinary Pending rejects. This is a local rule comparison, not a closed initial-program safety proof.

ReturnHints.Recursive.Local and Pending now check dependency syntax and retained scopes mutually. Sequencing, choice, handlers, resource scopes and cleanup use the same recursive judgment as resumption and disposal. Resumption checks the restored annotated syntax at the consumed owner phase. Disposal checks the abandoned segment under the actual closing delimiter and checks the waiting caller separately. Request checks retain the selected capture's cleanup obligations and owner bound. Cleanup callbacks receive their normal-return or unwind-return marker according to the traversal mode; they do not fall back to the old Local judgment.

The main resume theorem takes the recursive check of the whole current expression. Local.ready_resume uses rich-source inversion to derive its primitive invocation check, replacing the separate primitive-admission premise. Local.resume_at_cut reuses deterministic lexical lookup and the existing annotation split to identify the same cut as rich source. The theorem returns matching annotations and recursive Pending at the same successor stack, source scope, owner phase and output mode as recomposition. This replaces its old ModePending component: that component embeds ordinary-only invocation rules and cannot express every case admitted by the recursive judgment. The rich source, effect-row, ownership, usage and resource-support results remain.

The recursive judgment also supplies the actual lexical discard transition and the retained abandoned/waiting checks through Local.discard_step. Pending.cleanup_step supplies the actual callback-entry transition, its recursive dependency check and retained unwind suffix. Bind and beta reduction reuse existing rich-source substitution and value-silence results in SourceDependencyNeutral.Lexical.Recursive; no new substitution argument is introduced. Local examples check resumption under sequencing and a nested handler, and a callback that installs a handler before resuming. Consumed owners remain rejected for both invocation modes. These are local checking and transition results, not initial-program safety results.

The main capture theorem now derives recursive checks for both permitted primitive continuation actions at the newly allocated boundary. It uses the selected clause's actual code.requiredActions; no broader binder policy is substituted. resume_clause_from_retained derives the restored check from the saved and waiting source. dispose_clause_from_retained combines those checks with the current request's abandoned-callback check. Existing clause-mode selection supplies disposal permission, and protection proves that the captured segment preserves its input mode. Neither action assumes its successor check.

These derivations use return-aware history transport in SourceDependencyNeutral.lean. Its structural History relation inserts spent markers or pure cleanup frames on the active spine while preserving existing return-marker kinds and dormant continuations. Handler and owner cuts retain the existing lexical selection; erased ownership and protection observations reuse the existing neutral-scope proofs. Mutual induction transports the recursive checks, and pending_join recomposes the checked segments.

The existing structural declaration recipes now compile to recursive Local checks. compile_recipe_providers in SourceContextualRequirements.lean reuses all nine recipe constructors: resumption, disposal, silent sequencing, inherited requests, local-provider requests, the existing handled-request form, resources, pure cleanup and branch choice. It takes the primitive action interface and finite operation requirements, not a successful clause-body check. Return-aware provider transport in SourceDependencyProviders.lean retains callback and continuation modes; a matching provider may correctly replace handler dispatch with builtin dispatch. Substitution and instantiation reuse the existing preservation of a clause's required actions.

capture_selected_recipe in SourceContextualCapture.lean connects that compiler to an actual handler cut. The predecessor's finite forest test supplies the selected handler's requirements at its exact lexical tail. The selected operation and protection mode identify the recipe, including the actual clause's rights. The theorem derives the complete selected dependency-tree check and retained-stack check at the same allocated runtime stack. It also preserves the installed recipes and their finite forest test across capture. No selected-body or primitive-successor check is an input. The returned family lookup is the same one used by rich declaration typing to authenticate the actual clause code; recipe checking does not replace that source-to-dependency annotation proof.

Effectful cleanup wrappers now have a structural admission theorem for the recursive dependency checks. compile_footprint in SourceScheduledAdaptationCompilation.lean reuses SourceRequestFootprints.Footprint and the existing finite operation checker. Its induction covers sequencing, choice, nested handlers, nested cleanup and resource families. It has no successful callback-execution premise. Explicit continuation invocations are outside this footprint judgment and keep their independent capability obligations; inherited operation requirements still use resumption-only contracts.

cleanup_admission in SourceScheduledCleanupInterfaces.lean checks the body with the new armed frame present. Its structural Supplied relation records the callback's finite requirements at the exact registration suffix. Handler cuts split that evidence between captured and waiting segments. Owner cuts retain the dormant capture and move the registration evidence with its caller or waiting suffix. Mutual induction transports the recursive Local and Pending checks through resumption, disposal and both callback-return modes. No runtime plan is constructed, and no handler is removed during unwinding. The callback check is derived at the registration suffix whenever that frame is traversed.
