Existing owner inventories and pending owner bounds are preserved.

compile_recipe_cleanup joins this rule to the existing consuming-clause compiler. It accepts a structural body recipe, a callback footprint, their finite operation checks and the independent primitive continuation capabilities. It assumes neither the callback's execution check nor the wrapped body's check. registered_pending derives the new armed frame's retained check in either return mode. Examples check an effectful cell callback around both resume and discard. An inner handler installed by the body does not replace the callback's registration receiver; a masking handler already present at registration makes the finite check fail.

ClauseRecipe extends the existing structural consuming recipes with effectful cleanup, operation-footprint prefixes, resources and choices. It embeds existing recipes rather than replacing their established proofs. The operation interface filters requirements supplied by locally allocated providers; the declaration's receiving suffix supplies the remainder. Its compiler reuses cleanup_admission and the existing primitive continuation interface. No constructor contains a successful future-body check. This is an annotation judgment over the existing dependency syntax, not a second computation calculus.

ClauseDeclarations stores these recipes for both offered modes using the actual raw clause's required action rights. ClauseDeclarations.install combines that structural declaration evidence with its finite lexical scope test and preserves the existing annotated stack checks. capture_declared_clause selects the stored recipe at an actual handler cut, compiles its complete dependency tree, and preserves the declaration evidence and finite forest check. It reuses capture_clause_interface factored from the established capture proof in SourceContextualCapture.lean. The previous capture_selected_recipe theorem also uses that same factored proof, so the capture mechanics are not duplicated. Substitution and instantiation retain the new declarations by the existing required-action preservation lemmas. selected_typed_clause joins this structural compiler to the existing rich source-selection theorem. Its compiled dependency family is the same family that rich declaration typing authenticates for the actual clause, offered mode and higher-order parameter environment. Matching action rights alone cannot substitute a different dependency body.

Higher-order declaration retention reuses the existing SourcePlannedChecks.Certified judgment with an explicit lexical declaration policy. Its constructors traverse nested bodies and both offered clause modes; they contain no receiving stack or execution-success premise. ClauseDeclarations.signature_congr supplies the source law needed by the shared certification transport in SourcePlanSignatureChecking.lean. The previous recipe clients use that same transport proof. No alternative function type or source syntax is introduced: existing function types already retain the stable body signature.

bind_preserves and beta_preserves combine the existing synchronized-source substitution results with recursive lexical Local and declaration certification. All three facts are retained for the exact body selected by the function signature; neither successor certification nor successor Local is a premise. actual_source_handler retrieves the actual raw clause witness from rich source typing and transports its certification through signature equality. source_handler_install then combines it with the current scope test and retained stack facts for the actual handler-entry transition. It derives the successor body source/check, stored declarations, matching stack, recursive pending check and finite forest test. It does not yet join the separate row, store, usage and resource-support components of common preservation.

capture_source_clause now joins the stored structural declarations to the rich SourceDependencySchemes.Lexical.capture_mode_segments result. Its successor contains the selected clause's recursive Local check together with the same clause's source typing, row and store certificates, ownership balance, usage, ticket access and resource access. It derives the whole-clause check from the independently proved primitive capabilities and the actual selected declaration; no successor Local or primitive capability proof is an input. Stored declarations and finite receiving-scope checks survive this same capture. The proof reuses the existing rich capture theorem and clause compiler.

This closes the join between the selected clause's dependency check and the rich capture result for the supported declaration grammar. The predecessor must still supply source typing, structural declarations, recursive pending checks, the finite forest test, row/store annotations and operand support. The result also retains the exact cleanup-path premise for disposing capture. It does not prove initial admission or coverage of every required clause form. The separate planned-source result below retains latent declaration certification; joining it to this allocation result remains open.

source_handler_install also returns CertifiedClauses for the actual typed clause plans. selected_plan_certified follows the source lookup witness through its ordinary or protected mode and retains certification of that exact plan. Equality of dependency families alone is not used to identify clause plans.

capture_certified_source combines the lexical capture result with the existing planned-source clause selection and substitution proofs. It returns the selected body's stable signature and nested declaration certification, its recursive Local and retained Pending checks, the preserved installed declarations and finite scope test, and fresh-owner accounting. Instantiating its contract parameters with an existing allocated contract supplies the actual substituted Body and capture step. The existing refineContract law proves erasure equals that same contract; ownership demands, rows and effect interfaces are unchanged. Higher-order payloads use the existing refined value summary and substitution proof. This result alone does not select or construct the allocator's row/store contract. The planned mixed-mode source below retains its witness through capture and recomposition; capture_planned_allocation now joins capture to row/store allocation at that exact source witness.

CertifiedFrame retains one actual plan witness shared by pending-context source typing and certification. Handler frames retain their actual typed clause plans, structural declarations and CertifiedClauses; armed callbacks retain their typed callable signature and certification. It projects to the existing SourcePlannedFrames.Frame. Certification is not attached to a separately chosen typing proof, since that would not identify the same hidden plan.

PlannedModeSource extends planned source retention to the same normal and unwind boundaries as SourceDependencyFrames.ModeSource. Erasure produces that existing judgment with the same runtime stack, dependency scope, owner demand and requirements. There are no new runtime terms or transitions. Skipped code has no ordinary requirements; handlers and callbacks survive abandonment; live captures retain saved source, and abandoned captures retain their retirement.

Its append, split and handler_cut lift the existing structural proofs and requirement-evaluation equations while retaining the plan witnesses. unwind_source produces both the planned cleanup source and the existing UnwindSource at the same owner demand. unwind_reentry therefore reuses UnwindTemplate.ownership. resume_recomposition derives the caller's source at the captured return mode, restores the complete saved and caller prefixes, and proves the successor demand accounts for the physical owned continuations. It does not assume an already typed reentered caller, and it covers unwind return.

transport reuses existing expression, declaration and context extension proofs. capture_retention retains the saved and waiting planned source under the allocator's matching contract and fresh action entry. installed_declarations extracts the structural declarations from this source, including dormant captures. capture_from_planned_source then recovers the selected typed declaration and its certification at the actual handler cut and invokes capture_certified_source. Those three predecessor witnesses are now derived from retained source rather than supplied independently at capture.

capture_planned_allocation in SourceScheduledCleanupInterfaces.lean now joins the retained planned source to the actual capture allocation. Its predecessor supplies the planned request and stack source, the existing lexical checks, planned resume records, annotated stores and requirements, ownership/access judgments, finite scope check and operand resource bound. The selected handler declarations, clause plans and certification are extracted from that stack source.

capture_mode_segments_at_body in SourceDependencySchemes.lean factors the existing allocation argument to accept the exact source cut and selected clause body. The old capture_mode_segments_at_cut and capture_mode_segments interfaces remain wrappers with their previous contracts. The planned caller supplies the erasure of its selected body; it does not equate independently chosen source plans or effect interfaces. Allocation selects the continuation's owner demands, rows and store entries. refineContract retains those fields while restoring the planned input and answer types.

The joined result constructs the planned successor stack, substitutes the higher-order payload into the same selected clause, and instantiates that clause's own row certificate against the actual allocated store. The existing complete_allocated_clause proves its demand balance and combined requirement check. The same successor also carries whole-clause lexical checking, retained pending checks and declarations, finite scope checking, one-shot usage, ticket/resource access, the capture step and physical ownership accounting. The erased allocator's independently returned expression is not used as evidence for the planned expression's requirements.

PlannedResumeAnnotated retains the planned source and its certification for the exact stored requirement body, together with its captured-stack identity, contract lookup and recorded lexical scope. Its erasure supplies the existing ResumeAnnotated judgment to the row and ownership proofs. Capture constructs the fresh record and transports surviving records under the same registry extension. Resumption and administrative unwinding preserve surviving records using the existing location lemmas.

selected_planned_resume_source recovers the precise stored source through lookup, unique captured identity and the actual return mode. It does not assume that two source annotations for the same code are equal. resume_planned_fragments joins that source to the saved, caller and tail row checks after consumption. resume_fragment_rows factors the existing row/store proof so that both the older source theorem and the planned theorem use it.

resume_planned_segments now derives the planned successor source, normal and annotated requirement checks, ownership balance, one-shot usage, ticket/resource access and recursive pending checks for the actual resumed stack. It retains the saved record's annotation, the pending annotation and the selected caller cleanup branch. Surviving resume records keep their planned source certificates. The successor rows remain within the predecessor certificate's effect bound.

For an unwind return, unwind_source_evaluation derives the caller's planned cleanup source together with an existing UnwindSource whose requirement evaluation is equal. The established ownership proof supplies their common owner demand. The predecessor's selected cleanup branch then checks that same planned source; checked append joins it with the saved source and spent-owner suffix. Ordinary return reuses the caller's ordinary check. No reentered source or successor requirement check is a premise.

These results close the source/row connections for capture allocation and resume/recomposition, including unwind return. Capture still requires the predecessor's exact cleanup branch when disposal is available and its operand resource-support bound; resume still requires the exact caller-cleanup branch when returning into unwind. Initial admission must establish these annotations at every applicable site. Integration of disposal, cleanup and the remaining boundaries into the common invariant, complete clause/callback admission, common preservation and initial progress remain open. M1–M4 remain open.

The cleanup boundary connections now retain the same source and certificate witnesses. start_planned_cleanup derives the actual callback application, its declaration plan and recursive local check, the pending unwind-return stack, and their combined checked requirements. finish_planned_cleanup returns from that callback to unwinding; finish_planned_close returns from the closing marker to the waiting ordinary computation. Each theorem preserves ownership balance, one-shot usage, ticket/resource access, finite declaration checks, and all surviving planned resume and disposal records. The original annotated requirement tree remains a checked alternative with an explicit path, so this boundary step does not discard previously checked cleanup branches. These three transitions leave the continuation store and owner phases unchanged. They reuse the existing transition, access and ownership proofs; no successor check is a premise.

advance_planned_unwind now joins all six administrative cases to their actual store and phase changes. It derives the successor's planned source, normal requirement check within the predecessor certificate's row bound, recursive capability checks, stored source certificates, declaration checks, owner balance, one-shot usage and ticket/resource access. Opening a capture removes its callable records while leaving its ticket for the later retirement step.

The store proof reuses the checker's existing demand-uniqueness theorem. The saved cleanup demand cannot contain the opened owner because the same checked sequence already contains its later retirement. checked_remove_undemanded then removes that owner's records throughout the recursive saved check; the waiting suffix uses the existing removal theorem for consumed owners. recursive_local_restrict and recursive_pending_restrict lift the established live-owner availability argument to the recursive return-mode judgments. The actual successor stack supplies the availability bound, rather than a new source-admission premise.

advance_planned_unwind_annotated strengthens the administrative result with checked successor annotations and explicit retained paths. The earlier normal-row theorem is now a projection of this stronger result. UnwindAnnotationStep records three structural cases:

  • Plain, handler, cell and spent-frame pops retain the entire predecessor annotation as a checked alternative.
  • Ticket retirement retains the waiting source's annotated subtree, checked after consuming that ticket.
  • Opening a capture retains the saved-cleanup and waiting-source annotations, with paths at their original demand prefixes. Their checked sequence includes the intervening retirement, under the store with that owner's records removed.

The proof uses RowAnnotation.focus to select the exact source subtrees and RequirementPath.checked to obtain their checks. Annotations retain each subtree's owner demand, so the existing demand-uniqueness and store-removal proofs apply. Every path below either retained subtree can be composed with its successor path using the existing RequirementPath.trans. The successor's annotated row stays within the predecessor certificate's effect bound.

This closes local transport for those source-positioned annotation subtrees. It does not establish that they contain every cleanup branch required by source admission. Enclosing alternatives outside those subtrees are not retained on opening or retirement. Connecting all required cleanup paths to the common invariant, complete initial admission, common preservation and initial progress remain open. The conditional mixed-source disposal connection is proved below. M1–M4 remain open.

The capture allocator now exposes its choice of cleanup source. capture_mode_segments_with_closing and capture_planned_allocation_with_closing accept the exact stored cleanup requirements and their source proof, together with the existing certificate path when disposal is offered. They return an equation identifying the newly allocated disposal record. An unprotected capture receives that exact record; a protected capture retains only the previous records. This also covers the existing unprotected allocation case when the clause has no explicit disposal right. The previous allocation interfaces are wrappers with unchanged statements.

PlannedUnwindSource pairs a planned cleanup source with the exact stored UnwindSource and a proof that their requirements evaluate equally in every store, receiving context and owner phase. planned_unwind_source constructs this pair from a planned source using the established cleanup conversion. PlannedUnwindAnnotated retains the pair with the captured-stack identity and recorded scope. capture_planned_unwind_records uses the allocator's equation to attach that supplied pair and transports the existing records. Lookup uses physical capture uniqueness and the recorded scope; it does not require unique source typing.

PlannedUnwindSource.annotated_checked transfers a checked stored certificate to the paired planned cleanup, retains its annotation as a checked alternative, and supplies the existing cleanup ownership balance. Planned disposal records also retain their witnesses across resumption, discard rearrangement and administrative unwinding. These results connect the stored cleanup body to its planned source. The following discard result uses these exact witnesses. Initial admission and adoption of the stronger records throughout the common invariant remain open.

discard_planned_segments now joins the actual lexical discard transition to its planned source, recursive capability checks, normal and annotated effect checks, stored source records, owner balance, one-shot usage, ticket access and resource access. The successor opens the captured stack for unwinding, places one closing boundary before the waiting caller, and removes the discarded owner's callable records. Its requirements account for exactly the successor's physical continuation owners. Both the exact stored cleanup annotation and the waiting source's annotated subtree remain checked paths in the successor.

PlannedModeSource.extract_discard derives the ordinary waiting boundary from unprotected capture and the existing unwind_prefix_return_mode theorem. discard_waiting reuses source splitting, append and normalized-context transport to replace the live owner by its spent marker. discard_pending_at_cut identifies the same lexical cut in the recursive capability judgment and joins its saved and waiting checks through the actual closing boundary. Ownership, usage and resource preservation reuse the established discard and resumption lemmas. The closing boundary's scope typing follows from the resolved owner contract.

The predecessor certificate must contain a cleanup invocation checked with the protected closing boundary. The existing counterexample UnwindExamples.closing_delimiter_changes_check shows why an ordinary invocation check cannot replace it: an intervening interpretation can export an unprotected request, which the closing boundary protects again. discard_closing_annotation constructs this additional finite branch from the owner, cleanup demand and receiving context. discard_planned_fragments uses its checked stored body at the actual closing boundary, then recomposes the source and bounded effect row. There is no successor-validity or future-execution premise and no runtime plan.

This closes the conditional mixed-source discard connection. The generated annotation layer below discharges its separate protected-path premise. Complete source admission and preservation of required cleanup coverage remain open.

annotateDisposals constructs the protected invocation alternative at every explicit disposal leaf in a finite requirement tree. It preserves the owner demand and traverses sequences, both sides of choices and existing annotations. annotateDisposalStore applies the same construction to referenced source bodies, keeping their keys and demands. These are static checking data; execution and lexical cleanup rules do not change.

disposal_check_sound reuses the recursive checker to derive the normal source check and every generated disposal check at its original consumption phase. disposal_store_lookup authenticates the exact generated stored body; disposal_record_sound exposes its checks when that record is invoked. The existing checker supplies the recursion through referenced records. Generation commutes with receiving-context extension, consumed-owner removal and the administrative unwind store update. It does not assert that arbitrary source programs pass the stronger check.

disposal_source_focus selects the generated annotation of a source-positioned subtree. retained_disposal_path then carries every disposal check below such a retained subtree to its new demand prefix. This covers those retained subtrees; it does not establish coverage when a transition constructs a different source tree using only equality of ordinary requirement evaluations.

discard_planned_segments_generated uses the generated source and store check to supply the protected path required by discard_planned_segments. It has no separate protected-path premise and retains the full transition result, including source typing, recursive capabilities, effects, ownership and resource access. Its surviving store is exactly the generated annotation of the remaining records. The regression pair rejects the existing closing-boundary counterexample and accepts cleanup delegation when the receiving interpretation supports protected calls.

The capture allocator now exposes the exact disposal lookup in the annotated store through capture_mode_segments_with_closing_lookup. The existing allocator is a projection of that result; its execution and premises are unchanged. capture_planned_allocation_with_protected_closing carries the same lookup through rich planned source allocation.

ProtectedClauseInterface extends the ordinary clause interface with a disposal check under the actual closing boundary. protected_interface_from_record derives this check from the checked resume record, the exact stored cleanup body, and a retained protected cleanup path. It does not infer protected safety from the ordinary disposal check. protected_capture_annotation constructs the normal and protected cleanup paths as finite checking alternatives with the same ownership demand; it does not assert that the resulting check succeeds. The stronger capture result supplies the interface when that protected path is present in its accepted capture annotation.

protected_discard_source_checked connects the stronger interface to an actual richly typed discard expression and its generated requirement annotation. clause_disposals_checked extends this connection through every constructor of the existing open requirement derivation. Each additional disposal check uses that invocation's recorded receiver and consumption phase. The proof reuses ordinary request checks and invocation evidence; sequencing and alternatives keep their original ownership demands.

ClauseRowAdmission.ProtectedRows records the generated requirement derivation at a local protected continuation interface. Both SourcePlannedSources.Body and SourceAnnotatedSources.Body now require this certificate in addition to the ordinary row certificate. Hereditary offers retain both before capture. Existing source substitution, world extension and registry transport carry the same certificates. Erasure to the older source layer projects the ordinary one. The generator and protected interface live in the common clause-contract module so source admission and execution proofs use the same definitions.

The resume and discard admission constructors supply the protected certificate. ProtectedRows.of_unchanged reuses ordinary certificates when generation changes nothing. ProtectedRows.of_calls reuses an ordinary open derivation with a protected check for each disposal call at its exact lexical receiver; it does not transplant a base-interface check through an intervening handler.

capture_planned_allocation_with_protected_closing now instantiates the hereditary protected certificate after substituting the actual payload. Its result includes the rich source expression and checked generated requirements for that substituted clause at the allocated stack, within the advertised request and resumption budget. The protected capture path remains a predecessor premise. Complete initial admission must establish that path and caller cleanup coverage, resource support and the remaining callback checks; those results and common preservation/progress remain open.

capture_mode_segments_with_closing_store exposes the exact allocated checking store: the saved annotation is inserted first, followed by the prior resume records, the optional lexical cleanup record and the prior disposal records. The original lookup theorem is a projection with its statement unchanged. capture_planned_allocation_with_protected_store carries that equation through the rich source result. It also joins the generated clause check to the retained tail, proves their combined ownership demand and bounds the whole successor certificate. The ordinary clause-consumption proof supplies the ownership balance; the generated clause is checked at the same stack and owner phase. The prior protected-allocation API projects this stronger result.

capture_generated_store proves that allocation preserves the generated-store form when the predecessor store and saved annotation have that form. The proof constructs an annotated raw successor store and proves that its generation equals the actual allocation. The optional cleanup record is unchanged by generation, as established by its lexical unwind template. No successor check or successful cleanup is an input. These results connect the actual allocation to generated store and clause checks; they do not construct the required initial capture annotations or establish the common invariant.

capture_planned_allocation_generated connects those results at the capture entry point. It derives a generated split from the predecessor certificate and the handler-cut evaluation equation for the same source witnesses. Its normalized raw certificate retains the predecessor root and the ordinary split; the generated certificate checks both within the original effect budget. The chosen saved and tail annotations supply their generated fragment checks through paths in that certificate. The shared allocator consumes those derived checks, constructs the store, and supplies the source, lexical dependencies, access and ownership results. Existing path-based APIs still derive the split check from their paths and keep their statements unchanged.

The generated entry returns an annotated raw successor store whose generated image checks the actual substituted clause and waiting tail. It retains the exact raw saved annotation in the resume record. The lexical request guard supplies the unprotected-capture fact needed to map the ordinary and protected cleanup paths; no new protection premise is introduced. The result covers both protected captures without a cleanup record and unprotected captures with that record. Fragment checks and the successor certificate are outputs, not entry premises. Initial admission must still supply the required cleanup paths, and assembly under the common invariant remains open.

Generated cleanup checks now survive the paired cleanup-source reconstruction. unwind_template_disposals derives an abandonable prefix from the existing cleanup-template grammar and proves that disposal generation leaves its requirements unchanged. PlannedModeSource.unwind_disposals proves the same property for planned unwinding on that prefix. These requirements retain callback effects and retirements; the callbacks' separate source and capability checks remain required.

PlannedUnwindSource.disposal_evaluation therefore reuses the established ordinary equality to prove equality after generation for these paired cleanup representations. annotated_checked_generated reconstructs checked planned cleanup from its generated stored annotation. Its result is another generated annotation retaining the whole prior generated subtree, with the same effect bound and established ownership balance.

PlannedModeSource.append_disposals factors the existing append induction so one reconstructed source has both ordinary and generated evaluation equations. The old append result projects its ordinary equation. The generated equation uses the actual enclosing interpretation suffix and consumption phase; append_checked_generated uses it to join generated checks on the same stack append. These results close the paired-cleanup representation and raw-source append gaps.

PlannedModeSource.split_disposals similarly strengthens the existing split induction: the same source witnesses carry ordinary and generated evaluation equations. handler_cut_disposals retains the selected handler declaration and its value-or-unwind result boundary with both equations. The original split and handler-cut interfaces project their ordinary results.

disposal_annotation_map proves that generation preserves the existing RowAnnotation relation. handler_cut_checked_generated uses this fact to extract the generated source check from a root certificate with additional alternatives, then derives generated capture and tail checks at the actual handler cut. Their combined row stays within the root certificate's bound. Neither fragment check is an extra premise. Extraction leaves the original certificate available; it does not claim that every additional branch has been reconstructed in a successor certificate.

capture_annotation_generated_iff identifies the exact finite evidence for a source-derived capture cleanup annotation: the generated normal-source check, ordinary ClosingEffects, and ClosingEffects under the actual closing barrier. The proof reuses the existing cleanup-template ownership and effect checking results. Unique, available captured owners supply retirement readiness; no separate retirement check or cleanup-path premise is required.

capture_annotation_from_effects constructs the generated annotation and its retained normal, ordinary-cleanup and protected-cleanup paths from that evidence. It derives the equality of ownership demands from the source ownership balance and the cleanup template. Every branch stays within the supplied effect budget. The converse proves that these effect premises are necessary for this particular annotation, not an additional conservative restriction on its accepted checks.

The nested-capture example reuses the existing effectful callback and its two lexical handlers inside two dormant continuations. It constructs the annotation with ownership demand [8, 7]; the result does not depend on an empty-demand or pure-cleanup restriction. This is a construction from local effect evidence, not complete initial admission: source admission must still establish both callback-effect judgments at every applicable capture and preserve them through source transformations.

Generated annotations now survive the six administrative unwind rules in the same successor state as the established source, ownership and access results. PlannedModeSource.advance_generated_annotated_checked handles plain-frame and handler pops, cell removal, spent markers, retirement and opening a dormant capture. The first four retain the whole prior generated root. Retirement keeps the exact generated waiting subtree. Opening keeps the exact generated saved and waiting subtrees after removing the retiring owner's callable records. The existing append equations check their reconstructed source.

retire_annotation_checked_generated and open_annotation_checked_generated focus the original annotation before mapping the selected subtrees. This keeps the successor a generated annotation rather than merely an arbitrary checked requirement tree. The opening helper reuses the established retirement-readiness proof. UnwindAnnotationStep.disposals carries the retained-path account through the same generator, including the demand change at retirement.

advance_planned_unwind_generated reuses the full administrative preservation theorem for lexical source metadata, pending capabilities, stores, physical ownership and access. It supplies the generated successor check at the updated owner phase and exactly annotateDisposalStore (unwindStore stack annotatedStore). The successor therefore has the same generated-store and generated-annotation form as the predecessor. No new admission premise is added. This closes that transport obligation for administrative unwind; it does not establish all-site cleanup coverage or the common preservation theorem for other transition families.

Cleanup entry and both completion boundaries now preserve generated certificates in their full transition results. start_planned_cleanup_generated retains the callback's actual rich source and declaration plan, the waiting stack's generated check, and the whole prior generated annotation. finish_planned_cleanup_generated and finish_planned_close_generated retain the same whole-root evidence when returning to unwind or ordinary execution. The three results reuse the existing complete transition theorems for lexical capabilities, stores, ownership and access. Their generated source checks come from the corresponding PlannedModeSource lemmas; no successor certificate is an input.

outward_disposals proves that the existing outward-row grammar has no direct disposal invocation to annotate. beta_generated_annotated uses that fact with the existing rich beta-substitution and outward-extraction proofs to check the actual substituted lambda body and retain the prior generated annotation. The statement permits effectful bodies and internal handlers. Those handlers' clause bodies keep their independent source-admission certificates; the lemma does not assert that the entire program is free of continuation operations. This beta result concerns source and row preservation, not a new complete machine-transition theorem.

bind_generated_annotated preserves the actual substituted body and the whole prior generated annotation after a value binding. It reuses the value's empty ownership demand, source substitution and the existing annotated-body path. The result permits continuation invocations in the body.

SourcePlannedSources.focus_decompose_disposals and context_plug_disposals provide ordinary and generated evaluation equations for the same typed child, context and reconstructed source. Their proofs reuse the existing context cases and evaluation laws. template_value_disposals handles already evaluated operands: their immediate requirement trees contain no continuation invocation, while latent bodies keep their source judgments. The original decomposition and plug interfaces project the ordinary equations. focus_step_disposals carries both equations and the signature split through the existing runtime-frame preparation and unchanged ownership trace; the old focus-step statement is also preserved by projection.

focus_generated_annotated and plug_generated_annotated derive the generated successor check from the predecessor certificate and retain its entire raw and generated annotation as a subtree. Both checks remain within the predecessor effect bound. These results cover the existing evaluation-context forms without a new child, context or successor-check premise.

focus_planned_generated now joins focus's source and generated row proofs to one actual transition. It retains the certified child plan and saved context, recursive current and pending lexical checks, stack matching, annotation bounds, resume and disposal records, unchanged owners, and the existing use and access judgments. focus_signature_checks selects the actual certified subplans in all four signature cases. Right-pair focus reuses local_history, whose structural relation now permits inserting a pure waiting frame. The same induction retains handler selection, owner identity, callback modes and dormant captures; it does not change cleanup dispatch. The prior raw and generated root annotations stay as exact subtrees. plug_planned_generated now provides the corresponding joint connection for all ten context forms. It reuses the actual stored context and rich value, retaining latent types and the complete prior annotations. Assembly of the common runtime invariant remains open.

Resumption source extraction now returns ordinary and generated evaluation equations for the same source witnesses. PlannedModeSource.extract_live_disposals and extract_planned_recorded_resume_disposals reuse the established generated stack split and exact stored-source selection. The original extraction APIs project their ordinary equations without changing their statements.

disposal_store_annotation_map maps authenticated records while retaining keys and demands. resume_fragment_rows_generated uses that relation to reuse the existing resumption row-transport theorem. Exact lookup identifies the generated copy of the saved annotation; type equality alone is not used to identify a saved body. resume_planned_fragments_generated joins those checks to the actual saved, caller and tail source witnesses after consuming the owner and removing its callable records. It adds no fragment-check or reentered-source premise.

resume_planned_segments_generated completes that recomposition for ordinary and unwind return. It joins the generated saved, caller and tail checks at the actual successor stack and owner phase, removes the consumed owner's records, and retains the exact saved annotation, pending annotation and caller-cleanup branch. The generated successor annotation stays within the predecessor effect bound. Ownership, one-shot use, ticket access, resource support and recursive return hints use the existing resumption results. The structural remainder proof is reused for generated checks by requirement_remainder_generated. No successor source or fragment check is assumed. As in the original full resumption theorem, unwind return requires the predecessor's caller-cleanup branch; constructing that evidence through initial source admission remains open. This result closes generated resumption recomposition, not M1 or M2.

All initial capture/caller alternatives, preservation of additional annotation branches through every source transformation, and the common invariant remain open.

This removes the manual protected-path obligation for the generated discard entry point. Complete initial source admission, coverage through source reconstruction, automatic cleanup and unwind-return alternatives, and consistent use of the stronger records in the common invariant remain open. M1–M4 remain open; no complete milestone package is closed by this annotation layer.

Regression examples reuse the existing effectful-cleanup function through bind and beta reduction, preserving synchronized source typing and both checks. Another example substitutes a value into a callback inside a handler clause: the raw clauses change, while the same-signature certification is retained.

The installation-to-capture example checks a clause with an effectful cell cleanup and a resumption. Another example places cleanup inside resource allocation: its callback uses the local provider without exporting that request to the declaration's caller. These are dependency-admission results. Rich source typing must still authenticate the raw code and its dependency annotations, including nested declarations, effect bounds and resource support. The example does not claim to prove those separate facets.

The older DeclarationRecipes grammar remains unchanged for its existing compilers. The new lexical declaration path removes its pure-cleanup restriction for footprint callbacks, including wrappers inside resources and branches. Callbacks with explicit owner invocations, arbitrary nested-handler clause bodies and disposal-capable inherited request prefixes remain required by the milestone. The footprint checker still requires resumption-only inherited operation capabilities. Initial source admission must establish and retain the complete annotations through higher-order source; all-site cleanup coverage, resource-support admission, common preservation and initial progress remain unproved. M1–M4 remain open.

The same result now carries successor MachineUse and MachineTicketAccess from their predecessor judgments. scoped_least_enclosing_actions reuses the clause's usage proof under exactly code.requiredActions, matching the registry already used by source allocation. capture_machine_use and capture_ticket_access then supply the successor facets without equating those minimal rights to the potentially broader binder policy.

Capture now also carries the successor MachineAccess judgment. Its additional source premises are an independent finite bound for the operand's retained resources and inclusion of that bound in the selected source handler's outer lexical resources plus the ambient resources. The existing exact source-selection proof supplies the runtime capture condition through source_request_access. transition_access then preserves support across the same concrete capture step used by all the other results. The check follows actual operand support, including closures; it does not use a first-order operation-port restriction or recover physical captures from a function type. Initial admission must still establish and preserve these support annotations, just as for the existing resource-exit rule. The mixed local dependency invariant remains outstanding.

Initial source admission must still supply the required capture and caller branches at every applicable site and preserve their association with the actual lexical cleanup. Neither an arbitrary RowAnnotation nor the capture rule's normal fallback proves that obligation.

The same theorem now joins the actual resume transition to the independent one-shot usage, ticket-access and resource-support facets. Its inputs are their predecessor judgments and the existing structural ReentrySource for the caller's actual captured return mode. The typed operand supplies value closure; ReentrySource.bounds supplies the transition's local ownership conditions. source_resume_use, UseTransition.ticket_access and the existing raw-step resource-support theorem produce the three successor judgments for exactly the same stack used by source recomposition. The resume expression form discharges its resource-access side conditions through ScopedPorts.resume_access_checks. No successor usage, accessibility or resource-support judgment is assumed, and no new proof of their individual preservation is introduced.

These independent facets hold for the actual resume step; the joint successor source/effect result still requires the cleanup-branch coverage described above. The current expression's recursive source judgment supplies this successor's recursive retained dependency checks. The capture clause's recursive check is joined to its allocated source and rows by capture_planned_allocation above. Complete future cleanup coverage and initial admission remain outstanding. In particular, joining one-shot usage does not establish future callback capability checks.

Existing ResumeCertified consumers have not been silently reinterpreted as using ResumeAnnotated. Admission and preservation must supply the structural caller coverage at every applicable resume site and establish the common source and usage invariant. Sufficient initial admission and the common preservation/progress theorem remain outstanding.

Eleven ordinary boundary results in SourceDependencyNeutral.lean now use ModeSource and ModePending: cleanup registration, normal callback entry and return, handler entry and exit, resource entry and exit, cell read and write, spent-clause return, and closing-value return. Together with expression focus and plug, these retain the same recorded-scope bound over a suffix whose final mode can be ordinary or unwinding. Callback summaries, handler declarations, rich returned values and the resource-release support premise remain intact.

Fresh handler installation transports the existing source and pending checks only where the registries agree on installed identities. Resource installation reuses source transport and local world weakening. Cell updates preserve both judgments at the actual updated stack, including dormant captures and unwind modes. These proofs reuse the earlier boundary arguments; they introduce no runtime cleanup plan. They establish source and local-check preservation for these boundaries, not the complete requirement-row, record-store and physical ownership invariant needed by the common execution theorem.

Fixed milestone checklist

The selected lexical machine has eight outer transition constructors. Expanding its evaluation and administrative cases gives 20 applicable RawStep cases, six Advance cases and six other outer cases: 32 syntactic alternatives. The legacy plan-based raw discard is excluded. Some value-marker alternatives overlap, so this is a coverage count, not 32 independent proofs. The rich source judgment has 17 constructors; structural induction also covers arbitrarily nested handlers, values and callbacks through these same constructors.

M1's ordinary connection inventory has eight fixed batches, covering 17 raw cases after the joint focus result and conditional capture/resume results. The batches are a checklist within M1, not additional milestone packages. The implemented results below are conditional transition connections; they do not establish initial source admission or one common preservation theorem. The combined 424-module dependency build passed with warnings treated as errors.

Batch Cases Status and result
Plug 1 Implemented: plug_planned_generated joins rich/generated reconstruction, certified and recursive checks, and strong records.
Computation 4 Implemented: computation_planned_generated covers bind, beta and both Boolean branches through existing substitution and reduction proofs.
Cleanup registration 1 Implemented: register_cleanup_planned_generated retains the actual callback and latent source evidence.
Normal callback execution 2 Implemented: start_normal_cleanup_planned_generated and finish_normal_cleanup_planned_generated preserve the saved rich value and effectful callback source.
Handler boundaries 2 Implemented: enter_handler_planned_generated and leave_handler_planned_generated; fresh installation authenticates actual clauses and transports rich records under the extended registries.
Resource boundaries 2 Implemented: enter_resource_planned_generated and leave_resource_planned_generated; entry preserves row coverage under ordinary world freshness and exit retains its explicit support premise.
Cell operations 2 Implemented: read_cell_planned_generated and write_cell_planned_generated preserve the actual updated stack and stored sources.
Value-marker returns 3 Implemented: leave_clause_planned_generated, close_value_planned_generated and retire_value_planned_generated, including general-value outer rules.

A shared assembly obligation joins the already-proved generated capture, resumption, discard, administrative unwind and cleanup results to one common state. In particular, the state must retain PlannedUnwindAnnotated records: generated discard needs the rich record. The wrapper capture_planned_allocation_generated_recorded now carries those records through the same generated capture allocation. It reuses the original theorem's exact store equation and capture_planned_unwind_records; its supplied cleanup source is the paired rich source. The existing capture interface is unchanged, and its cleanup-effect premises remain explicit. All ordinary batches retain strong records. The existing generated resumption, administrative unwind, unwind callback entry/return and closing-return interfaces now also accept and return PlannedUnwindAnnotated, reusing the existing location and store-filtering lemmas. Generated discard already used this relation. These changes retain the exact cleanup source; they do not construct missing source budgets or caller cleanup evidence.

Common-state assembly must instantiate checker entries, owner phases, stores and receiving scopes consistently. Rich planned sources already project installed clause recipes. JoinedSource and JoinedState now collect these components, including finite checkForest, activation history and the lifetime ledger. JoinedState.computation preserves that shared component for bind, beta and both Boolean branches. Focus, plug, cleanup registration, normal callback entry/return, cell operations, value-marker returns, and handler/resource boundaries preserve the same component. JoinedState.advance now covers all six administrative unwind alternatives, and the three unwind callback/close wrappers cover callback entry, callback return and completion of abandonment. This connects 29 of the fixed 32 syntactic alternatives. The closing and retiring wrappers also cover their raw Unit subcases and general-value outer rules. Capture, resume and outer discard remain unjoined. The corrected discard_planned_segments_checked_generated now constructs the generated successor-annotation check from the original predecessor premises. It keeps raw annotations separate from their generated copies and retains the saved and pending paths; it assumes no annotation idempotence. The finite check for the actual new receiving suffix remains unresolved. A checked example with a covered, typed caller handler shows that retained declaration recipes and the old finite check alone do not imply that blanket successor check. The example has no callbacks: the abandoned handler only gets popped. It therefore exposes a possible excess in the unwind invariant, not a demonstrated execution failure or a complete JoinedState counterexample. No successor check or new source restriction has been added. Registration adds the exact cleanup owner to the lifetime ledger; callback return records its completion. These wrappers do not yet include the outstanding source-origin annotations below and are not the full admitted-state invariant. They also do not export the conditional helpers' old-root annotation paths as an additional state field. Non-handler forest transport and cell-update forest transport are checked; plug now also returns its current effect-scope typing. Other events still need the same assembly, followed by preservation of the completed source annotations. The installation-time check of actual declaration requirements remains a source obligation in M2. JoinedSource.HandlerEntryReady exposes that finite check through a coherent enhanced predecessor derivation. Since JoinedSource is a proposition, this does not establish identity of hidden annotation witnesses. Resource exit retains its explicit support bound; cell operations retain their builtin signature assumptions. These connections do not discharge those source origins. The combined dependency build passed with warnings treated as errors; the audit checks all 424 milestone modules and their exact dependency reports, using only the established axioms.

Resource entry no longer needs the earlier additional row-name exclusions. checked_open_resource_covered reuses residual coverage: installing a builtin may discharge requests and shrink the exported row while preserving its upper bound. The entry theorem therefore accepts every identity fresh for the source world. Ordinary world and lifetime freshness still apply; no extra allocation policy or renaming theorem is needed for this row check. Retirement retains the exact tail annotation after consuming its owner; other ordinary results retain the entire prior raw/generated root. Retaining a subtree does not by itself establish applicability of future source evidence after a scope change.

M2 has five remaining source-evidence families. These describe missing source origins for existing theorem premises, not new runtime semantics.

Family Required fact
Capture cleanup budgets Construct ordinary and protected cleanup-effect evidence for the actual captured fragment and retain its annotation paths. Local annotation construction from that evidence is already proved.
Caller cleanup on unwind return Construct and check caller cleanup at its actual receiver and return mode. A skipped ordinary caller branch is not a required checked alternative.
Owner locality Derive physical ownership from executable source demand in the actual return mode, and preserve lexical access separately. Legacy regional guards remain sufficient only for the fragment they cover.
Resource support Finite annotations and their rich substitution proof are now constructible. Derive the capture boundary and released-cell exclusion for returned values from admission, and preserve them through control flow.
Consuming declarations and callbacks Compile hereditary source evidence for both offered modes, continuation-using callbacks and disposing inherited requests.

The inventory fixes the constructors and premises to cover. It does not prove that the current source judgments supply them. Existing Local.request checks callback capabilities and owner bounds but does not carry budgeted ClosingEffects; current footprint-based declaration recipes also exclude invocations in some required positions. Source annotations and their structural construction/preservation must address these gaps. New helper lemmas belong under these existing obligations and must identify the case they discharge.

The owner-locality batch proves plain_pending_demand by source/context induction and supplies DemandPendingStack for finite region checks, including dormant captures. It reuses checked-demand and physical ownership proofs. It does not assume that all latent function dependencies are owner-local. The existing PendingFrame now has a demand-backed constructor, so the finite annotation converts directly to PendingStack and ReentrySource. Existing discard and resumption consumers use those annotations without a separate full-dependency-locality premise. The remaining region checks concern the front, saved continuation and tail at discard and unwind return.

The resource-support batch constructs SourceSupport.Bounds from actual lexical dependencies. Expression.annotate_substitution reuses the existing substitution bound and infers the finite support of the substituted rich source. The capture boundary and resource-release exclusion remain explicit checks to connect to admission. Result-value support remains separate from whole-body support: using a cell and returning an integer must not be rejected merely because the body used that cell.

SourceSupport.Returns provides a sufficient result-admission branch using the existing finite template checker. Resource entry constructs the opened rich body with its result bounded by the earlier resource world. Substitution and strict bind reduction retain that check; at a closed returned value it implies the required released-cell exclusion, including closure storage. The execution world may contain the local cell even when the result world excludes it. The checker may leave a final application, operation or handler result unknown; it is not the sole admission rule. General callable and clause result contracts, and transport through the other selected-machine boundaries, remain required.

The existing budget-gap fixture now also checks rows_and_protected_rows_do_not_supply_capture_cleanup: ordinary Rows and ProtectedRows, an authenticated source store and an empty normal capture row can coexist with rejection of an empty cleanup budget. Both row judgments are conditional on a continuation interface whose fields already contain the cleanup bounds. They cannot construct those bounds independently. This fixture does not establish reachability from an initially admitted closed program. Source admission must check the existing ordinary/protected cleanup alternatives within its advertised budget; the existing capture_annotation_generated_iff and capture_annotation_from_effects already connect that check to capture.

CleanupHints.Metadata now decorates the eight lexical cleanup-source forms with exact handler activation identities and callback latent rows. It erases to the existing return hints and reconstructs existing requirement syntax; there is no new evaluator or runtime cleanup plan. CleanupHints.extract derives agreement with the same typed cleanup source, including exact physical interpretation context and requirements. Dormant captures remain recursive. The finite metadata checker reuses the requirement evaluator. Its ordinary and protected checks imply the existing ClosingEffects judgments, and Agreement.capture_annotation constructs the actual generated annotation and all three retained paths. This removes the need to assume ClosingEffects at that bridge, but does not yet establish initial admission: contextual source rules must supply and preserve these finite checks at capture and unwind reentry. Registration-time checking alone is insufficient because resumption can insert caller interpretations beneath a saved callback.

CleanupRows.Rows decorates the existing stable signatures with nested callback rows; ValueRows retains that decoration in function input, output and body metadata. Auth authenticates it structurally through all 17 source constructors, with hereditary body, offer and declaration rules. Lambda bodies, application arguments/results, operation interfaces and continuation interfaces must use matching decorations. The cleanup constructor stores exactly the latent row of its recursively authenticated callback function type, including callbacks obtained through variables or applications. These are coherent rich typing witnesses, not a uniqueness claim about an earlier derivation. Auth.cleanup_callback extracts the actual typed callback and its matching metadata; Auth.lambda_body also recovers its outward-row evidence. Auth.cleanup_checked_site connects that authenticated row to the contextual cleanup-site checker, retaining explicit recursive checks and the actual-suffix obligation of the enclosing judgment. A closed-variable example constructs a lambda that performs an operation, binds it to a variable, and registers that variable as cleanup. Both its rich source and authentication are proved with a nonempty callback row. Its effect remains an explicit allowed interface; this example does not claim whole-machine admission or execution progress.

Metadata environment lookup, shadowing and commuting extensions are proved. Auth.value_context and Auth.value_summary reuse existing rich value transport while preserving the exact function input, result and body decorations. Auth.environment_congr, Auth.world_weaken and Auth.contract_extension retain those exact decorations through environment agreement, fresh resource worlds and compatible continuation contracts. Auth.substitution follows the existing rich source substitution theorem through all 17 expression forms and hereditary bodies, offers and declarations. It substitutes an authenticated closed value with matching input metadata and preserves the original result and checking metadata, including nested callback rows. Handler clause signatures reuse the established substitution equality; this adds no future-safety premise. Auth.bind_expression and Auth.beta_expression apply that result to actual bind and lambda-application reductions. They preserve the original ambient effect bound, exact body/result metadata and the existing requirement-evaluation equality. They do not yet connect these annotations to every machine transition.

This closes representation, structural authentication and closed substitution of nested cleanup rows. It does not establish complete source admission. Control-transition retention, contextual checks at actual capture/reentry suffixes, and the remaining O/S/D source obligations still need to be connected. The existing AuthBody deliberately retains the prior clause row obligations; it does not silently derive them from decoration data.

The contextual source facet now retains the cleanup checks structurally. Contextual.Context decorates the exact return hints with handler activation identities, pending rows and callback latent rows, preserving every return marker. Its partial cleanup projection rejects active normal, unwind and close callbacks and retains retiring owners. Context.Source ties the relevant data to actual typed callbacks and installed handler frames. It does not authenticate arbitrary stored clause or pending-expression decorations by itself.

Contextual.select agrees with existing nearest-handler lookup and returns the exact decorated prefix and tail. It cannot fall through a matching handler with missing operation metadata. Budgeted checks the eight stable-signature forms; application signatures include their authenticated latent body rows. Admitted retains that certificate alongside Auth, the independent existing capability judgment and actual context-source agreement. PendingBudget retains checks for pending code and callbacks under their actual return modes.

Admitted.request_effects derives the ordinary and protected ClosingEffects judgments for the physical selected prefix and receiving tail. Its inputs do not include fresh budget checks or a new agreement witness. Substitution, bind, application and cleanup registration preserve this current-source facet. Registration obtains the stored latent row from the actual authenticated callback. These results close the local consuming-request derivation; they do not close initial admission or capture/reentry preservation. The facet must still be joined to the common state, including real installation history and coherent pending/saved annotations.

Context.PlannedClosing now retains the rich typed callback and certified plan at the context's exact latent row and signature. Its structural projection constructs PlannedUnwindSource for those same cleanup requirements. Admitted.capture_planned_annotation joins that source with the normal, ordinary cleanup and protected cleanup paths in one generated annotation. The request supplies both cleanup-budget checks; the pending rich witness, physical cut, normal annotation and ownership evidence remain explicit structural inputs. Admitted.register_planned_cleanup obtains that rich callback witness from the actual authenticated cleanup expression when extending an abandonable region. It returns the body's admission and normal callback budget alongside the new closing context, using the existing callback-plan certification. The old region's closing evidence remains an input; running callback markers are not excluded from general source programs by this local lemma.

These results close the local witness/annotation bridge and its registration step, not construction from the full common state or retention through control transitions. The contextual source and pending budget judgments also preserve resource-world growth using the existing source and local-check transport lemmas.

Changed caller suffixes at resumption still require the existing R obligations; D/O/S remain outstanding.

AuthContext now authenticates all ten existing waiting-expression forms. Auth.focus_decompose obtains child and waiting-context authentication from the actual predecessor, sharing the intermediate value metadata. AuthContext.plug reconstructs authenticated source from that shared interface. Both preserve the existing ordinary and generated requirement equations. Cleanup context authentication also proves that its stored latent row equals the row in the callback's rich function type; these are one parameter.

FrameRows, ModeFrameRows and PendingRows refine the existing certified frame, mode-frame and pending-source judgments. They retain authenticated plain contexts, handler declarations, callback bodies and saved values through all return modes and recursive saved continuations. Adjacent frames share value metadata explicitly. Saved continuations use their owner's input and answer metadata, with an explicit ordinary-answer or unwind boundary. The projections recover physical context correspondence and rich cleanup witnesses when the selected context is abandonable. They do not infer hidden typing uniqueness from equality of proof terms.

PendingRows.cut_closing now obtains that rich witness from the whole pending source at the actual decorated handler cut; the suffix may contain active callbacks. Admitted.capture_from_pending aligns the current result metadata with that pending source and derives the exact cleanup source together with all three generated capture paths. It takes no separately chosen captured witness or new cleanup-budget check. Normal annotation and ownership checks remain independent inputs. Exact rich-witness transport and split/recomposition retain the metadata under contract extension and resource-world growth. The RetainedSource refinement now includes the authenticated source and pending metadata with their receiver-budget checks. Retaining those facets through all transitions remains an obligation.

The retained metadata now has exact structural split and append proofs. PendingRows.split_disposals extracts both physical segments, their rich source witnesses and one shared intermediate mode and value decoration at a supplied decorated boundary. PendingRows.append_disposals recomposes those witnesses with that same interface. Both retain ordinary and generated requirement evaluation equations, including live, opening and spent continuation cases. They add no receiver-budget premise; validity at a changed receiver remains a separate obligation. World weakening now transports authenticated declarations, expression contexts, frames and pending stacks with unchanged metadata, using the existing rich source transports.

FocusRows records the exact row split from authenticated expression focus. Transparent plain-frame insertion preserves nearest-handler selection and both cleanup checks beneath arbitrary lexical prefixes. FocusRows.budgeted uses that result to derive the child's budget under its waiting frame and the waiting expression's budget. Admitted.focus_retained connects these results to the actual raw focus transition: the child remains admitted, its plan remains certified, and the pushed pending frame retains authenticated source metadata and budget evidence. This covers all existing focus forms without a fresh successor check. Its stronger internal result keeps the requirement equations and waiting-context capability check from the same decomposition; the original interface projects that result. Both the older focus connection and the strengthened state reuse one generated-root annotation helper.

RetainedSource has evaluation and unwind constructors that share the exact pending witness, context and output metadata. Evaluation retains the current Admitted witness and its matching pending input metadata. Owner phases come from the actual stack, and installation metadata uses the state's activation history. Local checks and stack matching project from these same witnesses. The older forest, row, store and ownership obligations remain explicit. RetainedState combines that source with the eight existing non-source fields and projects directly to JoinedState.

RetainedState preserves the stronger state for focus, bind, beta, both branches, plug, cell read/write, cleanup registration and normal callback start/return, handler exit, consumed-clause/closing/retiring value returns and all six administrative unwind forms, resource entry/exit and the three unwind callback/close boundaries: 28 of the existing 32 syntactic alternatives. Their generated root checks refer to the same source witnesses as the authentication and pending metadata. Plug reconstructs all ten waiting-context forms with their exact input/output metadata and budget. The old and stronger plug connections reuse one root-annotation proof. Cell updates transport the same pending source and metadata through the actual physical update.

Cleanup registration uses one installed action and its authenticated callback throughout the source, budget and ownership evidence. Callback start saves the actual current value's metadata in that action's running frame; callback return restores that same saved authentication at the action's lexical scope. These proofs retain higher-order values and add no successor-check premise. Where the physical successor is fixed, the older joint preservation theorem supplies only its eight operational fields. Registration constructs those fields for the same chosen action. Neither approach infers equality between independently selected source derivations.

The conditional connection inventory remains 29 of 32, with capture, resume and outer discard outstanding; preservation of the new source facets remains open for four alternatives: handler entry, capture, resume and outer discard. These counts describe different obligations on the same fixed transition inventory, not additional work packages. Complete source admission and the common preservation/progress results remain open.

Resource entry opens the same authenticated body at the fresh identity and retains its result metadata in the exact allocated cell frame. The existing world transports preserve pending sources, callbacks and records. The older and strengthened entry proofs reuse one generated-root annotation lemma based on resource hiding and row inclusion; no exclusion of names in effect rows or invoked saved bodies is required. Resource exit preserves the existing explicit support and exclusion premises, including closure dependencies. Their source origin remains the S obligation.

Unwind callback entry uses the installed callback's actual authentication, latent rows and existing protected receiver budget. Callback return and closing return reuse the predecessor annotation's exact suffix subtree. They retain the same output metadata and recorded caller scopes without a fresh successor check.

Retirement preserves existing budget evidence by consuming an owner absent from the physical suffix. Context.owned records owners retained by the actual decorated context, including saved captures and retirement markers; source agreement proves these owners belong to the physical stack. Successful cleanup projection preserves that ownership demand exactly. Phase transport then follows structurally through cleanup metadata, selected request budgets, computation budgets and all thirteen pending-budget forms. Spent markers remain valid after consumption. Both ordinary and administrative retirement derive absence from the same source witness and lifetime uniqueness, without a new cleanup check. Opening a saved continuation retains its retirement marker and exact receiving scope; the later retirement step performs consumption.

The consumed-clause, closing and handler-return proofs reuse one value-marker root-annotation lemma. Pending budgets also preserve their exact receivers when installation history grows, reusing the existing computation-budget theorem.

PendingBudget.append and PendingBudget.split retain each check at its exact lexical receiver, including saved continuations and retirement markers. PendingRows.budget_output_mode proves that the independently checked budget has the rich source's return mode. PendingRows.split_budgeted therefore extracts both actual source fragments and their budget evidence with one shared typed boundary. It adds no check or closing premise. Reentry at a changed receiver still requires the existing caller-cleanup obligations.

Capture's primitive continuation interface has also been separated from the blanket declaration-forest check. SelectedRequirements.capture_selected_compiler extracts the actual selected recipe's finite requirements and compiles its local clause checks at the selected receiving tail. No unrelated handler or dormant branch is checked by that result. The request's source judgment must still supply that selected finite check. The existing recipe compiler still limits inherited requests to non-disposing handlers with both modes and lacks inherited owner invocations in footprint fragments. These are the existing D obligations; the new interface does not establish their generalization or justify a source restriction. The shared invariant has not yet replaced its blanket forest field.

Handler installation now preserves its authenticated source and pending metadata without assuming the legacy installation check. Admitted.install_handler uses one fresh activation for the physical frame, registry extension, body receiver and raw step. FrameRows.handler_install retains the actual declaration rows; PendingRows.registries transports all six pending forms, including saved and opening continuations, using agreement at existing installations. Body and pending budgets survive the extended installation history. Equality of clause signatures transports only the existing certification, not an independently chosen metadata witness. Both ordinary requirement equations remain explicit. The older entry theorem reuses handler_root_annotation for its generated budget calculation. Full RetainedState entry remains open because the common invariant still includes the declaration-forest check and its source origin.

AuthDeclarations.selected extracts the actual selected clause plans, rich body and retained rows in ordinary and protected modes, following ordered lookup. ClauseRows.Selected records selection in those same decorations. Fresh-owner instantiation retains the operation endpoints and handler answer metadata. AuthBody.fresh_substitution then authenticates the exact existing owner-extension and operand-substitution results, reusing Auth.substitution and contract extension. Higher-order operand metadata remains intact. These results close authentication through clause selection and argument binding; they do not establish the selected body's contextual cleanup budget or complete capture preservation. The four outstanding transition alternatives and M1–M4 status above are unchanged.

Consumed-owner history now transports the existing contextual budgets without changing the common invariant. SpentHistory retains exact row decorations and saved captures while adding only spent markers for one consumed owner on the active lexical spine. Builtin selection and handler cuts retain the same target; closing metadata retains both its ordinary and protected budget checks. Budgeted.history, PendingBudget.outside_history and PendingBudget.history reuse those checks through all computation and pending-source constructors, including saved continuations and retirement boundaries. This is a proof transport, not a new runtime cleanup plan. It adds no successor-check premise. The outstanding transition and source-origin counts are unchanged.

Cleanup metadata now exposes its callback and remainder checks at their exact phases. A live capture checks its saved cleanup below the retirement barrier, then checks the remainder after the saved owners and enclosing owner are spent. Retiring and spent markers expose their respective availability and consumption facts. Auth.unit_callback_checked uses the actual authenticated lambda, its outward summary and existing substitution proof to check the Unit-instantiated body at the callback boundary. These six results reuse the existing evaluator; they do not derive that body's internal RequestBudget checks at a changed receiver. That source-origin step and the four transition cases remain open.

The structural SourceAdmission.Code and Pending certificates now retain recursive cleanup-budget evidence at requests and continuation invocations. Their compiler projects to the existing capability and budget judgments while keeping the stronger source certificate available. Request admission follows one actual lexical cut; pending admission follows the actual stack and return mode. Exact splitting, permission extension and consumed-owner history reuse those certificates. The own-discard source rule derives its abandonment and waiting certificates from the actual request and retained source. Own-resume likewise derives the restored certificate, preserving protected captures and their actual intermediate return modes without an assumed successor check.

SourceAdmission.Admitted connects this certificate to the same authenticated expression, row decorations and physical receiving context. Substitution, binding, application, all four ordinary computation reductions, focusing, cleanup registration and handler installation retain the certificate. Value plugging retains it through all ten waiting expression forms, using the same authenticated successor and its exact row decoration. The existing computation, focus and plugging proofs expose those witnesses; their previous interfaces remain projections of the same proofs. World and installation-history extension preserve the same rows and receivers. Spending an owner absent from the actual retained context preserves both code and pending certificates. The pending theorem checks absence from the combined context and external receiver; it reuses the existing request-budget transport and phase-commutation proof. Pure-frame transport covers the additional frame needed by focusing, including requests, both owner invocations and saved continuations. It does not assert that arbitrary pending code can be inserted after a continuation invocation.

The common RetainedSource constructors now retain these certificates alongside the same authenticated rows and receiving context. Evaluation carries current Code and pending Pending; unwinding carries pending Pending in unwind mode. The existing 18 transition theorems, covering the established 28 alternatives, retain these fields. Ordinary evaluation, callback boundaries, resource scopes, marker returns and all six administrative unwind cases reuse their previous operational and ownership proofs. Retirement derives certificate transport from the same physical owner absence. The old capability and budget fields remain temporarily as projections available to those proofs.

ResumeBodyAgreement relates a found resume record to the actual saved demand and requirement body. The capture allocator establishes this agreement for the same source it records. RecordPendingRows now occupies the coherent-source field of the common state and refers to its actual resume store. A live owner retains the matching ordinary saved source. An owner pending in unwind mode retains both that ordinary source and the unwind source of the same physical capture and decorated context. Resumption can therefore recover its ordinary source without identifying ordinary and unwind requirement bodies.
